summary:
Eischen, Harris, Li and Skinner complete the construction of p-adic L-functions for unitary groups begun in Harris–Li–Skinner (2006). For a CM field 𝒦/𝒦⁺, a hermitian space V and a cuspidal anti-holomorphic representation π of U(V) that is (anti-)ordinary of type (κ, K) at p, with 𝕋_π the corresponding local component of Hida's big ordinary Hecke algebra, Main Theorem 9.2.2 gives, under the Gorenstein hypothesis 7.3.2, the global multiplicity one hypothesis 7.3.3 and the minimality hypothesis 7.3.5, a unique L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) in Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋_π whose specialization at a classical (χ, λ_{π′}) is c(π′, χ) Ω_{π′,χ}(φ, φ^♭) I_∞ I_S L_p(·, ord, π′, χ_u) L^S(m + 1/2, π′, χ_u)/P_{π′,χ}: the critical value of the standard L-function of U(V) × GL(1)_𝒦 over a normalized Petersson period, with a congruence factor, an explicit p-adic Euler factor, an archimedean factor that is shown nonzero but not evaluated, and volume factors at the bad places. The method is the doubling method: the Siegel Eisenstein series of U(V ⊕ −V) is pulled back to U(V) × U(−V) and paired against the Hida family; the paper's new inputs are Part II, the local zeta integrals (above all Theorem 4.3.10 at p, where the Godement–Jacquet functional equation produces the denominator of the Euler factor), and Part III, a formalism that turns any measure satisfying stated axioms into an element of Λ ⊗̂ 𝕋_π, which Eischen's Eisenstein measure (Theorem 8.2.2) then satisfies.

The extraction has 458 items: 1 in the libraries (Mathlib's AbstractMeasure), 417 planned and 40 missing. The atlas plans this paper by name: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4, 'Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method', asks for EHLS in its exact setting down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses, and the PEL, compactification, automorphic-bundle, Hida-theory and measure layers it imports plan the rest. What no layer plans is the general machinery of the doubling method that L4 applies — the degenerate principal series and Siegel Eisenstein series of U(W) with their continuation, the doubling identity and its unfolding, the unramified computation, the Garrett map and the MVW involution, the continuation of L(s, π, χ) and the archimedean local theory. Those 40 items go to one Part II of Automorphic L-functions and local factors, the same roadmap (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactorsPartIIDoubling) that PAPER-CAI-FRIEDBERG-KAPLAN-24 proposes for the generalized doubling method, so that the doubling method is planned once.

The paper was read in full, proofs included, and 160 mistakes are recorded. Most are misprints, but several reach stated results, above all in the local theory at p that the Main Theorem rests on. The Schwartz function (58) defining the section at p is evaluated on p. 59 in the wrong coordinates, so Theorem 4.3.10 computes the zeta integral of a translate of that section (in a ramified n = 1 case the integral of the section as defined vanishes, while the theorem gives a nonzero ε-factor; v1 had the translation explicitly). Also: (83) counts the local pairing at p twice; I_2 in Theorem 4.3.10 is off by the sign ω(−1); the p-adic factor should be L_p(s + 1/2, ord); Theorem 4.6.1 mishandles the places above p; and the unramified identity holds with χ^{−1} under the paper's own normalisation. Elsewhere, Lemma 6.6.12(iii), Theorem 6.6.9 and the control theorems 7.2.1(ii) and 7.3.1(ii) are false as printed; the canonical-bundle character of §6.1.3 has exponents ±2a_σ where ±a_σ is right; and the positivity condition on δ that makes the unitary PEL datum a PEL datum is never stated. No erratum exists; every mistake is new.

items.name: Formula (1) — expected shape of a p-adic L-function attached to motives
items.statement: Framework recalled from the conjectures (not a theorem): one is given a p-adic analytic space Y and a subset Y^class ⊂ Y of points such that for each y ∈ Y^class there is a motive M_y, and possibly an additional datum r_y (a refinement), such that 0 is a critical value of the L-function L(s, M_y). The p-adic L-function is a meromorphic function L_p on Y whose values at y ∈ Y^class can be expressed in terms of L(0, M_y): there is a p-adic period p(M_y, r_y) such that L_p(y)/p(M_y, r_y) is an algebraic number, and (1) L_p(y)/p(M_y, r_y) = Z_∞(M_y) Z_p(M_y, r_y) · L(0, M_y)/c⁺(M_y). Here c⁺(M_y) is the period in Deligne's conjecture on special values of L-functions (so L(0, M_y)/c⁺(M_y) is algebraic), and Z_∞, Z_p are correction factors built out of Euler factors and ε-factors of the zeta function of M_y at the archimedean primes and at the primes dividing p respectively.
items.note: Expository: the 'very precise and orderly conjectures' of [Coa89, CPR89, Pan94, Hid96a], cited in §1.1 p. 2; nothing is proved about (1). §1.1.2 states explicitly that the authors have not checked that the terms of (2) match those of (1) termwise (item limitations). For the project, the refinement r_y is superfluous because the forms are (nearly) ordinary (p. 5). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L5 states the Coates–Perrin-Riou/Panchishkin existence problem with a specified critical set, periods and interpolation formula; PeriodsAndSpecialValues PS.1 plans Deligne-type critical-value statements.

items.name: The space Y of pairs (λ, χ) and its classical points Y^class (§1.1)
items.statement: Setting: 𝒦 is a CM field over Q, a quadratic extension of a totally real field 𝒦⁺, and V an n-dimensional hermitian vector space over 𝒦. Y is the space of pairs (λ, χ), where λ runs through the set of ordinary p-adic modular forms on the Shimura variety Sh(V) attached to U(V) (in the project, λ denotes a character of Hida's (nearly) ordinary Hecke algebra) and χ runs through p-adic Hecke characters of 𝒦; both λ and χ are assumed to be unramified outside a finite set S of primes of 𝒦, including those dividing p, and of bounded level at primes not dividing p. Because the forms are ordinary (more precisely, nearly ordinary in Hida's sense), the ring O(Y) of holomorphic functions on Y is finite over some Iwasawa algebra, and the refinement is superfluous. If (λ, χ) ∈ Y^class then: (i) λ = λ_π for some automorphic representation π of U(V), namely the character of the ordinary Hecke algebra acting on vectors of π that are spherical outside S and (nearly) ordinary at the primes dividing p; (ii) χ is a Hecke character of type A_0; (iii) the standard L-function L(s, π, χ) has a critical value at s = 0. Replacing χ by its products with powers of the norm character, this accommodates all critical values of L(s, π, χ).
items.note: Informal description; the paper notes that 'nearly ordinary' terminology is used inconsistently in the literature. §1.1.1 warns that the Shimura variety is attached to GU(V), not U(V) (item def-gu-plus-gu), and that all statements of §1.1 must be modified accordingly. The precise families and the precise theorem are in §7 and Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 plans the inverse limit of ray class groups of p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus, its character space and locally algebraic Hecke characters.

items.name: Formula (2) — the automorphic interpolation formula (introduction's version)
items.statement: Under hypotheses discussed below (T_π Gorenstein, freeness of ordinary forms over T_π, local minimality hypotheses; item hyp-gorenstein-freeness-intro), for a classical point (λ_π, χ) ∈ Y^class: (2) L_p(λ_π, χ) = c(π) · Z_∞(π, χ) Z_p(π, χ) Z_S · L(0, π, χ)/P_{π,χ}. The left-hand side is the specialization at the point (λ_π, χ) of an element L_p ∈ O(Y) (more precisely L_p ∈ O_{Y_{π,χ}}, the ring of functions of the connected component Y_{π,χ} containing (λ_π, χ)). The right-hand side is purely automorphic: L(s, π, χ) is the standard Langlands L-function of U(V) × GL(1)_𝒦; P_{π,χ} is a product of several terms, of which the most important is a normalized Petersson inner product of holomorphic forms on U(V); the local term Z_S is, in the paper's normalization, a local volume multiplied by a local inner product (depending on the choices); Z_∞ and Z_p are explicit local zeta integrals given by the doubling method; c(π) is a generator of the congruence ideal of λ_π (item congruence-factor-c-pi), depending on the same choices as P_{π,χ}, so that the right-hand side is independent of all choices.
items.note: Introduction's statement only; the precise statement is Main Theorem 9.2.2. The archimedean factor Z_∞ is left unspecified in the paper: it depends only on the archimedean data (the weights), not on the Hecke eigenvalues, and has been evaluated only for scalar weight (Shimura [Shi97]) and weight 'half scalar' at every archimedean place (Garrett [Gar08]). The presence of c(π) is 'a sign that L_p is not quite the p-adic L-function'. §1.1.2 refers to the period of (2) as Q_{π,χ} — a leftover of the old notation (source issue on p. 9). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The standard L-function L(s, π, χ) of U(V) × GL(1)_𝒦
items.statement: For π a (cuspidal) automorphic representation of U(V) and χ a Hecke character of 𝒦, L(s, π, χ) is the standard Langlands L-function of U(V) × GL(1)_𝒦. Its analytic and arithmetic properties have been studied most thoroughly using the doubling method.
items.note: The introduction gives no further definition; the Euler factors used are those produced by the doubling method (unramified factors recalled in §4.2). In the doubling integral its unramified factors appear as L(s + 1/2, π, χ) (item doubling-method).that notation does not occur in §1.1. Planned: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.4 plans the unramified Euler polynomial of an L-group representation, the partial Euler product and the comparison with AL.1–3.

items.name: U(V), the opposite space −V and U(−V), Sh(−V)
items.statement: Let V be a hermitian space over 𝒦 with hermitian form ⟨·,·⟩_V (relative to 𝒦/𝒦⁺) and U(V) its symmetry group (unitary group). −V denotes the space V with the hermitian form −⟨·,·⟩_V, and U(−V) and Sh(−V) the corresponding unitary group and Shimura variety. The groups U(V) and U(−V) are canonically isomorphic, but the natural identification of Sh(−V) with Sh(V) is anti-holomorphic; thus holomorphic automorphic forms on Sh(V) are identified with anti-holomorphic automorphic forms, or coherent cohomology classes of top degree, on Sh(−V), and vice versa.
items.note: U(V) is an algebraic group over 𝒦⁺ (the paper writes its rational points U(V)(F), with F = 𝒦⁺ in §1.1). The Shimura varieties are really attached to the rational-similitude group GU(V) (item def-gu-plus-gu, §1.1.1). In §4 the groups are renamed G_1, G_2, G_4 and U_i = ker ν. Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field; PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: The doubled hermitian space W = V ⊕ (−V), its maximal parabolic P, and U(V) × U(−V) ⊂ U(W)
items.statement: The space W = V ⊕ (−V), endowed with the hermitian form ⟨·,·⟩_V ⊕ −⟨·,·⟩_V, is always maximally isotropic (it has isotropic 𝒦-subspaces of dimension n = ½ dim W), so U(W) has a maximal parabolic subgroup P with Levi factor isomorphic to GL(n)_𝒦. U(V) × U(−V) naturally embeds in U(W) (acting on the two summands).
items.note: The introduction does not name the isotropic subspace; §4.1.1 takes P to be the stabilizer of the diagonal V^d = {(x, x)} (the Siegel parabolic) in the similitude group G_4, with Δ: P → GL_𝒦(V^d) = GL_𝒦(V). 'Maximally isotropic' here means W is split (has a Lagrangian). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.2 — the degenerate principal series I(χ, s)
items.statement: Let χ = ⊗χ_w be a character of 𝒦^×\𝔸_𝒦^×. For s ∈ ℂ, I(χ, s) := Ind_{P(𝔸)}^{G(𝔸)}( χ(det ∘ Δ(·)) · δ_P^{-s/n}(·) · |ν(·)|^{sn/2} ), smooth and unitarily normalized induction. It factors as a restricted tensor product I(χ, s) = ⊗_v I_v(χ_v, s), with v running over the places of ℚ, I_v(χ_v, s) the analogous local induction from P(ℚ_v) to G(ℚ_v), and χ_v = ⊗_{w|v} χ_w. Explicitly, f ∈ I(χ,s) satisfies f(pg) = χ(det Δ(p)) |det Δ(p)|^{-s} |ν(p)|^{sn/2} δ_mod(p)^{1/2} f(g), δ_mod the modulus character of P. On U_4 = U(W) this reads f(pg) = χ(det Δ(p)) |det Δ(p)|^{-s-n/2} f(g).
items.note: 1). The absolute values are not specified. Reading all |·| as the idelic module |·|_𝒦 of 𝒦 (ν ∈ 𝔸^× ⊂ 𝔸_𝒦^×) makes the centre act by the unitary character χ^n, and |det∘Δ|_𝒦·|ν|_𝒦^{-n/2} is then trivial on G_1 ⊂ G_4, which is Marcil's ∇ (arXiv:2311.05466, §3.1.2). With |ν| = |ν|_{𝔸_ℚ} the centre would act by a non-unitary character. History of the |ν| exponent: v1–v3 had |ν|^{-sn/2}, v4–v5 have |ν|^{+sn/2}. Only the restriction to U_4 is used in the zeta-integral computations. With the right action, sections of I(χ,s) are sections of the left-action degenerate principal series for χ^{-1}; see source issue on §4.2.1. Source issues: sourceIssues E41, sourceIssues E43. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.4 — the doubling zeta integral I(φ, φ^♭, f, s)
items.statement: Let f = f_s(•) ∈ I(χ, s), and let φ ∈ π, φ^♭ ∈ π^♭ be factorizable vectors as in (48). The zeta integral is I(φ, φ^♭, f, s) = ∫_{Z_3(𝔸)G_3(ℚ)\G_3(𝔸)} E_f(s, (g_1, g_2)) χ^{-1}(det g_2) φ(g_1) φ^♭(g_2) d(g_1, g_2), with (g_1, g_2) ∈ G_3 ⊂ G_4. By cuspidality of φ and φ^♭ it converges absolutely for those s at which E_f(s, g) is defined, and defines a meromorphic function of s (holomorphic wherever E_f(s, g) is).
items.note: The Garrett map φ ↦ G(f, φ, s) (introduction, §1.1) does not occur in §4.1 (pp. 41–46). ⟨·,·⟩ is the L² pairing for the Tamagawa measure dg. Z_3(𝔸)-invariance of the integrand needs the centre to act unitarily on E_f; see the |·| convention in the note to degenerate-principal-series. The paper passes silently from G_1-representations to their U_1(𝔸)-constituents here. Source issues: sourceIssues E39. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.4 — unfolding of the doubling integral (Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis, cited)
items.statement: Suppose ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩ ≠ 0, where ⟨·,·⟩ is the L² pairing for Tamagawa measure. For Re(s) sufficiently large, unfolding the Eisenstein series gives I(φ, φ^♭, f, s) = ∫_{U_1(𝔸)} f_s(u, 1) ⟨π(u)φ, φ^♭⟩_π du, where (u, 1) ∈ U_1 × U_2 ⊂ U_4 and π(u) is right translation.
items.note: Cited from the unfolding in [GPSR87], not proved here.Check: with P = Stab(V^d) the identity lies in the open P-orbit on P\G_4/(U_1 × U_2), and its stabilizer is the diagonal. Writing (g_1, g_2) = (g_2, g_2)(g_2^{-1}g_1, 1), f((g_2, g_2)x) = χ(det g_2) f(x) cancels the factor χ^{-1}(det g_2), and the inner integral is ⟨π(u)φ, φ^♭⟩. The identity is consistent with §4.1.2. The passage from the G_3-quotient to U_1(𝔸) and the measure normalisations are glossed over. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Continuation and functional equation from the doubling method
items.statement: As f, φ, φ′ vary, the doubling integrals I(φ, φ′, f, s) provide the meromorphic continuation and functional equation of the standard L-function L(s, π, χ) of U(V) × GL(1)_𝒦.
items.note: Cited as part of 'the doubling method asserts' [Gar84, GPSR87]; used as a known input, not proved in the paper. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: The Garrett map φ ↦ G(f, φ) (§9.1.1, (178); introduction §1.1)
items.statement: Let π be cuspidal of type (κ, K), φ ∈ π^K anti-holomorphic, χ a Hecke character as in §4.1.2. The zeta integral of §4.1.4 is I(φ, φ′, f, s) = ∫_{Z_3(𝔸)G_3(ℚ)\G_3(𝔸)} E_f(s, (g_1, g_2)) χ^{−1}(det g_2) φ(g_1) φ′(g_2) d(g_1, g_2), with φ′ ∈ π̄ and E_f(s, ·) the Eisenstein series of a section f ∈ I(χ, s). Specialise s to a point m at which E_f(s, •) is nearly holomorphic (f_∞ satisfies the archimedean hypotheses of Definition 5.3.2). The Garrett map is G(f, φ)(g_2) = I(φ, f, m)(g_2) := χ^{−1}(det g_2) ∫_{Z_1(𝔸)G_1(ℚ)\G_1(𝔸)} E_f(m, (g_1, g_2)) φ(g_1) dg_1 (178); G(φ) := G(f, φ) when f is clear.
items.note: φ and G(φ) live on the same group GU(V) = GU(−V) but on different Shimura varieties: E_f(m, •) restricted to G_3 is holomorphic on Sh(V, −V), so pairing with an anti-holomorphic form on Sh(V) gives a holomorphic form on Sh(−V). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: The Hida family Y_{π,χ} through (λ_π, χ) and its ring of functions Λ ⊗̂ T_π
items.statement: The point (λ_π, χ) belongs to a Hida family, which here means a connected component Y_{π,χ} of the space Y (in other contexts one works with an irreducible component). The ring of functions on Y_{π,χ} is of the form Λ ⊗̂ T_π, where Λ is an Iwasawa algebra attached to χ and T_π is the localization of the big Hecke algebra at the maximal ideal attached to π.
items.note: Informal; the ordinary Hecke algebra T_π and its localization are defined in §6–§7 (e.g. Definition 6.7.9, T = T_π). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The special hypotheses underlying formula (2)
items.statement: The principal hypotheses are: (a) T_π is Gorenstein; (b) the module of ordinary modular forms (more precisely its Z_p-dual) is free over T_π. There are also (c) local hypotheses that correspond to the hypothesis of minimal level in the Taylor–Wiles theory of deformations of modular Galois representations. These hypotheses make it possible to define L_p as an element of O_{Y_{π,χ}}.
items.note: Hypotheses, not results. p. 4: these hypotheses 'are not indispensable, but they make the statements much more natural'; the integral information carried by Betti periods is recovered in the doubling method 'provided one works with Hida families that are free over their corresponding Hecke algebras, and one assumes that the Hecke algebras are Gorenstein'; the Gorenstein hypothesis, suitably interpreted, is 'particularly natural in the setting of the doubling method'. Precise forms: hypotheses of Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The congruence factor c(π)
items.statement: c(π) is a generator of the congruence ideal which measures congruences between λ_π and other characters λ_{π′} of T_π (of the same weight and level). The specific generator c(π) depends on the same choices used to define P_{π,χ}, so that the product on the right-hand side of (2) is independent of all choices; c(π) is only well defined up to multiplication by a p-adic unit. The appearance of c(π) in the specialization of L_p is a formal consequence of the Gorenstein hypothesis.
items.note: The congruence module C(π) and its generator are made precise in §6.7 (e.g. Lemma 6.7.7, where c(π, χ)Q_{π,χ} = Q[π, χ]). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: L_p without the special hypotheses (introduction)
items.statement: In the absence of the special hypotheses it is still possible to define L_p in the fraction field of Λ ⊗̂ T_π, but the statement is not so clean. In any case the p-adic valuations of c(π) are in principle unbounded, so the p-adic interpolation of the normalized critical values of standard L-functions is in general given by a meromorphic function on Y.
items.note: Informal claim; no proof in the introduction (cf. §9.3). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Implicit standing assumption: Arthur's multiplicity conjectures for unitary groups
items.statement: The authors 'have assumed implicitly that Arthur's multiplicity conjectures are known for unitary groups', needed because they work with unitary groups over totally real fields with arbitrary signatures (not only quasi-split ones). Context: the p-adic L-functions are best understood as p-adic analogues of standard L-functions of cuspidal automorphic representations of GL(n); the passage from unitary groups to GL(n) is by stable base change; a version adequate for the applications is due to Labesse [Lab11]; complete results including multiplicity formulas were proved by Mok for quasi-split unitary groups [Mok15], which does not suffice; the general case is being completed by Kaletha, Minguez, Shin and White, and [KMSW14] works out the multiplicities of tempered representations and 'is probably sufficient for the purposes of the present project'.
items.note: A global hypothesis a formaliser must track: it is not stated as a numbered hypothesis anywhere in §§1–2.5. Compare the global multiplicity-one hypothesis of Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 plans the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs; EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a plans unitary-to-GL_m base-change identities.

items.name: Anti-ordinary representations (introduction)
items.statement: Hida's theory of (nearly) ordinary modular forms applies to holomorphic automorphic representations, but the doubling method requires anti-holomorphic representations. The eigenvalues of the U_p-operators on (anti-holomorphic) representations do not coincide with those on their holomorphic duals; 'for lack of a better terminology', the anti-holomorphic representations corresponding to ordinary ones are called anti-ordinary. Keeping track of the normalizations adds bookkeeping but no essential difficulty.
items.note: Informal; the precise local theory of ordinary and anti-ordinary vectors at p-adic places is §8. Also on p. 8: the ordinary hypotheses for unitary groups of different signatures represent different branches of a p-adic L-function for GL(n), related only in a general overconvergent family. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §1.1.2 — what the project does not accomplish
items.statement: The authors list the following restrictions. (i) They have not verified that the local terms (Z_p, Z_∞, Z_S) and the global terms (L(0, π, χ), P_{π,χ}) in (2) correspond termwise with those predicted by the general conjectures on p-adic L-functions for motives; comparing (1) with (2), the motive M_y corresponds to the hypothetical motive attached to π, whose ℓ-adic realization is the n-dimensional representation of Gal(Q̄/𝒦) constructed in [Che04] (among many other places), twisted by the ℓ-adic Galois character attached to χ; the local factor Z_p has the same shape as the local factors in the conjectures of [Coa89, CPR89], but it has not been checked that the Frobenius eigenvalues there are exactly the ones found here; until Z_∞(π, χ) is computed explicitly it cannot be compared with anything motivic. (ii) Local factors at ramified finite primes for π and χ are not analysed: the geometry of the moduli space has no obvious connection with the local theory of the doubling method, and a complete treatment needs a p-integral doubling method (possibly available through work of Minguez, Helm, Emerton–Helm, Moss); instead local data at bad primes are chosen to give simple volume factors. (iii) General overconvergent families, where Hida theory is not appropriate, are not treated. (iv) P-ordinary forms in the sense of [Hid98] (for P ⊂ G a parabolic; P = B gives (nearly) ordinary forms; for P of p-adic rank r they vary in r-dimensional families up to global adjustments; a form can be P-ordinary without being B-ordinary) are not treated, although the theory applies to them; [EM19] is a first step. (v) The p-adic adjoint L-function whose specialization at π should be c(π) is not constructed (item c-pi-adjoint-expectation). (vi) The base field 𝒦 is always assumed unramified at p; this is unnecessary thanks to [Lan18] but simplifies statements.
items.note: Restricted to §1.1.2; the discussion in §9.3 (Gorenstein hypothesis, multiplicity one, pp. 145–146) belongs to §9.3's items. The printed text of (i) calls the period Q_{π,χ} (misprint for P_{π,χ}; source issue). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Standing hypothesis on p
items.statement: p is a fixed prime that is unramified in 𝒦 and such that every place of 𝒦⁺ above p splits in 𝒦.
items.note: Standing hypothesis for the whole paper. §1.1.2: the unramifiedness of 𝒦 at p is unnecessary thanks to [Lan18] but simplifies statements. The splitting condition is what makes (9), the CM type Σ of §2.3 and the ordinary theory work. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The unitary similitude groups GU⁺(V) (over 𝒦⁺) and GU(V) (over Q, rational similitude factor)
items.statement: For a hermitian space V over 𝒦 with hermitian form ⟨,⟩, GU⁺(V) is the group scheme over 𝒦⁺ of unitary similitudes of V: for any 𝒦⁺-algebra R, GU⁺(V)(R) = {g ∈ GL(V ⊗_{𝒦⁺} R) | ⟨g(v), g(v′)⟩ = ν(g)⟨v, v′⟩ ∀ v, v′ ∈ V ⊗_{𝒦⁺} R}, where ν(g) ∈ R^× (this is the group usually denoted GU(V)). GU(V) denotes the Q-subgroup scheme of R_{𝒦⁺/Q} GU⁺(V) given by the fibre product GU(V) = R_{𝒦⁺/Q} GU⁺(V) ×_{R_{𝒦⁺/Q} G_{m,𝒦⁺}} G_m, where R_{𝒦⁺/Q}GU⁺(V) → R_{𝒦⁺/Q}G_{m,𝒦⁺} is ν and G_m ↪ R_{𝒦⁺/Q} G_{m,𝒦⁺} is the canonical inclusion (unitary similitudes with rational similitude factor).
items.note: §1.1.1: the Shimura variety is attached not to U(V) but to GU(V), 'the subgroup of the similitude group of V with rational similitude factor'; 'this detail plagues the paper from beginning to end'. 𝒦-linearity of g is automatic from nondegeneracy of ⟨,⟩ (⟨g(av), g v′⟩ = ⟨a g(v), g v′⟩). GU⁺(b_σ) reappears in (17). Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field.

items.name: Automorphic representations for a Shimura datum (convention)
items.statement: When (G, X) is a Shimura datum, an automorphic representation of G is defined to be a (g, K) × G(A_f)-submodule of the space of automorphic forms, where K is the stabilizer of a point in X; in particular K contains the center of G(R) but does not in general contain a full maximal compact subgroup. In this way holomorphic and anti-holomorphic representations are kept separate (of fundamental importance for coherent cohomology and the construction of p-adic L-functions).
items.note: Non-standard convention a formaliser must adopt: e.g. for GL_2, K = R^× SO(2), not R^× O(2). Planned: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.2 plans automorphic representations and their restricted tensor factorization.

items.name: Hypotheses 1.4.4(1) — volume 1 on hyperspecial subgroups
items.statement: Setting of §1.4.3: G is a reductive group over a number field F, dg a Haar measure on G(A), taken for definiteness to be Tamagawa measure, written dg = ∏_v dg_v with dg_v a Haar measure on G(F_v). Hypothesis: at all finite places v at which G is unramified, dg_v is the measure that gives volume 1 to a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup.
items.note: Measure normalization (paper-wide convention). Well defined: hyperspecial subgroups are conjugate under G_ad(F_v), which preserves Haar measure of G(F_v). The paper says it is 'not so concerned with the precise choice of measure' since archimedean zeta integrals are not computed, 'but we do want to be consistent'. Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 plans invariant quotient and Tamagawa measures.

items.name: Hypotheses 1.4.4(2) — volume 1 on ∏ GL(n_i, O_i)
items.statement: At all finite places v at which G is isomorphic to ∏_i GL(n_i, F_{i,w_i}), where F_{i,w_i} is a finite extension of F_v with integer ring O_i (whether or not F_{i,w_i} is ramified over the corresponding completion of Q), dg_v is the measure that gives volume 1 to the group ∏_i GL(n_i, O_i).
items.note: Consistent with (1) when both apply (∏ GL(n_i, O_i) is hyperspecial when every F_{i,w_i}/F_v is unramified). Applies to unitary groups at split places (U(V)(𝒦⁺_v) ≅ GL_n(𝒦_w)). Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 plans invariant quotient and Tamagawa measures.

items.name: Hypotheses 1.4.4(3) — rational volumes
items.statement: At all finite places v, the values of dg_v on open compact subgroups are rational numbers.
items.note: Needed for rationality/integrality of volume factors in the local zeta integrals. Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 plans invariant quotient and Tamagawa measures.

items.name: Hypotheses 1.4.4(4) — archimedean normalization to Tamagawa measure
items.statement: At archimedean places v, the measures dg_v are chosen such that ∏_v dg_v is Tamagawa measure.
items.note: Given (1)–(3) at finite places this fixes the archimedean measure. For groups with a split central torus the Tamagawa normalization needs the usual convergence-factor/centre conventions, which the paper does not spell out. Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 plans invariant quotient and Tamagawa measures.

items.name: The bilinear Petersson pairing ⟨f_1, f_2⟩_Z (3)
items.statement: Let Z_G ⊂ G be the center of G and Z ⊂ Z_G(A) a closed subgroup such that Z · Z_G(F)\Z_G(A) is compact (printed: 'Z_G(A)/Z is compact'; see source issue); for example Z can be taken to be the group of real points of the maximal F-split subgroup of Z_G. Choose a Haar measure on Z satisfying the conditions of 1.4.4 if Z is the group of adèles of an F-subgroup of Z_G. The measure dg defines a bilinear pairing ⟨,⟩ on L²(Z · G(F)\G(A)); more generally, if f_1(zg) f_2(zg) = f_1(g) f_2(g) for all z ∈ Z, put (3) ⟨f_1, f_2⟩_Z = ∫_{Z·G(F)\G(A)} f_1(g) f_2(g) dg, and if not, set ⟨f_1, f_2⟩_Z = 0. If π and π^∨ are irreducible cuspidal automorphic representations of G, then ⟨,⟩_Z: π ⊗ π^∨ → C is a canonically defined pairing.
items.note: Bilinear (not hermitian) pairing; the measure on the quotient is dg divided by the chosen measure on Z. π^∨ means the automorphic realization of the contragredient (central characters inverse on Z). Planned: AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.2 plans invariant quotient and Tamagawa measures; AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.2 plans automorphic representations and their restricted tensor factorization.

items.name: The constant C(dg, fac_π, fac_{π^∨}, ∏⟨,⟩_{π_v}) of (6)
items.statement: Let π, π^∨ be irreducible cuspidal automorphic representations of G with factorizations (4) fac_π: π ≅ ⊗′_v π_v, fac_{π^∨}: π^∨ ≅ ⊗′_v π_v^∨ (π_v irreducible representations of G(F_v)), and let (5) ⟨,⟩_{π_v}: π_v ⊗ π_v^∨ → C be non-degenerate pairings of G(F_v)-spaces for all v, normalized — implicitly; see source issue — so that ⟨φ_v^0, φ_v^{∨,0}⟩_{π_v} = 1 for the distinguished vectors defining the restricted tensor products at almost all v. Then there is a constant C = C(dg, fac_π, fac_{π^∨}, ∏_v ⟨,⟩_{π_v}) such that for all φ ∈ π, φ^∨ ∈ π^∨ that are factorizable, fac_π(φ) = ⊗_v φ_v and fac_{π^∨}(φ^∨) = ⊗_v φ_v^∨, (6) ⟨φ, φ^∨⟩_Z = C(dg, fac_π, fac_{π^∨}, ∏_v ⟨,⟩_{π_v}) ∏_v ⟨φ_v, φ_v^∨⟩_{π_v}.
items.note: Stated without proof; it follows from Schur's lemma: both sides are G(A)-invariant bilinear forms on π ⊗ π^∨ and Hom_{G(A)}(π ⊗ π^∨, C) is one-dimensional. The normalization in the statement is not printed (source issue); it holds for the standard local pairing (7) with spherical vectors normalized by f(1) = 1, since vol(K_v) = 1. Planned: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.2 plans automorphic representations and their restricted tensor factorization.

items.name: The standard local pairing (7)
items.statement: When G is quasi-split and unramified over F_v and π_v is a principal series representation induced from a Borel subgroup B ⊂ G(F_v) (so that for f ∈ π_v, f^∨ ∈ π_v^∨ realized in the induced models, f·f^∨ transforms on the left under B by δ_B), choose a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup K_v ⊂ G(F_v) and define the standard local pairing (7) ⟨f, f^∨⟩_{π_v} = ∫_{K_v} f(g_v) f^∨(g_v) dg_v. In situation (2) of Hypotheses 1.4.4, K_v = ∏_i GL(n_i, O_i). Correction: the paper adds that 'the pairing (7) does not depend on the choice of K_v'; this is false — replacing K_v by K_v′ = b K_v b^{−1} (b ∈ B, the general case since G(F_v) = B K_v) multiplies (7) by δ_B(b) — so K_v must be fixed once and for all (source issue).
items.note: G(F_v)-invariance of (7) follows from the Iwasawa decomposition G(F_v) = B K_v and the invariance of F ↦ ∫_{K_v} F on the space of functions with F(bg) = δ_B(b)F(g). The constant C of (6) absorbs a change of K_v, so the error is harmless if one K_v is used consistently. Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Jacquet functors and duals; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3 plans smooth contragredient duality.

items.name: PEL datum
items.statement: A PEL datum is a tuple P = (B, ∗, O_B, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h) where: B is a semisimple Q-algebra with positive involution ∗, written b ↦ b^∗; O_B is a ∗-stable Z-order in B; L is a Z-lattice with a left O_B-action and a non-degenerate alternating pairing ⟨·,·⟩: L × L → Z(1) such that ⟨bx, y⟩ = ⟨x, b^∗y⟩ for x, y ∈ L and b ∈ O_B; h: C → End_{O_B⊗R}(L ⊗ R) is a homomorphism (of R-algebras) such that ⟨h(z)x, y⟩ = ⟨x, h(z̄)y⟩ for x, y ∈ L ⊗ R and z ∈ C, and −√−1⟨·, h(√−1)·⟩ is positive definite and symmetric.
items.note: Follows [Lan13, §1.2]. Since ⟨,⟩ is Z(1) = 2π√−1 Z-valued, −√−1⟨·, h(√−1)·⟩ is real-valued; its sign agrees with Lan's normalization (2π√−1)^{−1}⟨·, h(√−1)·⟩. Symmetry is automatic from ⟨h(z)x, y⟩ = ⟨x, h(z̄)y⟩ and alternation. Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field.

items.name: Standing conditions on PEL data at p (for p-adic modular forms)
items.statement: For defining p-adic modular forms the PEL data considered are assumed also to satisfy: (a) B has no type D factor; (b) ⟨·,·⟩: (L ⊗ Z_p) × (L ⊗ Z_p) → Z_p(1) is a perfect pairing; (c) p ∤ Disc(O_B), where Disc(O_B) is the discriminant of O_B over Z defined in [Lan13, Def. 1.1.1.6] — this implies that O_B ⊗ Z_(p) is a maximal Z_(p)-order in B and that O_B ⊗ Z_p is a product of matrix algebras; (d) the technical [Lan13, Condition 1.4.3.10] is satisfied.
items.note: Standing hypotheses (one list, kept as one item). The consequences in (c) are cited from Lan. For the unitary data of §2.3, (b)–(c) follow from p unramified in 𝒦, δ prime to p and the choice of L_i. Planned: PELModuli M2 plans representability and smoothness at good level, with the good-prime conditions.

items.name: The group scheme G = G_P over Z
items.statement: To a PEL datum P as above one associates the group scheme G = G_P over Z: for any Z-algebra R, G(R) = {(g, ν) ∈ GL_{O_B⊗R}(L ⊗ R) × R^× : ⟨gx, gy⟩ = ν⟨x, y⟩ ∀ x, y ∈ L ⊗ R}. ν: G → G_m is the similitude character.
items.note: ⟨,⟩ is extended R(1)-valued to L ⊗ R. For unitary data (§2.3) G is the unitary similitude group with rational similitude (cf. item def-gu-plus-gu). Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field.

items.name: G_{/Q} is reductive; G_{/Z_p} smooth and G(Z_p) hyperspecial
items.statement: G_{/Q} is a reductive group, and by the hypotheses with respect to p (item hyp-pel-p-conditions), G_{/Z_p} is smooth and G(Z_p) is a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of G(Q_p).
items.note: Asserted without proof or reference; standard (cf. Kottwitz [Kot92, §5] and Lan). 'No type D factor' is what makes G_{/Q} connected. For unitary type it also follows from (9). Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans parahoric and congruence group schemes.

items.name: Reflex field F, the set □, S_□, and the level K
items.statement: F ⊂ C is the reflex field of (L, ⟨·,·⟩, h) (or of P) as defined in [Lan13, 1.2.5.4], and O_F its ring of integers. □ = {p} or ∅, Z_(□) is the localization of Z at the primes in □ (so Z_({p}) = Z_(p) and Z_(∅) = Q), and S_□ = O_F ⊗ Z_(□). K^□ ⊂ G(A_f^□) is an open compact subgroup, and K ⊂ G(A_f) is K^□ if □ = ∅ and G(Z_p)K^□ otherwise. K is assumed neat, as defined in [Lan13, Def. 1.4.1.8].
items.note: Notation: with □ = {p}, K^□ = K^p (also written K^(p) in §2.5). Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field.

items.name: The PEL moduli problem M_K = M_K(P)
items.statement: M_K is the functor on locally noetherian S_□-schemes that assigns to such a scheme T the set of equivalence classes of quadruples (A, λ, ι, α) where: A is an abelian scheme over T; λ: A → A^∨ is a prime-to-□ polarization; ι: O_B ⊗ Z_(□) → End_T A ⊗ Z_(□) satisfies ι(b)^∨∘λ = λ∘ι(b^∗); α is a K^□-level structure, i.e. it assigns to a geometric point t on each connected component of T a π_1(T, t)-stable K^□-orbit of O_B ⊗ A_f^□-isomorphisms α_t: L ⊗ A_f^□ ≅ H_1(A_t, A_f^□) that identify ⟨·,·⟩ with an A_f^{□,×}-multiple of the symplectic pairing on the Tate module H_1(A_t, A_f^□) defined by λ and the Weil pairing; and Lie_T A satisfies the Kottwitz determinant condition defined by (L ⊗ R, ⟨·,·⟩, h) [Lan13, Def. 1.3.4.1]. Two quadruples (A, λ, ι, α) and (A′, λ′, ι′, α′) are equivalent if there exists a prime-to-□ isogeny — to be read as prime-to-□ quasi-isogeny, see source issue — f: A → A′ such that λ equals f^∨∘λ′∘f up to some positive element of Z_(□)^×, ι′(b)∘f = f∘ι(b) for all b ∈ O_B, and α′ = f∘α.
items.note: Lan's formulation by Z_(□)^×-isogeny classes with rational level structures. K^□ acts on the α_t by right composition. §1.1.1: this moduli space is in general a union of several Shimura varieties indexed by the defect of the Hasse principle (item kot92-moduli-decomposition); p-adic modular forms are defined on it, computations are done on one Shimura variety. Planned: PELModuli M1 plans the PEL moduli functors.

items.name: Representability of M_K by a smooth quasi-projective S_□-scheme
items.statement: Suppose K is neat. Then there is a smooth, quasi-projective S_□-scheme M_K = M_K(P) that represents the functor of item pel-moduli.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'as explained in [Lan13, Cor. 7.2.3.10]'. Planned: PELModuli M2 plans representability and smoothness at good level, with the good-prime conditions; ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans Lan's integral PEL toroidal compactifications.

items.name: PEL datum of unitary type; e_i, n_i, O_{B,w}, L_w
items.statement: A PEL datum P = (B, ∗, O_B, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h) as in §2.1 is of unitary type if B = 𝒦^m (the product of m copies of 𝒦), ∗ is the involution acting as c on each factor of 𝒦, and O_B ∩ 𝒦 = O where 𝒦 maps to B = 𝒦^m diagonally. By maximality (p ∤ Disc(O_B)), O_B ⊗ Z_(p) = O_1 × ⋯ × O_m = O_(p) × ⋯ × O_(p) (each O_i a maximal Z_(p)-order in 𝒦), so O_B ⊗ Z_p ≅ ∏_{w|p} ∏_{i=1}^m O_w. e_i ∈ O_B ⊗ Z_(p) is the idempotent projecting B to the i-th copy of 𝒦, and n_i = dim_𝒦 e_i(L ⊗ Q). For w | p, O_{B,w} = O_B ⊗_O O_w and L_w = L ⊗_O O_w.
items.note: O_{B,w} is used in (8) before being defined (p. 16, defined later on the same page). e_i^∗ = e_i, so e_iL_w pairs only with e_iL_w̄. Planned: PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: The isomorphism (8) GL_{O_B⊗Z_p}(L ⊗ Z_p) ≅ ∏_{w|p} ∏_i GL_{O_w}(e_iL_w)
items.statement: Over Z_p there is a canonical isomorphism (8) GL_{O_B⊗Z_p}(L ⊗ Z_p) ≅ ∏_{w|p} ∏_{i=1}^m GL_{O_w}(e_i L_w), g ↦ (g_{w,i}), induced by the O_B ⊗ Z_p = ∏_{w|p} O_{B,w}-decomposition L ⊗ Z_p = ∏_{w|p} L_w.
items.note: Immediate from O_B ⊗ Z_p ≅ ∏_{w,i} O_w; checked. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The isomorphism (9) G_{/Z_p} ≅ G_m × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_i GL_{O_w}(e_iL_w)
items.statement: The isomorphism (8) induces (9) G_{/Z_p} ≅ G_m × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_{i=1}^m GL_{O_w}(e_i L_w), (g, ν) ↦ (ν, (g_{w,i})), with the convention of Remark 1.4.2.
items.note: No proof given; checked: ⟨e_w x, y⟩ = ⟨x, e_w̄ y⟩ so L_w ⊥ L_{w′} unless w′ = w̄, and ⟨,⟩: L_w × L_w̄ → Z_p(1) is perfect; for (g, ν) ∈ G, g_{w̄,i} = ν·(g_{w,i}^∗)^{−1} (adjoint for this pairing) is determined by ν and g_{w,i}, and every (ν, (g_{w,i})_{w∈Σ_p}) arises. Uses the standing hypothesis that every place of 𝒦⁺ above p splits. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The signature {(a_{σ,i}, b_{σ,i})} of h
items.statement: The homomorphism h determines a pure Hodge structure of weight −1 on V = L ⊗ C, V = V^{−1,0} ⊕ V^{0,−1}. Let V^0 ⊂ V be the O_B ⊗ C-submodule V^{−1,0} ≅ V/V^{0,−1} (the summand on which h(z) acts by z; the Lie-algebra side of the Kottwitz condition) — the paper says 'the degree 0 piece of the Hodge filtration', which is V^{0,−1} and contradicts §2.3 and §2.6.3 (source issue). For each σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 let a_{σ,i} = dim_C e_i(V^0 ⊗_{O⊗C,σ} C) and b_{σ,i} = n_i − a_{σ,i}. The collection {(a_{σ,i}, b_{σ,i})}_{σ∈Σ_𝒦} is the signature of h. Then (a_{σc,i}, b_{σc,i}) = (b_{σ,i}, a_{σ,i}).
items.note: Corrected statement (see source issue on the Hodge filtration). The symmetry (a_{σc}, b_{σc}) = (b_σ, a_σ) holds for either reading since complex conjugation exchanges V^{−1,0} and V^{0,−1} and the σ- and σc-components. §2.6.3 uses rank e_iΛ_{0,σ} = a_{σ,i} with Λ_0 ⊗ C = V/V^{0,−1}. Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field.

items.name: Hypothesis 2.2.1 (Ordinary hypothesis) and (a_{w,i}, b_{w,i})
items.statement: Assumed throughout: for σ, σ′ ∈ Σ_𝒦 (and each i), p_σ = p_{σ′} ⟹ a_{σ,i} = a_{σ′,i}. For w | p a place of 𝒦 one then defines (a_{w,i}, b_{w,i}) = (a_{σ,i}, b_{σ,i}) for any σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 such that p_w = p_σ.
items.note: 'Fundamental hypothesis'. Consequence: (a_{w̄,i}, b_{w̄,i}) = (b_{w,i}, a_{w,i}) (from c(p_σ) = p_{σc}). This is the condition under which the p-adic theory (ordinary locus, L^±) is set up. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The polarization L ⊗ Z_p = L⁺ ⊕ L⁻
items.statement: Fix an O_B ⊗ Z_p-decomposition L ⊗ Z_p = L⁺ ⊕ L⁻ such that: L⁺ = ∏_{w|p} L_w⁺ is an O_B ⊗ Z_p = ∏_{w|p} O_{B,w}-module with rank_{O_w}(e_i L_w⁺) = a_{w,i} (so L⁻ = ∏_{w|p} L_w⁻ with rank_{O_w}(e_i L_w⁻) = b_{w,i} and L_w = L_w⁺ ⊕ L_w⁻); and L_w^± is the annihilator of L_w̄^± for the perfect pairing ⟨·,·⟩: L_w × L_w̄ → Z_p(1).
items.note: Existence (not argued in the paper; checked): choose L_w^± for w ∈ Σ_p with the right ranks and let L_w̄^± be their annihilators; ranks match because a_{w̄,i} = b_{w,i}. Consequences: L⁺ is a Lagrangian O_B ⊗ Z_p-submodule and e_iL_w⁺ is Z_p-dual to e_iL_w̄⁻ via ⟨,⟩. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Bases of e_iL_w^± and the isomorphisms (10)
items.statement: Fix a decomposition of e_iL_w⁺ as a direct sum of copies of O_w (for each w | p). Taking Z_p-duals via ⟨·,·⟩ yields a decomposition of e_iL_w̄⁻ as a direct sum of copies of O_w̄ ≅ Hom_{Z_p}(O_w, Z_p) (the O_B-action on Hom_{Z_p}(O_w, Z_p) — printed 'Hom_{Z_p}(E_{i,w}, Z_p)', source issue — factors through e_iO_B ⊗ Z_(p) and is given by bφ(x) = φ(b^∗x)). The choice of these decompositions determines isomorphisms (10) GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w⁺) ≅ GL_{a_{w,i}}(O_w), GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w⁻) ≅ GL_{b_{w,i}}(O_w), and GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w) ≅ GL_{n_i}(O_w), with respect to which the embedding GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w⁺) × GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w⁻) ↪ GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w) = GL_{O_{i,w}}(e_iL_w⁺ ⊕ e_iL_w⁻) is the block diagonal map (A, B) ↦ diag(A, B).
items.note: O_{i,w} is not defined; it means e_iO_{B,w} ≅ O_w (in (8) the same groups are written GL_{O_w}). The O-action on Hom_{Z_p}(O_w, Z_p) via b ↦ (φ ↦ φ(b^∗·)) is through c, i.e. through O_w̄, which is why the dual of a copy of O_w is a copy of O_w̄ (p unramified: the trace dual of O_w is O_w). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The PEL datum of unitary type attached to hermitian pairs 𝒱 = (V_i, ⟨·,·⟩_{V_i})
items.statement: Let 𝒱 = (V_i, ⟨·,·⟩_{V_i})_{1≤i≤m} be hermitian pairs over 𝒦: V_i a finite-dimensional 𝒦-space and ⟨·,·⟩_{V_i}: V_i × V_i → 𝒦 hermitian relative to 𝒦/𝒦⁺. Let δ ∈ O be totally imaginary and prime to p, and — a condition missing from the paper (source issue) — such that Im σ(δ) > 0 for all σ ∈ Σ if ⟨·,·⟩_{V_i} is 𝒦-linear in the first variable (Im σ(δ) < 0 for all σ ∈ Σ if linear in the second). Put ⟨·,·⟩_i = trace_{𝒦/Q} δ⟨·,·⟩_{V_i}, and let L_i ⊂ V_i be an O-lattice with ⟨L_i, L_i⟩_i ⊂ Z such that ⟨·,·⟩_i is a perfect pairing on L_i ⊗ Z_p. For each σ ∈ Σ_𝒦, V_{i,σ} = V_i ⊗_{𝒦,σ} C has a C-basis with respect to which ⟨·,·⟩_{i,σ} = ⟨·,·⟩_{V_i,σ} is given by diag(1_{r_{i,σ}}, −1_{s_{i,σ}}); fixing such a basis, let h_{i,σ}: C → End_R(V_{i,σ}) be h_{i,σ}(z) = diag(z 1_{r_{i,σ}}, z̄ 1_{s_{i,σ}}). Let Σ = {σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 : p_σ ∈ Σ_p} and h_i = ∏_{σ∈Σ} h_{i,σ}: C → End_{𝒦⁺⊗R}(V_i ⊗ R) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} End_R(V_{i,σ}). Let B = 𝒦^m, ∗ the involution acting by c on each 𝒦-factor, O_B = O^m, L = ∏_i L_i with the i-th factor of O_B = O^m acting by scalar multiplication on the i-th factor of L, ⟨·,·⟩ = Σ_i ⟨·,·⟩_i, and h = ∏_i h_i. Then P = (B, ∗, O_B, L, 2π√−1⟨·,·⟩, h) is a PEL datum of unitary type.
items.note: Corrected statement (δ-sign condition; source issue). Other axioms checked: ⟨·,·⟩_i is alternating (δH(x, x) is totally imaginary), ⟨bx, y⟩ = ⟨x, b^∗y⟩, ⟨h(z)x, y⟩ = ⟨x, h(z̄)y⟩ (the r- and s-parts are orthogonal), p ∤ Disc(O^m). This is the source of all the unitary PEL data P_1, …, P_4 of §3 (§4.1 uses ⟨·,·⟩_1 = trace δ⟨·,·⟩_V with the same δ). Planned: PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: Existence of the lattices L_i
items.statement: An O-lattice L_i ⊂ V_i with ⟨L_i, L_i⟩_i ⊂ Z such that ⟨·,·⟩_i is a perfect pairing on L_i ⊗ Z_p exists, because of the hypotheses on p (unramified in 𝒦; every place of 𝒦⁺ above p split) and on δ (prime to p).
items.note: Asserted with this one-line justification; correct: at w ∈ Σ_p take any O_w-lattice in V_i ⊗ 𝒦_w and at w̄ its dual for the perfect pairing induced by trace∘δ (perfect since p is unramified and δ is a unit at p); away from p scale to get integrality. Planned: PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: Σ = {σ : p_σ ∈ Σ_p} is a CM type
items.statement: The set Σ = {σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 : p_σ ∈ Σ_p} is a CM type of 𝒦.
items.note: Stated without proof; checked: c(p_σ) = p_{σc} ≠ p_σ (splitting), and Σ_p contains exactly one of p_σ, p_{σc}, so Σ ⊔ Σc = Σ_𝒦. Notation clash: from §2.4 on, Σ also denotes a polyhedral cone decomposition. Planned: PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: Signature of h versus the signatures (r_{i,σ}, s_{i,σ})
items.statement: For P as in item pel-from-hermitian-pairs, (a_{σ,i}, b_{σ,i}) equals (r_{i,σ}, s_{i,σ}) if σ ∈ Σ and otherwise equals (s_{i,σ}, r_{i,σ}).
items.note: True with the corrected definition of V^0 (V^{−1,0}, on which h(z) acts by z, Deligne's convention) in item def-signature-of-h: the σ-component of V_i ⊗ C for σ ∈ Σ is V_{i,σ} with h acting by diag(z 1_r, z̄ 1_s); for σ ∉ Σ use (a_{σc}, b_{σc}) = (b_σ, a_σ) and r_{i,σc} = r_{i,σ}. With the printed definition (F^0 = V^{0,−1}) the two cases would be interchanged (source issue). Planned: PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: The reflex field of a unitary PEL datum
items.statement: The reflex field of the PEL datum P of §2.3 is F = Q[{Σ_{σ∈Σ_𝒦} a_{σ,i} σ(a) : a ∈ 𝒦, i = 1, …, m}] ⊂ C. F is contained in the Galois closure 𝒦′ of 𝒦 in C.
items.note: Cited: 'follows, for example, from [Lan13, Cor. 1.2.5.6]'. Insensitive to the V^0 convention: replacing a_{σ,i} by b_{σ,i} = a_{σc,i} replaces F by its complex conjugate, and F ⊂ 𝒦′ (a CM field) is stable under complex conjugation. Planned: PELModuli M0 plans PEL data, the similitude group, signatures and the reflex field; PELModuli M5 plans a unitary PEL example over a CM field with specified signatures.

items.name: M_{K/F} as a union of |ker¹(Q, G)| copies of the canonical model (Kottwitz)
items.statement: Over the reflex field F, the moduli space M_{K/F} associated with P is the union of |ker¹(Q, G)| copies of the canonical model of the Shimura variety S_K(G, X_P) associated to (G, h_P, K); here (G, X_P) is the Shimura datum for which h_P = h ∈ X_P and ker¹(Q, G) := ker(H¹(Q, G) → ∏_v H¹(Q_v, G)). More precisely, the elements of ker¹(Q, G) classify the similitude classes (with a common similitude factor for all j) of hermitian tuples 𝒱′ = (V_j′, ⟨·,·⟩_{V_j′})_{1≤j≤m} that are similar to 𝒱 (with a common local similitude factor) at every place of Q — printed: 'isomorphism classes of hermitian tuples … that are locally isomorphic to 𝒱 at every place of Q' (source issue). Let 𝒱 = 𝒱^(1), …, 𝒱^(k) be representatives; then M_{K/F} is naturally a disjoint union of F-schemes M_{K/F} = ⊔_j M_{K,𝒱^(j)}, the scheme M_{K,𝒱} = M_{K,𝒱^(1)} is the canonical model of S_K(G, X_P), and for each j there is an F-automorphism of M_{K/F} mapping M_{K,𝒱} isomorphically onto M_{K,𝒱^(j)}.
items.note: Cited from [Kot92, §8] (see also (24)); 'Kottwitz only treats the case where m = 1, but the reasoning is the same in the general case' — the general-m extension is asserted, not proved. Planned: PELModuli M3 plans the complex comparison and the ker¹(Q, G)-indexed decomposition into Shimura varieties.

items.name: Hasse principle for G when m = 1 and dim V_1 is even
items.statement: If m = 1 and dim_𝒦 V_1 is even, then G satisfies the Hasse principle (ker¹(Q, G) = 0); in this case M_K is an integral model of the Shimura variety S_K(G, X_P). If dim_𝒦 V_1 is odd or m > 1 (printed 'm ≥ 1', source issue), this is no longer the case in general.
items.note: Cited implicitly from Kottwitz [Kot92, §7]; not proved. Because of this, the paper works with one copy M_{K,L} (item def-shimura-variety-mkl). Planned: PELModuli M3 plans the complex comparison and the ker¹(Q, G)-indexed decomposition into Shimura varieties.

items.name: The Shimura variety M_{K,L} and s_L: M_{K,L} ↪ M_K (11)
items.statement: For applications to automorphic forms only one copy of S_K(G, X_P) is needed. M_{K,L} is the scheme-theoretic closure of the F-scheme M_{K,𝒱} in M_K; it is a smooth, quasi-projective S_□-scheme. s_L: M_{K,L} ↪ M_K (11) is the inclusion. M_K is called the moduli space and M_{K,L} the Shimura variety.
items.note: Smoothness checked: M_K is smooth, hence flat, over the Dedekind scheme S_□, so its connected components are irreducible and meet the generic fibre in irreducible open subsets; M_{K,𝒱} is open and closed in M_{K/F}, so its closure is a union of connected components of M_K. The subscript L refers to the chosen component, not to the lattice. Planned: PELModuli M3 plans the complex comparison and the ker¹(Q, G)-indexed decomposition into Shimura varieties.

items.name: Remark 2.3.1 — Lan's realization of the canonical model inside M_{K/F}
items.statement: For any PEL datum P, the canonical model of the Shimura variety S_K(G, X_P) is realized as an open and closed subscheme of M_{K/F} [Lan12, §2], with a smooth, quasi-projective S_□-model provided by its scheme-theoretic closure in M_K (printed 'S_0-model', Lan's notation; source issue). This is the model M_{K,L} described above.
items.note: Cited from [Lan12, §2]. Planned: PELModuli M4 plans the identification with canonical models.

items.name: §2.3.2 — CM tori J_0′ and CM Shimura subvarieties
items.statement: Suppose m = 1; let (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V) = (V_1, ⟨·,·⟩_{V_1}) and n = dim_𝒦 V. Let 𝒦_1, …, 𝒦_r be finite CM extensions of 𝒦 with Σ_{i=1}^r [𝒦_i : 𝒦] = n. For each i let J_{0,i} be the Serre subtorus of Res_{𝒦_i/Q} G_m (defined in e.g. [CCO14, Def. A.4.3.1]) and ν_i: J_{0,i} → G_m its similitude map, and let J_0′ ⊂ ∏_{i=1}^r J_{0,i} be the subtorus defined by equality of all the ν_i. Let V_i′ = 𝒦_i, viewed as a 𝒦-space of dimension [𝒦_i : 𝒦]. Suppose that each V_i′ can be given a 𝒦_i-hermitian structure such that ⊕_i V_i′ is isomorphic to V as a hermitian space over 𝒦 (the paper asserts this is always possible; it is not — source issue). Such an isomorphism determines an embedding of J_0′ in G; with respect to it there exists a point h_0 ∈ X_P that factors through the image of J_0′(R) in G(R), and the corresponding embedding of Shimura data (J_0′, h_0) → (G, X_P) defines a CM Shimura subvariety of M_{K,L}.
items.note: Corrected statement (hypothesis made explicit). The hypothesis holds when all 𝒦_i = 𝒦 (orthogonal diagonalization; item def-standard-base-point). Used in §3.2.4 (base point restrictions, Proposition 3.2.5), which only needs CM pairs (J_0′, h_0) that exist. J_{0,i} is presumably {x ∈ Res_{𝒦_i/Q}G_m : x x̄ ∈ G_m} with ν_i(x) = x x̄; the paper does not spell it out. Existence of h_0 ∈ X_P: choose CM types of the 𝒦_i compatible with the signs of the hermitian structures at the real places. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ShimuraData D4 plans special points and special pairs.

items.name: J_0^{(n)} and standard base points
items.statement: For 𝒦_i = 𝒦 for all i (so r = n), J_0^{(n)} denotes J_0′; this corresponds to a PEL datum as in §2.1 with B = 𝒦^n. The base point h ∈ X_P is called standard if it factors through an inclusion of J_0^{(n)}. Concretely, h is standard iff V has a 𝒦-basis with respect to which ⟨·,·⟩_V is diagonalized and each h_σ has image in the diagonal matrices with respect to the induced basis of V ⊗_{𝒦,σ} C.
items.note: Here the basis of V ⊗_{𝒦,σ} C used for h_σ in §2.3 is the rescaled image of the 𝒦-basis (the diagonal entries σ(a_j) are real and can be normalized to ±1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Standing assumption: the base point h of P is standard
items.statement: From §2.3.2 on, the base point h in the PEL datum P is assumed to be standard. This guarantees that later constructions involving Harish-Chandra modules are rational over the Galois closure of 𝒦.
items.note: Standing assumption (stated for m = 1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Smooth toroidal compactifications M^tor_{K,Σ} (Lan)
items.statement: M_K admits smooth toroidal compactifications M^tor_{K,Σ} over S_□ associated to certain smooth projective polyhedral cone decompositions Σ (not made precise in the paper); when □ = ∅ this was already known.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'one of the main results of [Lan13]'; the main statements used are in [Lan13, Section 6.4].9; those are outside §§1–2.5. Σ here is a cone decomposition, not the CM type of §2.3. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans Lan's integral PEL toroidal compactifications.

items.name: Refinement maps π_{Σ′,Σ}
items.statement: There is a notion of one polyhedral cone decomposition refining another that partially orders the Σ's. If Σ′ refines Σ, then there is a canonical proper surjective map π_{Σ′,Σ}: M^tor_{K,Σ′} → M^tor_{K,Σ} that is the identity on M_K.
items.note: Cited from [Lan13, §6.4]. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans refinements and Hecke maps of toroidal compactifications.

items.name: The tower M^tor_K
items.statement: M^tor_K denotes the tower of compactifications {M^tor_{K,Σ}}_Σ (with the maps π_{Σ′,Σ}). It is used (e.g. when changing K or defining Hecke operators) to avoid making specific compatible choices of Σ. Constructions over M^tor_K are described as though M^tor_K were a single scheme; this means a tower of such constructions over each M^tor_{K,Σ}.
items.note: Convention. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans refinements and Hecke maps of toroidal compactifications.

items.name: Change of level and the right action of G(A_f^□) on the towers
items.statement: If K_1^□ ⊂ K_2^□ then the natural map M_{K_1} → M_{K_2} extends canonically to a map of towers M^tor_{K_1} → M^tor_{K_2}. If g ∈ G(A_f^□), the map [g]: M_{gKg^{−1}} → M_K, (A, λ, ι, α) ↦ (A, λ, ι, αg), extends canonically to a map M^tor_{gKg^{−1}} → M^tor_K. This defines a right action of G(A_f^□) on the tower of towers {M^tor_K}_{K^□ ⊂ G(A_f^□)}.
items.note: Checked: if α is a gK^□g^{−1}-orbit then αg is a K^□-orbit, and [g]∘[h] = [hg], so the action is on the right. The extensions to compactifications are cited from [Lan13, §6.4]. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans refinements and Hecke maps of toroidal compactifications.

items.name: M^tor_{K,L,Σ}: toroidal compactification of the Shimura variety
items.statement: In the setting of §2.3, M^tor_{K,L,Σ} is the scheme-theoretic closure of M_{K,𝒱} in M^tor_{K,Σ}. It is a smooth toroidal compactification of the Shimura variety M_{K,L} ([LS13, §4.1], [Lan12, §3–§4]); its base change to F is the usual toroidal compactification of the canonical model. s_L also denotes the induced inclusion M^tor_{K,L,Σ} ⊂ M^tor_{K,Σ}. Varying Σ and K induces maps between the M^tor_{K,L,Σ}; M^tor_{K,L} is the tower {M^tor_{K,L,Σ}}_Σ, and the action of G(A_f^□) on {M^tor_K}_{K^□} induces an action on {M^tor_{K,L}}_{K^□}.
items.note: Smoothness and identification cited from [LS13, §4.1] and [Lan12, §3–§4]. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans Lan's integral PEL toroidal compactifications.

items.name: H = GL_{O_B⊗Z_p}(L⁺), its Borel B_H, B_H^u and T_H
items.statement: Let H = GL_{O_B⊗Z_p}(L⁺). The identification (10) determines (12) H ≅ ∏_{w|p} ∏_{i=1}^m GL_{a_{w,i}}(O_w). B_H ⊂ H is the Z_p-Borel corresponding via (12) to the product of the upper-triangular Borels, B_H^u is its unipotent radical, and T_H = B_H/B_H^u, identified by (12) with the diagonal matrices.
items.note: Uses the bases fixed in (10) for e_iL_w⁺ for every w | p. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The semiabelian scheme 𝒜 over M^tor_K (Lan)
items.statement: Suppose □ = {p}. There exists a semiabelian scheme 𝒜 over M^tor_K that is part of a degenerating family as in [Lan13, Thm. 6.4.1.1]. In particular there exist a dual semiabelian scheme 𝒜^∨ (in the sense of [Lan13, Thm. 3.4.3.2]), a homomorphism λ: 𝒜 → 𝒜^∨, a homomorphism ι: O_B ⊗ Z_(p) → End_{M^tor_K}(𝒜), and a K^p-level structure α on 𝒜_{/M_K}, such that the restriction of (𝒜, λ, ι, α) over M_K represents the universal tuple (the tautological tuple of [Lan13, Thm. 6.4.1.1(1)]).
items.note: Cited from [Lan13, Thm. 6.4.1.1, Thm. 3.4.3.2]; the paper writes K^(p) for K^p = K^□. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C4 plans degenerations of polarized abelian schemes; ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans Lan's integral PEL toroidal compactifications.

items.name: The Igusa-type covers M̄_{K_r} → M^tor_K and M_{K_r}, M̄_{K_r,L}, M_{K_r,L}
items.statement: M̄_{K_r} is the scheme over M^tor_K whose S-points classify the B_H^u(Z_p)-orbits of O_B ⊗ Z_p-injections φ: L⁺ ⊗ μ_{p^r} ↪ 𝒜^∨[p^r]_{/S} of group schemes with image an isotropic subgroup scheme; M_{K_r} is its restriction over M_K. The group B_H(Z_p) acts on M̄_{K_r} on the right (φ ↦ φ∘b) through its quotient T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p). M̄_{K_r,L} is the pullback of M̄_{K_r} over M^tor_{K,L} and M_{K_r,L} the pullback over M_{K,L}. In general M̄_{K_r} (resp. M̄_{K_r,L}) is étale and quasi-finite but not finite over M^tor_K (resp. M^tor_{K,L}; printed M^tor_{K_r,L}, source issue). s_L also denotes the inclusions M_{K_r,L} ↪ M_{K_r} and M̄_{K_r,L} ↪ M̄_{K_r}.
items.note: The action factoring through T_H(Z_p/p^r) is checked (B_H^u normal in B_H; φ only sees b mod p^r). 'Isotropic' presumably refers to the λ-Weil pairing (λ is an isomorphism on p-torsion); unspecified. §2.6.6 (footnote 2) uses that M̄_{K_r} is a special case of the ordinary locus of [Lan18]. Representability is asserted without argument. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The Borel B⁺ ⊂ G_{/Z_p} stabilizing L⁺ (13), (14)
items.statement: B⁺ ⊂ G_{/Z_p} is the Borel subgroup that stabilizes L⁺ and is such that (13) B⁺ ↠ G_m × B_H ⊂ G_m × H, where the map to the first factor is the similitude character ν and the map to the second is projection to H (restriction to L⁺). B^u ⊂ B⁺ is its unipotent radical. Under (9) and (10), (14) B⁺ ≅ G_m × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_{i=1}^m {(A B; 0 D) ∈ GL_{n_i}(O_w) : A ∈ GL_{a_{w,i}}(O_w) is upper-triangular, D ∈ GL_{b_{w,i}}(O_w) is lower-triangular}.
items.note: Checked: for w ∈ Σ_p, g preserving L⁺ has block form (A B; 0 D) on e_iL_w = e_iL_w⁺ ⊕ e_iL_w⁻; on e_iL_w̄⁺ ≅ dual of e_iL_w⁻ (dual bases fixed in (10)) g acts by ν·ᵗD^{−1}, which is upper-triangular iff D is lower-triangular. (13) is surjective with kernel the B-blocks; the maximal torus of B⁺ maps isomorphically onto G_m × T_H. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The level subgroups I_r^0 ⊃ I_r and K_r = I_rK^p, K_r^0 = I_r^0K^p
items.statement: I_r^0 ⊂ G(Z_p) consists of those g with g mod p^r ∈ B⁺(Z_p/p^rZ_p), and I_r ⊂ I_r^0 of those g projecting under the surjection (13) to an element of (Z_p/p^rZ_p)^× × B_H^u(Z_p/p^rZ_p). Then I_r^0/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p). One puts K_r = I_rK^p and K_r^0 = I_r^0K^p.
items.note: Isomorphism checked: G(Z_p) → G(Z/p^r) is surjective (G smooth over Z_p), (13) is surjective mod p^r, and I_r is the preimage of the normal subgroup (Z/p^r)^× × B_H^u(Z/p^r). Note I_r acts unipotently on L⁺ and by ν on the diagonal of L⁻. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3 plans parahoric and congruence group schemes.

items.name: M_{K_r} over F versus the Shimura variety of level I_rK^p
items.statement: Over F: after base change to F(μ_{p^r}) (source issue; the paper says simply 'the choice of a basis of Z_p(1) naturally identifies'), a choice of basis of Z_p(1) identifies M_{K_r/F} (resp. M_{K_r,L/F}) with M_{I_rK^p/F} (resp. M_{I_rK^p,L/F} = S_{I_rK^p}(G, X_P)); and M̄_{K_r/F} (resp. M̄_{K_r,L/F}) is an open subscheme of the normalization of M^tor_{K/F} (resp. M^tor_{K,L/F}) in M_{K_r/F} (resp. M_{K_r,L/F}) — printed: 'is the normalization'; false when the boundary is non-empty (source issue). Accordingly K_r denotes I_rK^p (and K_r^0 = I_r^0K^p).
items.note: Corrected statement; both corrections are recorded as source issues. Level-K_r modular forms in §2.6.6 are defined as sections over M̄_{K_r}, with the Koecher principle (20) comparing with sections over M_{K_r}; so the uses of this paragraph are the comparison of classical forms with automorphic forms over C. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The groups G_0 ⊃ H_0 and the lattice Λ = Λ_0 ⊕ Λ_0^∨
items.statement: Let V = L ⊗ C. The homomorphism h defines a pure Hodge structure V = V^{−1,0} ⊕ V^{0,−1} of weight −1; let W = V/V^{0,−1}, which is defined over the reflex field F. Let Λ_0 ⊂ W be an O_B-stable S_□-submodule with Λ_0 ⊗_{S_□} C = W (S_□ = O_F ⊗ Z_(□)). Let Λ_0^∨ = Hom_{Z_(p)}(Λ_0, Z_(p)(1)) with O_B ⊗ S_□-action (b ⊗ s)f(x) = f(b^* s x). Put Λ = Λ_0 ⊕ Λ_0^∨ with the alternating pairing ⟨·,·⟩_can : Λ × Λ → Z_(p)(1), ⟨(x_1, f_1), (x_2, f_2)⟩_can = f_2(x_1) − f_1(x_2). Then Λ_0 and Λ_0^∨ are isotropic and ⟨bx, y⟩_can = ⟨x, b^* y⟩_can. G_0 is the group scheme over S_□ with G_0(R) = {(g, ν) ∈ GL_{O_B⊗R}(Λ ⊗_{S_□} R) × R^× : ⟨gx, gy⟩_can = ν⟨x, y⟩_can for all x, y ∈ Λ ⊗_{S_□} R} for every S_□-algebra R. H_0 ⊂ G_0 is the stabilizer of the polarization Λ = Λ_0 ⊕ Λ_0^∨, and the projection H_0 → G_m × GL_{O_B⊗S_□}(Λ_0^∨) (the first coordinate being the similitude factor ν) is an isomorphism. There is a canonical isomorphism V ≅ Λ ⊗_{S_□} C of O_B ⊗ C-modules identifying V^{−1,0} with Λ_0 ⊗_{S_□} C, V^{0,−1} with Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_□} C and ⟨·,·⟩ with ⟨·,·⟩_can; it identifies G_{/C} with G_{0/C}. Let C ⊂ G_{/R} be the centralizer of h and U_∞ = U_h := C(R); the identification G_{/C} = G_{0/C} identifies C(C) with H_0(C).
items.note: Standing setting of §2: P = (B, *, O_B, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h) a PEL datum of unitary type (§§2.1–2.3), □ ∈ {∅, {p}}, S_□ = O_F ⊗ Z_(□), F the reflex field. The isomorphism H_0 ≅ G_m × GL(Λ_0^∨) holds because an element of H_0 acting on Λ_0^∨ by D and with similitude ν acts on Λ_0 by the ν-multiple of the contragredient of D. The coefficient ring Z_(p) in Λ_0^∨ and in ⟨·,·⟩_can should read Z_(□) (sourceIssues E17). G_0, H_0, Λ_0, Λ_0^∨ recur in §2.9.4 and, for each of the four PEL data, in §3.1.2. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms and the Hodge summands of a unitary PEL example.

items.name: The canonical bundle ω and the H_0-torsors E, E_r
items.statement: Let A be the semiabelian scheme over M^tor_K of §2.5 and A^∨ the associated dual semiabelian scheme. Let ω be the O_{M^tor_K}-dual of Lie_{M^tor_K} A^∨. The Kottwitz determinant condition implies that ω is locally isomorphic to Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_□} O_{M^tor_K} as an O_B ⊗ O_{M^tor_K}-module. Let E = Isom_{O_B⊗O_{M^tor_K}}((ω, O_{M^tor_K}(1)), (Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_□} O_{M^tor_K}, O_{M^tor_K}(1))). This is an H_0-torsor over M^tor_K; let π : E → M^tor_K be the structure map. For an S_□-algebra R, an R-valued function f on E is viewed as a functorial rule assigning to a pair (A, ε) over an R-algebra S an element f(A, ε) ∈ S, where A is a tuple classified by M_K(S) and ε is a corresponding element of E(S). Put E_r = E ×_{M^tor_K} \overline{M}_{K_r} with structure map π_r : E_r → \overline{M}_{K_r}; sections of π_{r,*}O_{E_r} are functorial rules on pairs (X, ε), where X = (A, φ) is a tuple classified by M_{K_r}(S) and ε is a corresponding element of E_r(S).
items.note: Uses the level-p moduli \overline{M}_{K_r} ⊃ M_{K_r} of §2.5 (classifying B_H^u(Z_p)-orbits of O_B ⊗ Z_p-injections φ : L^+ ⊗ μ_{p^r} ↪ A^∨[p^r] with isotropic image). The paper writes 'An R-valued point f ∈ E' for what is an R-valued function on E. The O(1)-component of ε carries the similitude and is what the form f_a of §2.6.11 reads off. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B2 plans automorphic vector bundles attached to representations of the Levi.

items.name: The ring S_0 and the isomorphism (15) H_{0/S_0} ≅ G_m × ∏ GL_{b_{σ,i}}; the Borel B_{H_0}
items.statement: Let K′ be the Galois closure of K and p′ ⊂ O_{K′} the prime determined by incl_p. Put S_0 = S_□ ⊗_{O_{F,(p)}} O_{K′,(p′)} (so S_0 = K′ if □ = ∅ and S_0 = O_{K′,(p′)} if □ = {p}). The isomorphism O ⊗ S_0 ≅ ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} S_0, a ⊗ s ↦ (σ(a)s)_σ, induces O_B ⊗ S_0 ≅ O_B ⊗_O (O ⊗ S_0) ≅ ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} O_B ⊗_{O,σ} S_0 = ∏_σ O_{B,σ}, and hence decompositions Λ_0 ⊗_{S_□} S_0 = ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} Λ_{0,σ} and Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_□} S_0 = ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} Λ^∨_{0,σ}; the pairing ⟨·,·⟩_can identifies Λ^∨_{0,σc} = Hom_{Z_(p)}(Λ_{0,σ}, Z_(p)(1)). Since S_0 is a PID, e_iΛ_{0,σ} and e_iΛ^∨_{0,σ} are free S_0-modules of ranks a_{σ,i} and b_{σ,i}. Fixing an S_0-basis of each e_iΛ_{0,σ} (and the dual basis of e_iΛ^∨_{0,σc}) yields (15): H_{0/S_0} ≅ G_m × ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} ∏_{i=1}^m GL_{O_i⊗_{O,σ}S_0}(e_iΛ^∨_{0,σ}) ≅ G_m × ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} ∏_{i=1}^m GL_{b_{σ,i}}(S_0). B_{H_0} ⊂ H_{0/S_0} is the S_0-Borel corresponding under (15) to the product of the lower-triangular Borels; T_{H_0} ⊂ B_{H_0} is the diagonal torus and B^u_{H_0} ⊂ B_{H_0} the unipotent radical.
items.note: The printed formulas write S′_0 (twice) where S_0 is meant (sourceIssues E18). The ranks follow from the signature convention of §2.2 ((a_{σc,i}, b_{σc,i}) = (b_{σ,i}, a_{σ,i})), consistent with the duality Λ^∨_{0,σc} ≅ (Λ_{0,σ})^∨. Note B_{H_0} is LOWER triangular; dominance is taken with respect to the opposite Borel (next item). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms and the Hodge summands of a unitary PEL example.

items.name: Dominant characters κ = (κ_0, (κ_{σ,i})) of T_{H_0} (16)
items.statement: A character κ of T_{H_0} defined over an S_0-algebra R is a dominant character of T_{H_0} if it is dominant with respect to the opposite (upper-triangular) Borel B^op_{H_0}. Via (15) the characters of T_{H_0} are identified with tuples κ = (κ_0, (κ_{σ,i})_{σ∈Σ_K, 1≤i≤m}), κ_0 ∈ Z, κ_{σ,i} = (κ_{σ,i,j})_j ∈ Z^{b_{σ,i}}, by κ(t) = t_0^{κ_0} · ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} ∏_{i=1}^m ∏_{j=1}^{b_{σ,i}} t_{σ,i,j}^{κ_{σ,i,j}} for t = (t_0, (diag(t_{σ,i,1}, …, t_{σ,i,b_{σ,i}}))_{σ∈Σ_K, 1≤i≤m}) ∈ T_{H_0}; the dominant characters are those with (16) κ_{σ,i,1} ≥ ⋯ ≥ κ_{σ,i,b_{σ,i}} for all σ ∈ Σ_K and i = 1, …, m.
items.note: The printed product is over 'σ ∈ K' instead of σ ∈ Σ_K (sourceIssues E19). This weight convention (κ_{σ,i} of length b_{σ,i}, indexed by all σ ∈ Σ_K, plus κ_0 for the similitude) is the 'classical weight' used in the rest of the paper; the p-adic weight κ_p of §2.9.4 re-indexes it. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms and the Hodge summands of a unitary PEL example; Tau Ceti's ClassicalGroups Layer 3 plans the highest-weight classification of GL_n-representations.

items.name: The representation W_κ, the dual weight κ^∨ and W_κ^∨
items.statement: Given a dominant character κ of T_{H_0} over an S_0-algebra R, let W_κ(R) = {φ : H_{0/R} → G_a : φ(bh) = κ(b)φ(h), b ∈ B_{H_0}}, where κ is extended trivially to B^u_{H_0}; H_0 acts by right translation. Let w ∈ W(T_{H_0}, H_{0/S_0}) be the longest element of the Weyl group and κ^∨ the dominant character of T_{H_0} defined by κ^∨(t) = κ(w^{−1}t^{−1}w). The dual is W_κ^∨(R) = Hom_R(W_κ(R), R).
items.note: Induction from the lower Borel B_{H_0}; checked on GL_2: W_κ ≅ det^{κ_2} ⊗ Sym^{κ_1−κ_2}, with highest weight κ for the upper Borel. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B2 plans automorphic vector bundles attached to representations of the Levi; Tau Ceti's ClassicalGroups Layer 3 plans the highest-weight classification of GL_n-representations.

items.name: Structure of W_κ and W_κ^∨ (highest-weight vectors φ_κ, ℓ_κ; Hom_{H_0}(W_κ^∨, W_{κ^∨}) = R)
items.statement: Let κ be a dominant character of T_{H_0} and R a flat S_0-algebra. (a) W_κ(R) is an R-model of the irreducible algebraic representation of H_0 of highest weight κ with respect to (T_{H_0}, B^op_{H_0}), and W_κ^∨(R) is an R-model of the representation with highest weight κ^∨. (b) The submodule W_κ(R)^{B^u_{H_0}} is a free R-module of rank one spanned by φ_κ, the function whose support contains the big cell B_{H_0}wB_{H_0} (and equals it if κ is regular) and such that φ_κ(wB^u_{H_0}) = 1; wφ_κ is a highest-weight vector. (c) W_κ^∨ is generated over R as an H_0-representation by the functional ℓ_κ = (evaluation at 1); wℓ_κ is a highest-weight vector. (d) Hom_{H_0}(W_κ^∨(R), W_{κ^∨}(R)) = R, with basis the homomorphism sending ℓ_κ to φ_{κ^∨}.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'For all this, see [Hid04], Section 8.1.2, and the text of Jantzen cited there.' Parts proved together in the source. Checked for GL_2 (B lower triangular, κ = (κ_1 ≥ κ_2)): φ_κ(h) = det(h)^{κ_2} h_{12}^{κ_1−κ_2}, supported on the big cell when κ_1 > κ_2; its weight is wκ, so wφ_κ has weight κ; ℓ_κ has weight −κ = w(κ^∨), matching (d). The normalisation φ_κ(w) = 1 requires rescaling by (−1)^{κ_2} in this example, which is harmless. Planned: Tau Ceti's ClassicalGroups Layer 3 plans the highest-weight classification of GL_n-representations.

items.name: Identification (17) of U_∞ = C(R) inside H_0(C)
items.statement: Via the isomorphism (15), the identification of C(C) with H_0(C) identifies (17) U_∞ = C(R) ≅ {(h_0, (h_σ)_{σ∈Σ_K}) ∈ H_0(C) : h_0 ∈ R^×, h_0 · ᵗh̄_σ^{−1} = h_σ}, where ¯ denotes complex conjugation on C. That is, U_∞ is identified with the subgroup of the product ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} GU^+(b_σ) of full unitary similitude groups (Section 1.4) in which all the similitude factors agree.
items.note: Checked: since b_{σc} = a_σ, ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} U(b_σ) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} U(a_σ) × U(b_σ), the maximal compact of the unitary group of signature (a_σ, b_σ), and the dimensions of C(R) and H_0(C) agree. The condition forces h_0 > 0 whenever some b_σ ≥ 1. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms and the Hodge summands of a unitary PEL example.

items.name: The automorphic sheaves ω_{κ,M}, ω_{r,κ,M}, ω_κ, ω_{r,κ} (18)
items.statement: Let R be an S_0-algebra and κ a dominant R-character of T_{H_0}. Let ω_{κ,M} = π_*O_E[κ] and ω_{r,κ,M} = π_{r,*}O_{E_r}[κ] be the subsheaves of the quasicoherent sheaves π_*O_E on M^tor_{K/R} and π_{r,*}O_{E_r} on \overline{M}_{K_r/R}, respectively, on which B_{H_0} acts via κ. Put (18) ω_κ = s_{L,*}s_L^*ω_{κ,M} and ω_{r,κ} = s_{L,*}s_L^*ω_{r,κ,M}: these are the restrictions of ω_{κ,M} and ω_{r,κ,M} to the toroidal compactifications of the Shimura varieties M_{K,L/R} and M_{K_r,L/R}, extended by zero to the full moduli space. The same notation denotes their restrictions over M_{K,L} and M_{K_r,L}.
items.note: Construction cited to [Hid04, §§8.1.2–8.1.3]. s_L : M_{K,L} ↪ M_K is the inclusion (11) of the Shimura variety (one copy of the canonical model) into the moduli space; the level-p version uses \overline{M}_{K_r,L}.6.5–2.6.6 (now split into separate items). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B2 plans automorphic vector bundles attached to representations of the Levi; AutomorphicBundles B3 plans canonical and subcanonical extensions and independence of the fan.

items.name: Modular forms M_κ(K;R) and cuspforms S_κ(K;R) of level K
items.statement: Let R be an S_0-algebra and κ a dominant character of T_{H_0}. The R-module of modular forms on G over R of weight κ and level K is M_κ(K;R) = H^0(M^tor_{K,L/R}, ω_κ). By (19), f ∈ M_κ(K;R) can be viewed as a functorial rule assigning to a pair (A, ε) over an R-algebra S that is an S-valued point of the Shimura variety M_{K,L} an element f(A, ε) ∈ S, with f(A, bε) = κ(b)f(A, ε) for b ∈ B_{H_0}(S). Let D_∞ be the Cartier divisor M^tor_K − M_K with its structure of reduced closed subscheme. The R-module of cuspforms on G over R of weight κ and level K is the submodule S_κ(K;R) = H^0(M^tor_{K/R}, ω_κ(−D_∞)) of M_κ(K;R).
items.note: K = G(Z_p)K^□ neat when □ = {p}. H^0 over the tower M^tor_K means the direct limit over cone decompositions (§2.4). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms and the Hodge summands of a unitary PEL example.

items.name: Köcher principle (19): M_κ(K;R) = H^0(M_{K,L/R}, ω_κ)
items.statement: For every S_0-algebra R and dominant κ, M_κ(K;R) = H^0(M_{K,L/R}, ω_κ) (19), except when K^+ = Q (printed 'F_0 = Q') and G^der/Q has an irreducible factor isomorphic to SU(1,1). In that exceptional case the toroidal compactifications are the same as the minimal compactification and therefore canonical.
items.note: Cited: 'The Köcher principle [Lan16] and the definition (18) implies'. The paper leaves the adjustments in the exceptional case to the reader and 'will generally refrain from referring explicitly to this exception' (also footnote 2). The symbol F_0 is never defined; the maximal totally real subfield K^+ is meant (sourceIssues E20). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B3 plans canonical and subcanonical extensions and independence of the fan; AutomorphicBundles B5 plans Hecke actions and Fourier–Jacobi expansions.

items.name: S_κ(K;R) is independent of the toroidal compactification
items.statement: The module of cuspforms S_κ(K;R) = H^0(M^tor_{K/R}, ω_κ(−D_∞)) is independent of the choice of toroidal compactification.
items.note: Cited: 'It follows from Proposition 7.5 of [Lan17]'. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B3 plans canonical and subcanonical extensions and independence of the fan.

items.name: Modular forms and cuspforms of level K_r with Nebentypus ψ
items.statement: Let ψ : T_H(Z_p) → \overline{Q}^× be a character factoring through T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p), and let R be an algebra over S_0[ψ] (S_0 with the values of ψ adjoined). The R-module of modular forms on G over R of weight κ, level K_r and character ψ is M_κ(K_r, ψ; R) = {f ∈ H^0(\overline{M}_{K_r/R}, ω_{r,κ}) : t·f = ψ(t)f for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p)}. A section f ∈ M_κ(K_r, ψ; R) is a functorial rule assigning to a pair (X, ε) over an R-algebra S that is an S-valued point of M_{K_r,L} an element f(X, ε) ∈ S, X = (A, φ), satisfying f(A, φ∘t, bε) = ψ(t)κ(b)f(X, ε) for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p) and b ∈ B_{H_0}(S). The submodule of cuspforms of character ψ is S_κ(K_r, ψ; R) = {f ∈ H^0(\overline{M}_{K_r/R}, ω_{r,κ}(−D_{∞,r})) : t·f = ψ(t)f for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p)}, where D_{∞,r} := \overline{M}_{K_r} − M_{K_r} with the structure of a reduced closed subscheme (cf. [Lan18, Thm. 5.2.1.1(3)]).
items.note: T_H(Z_p) acts on \overline{M}_{K_r} through I_r^0/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p) (§2.5), i.e. by φ ↦ φ∘t. K_r = I_rK^p. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Köcher principle at level K_r (20)
items.statement: M_κ(K_r, ψ; R[1/p]) = {f ∈ H^0(M_{K_r/R[1/p]}, ω_{r,κ}) : t·f = ψ(t)f for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p)} (20).
items.note: Cited: 'It follows from Remark 10.2 of [Lan16] that the Köcher principle applies'; footnote 2 ignores the exceptional case (K^+ = Q with an SU(1,1) factor) and uses that the M_{K_r} defined here is a special case of the ordinary locus of [Lan18]. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicBundles B3 plans canonical and subcanonical extensions and independence of the fan.

items.name: Actions of G(A_f^□) and G(A_f^p) on modular forms (§2.6.7)
items.statement: The action of G(A_f^□) on the tower {M^tor_K}_{K^□} gives an action of G(A_f^□) on lim_{→K^□} M_κ(K;R) and lim_{→K^□} S_κ(K;R). Similarly the action of G(A_f^p) extends to {\overline{M}_{K_r}}_{K^p}, giving an action of G(A_f^p) on lim_{→K^p} M_κ(K_r, ψ; R) and lim_{→K^p} S_κ(K_r, ψ; R). The submodules fixed by K^□ (resp. K^p) are exactly the modular forms and cuspforms of weight κ and level K (resp. prime-to-p level K^p).
