items.note: The last statement uses that the toroidal compactifications are normal schemes over Spec(R) [Lan17, Prop. 7.5]. The right action on the tower is [g] : M_{gKg^{−1}} → M_K, (A, λ, ι, α) ↦ (A, λ, ι, αg) (§2.4). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B5 plans Hecke actions and Fourier–Jacobi expansions.

items.name: Hecke operators away from p, (21)–(22)
items.statement: Let K_j = G(Z_p)K_j^p ⊂ G(A_f), j = 1, 2, be neat open compact subgroups. For g ∈ G(A_f^p) the Hecke operators [K_2gK_1] : M_κ(K_1;R) → M_κ(K_2;R) and [K_{2,r}gK_{1,r}] : M_κ(K_{1,r}, ψ; R) → M_κ(K_{2,r}, ψ; R) are defined through the action of G(A_f^p): (21) [K_{2,r}gK_{1,r}]f = Σ_{g_j} [g_j]^*f, where K_2^p g K_1^p = ⊔_{g_j} g_jK_1^p. In particular (22) ([K_{2,r}gK_{1,r}]f)(A, λ, ι, αK_2^p, φ, ε) = Σ_{g_j} f(A, λ, ι, αg_jK_1^p, φ, ε). These actions map cuspforms to cuspforms. When K_2 = K_1 is understood one writes T(g) = [K_1gK_1] and T_r(g) = [K_{1,r}gK_{1,r}], dropping r when understood.
items.note: Well defined because K_2^p permutes the cosets g_jK_1^p. Complex counterpart: (26). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B5 plans Hecke actions and Fourier–Jacobi expansions.

items.name: Hecke operators at p: t^±_{w,i,j} and U_{w,i,j}, U^−_{w,i,j} (23)
items.statement: If p is invertible in R, Hecke operators T(g) = [KgK] and T_r(g) = [K_rgK_r] are defined on modular forms and cuspforms over R as in §2.6.8. For w ∈ Σ_p, 1 ≤ i ≤ m, 1 ≤ j ≤ n_i, let t^+_{w,i,j} ∈ B^+(Q_p) be the element identified via (14) with (1, (t_{w′,i′,j})), where, in GL_{n_{i′}}(K_{w′}), t_{w′,i′,j} = diag(p1_j, 1_{n_i−j}) if w = w′, i = i′, j ≤ a_{w,i}; t_{w′,i′,j} = diag(p1_{a_{w,i}}, 1_{n_i−j}, p1_{j−a_{w,i}}) if w = w′, i = i′, j > a_{w,i}; and t_{w′,i′,j} = 1_{n_{i′}} otherwise. Let t^−_{w,i,j} = (t^+_{w,i,j})^{−1}, and put (23) U_{w,i,j} = K_r t^+_{w,i,j} K_r, U^−_{w,i,j} = K_r t^−_{w,i,j} K_r. The element t^+_{w,i,j} is positive for B^+: t^+ N^+(Z_p) (t^+)^{−1} ⊂ N^+(Z_p) and (t^+)^{−1} N^−(p^rZ_p) t^+ ⊂ N^−(p^rZ_p), where N^+ is the unipotent radical of B^+ and N^− that of the opposite Borel. [The paper instead prints t^+_{w,i,j} I_r^0 (t^+_{w,i,j})^{−1} ⊂ I_r^0, which is false for j < n_i and r ≥ 1.]
items.note: Printed with n and a_w in place of n_i and a_{w,i} (sourceIssues E21). The printed inclusion t^+ I_r^0 t^{+,−1} ⊂ I_r^0 fails (sourceIssues E22); the corrected property (contraction of N^+, expansion of N^−) is what makes I_r t^+ I_r = ⊔_{u ∈ N^+(Z_p)/t^+N^+(Z_p)(t^+)^{−1}} u t^+ I_r. B^+ is the Borel of (14): in each GL_{n_i}(O_w), block matrices (A B; 0 D) with A upper triangular (size a_{w,i}) and D lower triangular (size b_{w,i}). Hida defines these operators on p-adic forms when p is only a non-zero-divisor (§2.9.5). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 2.6.10 — cone decompositions needed for Hecke operators on higher coherent cohomology
items.statement: To define the actions of these Hecke operators on higher coherent cohomology of automorphic vector bundles it is necessary to use the class of smooth projective polyhedral cone decompositions used to define toroidal compactifications in [Lan13, Lan18]. For holomorphic forms this is generally superfluous because of the Koecher principle [Lan16].
items.note: Expository remark, recorded because §6 works with higher coherent cohomology H^d. Planned: ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans refinements and Hecke maps of toroidal compactifications.

items.name: The similitude form f_a ∈ M_{κ_a}(K;R)
items.statement: Given an integer a, let κ_a be the weight κ_a = (a, (0)). Define f_a ∈ M_{κ_a}(K;R) by f_a(A, ε) = λ^a, where (A, ε) is a pair over an R-algebra S and the isomorphism from S(1) to itself induced by ε is multiplication by λ ∈ S^×.
items.note: f_a has weight κ_a because b ∈ B_{H_0} with similitude ν_b rescales the O(1)-component of ε by ν_b, and κ_a(b) = ν_b^a. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Comparing spaces of modular forms of different weight (§2.6.11)
items.statement: Let κ = (κ_0, (κ_{σ,i})) be a weight and κ′ = (κ_0 + a, (κ_{σ,i})). Multiplication by f_a gives isomorphisms M_κ(K;R) → M_{κ′}(K;R), f ↦ f_a·f, and M_κ(K_r, ψ; R) → M_{κ′}(K_r, ψ; R), f ↦ f_a·f. These induce isomorphisms on spaces of cuspforms, and the Hecke operators T(g) satisfy f_a·T(g)f = ||ν(g)||^a T(g)(f_a·f).
items.note: Stated without proof (f_a is invertible, its inverse being f_{−a}). The factor ||ν(g)||^a comes from the effect of [g] on the similitude component of ε; the sign convention could not be checked independently, but it is consistent with (29) and with f_{p-adic} = (f_a f)_{p-adic} (§2.9.4). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Complex uniformization (24) of M_{K,L} and M_{K_r,L}
items.statement: Let X be the G(R)-orbit under conjugation of h; since the stabilizer of h is U_∞ = C(R), g ↦ ghg^{−1} identifies G(R)/C(R) ≅ X. With P_0 ⊂ G_0 the stabilizer of Λ_0, the identification G_{/C} = G_{0/C} identifies X with an open subspace of G_0(C)/P_0(C), giving X a complex structure. There are natural complex-analytic identifications (24) M_{K,L}(C) = G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K and M_{K_r,L}(C) = G(Q)\X × G(A_f)/K_r, where the class of (h′, g) ∈ X × G(A_f) with g_p ∈ G(Z_p) corresponds to the class of the tuple A_{h′,g} = (A_{h′}, λ_{h′}, ι, η_g) (or X_{h′,g} = (A_{h′,g}, φ_g)): A_{h′} = (L ⊗ R)/L with the complex structure determined by h′, with dual A^∨_{h′} := (L ⊗ R)/L^#, L^# = {x ∈ L ⊗ R : ⟨x, L⟩ ⊆ Z(1)}; λ_{h′} : A_{h′} → A^∨_{h′} is the isogeny induced by the identity of L ⊗ R; ι is induced by the action of O_B on L; η_g is the K^p-orbit of translation by g, g^p : L ⊗ A_f^p ≅ L ⊗ A_f^p = H_1(A_{h′}, A_f^p); and for M_{K_r,L}, φ_g is the B_H^u(Z_p)-orbit of the map L^+ ⊗ μ_{p^r} ↪ A^∨_{h′}[p^r] = p^{−r}L^#/L^# = (L^# ⊗ Z_p)/(p^rL^# ⊗ Z_p), v ⊗ e^{2π√−1/p^r} ↦ g_pv mod (p^rL^# ⊗ Z_p).
items.note: For the identification of adelic double cosets with complex points the paper refers to [Kot92, §8]; it uses that the simple factors of G^der_{/R} are all of type A [Kot92, §§7–8]. □ = {p} here. Representatives with g_p ∈ G(Z_p) exist by weak approximation. Planned: PELModuli M3 plans the complex comparison and the ker¹(Q, G)-indexed decomposition into Shimura varieties.

items.name: Complex points of E and E_r (25)
items.statement: The dual of the Lie algebra of A^∨_{h′} is ω_{A^∨_{h′}} = Hom_C(L ⊗ R, C) (complex structure from h′). Since L ⊗ R ≅ W = Λ_0 ⊗_{S_0} C is C-linear for the complex structure determined by h, there is a canonical O_B ⊗ C-identification ε_0 : ω_{A^∨_h} ≅ Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_0} C; if h′ = ghg^{−1} then ε_{h′}(λ) = ε_0(g^{−1}λ) is an O_B ⊗ C-identification of ω_{A^∨_{h′}} with Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_0} C. The complex points of the H_0-torsors E/M_{K,L} and E_r/M_{K_r,L} are (25) E(C) = G(Q)\G(R) × H_0(C) × G(A_f)/U_∞K and E_r(C) = G(Q)\G(R) × H_0(C) × G(A_f)/U_∞K_r, the class of (g, x, g_f) ∈ G(R) × H_0(C) × G(A_f) corresponding to (A_{ghg^{−1},g_f}, (xε_0(g^{−1}·), ν(x))) and (X_{ghg^{−1},g_f}, (xε_0(g^{−1}·), ν(x))) respectively.
items.note: U_∞ acts on G(R) × H_0(C) by (g, x)u = (gu, xu) (check: (gu, xu) and (g, x) give the same point since ε_0 is C(C)-equivariant). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B2 plans automorphic vector bundles attached to representations of the Levi.

items.name: Classical modular forms as functions on G(A) (§2.7.2)
items.statement: Viewing C as a Z_p-algebra via ι_p, a weight κ modular form over C is identified with a smooth function φ : G(A) × H_0(C) → C such that φ(γguk, bxu) = κ(b)φ(g, x) for γ ∈ G(Q), g ∈ G(A), x ∈ H_0(C), u ∈ U_∞, b ∈ B_{H_0}(C) and k ∈ K or K_r. The space W_κ(C) = {φ : H_0(C) → C : φ holomorphic, φ(bx) = κ(b)φ(x) for all b ∈ B_{H_0}(C)} is the irreducible C-representation of H_0 of highest weight κ with respect to (T_{H_0}, B^op_{H_0}) (Borel–Weil), so a weight κ form is also a smooth f : G(A) → W_κ(C) with f(γguk) = u^{−1}f(g) (γ ∈ G(Q), u ∈ U_∞, k ∈ K or K_r), U_∞ acting on W_κ(C) by uφ(x) = φ(xu); the two are related by f(g)(x) = φ(g, x). Let g = Lie(G(R))_C = p^− ⊕ k ⊕ p^+ be the Cartan decomposition for the involution Ad h(√−1), with p^± the subspaces on which Ad h(z) acts by (z/z̄)^{±1}. The identification of G(C) with G_0(C) identifies Lie(P_0(C)) with k ⊕ p^+, and f is holomorphic if and only if p^− ∗ f = 0. For ψ : T_H(Z_p) → \overline{Q}^× a finite character factoring through T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p), the condition that the form has character ψ is f(gt) = ψ(t)f(g) for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p), t acting via (13).
items.note: The printed text says 'ad h(√−1) acts as ±√−1 on p^±', which is wrong: Ad h(√−1) is an involution, equal to −1 on p^+ ⊕ p^− (sourceIssues E23). The statement above uses the standard characterisation. Checked f(gu) = u^{−1}f(g) against φ(gu, xu) = φ(g, x). Planned: AutomorphicBundles B4 plans classical forms and the Hodge summands of a unitary PEL example.

items.name: Hecke operators on functions G(A) → W_κ(C) (26)
items.statement: The actions of the Hecke operators of §§2.6.8–2.6.9 correspond to the following actions on functions f : G(A) → W_κ(C): the action of [K_2gK_1] is f(g) ↦ Σ_{g_j} f(gg_j), where K_2gK_1 = ⊔ g_jK_1 (26), and similarly with K_i replaced by K_{i,r}.
items.note: Consistent with (22) under α ↦ αg_j. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B5 plans Hecke actions and Fourier–Jacobi expansions.

items.name: The ordinary locus S_m and the Igusa tower T_{n,m}/S_m
items.statement: Let □ = {p}. Hypothesis 2.2.1 implies that the completion of incl_p(S_□) is Z_p, so Z_p is an S_□-algebra. Let k > 0 be so large that the k-th power of the Hasse invariant has a lift to a section E of weight det^{k(p−1)} over Z_p (printed E ∈ M_{det^k}(K; Z_p)). Put S_m = M^tor_{K,L}[1/E]_{/Z_p/p^mZ_p} and S_m^0 = M_{K,L}[1/E]_{/Z_p/p^mZ_p}, an open subscheme of S_m. For n ≥ m let T_{n,m}/S_m be the finite étale S_m-scheme such that for any S_m-scheme S, T_{n,m}(S) = Isom_S(L^+ ⊗ μ_{p^n}, A^∨[p^n]°), where ° denotes the identity component and the isomorphisms are of finite flat group schemes over S with O_B ⊗ Z_p-actions. T_{n,m} is Galois over S_m with Galois group canonically isomorphic to H(Z_p/p^nZ_p). The collection {T_{n,m}}_n is the Igusa tower over S_m.
items.note: Definition of the Hasse invariant on the toroidal compactification: [Lan18, §6.3.1]; T_{n,m} after [Hid04, §8.1.1]. The printed weight det^k should be det^{k(p−1)} (sourceIssues E24). H = GL_{O_B⊗Z_p}(L^+) (§2.5).9). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Density of the ordinary locus: S_1 is dense in the special fibre of M^tor_{K,L}
items.statement: S_1 = M^tor_{K,L}[1/E]_{/F_p} is dense in the special fibre of M^tor_{K,L}.
items.note: Stated as following 'from our hypotheses on the moduli problem and the discussion in [Lan18, Section 6.3.3]' (Hypothesis 2.2.1 makes the μ-ordinary locus the ordinary locus; cf. [Wed99]). Used for the injectivity of (28). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: p-adic modular forms V(K^p, R) and p-adic cuspforms V(K^p, R)^cusp
items.statement: Let D_{n,m} be the preimage in T_{n,m} of D_m = S_m − S_m^0 (with reduced closed subscheme structure; the preimage is reduced since T_{n,m} → S_m is étale). For a p-adic ring R (R = lim_{←m} R/p^mR) let V_{n,m}(R) = H^0(T_{n,m/R}, O_{T_{n,m}}) and V^cusp_{n,m}(R) = H^0(T_{n,m/R}, O_{T_{n,m}}(−D_{n,m})). H(Z_p) acts on each through its quotient H(Z_p/p^nZ_p), the Galois group of T_{n,m}/S_m. The R-module of p-adic modular forms (for G) over R of level K^p is V(K^p, R) = lim_{←m} lim_{→n} V_{n,m}(R)^{B^u_H(Z_p)}, and that of p-adic cuspforms is V(K^p, R)^cusp = lim_{←m} lim_{→n} V^cusp_{n,m}(R)^{B^u_H(Z_p)}. The group T_H(Z_p) = B_H(Z_p)/B^u_H(Z_p) acts on these modules. A p-adic modular form over R is a functorial rule assigning an element of a p-adic R-algebra S to each tuple (A, φ) over S, where A = (A_m) ∈ lim_← S_m(S) and φ = (φ_{n,m}) ∈ lim_{←m} lim_{←n} T_{n,m}(S) with each φ_{n,m} over A_m.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: p-adic weights κ, characters κ_ψ, and V_κ(K^p, ψ, R), V_κ^cusp(K^p, ψ, R)
items.statement: Let L′ ⊂ \overline{Q}_p be the extension of Q_p generated by the images of all embeddings of K into \overline{Q}_p, and O′ its ring of integers. A p-adic weight is κ = (κ_{σ,i})_{σ∈Σ_K, 1≤i≤m} with κ_{σ,i} ∈ Z^{a_{σ,i}}; it defines the O′-valued character of T_H(Z_p) κ(t) = ∏_{w|p} ∏_{σ∈Σ_K, p_σ = p_w} ∏_{i=1}^m ∏_{j=1}^{a_{σ,i}} σ(t_{w,i,j})^{κ_{σ,i,j}}, t = (diag(t_{w,i,1}, …, t_{w,i,a_{w,i}}))_{w|p, 1≤i≤m} ∈ T_H(Z_p). For a finite-order character ψ : T_H(Z_p) → \overline{Q}_p^×, κ_ψ(t) = ψ(t)κ(t) is an O′[ψ]-valued character of T_H(Z_p). For a p-adic ring R that is an O′[ψ]-algebra, the p-adic modular forms and cuspforms of weight κ and character ψ are V_κ(K^p, ψ, R) = {f ∈ V(K^p, R) : t·f = κ_ψ(t)f for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p)} and V_κ^cusp(K^p, ψ, R) = {f ∈ V^cusp(K^p, R) : t·f = κ_ψ(t)f for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p)}. As a functorial rule, f(A, φ∘t) = κ_ψ(t)f(A, φ) for all t ∈ T_H(Z_p).
items.note: Here κ_{σ,i} has length a_{σ,i} (not b_{σ,i} as for classical weights); §2.9.4 converts. T_H(Z_p) ≅ ∏_{w|p} ∏_i (O_w^×)^{a_{w,i}} via (12). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0a plans character and weight spaces.

items.name: Action of G(A_f^p) and Hecke operators away from p on p-adic forms (§§2.9.2–2.9.3)
items.statement: The action of G(A_f^p) on {M^tor_{K,L/R}}_{K^p} induces actions on {S_m}_{K^p} and {T_{n,m}}_{n,K^p}, giving an action of G(A_f^p) on lim_{→K^p} V(K^p, R) and lim_{→K^p} V_κ(K^p, ψ, R) and on their submodules of cuspforms (printed with lim_{←K^p}). The spaces of p-adic modular forms do not depend on the choice of the lift E, since the reduction of E mod p is G(A_f^p)-invariant. The submodules fixed by K^p are the p-adic modular forms and cuspforms of weight κ and prime-to-p level K^p. For neat open compact K_j^p ⊂ G(A_f^p), j = 1, 2, and g ∈ G(A_f^p), a Hecke operator [K_2^pgK_1^p] on p-adic modular forms and cuspforms is defined as in §2.6.8.
items.note: Uses that the Igusa varieties are normal over Spec(R) [Lan18, Thm. 5.2.1.1]; for a canonical construction the paper refers to [Lan18, §§8.1.4, 8.3.6]. The printed inverse limit over K^p should be a direct limit (sourceIssues E25). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Identification (27) H_{0/O′} ≅ G_m × H_{/O′} and the p-adic weight κ_p of a classical weight κ
items.statement: Let □ = {p}. Under Hypothesis 2.2.1, incl_p identifies Z_p as an S_(p)-algebra and O′ as an S_0-algebra, and O_B ⊗ O′ = ∏_{w|p} ∏_{i=1}^m O_w ⊗ O′ ≅ ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} ∏_{i=1}^m O′. The choices of §§2.6.3 and 2.2 give O_B ⊗ O′-decompositions Λ_0 ⊗_{S_□} O′ = ∏_σ ∏_i e_iΛ_{0,σ} ⊗_{S_0} O′ = ∏_σ ∏_i (O′)^{a_{σ,i}} and L^+ ⊗_{Z_p} O′ = ∏_{w|p} ∏_i e_iL^+_w ⊗_{Z_p} O′ = ∏_{w|p} ∏_i (O_w ⊗ O′)^{a_{w,i}} = ∏_{w|p} ∏_{σ: p_σ=p_w} ∏_i (O′)^{a_{σ,i}}, hence an O_B ⊗ O′-identification Λ_0 ⊗_{S_□} O′ = L^+ ⊗_{Z_p} O′. Since H_{0/O′} ≅ G_m × GL_{O_B⊗O′}(Λ_0 ⊗_{S_□} O′), this determines H_{0/O′} ≅ G_m × H_{/O′}, explicitly (27) (ν, (g_{σ,i})_{σ∈Σ_K}) ↦ (ν, (∏_{σ∈Σ_K, p_σ=p_w} ν·ᵗg_{σc,i}^{−1})_{w|p}), using GL_r(O_w ⊗_{Z_p} O′) ≅ ∏_{σ∈Σ_K, p_σ=p_w} GL_r(O′). It identifies B_{H_0/O′} = G_m × B_{H/O′}, B^u_{H_0/O′} = B^u_{H/O′} and T_{H_0/O′} = G_m × T_{H/O′}. To a classical weight κ = (κ_0, (κ_{σ,i})) (§2.6.3) associate the p-adic weight κ_p = (κ_{σc,i}) (note κ_{σc,i} ∈ Z^{b_{σc,i}} = Z^{a_{σ,i}}), so κ_p(t) = ∏_{w|p} ∏_{σ: p_σ=p_w} ∏_{i=1}^m ∏_{j=1}^{a_{w,i}} σ(t_{w,i,j})^{κ_{σc,i,j}} for t = (diag(t_{w,i,1}, …, t_{w,i,a_{w,i}})) ∈ T_H(Z_p). If x = (t_0, t) ∈ Z_p^× × T_H(Z_p) ⊂ T_{H_0}(O′), then κ(x) = t_0^{c_0} κ_p(t^{−1}), c_0 = κ_0 + Σ_{σ,i,j} κ_{σ,i,j}.
items.note: Printed with 'e_iL_w' for e_iL^+_w and '∏O' for ∏O′ (sourceIssues E26). Checked: under (27), (t_0, t) corresponds to g_{σc,i} = t_0·diag(σ(t_{w,i,j}))^{−1}, and substituting into κ gives t_0^{κ_0 + Σκ_{σ,i,j}} κ_p(t^{−1}); lower-triangular B_{H_0} maps to upper-triangular B_H under g ↦ ᵗg^{−1}. 'as in (2.6.3)' refers to §2.6.3, not an equation. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The p-adic modular form f_{p-adic} attached to a classical form f
items.statement: Fixing G_m = Spec(Z[x, 1/x]) identifies μ_{p^n} = Spec(Z[x, 1/x]/(x^{p^n} − 1)), and for every Z/p^nZ-scheme S identifies Lie_S(μ_{p^n}) = O_S·x(d/dx) = O_S, compatibly in n. If n ≥ m, S is a Z_p/p^mZ_p-scheme and φ ∈ T_{n,m}(S), this gives an isomorphism Lie(φ) : L^+ ⊗ O_S = L^+ ⊗ Lie_S(μ_{p^n}) ≅ Lie_S(A^∨_{/S}[p^n]°) = Lie_S A^∨_{/S}, and the identification Λ_0 ⊗ Z_p = L^+ gives (Lie(φ)^∨, id) ∈ E(S). For R a p-adic O′[ψ]-algebra and f ∈ M_κ(K_r, ψ; R), the p-adic modular form f_{p-adic} takes, on a p-adic test object (A, φ) over a p-adic R-algebra S, the value f_{p-adic}(A, φ) = lim_{←m} f(A_m, φ_{m,m,r}, (Lie(φ_{m,m})^∨, id)) ∈ lim_{←m} S/p^mS = S, where for n ≥ max{r, m}, φ_{n,m,r} : L^+ ⊗ μ_{p^r} ≅ A^∨_{/S}[p^r]° is the isomorphism determined by φ_{n,m}. For t ∈ T_H(Z_p), Lie(φ∘t)^∨ = t^{−1}·Lie(φ)^∨, so (t·f_{p-adic})(A, φ) = lim_{←m} f(A_m, φ_{m,m,r}∘t, (Lie(φ_{m,m}∘t)^∨, id)) = ψ(t)κ_p(t)f_{p-adic}(A, φ); hence f_{p-adic} ∈ V_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R), and if f is a cuspform then f_{p-adic} is a p-adic cuspform.
items.note: Corrected transcription. The paper writes 'Lie_{Z_p}(μ_{p^n}) = Z x d/dx' and 'For any scheme S, this identifies Lie_S(μ_{p^n}) with O_S' (true only when p^n = 0 on S; sourceIssues E27); it writes Lie(φ_{m,m,r}) in the first formula and φ_{m,m,t} in the second (sourceIssues E28); and it writes E_n(S) for the torsor. The weight check uses κ(x) = t_0^{c_0}κ_p(t^{−1}) from (27) with x = (1, t^{−1}). Footnote 3: a modular form can be a p-adic cuspform without being cuspidal, e.g. the critical p-stabilization E*_{2k}(z) = E_{2k}(z) − E_{2k}(pz) of the level 1 weight 2k ≥ 4 Eisenstein series. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The embeddings (28) of classical into p-adic modular forms
items.statement: For ψ : T_H(Z_p) → \overline{Q}_p^× of finite order, R a p-adic O′[ψ]-algebra and κ satisfying (16), f ↦ f_{p-adic} defines injective R-module homomorphisms (28) M_κ(K_r, ψ; R) ↪ V_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R) and S_κ(K_r, ψ; R) ↪ V^cusp_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R).
items.note: Injectivity is justified only by 'as already noted, S_1 is dense in the special fiber of M^tor_{K,L}'. At level K_r the special fibre of \overline{M}_{K_r} already lies over the ordinary locus, so what is needed is that every connected component of \overline{M}_{K_r,L/R} meets the special fibre, together with p-adic separatedness (and flatness of R); this is standard (Hida, Lan) but not argued (sourceIssues E29). The paper says 'weight κ' where κ_p is meant. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hecke compatibility (29) of f ↦ f_{p-adic}, and invariance under f ↦ f_a f
items.statement: The maps (28) are compatible with Hecke operators away from p in the sense that (T(g)·f)_{p-adic} = ||ν(g)||^{−κ_0} T(g)·f_{p-adic} (29) for g ∈ G(A_f^p). If κ′ = (κ_0 + a, (κ_{σ,i})) then κ′_p = κ_p, and for f ∈ M_κ(K;R) and f′ = f_af ∈ M_{κ′}(K;R) (§2.6.11), f_{p-adic} = f′_{p-adic}.
items.note: Stated without proof. f_{p-adic} = f′_{p-adic} holds because the test objects use ε = (Lie(φ)^∨, id), on which f_a = 1. Checked that (29) is consistent with f_a·T(g)f = ||ν(g)||^aT(g)(f_af): both sides of (29) for f′ carry the factor ||ν(g)||^{−κ_0−a}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida's operators u_{w,i,j} on p-adic forms and their relation (30) to U_{w,i,j}
items.statement: Hida defined an action of the double cosets u_{w,i,j} = B^u_H(Z_p) t_{w,i,j} B^u_H(Z_p) (t_{w,i,j} being the image of t^+_{w,i,j} in H(Q_p)) on the modules of p-adic modular forms and cuspforms, via correspondences on the Igusa tower. If R is a p-adic domain in which p is not zero, κ a weight and f ∈ M_κ(K_r, ψ; R), then u_{w,i,j}·f ∈ M_κ(K_r, ψ; R) and (30) u_{w,i,j}·f = |κ_norm(t_{w,i,j})|_p^{−1} U_{w,i,j}·f, κ_norm = (κ_{σ,i′} − b_{σ,i′}).
items.note: Cited: [Hid04, 8.3.1] (see also [SU02]). The normalisation κ_norm (subtract b_{σ,i′} from every entry of κ_{σ,i′}) is taken from the source and was not re-derived here. 'κ as in Section 2.9.1' in the source conflates the p-adic and classical weights; here κ is classical and f is identified with f_{p-adic} via (28). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida's ordinary projector e (31) and the ordinary submodules
items.statement: Put u_p = ∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_{i=1}^m ∏_{j=1}^{n_i} u_{w,i,j} and define the projector (31) e = lim_{→n} u_p^{n!}. For a p-adic ring R the submodules of ordinary p-adic forms are V^ord(K^p, R) = eV(K^p, R) and V^{ord,cusp}(K^p, R) = eV^cusp(K^p, R), and those of weight κ and character ψ are M_κ^ord(K_r, ψ; R) = eM_κ(K_r, ψ; R), S_κ^ord(K_r, ψ; R) = eS_κ(K_r, ψ; R), V^ord_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R) = eV_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R), V^{ord,cusp}_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R) = eV^cusp_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R).
items.note: Following [Hid04].the classicality theorem (32) is a separate item. Planned: PadicFamilies L0a plans the finite and profinite ordinary projector; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida's classicality theorem for ordinary forms (32)
items.statement: If R is a finite O′[ψ]-domain (resp. a finite O′-domain) then V^{ord,cusp}_{κ_p}(K^p, ψ, R) = S^ord_κ(K_r, ψ; R) (resp. V^{ord,cusp}_{κ_p}(K^p, R) = S^ord_κ(K_r; R)) provided κ_{σ,i,b_{σ,i}} + κ_{σc,i,a_{σ,i}} ≫ 0 for all σ ∈ Σ_K, 1 ≤ i ≤ m (κ the classical weight; printed as κ_{σ,i,a_{σ,i}} + κ_{σc,i,b_{σ,i}} ≫ n_ir_i, which is this condition written in the p-adic indexing of κ_p).
items.note: Cited: proved (with more precise inequalities) in [Hid04, Hid02] under conditions (G1)–(G3) of [Hid02, §7], proved by Lan [Lan13] (footnote 4). The printed indices refer to the p-adic weight (§2.9.1 indexing) while S_κ uses the classical weight, and r_i is not defined in the paper (sourceIssues E30). Used later for Λ-adic specialisation (§§7–9). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida's conditions (G1)–(G3) hold (Lan)
items.statement: The conditions (G1)–(G3) of [Hid02, §7], under which Hida proves the classicality theorem (32) and the control theorems (33)–(34), hold for the PEL moduli problems considered here: Theorem 6.4.1.1 of [Lan13] contains (G2) and part of (G1); the remaining (projectivity) assertion of (G1) is [Lan13, Thm. 7.3.3.4]; (G3) is proved in [Lan13, §7.2.3].
items.note: The paper does not restate (G1)–(G3); it cites them to [Hid02, §7] and their proofs to [Lan13]. Invoked again for (33)–(34) and in the proof of Prop. 3.2.5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans Lan's integral PEL toroidal compactifications.

items.name: Ordinary complex cusp forms (relative to ι)
items.statement: Let R be as in (32) and let E_0 ⊂ Frac(R) be a number field over which S_κ(K_r, ψ; R) ⊗ Q has a rational model, given by the E_0-rational cusp forms of type κ and level K_r (e.g. containing K′ and the values of ψ), and let O^+ be the integral closure of Z_(p) in E_0. The intersection of this rational model with S^ord_κ(K_r, ψ; R) is an O^+-lattice S^ord_κ(K_r, ψ; O^+). For any embedding ι : O^+ ↪ C, the image of S^ord_κ(K_r, ψ; O^+) in S_κ(K_r, ψ; C) is the space of ordinary complex cusp forms (relative to ι) of type κ and level K_r.
items.note: Corrected statement. The paper defines O^+ as 'the integral closure of Z_(p) in R' and asserts that Frac(O^+) is a number field; this is false (e.g. for R = Z_p, O^+ = Z_p ∩ \overline{Q} has fraction field of infinite degree over Q) (sourceIssues E31). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: p-adic measures on T_H(Z_p) and their identification with the completed group ring
items.statement: Let R be a p-adic ring. The space of R-valued measures on T_H(Z_p) is Meas(T_H(Z_p); R) = Hom_{Z_p}(C(T_H(Z_p), Z_p), R), where C(T_H(Z_p), Z_p) is the Z_p-module of continuous Z_p-valued functions on T_H(Z_p). Since C(T_H(Z_p), R) = C(T_H(Z_p), Z_p) ⊗̂_{Z_p} R, also Meas(T_H(Z_p); R) = Hom_R(C(T_H(Z_p), R), R). For a complete R-module M the R-module of M-valued measures is defined in the same way, and it is naturally identified with R[[T_H(Z_p)]] ⊗̂_R M; the identification of a measure μ with an element f of the completed group ring is such that, for every continuous homomorphism χ : T_H(Z_p) → R^×, μ(χ) = χ(f), where χ(f) is the image of f under the homomorphism R[[T_H(Z_p)]] → R induced by χ.
items.note: Standard (Amice–Mahler type) facts, stated without proof.Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0 plans measures on profinite spaces; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence.

items.name: Λ_H-adic modular forms and cuspforms; ordinary Λ_H-adic cuspforms S^ord(K^p, R)
items.statement: Let Λ_H = O′[[T_H(Z_p)]]. For R a p-adic O′-algebra, V(K^p, R) and V^cusp(K^p, R) are Λ_H-modules via the actions of T_H(Z_p). A Λ_H-adic modular form over R is a μ ∈ Meas(T_H(Z_p); V(K^p, R)) such that μ(t·f) = t·μ(f) for all t ∈ Λ_H. In particular, if R is an O′[ψ]-algebra then μ(κ_ψ) ∈ V_κ(K^p, ψ, R). Λ_H-adic cuspforms are defined in the same way with cuspforms, and ordinary Λ_H-adic modular forms or cuspforms by replacing the forms with the ordinary forms. If μ is a Λ-adic modular form, eμ (the composition of μ with the R-linear projector V(K^p, R) → eV(K^p, R) = V^ord(K^p, R)) is an ordinary Λ_H-adic form. Let S^ord(K^p, R) = {ordinary Λ_H-adic cuspforms μ ∈ Meas(T_H(Z_p); V^{ord,cusp}(K^p, R))}. The Hecke operators of §§2.9.3 and 2.9.5 act on S^ord(K^p, R) through their actions on V^{ord,cusp}(K^p, R).
items.note: Checked: μ(t·κ_ψ) = κ_ψ(t)μ(κ_ψ) gives μ(κ_ψ) ∈ V_κ(K^p, ψ, R) when T_H acts on functions by translation. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Decomposition T_H(Z_p) = Δ × W, Λ^o = O′[[W]], and the isotypic pieces S^ord_ω
items.statement: Let Δ ⊂ T_H(Z_p) be the torsion subgroup. For p odd (p is unramified in K), (12) induces Δ ≅ ∏_{w|p} ∏_{i=1}^m (k_w^×)^{a_{w,i}}, k_w the residue field of O_w; in particular Δ has order prime to p, and S^ord(K^p, R) = ⊕_{ω∈Δ̂} S^ord_ω(K^p, R), the sum of the isotypical pieces for the O′-characters ω of Δ. Let W ⊂ T_H(Z_p) be a free Z_p-submodule with T_H(Z_p) ≅ Δ × W. Then Λ_H = O′[[Δ × W]] = Λ^o[Δ] with Λ^o = O′[[W]], and each S^ord_ω(K^p, R) is a Λ^o-module. For R ⊂ \overline{Q}_p a finite O′-algebra, Λ^o_R = Λ^o ⊗_{O′} R = R[[W]].
items.note: The paper does not assume p odd; for p = 2 the torsion of O_w^× contains −1, so the displayed identification and 'prime to p' fail (sourceIssues E32). The paper writes 'is a Λ-module' although it renamed Λ to Λ^o (sourceIssues E33). Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida's freeness theorem (33): S^ord_ω(K^p, R) is free of finite rank over Λ^o_R
items.statement: Let R ⊂ \overline{Q}_p be a finite O′-algebra. For every ω ∈ Δ̂, S^ord_ω(K^p, R) is a free Λ^o_R-module of finite rank (33).
items.note: Cited: [Hid02, Thm. 7.1(5)], under conditions (G1)–(G3), which were proved in [Lan13]. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida's control theorem (34): specialisation of ordinary Λ-adic cuspforms
items.statement: Let R ⊂ \overline{Q}_p be a finite O′-algebra and ω ∈ Δ̂. For every finite character ψ : W → \overline{Q}_p^× trivial on W^{p^{r−1}} and every weight κ satisfying the restriction in (32), the map μ ↦ μ(κψ) induces an isomorphism (34) (S^ord_ω(K^p, R) ⊗_R R[ψ]) / p_{κψ}(S^ord_ω(K^p, R) ⊗_R R[ψ]) ≅ S^ord_κ(K_r, ωω_κψ, R[ψ]), where p_{κψ} is the kernel of the homomorphism Λ^o_R ⊗_R R[ψ] → R[ψ] induced by the character κψ, and ω_κ ∈ Δ̂ is κ|_Δ.
items.note: Cited: [Hid02, Thm. 7.1(5)] under (G1)–(G3) [Lan13]. Transcribed as printed. With the paper's own conventions (Δ acting on V through T_H(Z_p), t·f_{p-adic} = ψ(t)κ_p(t)f_{p-adic}, and ω_κ = κ_p|_Δ for κ as in §2.9.1) the nebentypus of the specialisation should be ωω_κ^{−1}ψ; the printed ωω_κψ is right only if ω_κ is read as the classical weight restricted to Δ via x = (1, t), which equals κ_p^{−1}|_Δ (sourceIssues E34). S^ord_κ here uses the classical weight whose p-adic weight is κ (v1–v3 wrote κ*). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 2.10.3 — Λ-adic cuspforms with types W_S
items.statement: One can include types (irreducible representations W_S of compact open subgroups K_S ⊂ K^p, for some finite set S of primes) in the definition of Λ-adic cuspforms; the module of Λ-adic cuspforms of type W_S is written S^ord(K^p, W_S, R). The analogues of the maps (34) in this context are also isomorphisms, using the fact that p_{κψ} is generated by a regular sequence.
items.note: Asserted ('It can be shown'), not proved. Used in §§7–9 where forms with types at S are needed. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The four PEL data P_1, …, P_4 of the doubling, their groups G_i, H_i and the isomorphisms (35)–(36)
items.statement: Let P = (K, c, O, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h) be a PEL datum of unitary type attached to a hermitian pair (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V) as in §§2.1–2.3, with m = 1. Consider the unitary PEL data P_i = (B_i, *_i, O_{B_i}, L_i, ⟨·,·⟩_i, h_i) with O_{B_i} ⊗ Z_p-decompositions L_i ⊗ Z_p = L_i^+ ⊕ L_i^−: P_1 = P, L_1^± = L^±; P_2 = (K, c, O, L, −⟨·,·⟩, h(z̄)), L_2^± = L^∓; P_3 = (K × K, c × c, O × O, L_1 ⊕ L_2, ⟨·,·⟩_1 ⊕ ⟨·,·⟩_2, h_1 ⊕ h_2), L_3^± = L_1^± ⊕ L_2^±; P_4 = (K, c, O, L_3, ⟨·,·⟩_3, h_3), L_4^± = L_3^±. The reflex fields of P_1, P_2, P_3 equal the reflex field F of P; that of P_4 is Q. Put G_i = G_{P_i} and H_i = GL_{O_{B_i}⊗Z_p}(L_i^+). Then G_1 = G_2, and there are canonical inclusions G_3 ↪ G_4 and G_3 ↪ G_1 × G_2 inducing H_3 ↪ H_4 and H_3 ↪ H_1 × H_2. For neat K ⊂ G_i(A_f) with K = G_i(Z_p)K^□ if □ = {p}, M_{i,K} = M_K(P_i) is the moduli scheme over S_□. The O_w-decompositions of L_w^± give O_{B_i,w}-decompositions of L^±_{i,w} = L_i ⊗_{O⊗Z_p} O_w and isomorphisms (35) G_{i/Z_p} ≅ G_m × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} GL_n(O_w) (i = 1, 2), GL_n(O_w) × GL_n(O_w) (i = 3), GL_{2n}(O_w) (i = 4); and (36) H_{i/Z_p} ≅ ∏_{w|p} GL_{a_w}(O_w) (i = 1), GL_{b_w}(O_w) (i = 2), GL_{a_w}(O_w) × GL_{b_w}(O_w) (i = 3), GL_n(O_w) (i = 4). Under these, the canonical inclusions are the identity on similitude factors and the obvious (block-diagonal for G_3 ↪ G_4 and H_3 ↪ H_4) inclusions of GL-parts.
items.note: Checked: signature of P_4 is (n, n) at every σ (hence reflex field Q); ranks of L_4^+ = L^+ ⊕ L^− are a_w + b_w = n. §4 onward writes G = G_4 and uses W = V ⊕ V with ⟨·,·⟩_W = ⟨·,·⟩_V ⊕ −⟨·,·⟩_V.Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The morphisms (37) M_{3,K_3} → M_{4,K_4} and (38) M_{3,K_3} → M_{1,K_1} × M_{2,K_2}
items.statement: Let K_i^□ ⊂ G_i(A_f^□) be neat open compact subgroups, K_i = K_i^□ if □ = ∅ and K_i = G_i(Z_p)K_i^□ otherwise. If K_3^□ ⊂ K_4^□ ∩ G_3(A_f^□), there is a natural S_□-morphism (37) M_{3,K_3} → M_{4,K_4}, A = (A, λ, ι, α) ↦ A_4 = (A, λ, ι∘diag, αK_4^□), where diag : K ↪ K ⊕ K is the diagonal embedding. Let e_i ∈ O ⊕ O (i = 1, 2) be the idempotent projecting to the i-th factor. If K_3^□ ⊂ (K_1^□ × K_2^□) ∩ G_3(A_f^□), there is a natural S_□-morphism (38) M_{3,K_3} → M_{1,K_1} ×_{S_□} M_{2,K_2}, A ↦ (A_1, A_2) = (A_1, λ_1, ι_1, α_1) × (A_2, λ_2, ι_2, α_2), where A_i = ι(e_i)A (so A = A_1 × A_2), λ_i = ι^∨(e_i)∘λ∘ι(e_i), ι_i is the restriction of ι to the i-th factor, and α_{i,s} : L_i ⊗ A_f^□ ≅ H_1(A_{i,s}, A_f^□) is the restriction of α_s to L_i ⊗ A_f^□ ⊂ L_3 ⊗ A_f^□ = (L_1 ⊗ A_f^□) ⊕ (L_2 ⊗ A_f^□) composed with the projection H_1(A_s, A_f^□) → H_1(A_{i,s}, A_f^□).
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Extension of (37)–(38) to toroidal compactifications
items.statement: For suitably compatible choices of polyhedral cone decompositions, the morphisms (37) and (38) extend to maps of toroidal compactifications.
items.note: Cited: [Har89, Prop. 3.4]. Footnote 5: [Har89] works only in characteristic zero, but the cone decompositions defining Lan's toroidal compactifications [Lan13] are independent of the characteristic, so the arguments of [Har89] go through without change. That extension is asserted, not checked. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ShimuraCompactifications C3 plans refinements and Hecke maps of toroidal compactifications.

items.name: Level structures at p for the four PEL data (§3.1.1)
items.statement: The definitions of level structures at p of §2.5 for the PEL data P_i are compatible, and the morphisms (37) and (38) extend to S_□-morphisms with each M_{i,K_i} replaced by M_{i,K_{i,r}} = M_{K_{i,r}}(P_i).
items.note: Level at p is taken relative to L_i^+ (so L_4^+ = L_3^+ = L_1^+ ⊕ L_2^+ = L^+ ⊕ L^−); in matrix coordinates adapted to V ⊕ (−V) this introduces the translation γ_{V_p} of Remark 3.1.4. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Canonical bundles for P_1, …, P_4: Λ_{0,i}, (39), weights on T_{H_{0,3}}, and the bundle maps (40)–(41)
items.statement: Let V_i = L_i ⊗ C with the Hodge structure defined by h_i and W_i = V_i/V_i^{0,−1}. Take Λ_{0,1} = Λ_0; since V_2 = V_1 with Hodge indices reversed (V_2^{0,−1} = V_1^{−1,0}), take Λ_{0,2} to be the image of Λ_0^∨ in W_2 = V_2/V_2^{0,−1} = V_1/V_1^{−1,0} under V_1^{0,−1} = V^{0,−1} ≅ Λ_0^∨ ⊗_{S_0} C. Then Λ_1 = Λ and Λ_2 = Λ_0^∨ ⊕ (Λ_0^∨)^∨ = Λ with their canonical pairings; set Λ_{0,3} = Λ_{0,4} = Λ_{0,1} ⊕ Λ_{0,2} and Λ_3 = Λ_4 = Λ_1 ⊕ Λ_2. The fixed O_B ⊗ Z_p-decompositions of Λ_0, Λ_0^∨ give compatible isomorphisms (39) H_{0,i/Z_p} ≅ G_m × ∏_{w|p} GL_{b_w}(O_w) (i = 1), GL_{a_w}(O_w) (i = 2), GL_{b_w}(O_w) × GL_{a_w}(O_w) (i = 3), GL_n(O_w) (i = 4). The canonical inclusions H_{0,3} ↪ H_{0,4} and H_{0,3} ↪ H_{0,1} × H_{0,2} induce the identity on the G_m-factor and, on GL-factors, the (block) diagonal map and the identity respectively; similarly for the lower-triangular Borels B_{H_{0,i}} and diagonal tori T_{H_{0,i}}. In particular a dominant character κ of T_{H_{0,4}}, or a pair κ = (κ_1, κ_2) of dominant characters of T_{H_{0,1}} and T_{H_{0,2}}, restricts to a dominant character of T_{H_{0,3}}, also denoted κ. With π_i : E_i → M_{K_i} the canonical bundles, (37) and (38) extend to (40) E_3 → E_4, (A, λ, ι, α, ε) ↦ (A, λ, ι∘diag, αK_4^□, ε), and (41) E_3 → E_1 ×_{S_□} E_2, (A, λ, ι, α, ε) ↦ (A_1, λ_1, ι_1, α_1, ε_1) × (A_2, λ_2, ι_2, α_2, ε_2), with ε_i = e_i∘ε∘ι(e_i); similarly for E_{i,r} = E_i ×_{M^tor_{i,K_i}} \overline{M}_{i,K_{i,r}}.
items.note: On the common G_m of H_{0,3} ↪ H_{0,1} × H_{0,2} the map is diagonal, so a pair (κ_1, κ_2) restricts with κ_0 = κ_{1,0} + κ_{2,0}. Dominance is preserved since block-diagonal restriction of a decreasing tuple gives decreasing blocks. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Maps of Igusa towers (42)–(43)
items.statement: Let T_{n,m,i}/S_{m,i} (i = 1, …, 4) be the Igusa tower for M_{i,K_i} as in §2.8. The maps (37) and (38) extend to maps of Igusa towers (42) T_{n,m,3} → T_{n,m,4}, (A, φ) ↦ (A_4, φ), and (43) T_{n,m,3} → T_{n,m,1} ×_{Z_p} T_{n,m,2}, (A, φ) ↦ ((A_1, φ_1), (A_2, φ_2)), where φ_i is the restriction of φ to L_i^+ ⊗ μ_{p^n} composed with the projection to A_i^∨[p^n]°.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 3.1.4 — the translation γ_{V_p} and the Igusa varieties Ig_i with maps (44)
items.statement: As explained in [HLS06, §2.1.11], the inclusion (42) does not restrict on complex points to the map i_3 of Shimura varieties determined by G_3 ⊂ G_4. For each prime w of K^+ dividing p let γ_{V_w} ∈ G_4(K^+_w) be the block matrix with rows (1_{a_w}, 0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 0, 1_{b_w}), (0, 0, 1_{a_w}, 0), (0, 1_{b_w}, 0, 0) (block sizes a_w, b_w, a_w, b_w), and γ_{V_p} = (γ_{V_w})_{w|p} ∈ G_4(K^+_p). Then (42) is i_3 composed with right translation by γ_{V_p} (see (73)). The collection {T_{n,m,i}}, equivalently lim_{→m} lim_{←n} T_{n,m,i}, is denoted Ig_i (1 ≤ i ≤ 4). If K_i^p are prime-to-p level subgroups of G_i(A_f^p) with K_3^p ⊂ K_4^p and K_3^p ⊂ K_1^p × K_2^p, there are Igusa varieties _{K_i^p}Ig_i and inclusions (44) γ_{V_p}∘i_3 : _{K_3^p}Ig_3 → _{K_4^p}Ig_4 and i_4 : _{K_3^p}Ig_3 → _{K_1^p}Ig_1 × _{K_2^p}Ig_2.
items.note: Printed with 'prime w of F^+' and G_4(F^+_w) (F^+ undefined; K^+ meant) and 'subgroups of G_i(A_f)' for G_i(A_f^p) (sourceIssues E35). γ_{V_w} swaps the 2nd and 4th blocks, reordering a basis adapted to L_1 ⊕ L_2 into one adapted to L_4^+ ⊕ L_4^−. Later, res_3 := (γ_{V_p}∘ι_3)^* (§8.1, p. 121). The name i_4 for the map to Ig_1 × Ig_2 has nothing to do with G_4. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Restriction maps res_1, …, res_4 of classical modular forms (45)
items.statement: Let R be a Z_p-algebra and κ either a dominant character of T_{H_{0,4}} or a pair κ = (κ_1, κ_2) of dominant characters of T_{H_{0,1}}, T_{H_{0,2}}. The maps (40) and (41) yield res_1 : M_κ(K_4; R) → M_κ(K_3; R) and res_2 : M_{κ_1}(K_1; R) ⊗_R M_{κ_2}(K_2; R) → M_κ(K_3; R). Let ψ be either a \overline{Q}_p^×-valued character of T_{H_4}(Z_p/p^rZ_p) or a pair ψ = (ψ_1, ψ_2) of \overline{Q}_p^×-valued characters of T_{H_1}(Z_p/p^rZ_p) and T_{H_2}(Z_p/p^rZ_p); ψ defines a character of T_{H_3}(Z_p/p^rZ_p), also written ψ. For R a Z_p[ψ]-algebra, the analogues of (40)–(41) with level structure at p yield (45) res_3 : M_κ(K_{4,r}, ψ; R) → M_κ(K_{3,r}, ψ; R) and res_4 : M_{κ_1}(K_{1,r}, ψ_1; R) ⊗_R M_{κ_2}(K_{2,r}, ψ_2; R) → M_κ(K_{3,r}, ψ; R).
items.note: res_3 is the pullback used for the Eisenstein measure (§§7–8). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Complex description of the restrictions (§3.2.2)
items.statement: In terms of the complex uniformizations (25), the restrictions (40) and (41) correspond to the maps induced by the canonical inclusions of G_3 and H_{0,3} into G_4 and H_{0,4}, and into G_1 × G_2 and H_{0,1} × H_{0,2}, respectively. If φ : G_4(A) × H_{0,4}(C) → C corresponds to a weight κ modular form on G_4 of level K_4, its image under res_1 or res_3 corresponds to the restriction of φ to G_3(A) × H_{0,3}(C). If φ corresponds to f : G_4(A) → W_{κ,4}(C) (W_{κ,i} the irreducible representation of H_{0,i} of highest weight κ), its image under res_1 or res_3 is the restriction of f to G_3(A) composed with the projection W_{κ,4}(C) → W_{κ,3}(C), φ ↦ φ|_{H_{0,3}(C)}. The same holds for res_2 and res_4.
items.note: Stated without proof. For res_3 this presupposes the abstract (lattice-theoretic) description (24) of level-p structures on G_4, with I_r relative to L_4^+ = L_3^+; in block-matrix coordinates adapted to V ⊕ (−V), Remark 3.1.4 inserts the right translation by γ_{V_p} (see readingNotes). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Restriction of p-adic forms (§3.2.3)
items.statement: The maps (42) and (43) induce the obvious restriction maps on modules of p-adic modular forms, also denoted res_i, compatible with weights κ and characters ψ in the obvious way and with the inclusion (28) of spaces of modular forms into p-adic modular forms. (The source adds: compatible 'with restriction to similitude components', and 'the isomorphisms described above extend to isomorphism of spaces of p-adic modular forms (with the tensor product ⊗_R replaced by the completed tensor product ⊗̂_R)'; see note.)
items.note: The source adds 'as well as with ... restriction to similitude components. In particular, the isomorphisms described above extend to isomorphism of spaces of p-adic modular forms'. These refer to material (a §3.1.5 on similitude components and isomorphisms ⊕_α M_{κ_1}(K_1)^α ⊗ M_{κ_2}(K_2)^α ≅ M_κ(K_3)) present in v1–v3 and removed in v4, so no isomorphisms are 'described above' in v5 (sourceIssues E36). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Ordinary CM pairs (J′_0, h_0), their Igusa towers (46), and base point restrictions res_{J′_0,h_0}, res_{p,J′_0,h_0}
items.statement: Let V = V_i for i ∈ {1, 2, 3, 4} and G = G_{P_i}, so (G, X) is the Shimura datum of the moduli problem P_i. Let J′_0 be a torus as in §2.3.2 and (J′_0, h_0) → (G, X) the corresponding morphism of Shimura data. (J′_0, h_0) is ordinary if the points in the image of S(J′_0, h_0) → S(G, X) reduce to points corresponding to ordinary abelian varieties. If (J′_0, h_0) is ordinary it has an associated Igusa tower T_{n,m}(J′_0, h_0) (all n, m) with T_{0,m}(J′_0, h_0) = S_m(J′_0, h_0), the reduction modulo p^m of an integral model of S(J′_0, h_0), each T_{n,m}(J′_0, h_0) finite over S_m; with T_{n,m}(G, X) = T_{n,m}(P_i) there is a morphism of Igusa towers (46) T_{n,m}(J′_0, h_0) → T_{n,m}(G, X). Hence for any r there are restriction maps res_{J′_0,h_0} : M_κ(K_{i,r}, R) → M_κ((J′_0, h_0), R), whose image lies in forms of (unspecified) level r on S(J′_0, h_0), and res_{p,J′_0,h_0} for p-adic modular forms. V_{κ_p}((G, X); K^p, R) denotes p-adic modular forms of weight κ_p and level K^p on the Igusa tower for S(G, X), V^ord_{κ_p}((G, X); K^p, R) the image of the ordinary projector, and V_{κ_p}((J′_0, h_0), R) the corresponding object for S(J′_0, h_0) (level away from p unspecified).
items.note: J′_0 ⊂ ∏ J_{0,i}: equal-similitude subtorus of the product of Serre tori of CM extensions K_i/K with Σ[K_i:K] = n (§2.3.2). Several notions ('level r on S(J′_0,h_0) in an appropriate sense') are deliberately left imprecise by the paper. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.5(i) — restriction to CM points commutes with passage to p-adic forms (commutative square)
items.statement: Let (J′_0, h_0) → (G, X) be a morphism of Shimura data with J′_0 a torus, and suppose (J′_0, h_0) is ordinary. Let G = G_{P_i} for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, let κ be a dominant weight and κ_p the corresponding p-adic weight (as in §2.9.1, via §2.9.4), and let R be a p-adic ring. Then the following diagram commutes. Objects: top-left M_κ(K_{i,r}, R); top-right V_{κ_p}(K_i^p, R); bottom-left M_κ((J′_0, h_0), R); bottom-right V_{κ_p}((J′_0, h_0), R). Arrows: top horizontal R_{κ,G,X} : M_κ(K_{i,r}, R) → V_{κ_p}(K_i^p, R); bottom horizontal R_{κ,J′_0,h_0} : M_κ((J′_0, h_0), R) → V_{κ_p}((J′_0, h_0), R); left vertical res_{J′_0,h_0} : M_κ(K_{i,r}, R) → M_κ((J′_0, h_0), R); right vertical res_{p,J′_0,h_0} : V_{κ_p}(K_i^p, R) → V_{κ_p}((J′_0, h_0), R). That is, res_{p,J′_0,h_0} ∘ R_{κ,G,X} = R_{κ,J′_0,h_0} ∘ res_{J′_0,h_0}. The horizontal maps are those defined in (28) (f ↦ f_{p-adic}, for G and for the CM Shimura variety S(J′_0, h_0) respectively).
items.note: Proof: 'an immediate consequence of the definitions' (both composites evaluate f on the same test objects (A, φ, (Lie(φ)^∨, id)) pulled back along (46)). The source suppresses ψ in M_κ(K_{i,r}, R) and V_{κ_p}(K_i^p, R).Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 3.2.5(ii) — an ordinary p-adic form vanishing at all ordinary CM points is zero
items.statement: Let G = G_{P_i} (i = 1, …, 4) and R a p-adic ring. Let f ∈ V^ord_{κ_p}((G, X); K^p, R). Suppose that for every ordinary CM pair (J′_0, h_0) mapping to (G, X) the restriction res_{p,J′_0,h_0}(f) = 0. Then f = 0.
items.note: The source writes res_{J′_0,h_0}(f) for the p-adic restriction (sourceIssues E37). Proof in the source: V^ord_{κ_p}((G, X); K^p, R) is the R-dual of a finite-rank module over an Iwasawa algebra by Hida theory, so f lies in a finite-rank R-module; (ii) then 'follows from the Zariski density of the ordinary locus in the integral model of S(G, X) [Wed99], provided we know there are enough CM points in the ordinary locus', and every point of the ordinary locus over a finite field lifts with its polarization, endomorphisms and prime-to-p level structure to the generic fibre [Moo04, Prop. 2.3.12] (Serre–Tate canonical lifts, which are CM). The argument is only sketched (sourceIssues E38). Used in §8.1 (p. 123) to reduce identities between p-adic forms to ordinary CM points. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Density of the ordinary locus (Wedhorn)
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 2.2.1 (and p unramified in K), the ordinary locus is Zariski dense in the special fibre of the integral model of S(G, X).
items.note: Cited: [Wed99] ('Ordinariness in good reductions of Shimura varieties of PEL-type'). Invoked as a black box in the proof of Prop. 3.2.5(ii); the same density (for S_1 ⊂ M^tor_{K,L}) is used for (28) via [Lan18, §6.3.3]. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lifting of ordinary points to CM points in characteristic 0 (Moonen; Serre–Tate)
items.statement: Every point of the ordinary locus of the PEL moduli space over a finite field lifts, together with its polarization, endomorphisms and prime-to-p level structure, to a point of the generic fibre (the Serre–Tate canonical lift, which has CM).
items.note: Cited: 'see for example [Moo04, Proposition 2.3.12]'. Planned: AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli A4 plans the Serre–Tate equivalence with endomorphism and polarization structures; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Setting of §4: the doubled hermitian space W = V ⊕ V and the groups G_1, G_4 = G, U_i
items.statement: Throughout §4 one is in the setting of Section 3: (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V) is a hermitian pair over the CM field 𝒦 with V = L_1 ⊗ ℚ and ⟨·,·⟩_1 = trace_{𝒦/ℚ} δ⟨·,·⟩_V, and G_1/ℚ is the unitary similitude group of (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V). (W, ⟨·,·⟩_W) is the hermitian pair with W = V ⊕ V and ⟨·,·⟩_W = ⟨·,·⟩_V ⊕ −⟨·,·⟩_V; G_4/ℚ is its unitary similitude group, written G. Z_i denotes the centre of G_i. One has G_2(𝔸) = G_1(𝔸), so functions and representations of one group are viewed as functions and representations of the other. U_i := ker(ν : G_i → 𝔾_m). n := dim_𝒦 V, and S_0 is the set of primes dividing the discriminant of ⟨·,·⟩_1 or the discriminant of 𝒦. G acts on W on the right.
items.locator: arXiv:1602.01776v5, §4.1, p. 41 (and §4.1.1, p. 42 for the right action)
items.note: Standing notation for all of §4. G_3 (not defined in this range) is the similitude group of V ⊕ (−V), i.e. pairs (g_1, g_2) ∈ G_1 × G_2 with equal similitude factor, embedded in G_4. Because G acts on the right, matrices are with respect to row vectors; this convention governs every sign/inverse in §4 (see the issues on δ_P, (54) and §4.2.1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.1.1 — the Siegel parabolic P = Stab(V^d), its Levi M, unipotent radical N and the map Δ
items.statement: Let V^d = {(x,x) ∈ W : x ∈ V} and V_d = {(x,−x) ∈ W : x ∈ V}, so W = V_d ⊕ V^d is a polarization of ⟨·,·⟩_W; projection to the first summand identifies V^d and V_d with V. Let P ⊂ G be the stabilizer of V^d (a maximal ℚ-parabolic, the Siegel parabolic), M ⊂ P the stabilizer of the polarization W = V_d ⊕ V^d (a Levi subgroup) and N ⊂ P the subgroup fixing both V^d and W/V^d (the unipotent radical). Let Δ : P → GL_𝒦(V^d) = GL_𝒦(V) be the canonical map. Then M ≅ GL_𝒦(V) × 𝔾_m via m ↦ (Δ(m), ν(m)), with inverse (A, λ) ↦ m(A, λ) = diag(λ(A^*)^{-1}, A), where A^* = ᵗA^c. Fixing a basis of V gives Δ′ : N ≅ Her_n(𝒦) (n × n hermitian matrices) and, with respect to this basis and the polarization, N ≅ {(1_n, Δ′(N); 0, 1_n)} ⊆ GL_{2n}(𝒦).
items.note: Blocks are with respect to W = V_d ⊕ V^d and row vectors (G acts on the right), so P is block upper triangular and Δ(p) is the lower-right block D. Check: for m = diag(a, d), m·n(X)·m^{-1} = n(aXd^{-1}). The formula diag(λ(A^*)^{-1}, A) is exact only for a basis of V in which the matrix H of ⟨·,·⟩_V is scalar (in general the V_d-block is λH(A^*)^{-1}H^{-1}, since ⟨ι_d(x), ι^d(y)⟩_W = 2⟨x,y⟩_V). This does not matter, since only det of the blocks enters later. v1–v3 printed diag(λA^*, A); v4 corrected it. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.1 — the character δ_P(·) = |det ∘ Δ(·)|^n
items.statement: Define δ_P(·) := |det ∘ Δ(·)|^n, a character of P(𝔸) (or P(ℚ_v)).
items.note: This is a definition, and it is not the modulus character of P. Under the paper's right-action convention the modulus character is δ_mod(m(A,λ)) = |ν|_{𝒦^+}^{n^2}·|det A|_𝒦^{-n}, so on U(W) δ_mod = |det∘Δ|^{-n} = δ_P^{-1}. Locally at a split place, P_n is block upper triangular in GL_{2n}, with δ_mod((A,B;0,D)) = |det A|^n|det D|^{-n}. v1–v3 said 'The modulus character of P is δ_P(·) = |det∘Δ(·)|^n', which is false for the right action. v4 and v5 changed this to 'Define'. δ_P enters only through δ_P^{-s/n} = |det∘Δ|^{-s} in I(χ,s), while 'unitarily normalized' in §4.1.2 must mean the true modulus character δ_mod^{1/2}. Only with that reading is (55) an element of I(χ,s), since (55) transforms by |A^{-1}D|^{-s-n/2}. D. Marcil (arXiv:2311.05466, §3.1.2) repeats the incorrect claim 'the modulus character δ_Sgl equals ∇^n'. This is harmless here because δ_P is explicitly defined, so it is recorded here and not as a source issue. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.3 — the Siegel Eisenstein series E(f, g) and E_f(s, g)
items.statement: For f = f_{χ,s} ∈ I(χ, s) the standard (non-normalized) Eisenstein series is E(f, g) = Σ_{γ ∈ P(ℚ)\G(ℚ)} f(γg), g ∈ G(𝔸). If Re(s) is sufficiently large it converges absolutely and uniformly on compact subsets and defines an automorphic form on G(𝔸). Given a unitary character χ and a Siegel–Weil section f ∈ I(χ, s) (a function used to define Siegel–Weil Eisenstein series as in [Har08]) one puts f_s := f_{χ,s} := f and E_f(s, g) := E_{f_s}(g).
items.note: the paper's notation is E(f, g) and E_f(s, g). Absolute convergence for Re(s) ≫ 0 is standard and the paper gives no reference. v4 wrote the sum over P(ℚ)/G(ℚ); v5 corrects this to P(ℚ)\G(ℚ). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.3 — meromorphic continuation of Siegel Eisenstein series (cited)
items.statement: If f_s ∈ I(χ, s) is K-finite for a maximal compact subgroup K ⊂ G(𝔸), then the Eisenstein series E_f(s, g) has a meromorphic continuation in s.
items.note: Stated without proof or reference (Langlands' theory of Eisenstein series). Used as a black box. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.1.4, (47)–(48) — the U_1-constituents π, π^♭, their factorizations and factorizable test vectors
items.statement: Let O_{𝒦^+} be the ring of integers of 𝒦^+. For i = 1,…,4 write U_i(𝔸) = ∏′_v U_{i,v} over the places v of 𝒦^+; G(𝔸) = G_∞ × ∏′_q G_q and P(𝔸) = P_∞ × ∏′_q P_q over rational primes q, with G_p = ℚ_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} G_w and P_p = ℚ_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} P_w. Let π be an irreducible cuspidal automorphic representation of G_1(𝔸), π^∨ its contragredient (a twist of the complex conjugate of π, hence cuspidal), and S_π the set of finite primes v of O_{𝒦^+} with π_v ramified. Choose an irreducible U_1(𝔸)-constituent π̲ ⊂ π occurring in the automorphic forms on U_1, with dual π̲^♭ (which occurs in π^∨|_{U_1(𝔸)}), and assume π̲ contains the spherical vectors for K^{S_π}. Fix nonzero unramified φ_{w,0} ∈ π_w and φ′_{w,0} ∈ π^∨_w for finite w ∉ S_π and factorizations (47) π̲ ≅ π̲_∞ ⊗ π̲_f, π̲_f ≅ π̲^{S_π,p} ⊗ π̲_p ⊗ π̲_{S_π}, π̲_p ≅ ⊗_{w|p} π̲_w, π̲_{S_π} ≅ ⊗_{w∈S_π} π̲_w compatible with them, and similarly for π̲^♭ (viewed as an anti-holomorphic automorphic representation of G_2). Vectors φ ∈ π̲^{K^{S_π}}, φ^♭ ∈ π̲^{♭,K^{S_π}} (forms on G_1, G_2) are assumed factorizable (48): φ = ⊗_v φ_v, φ^♭ = ⊗_v φ^♭_v with φ_v = φ_{v,0}, φ^♭_v = φ′_{v,0} for v ∉ S_π. Local U_1(𝒦_v^+)-invariant pairings ⟨·,·⟩_{π_v} : π_v × π_v^∨ → ℂ are fixed with ⟨φ_{v,0}, φ^♭_{v,0}⟩_{π_v} = 1 for v ∉ S_π. From then on π, π^♭ denote these irreducible U_1(𝔸)-constituents.
items.note: The paper asserts that the standard L-function does not depend on the choice of constituent ('well known, and follows from the unfolding computation'). The formulas depend on the factorizations (47). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (49)–(50) and Remark 4.1.5 — anti-ordinary vectors at p and anti-holomorphic vectors at ∞
items.statement: The local components at p and at ∞ are chosen as (49) φ_p := ⊗_{w|p} φ_w = ⊗_{w|p} φ^{a-ord}_{w,r,π_w}, φ^♭_p := ⊗_{w|p} φ^♭_w = ⊗_{w|p} φ^{a-ord}_{w,r,π^♭_w}, and (50) φ_∞ := ⊗_{σ|∞} φ_σ = φ_{κ_σ,−}, φ^♭_∞ := ⊗_{σ|∞} φ^♭_σ = φ_{κ^♭_σ,−}. Remark 4.1.5: (i) φ_p (resp. φ^♭_p) is anti-ordinary with respect to a group I_r (resp. I^♭_r) in the sense of §8.3.5 (resp. §8.4.4); (ii) r is an integer chosen in (60) to be sufficiently large.
items.note: The notation is explained in §§8.3.5, 8.4.4 (anti-ordinary vectors) and §4.4.14 (anti-holomorphic vectors). §4.3.4 ((64), (70), (60)) states that (64) and (70) correspond to condition (i) and (60) to condition (ii). All cross-references checked: §8.3.5, §8.4.4, §4.4.14 exist in v5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.1.4 — the doubling integral vanishes unless π′ ≅ π^∨ (corrected form of the 'invariant pairing' claim)
items.statement: Assume the multiplicity one Hypothesis 7.3.3. After unfolding, I(φ, φ′, f, s) depends on (φ, φ′) only through the L² pairings ⟨π(u)φ, φ′⟩, u ∈ U_1(𝔸). Hence, for automorphic representations π, π′ of G_1, I(φ, φ′, f, s) ≡ 0 unless π′ ≅ π^∨ (upon restriction to U(V)). If ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩ ≠ 0 then ⟨φ_v, φ^♭_v⟩_{π_v} ≠ 0 for all v. [The paper instead asserts that (φ, φ′) ↦ I(φ, φ′, f, s) is a G_1(𝔸)-invariant pairing for fixed f, that Hypothesis 7.3.3 makes the space of such pairings at most one-dimensional (exactly one-dimensional when π′ = π^∨), and hence that ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩ = 0 implies I(φ, φ^♭, f, s) = 0 for all s. This is false in general; see the source issue.]
items.note: Corrected statement; see the source issue on p. 45. The paper immediately restricts to ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩ ≠ 0, so the false implication is not used later. Where Z_v = vol(𝒰_v)·⟨φ_v, φ^♭_v⟩, as for the ramified sections of Lemma 4.2.3, the vanishing does hold place by place. Source issues: sourceIssues E39. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (51) — factorization of the doubling integral into local factors I_v and local zeta integrals Z_v
items.statement: Let f_U be the restriction of f to U_4(𝔸) and assume f_U(g) = ⊗_v f_v(g_v) with f_v = f_{v,s} ∈ I_v(χ_v, s), χ_v = ⊗_{w|v} χ_w (v over places of 𝒦^+). Then (51) I(φ, φ^♭, f, s) = ∏_v I_v(φ_v, φ^♭_v, f_v, s) · ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩, where I_v(φ_v, φ^♭_v, f_v, s) = ∫_{U_{1,v}} f_{v,s}(u, 1) ⟨π_v(u)φ_v, φ^♭_v⟩_{π_v} du / ⟨φ_v, φ^♭_v⟩_{π_v}. The denominator equals 1 for v ∉ S_π. The numerator is denoted Z_v(φ_v, φ^♭_v, f_v, s).
items.note: This follows from the unfolding and from the factorization of the global invariant pairing as a constant times ∏_v⟨·,·⟩_{π_v}; the constant cancels. It needs the product of local Haar measures du_v to agree with the global measure du, which the paper leaves implicit. Only the restriction to U_4 of the section is ever specified locally, and this is what makes the similitude-factor issue in (54) harmless. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Remark 4.1.6 — the χ-twisted pairing ⟨·,·⟩_χ and the vectors φ^♭_χ
items.statement: To define the arithmetically normalized period one takes as inputs φ ∈ π and φ^♭_χ := φ^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det ∈ π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det. For φ_1 ∈ π and φ_2 ∈ π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det, ⟨φ_1, φ_2⟩_χ is defined as the L² pairing of φ_1 with φ_2 ⊗ χ∘det, so ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩_χ = ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩. In the final result one takes vectors φ ⊗ φ^♭_χ integral for a structure native to π ⊗ π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det, and the resulting periods differ by CM periods.
items.note: The statement is corrected: the paper prints 'φ_2 ∈ π ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det' and 'π ⊗ π ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det' where π^♭ is meant (see source issue). The remark is new in v5 and absent from v4 (v4, p. 41). Source issues: sourceIssues E40. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (52) — the CM type Σ and the unitary Hecke character χ with prescribed infinity type
items.statement: As in §2.3 let Σ = {σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 : 𝔭_σ ∈ Σ_p}, a CM type for 𝒦. Throughout the rest of §4, χ : 𝒦^×\𝔸_𝒦^× → ℂ^× is a unitary character such that χ_∞ = ⊗_{σ∈Σ} χ_σ is given by (52) χ_∞((z_σ)) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} z_σ^{-(k_σ + 2ν_σ)} (z_σ z̄_σ)^{k_σ/2 + ν_σ}, (z_σ) ∈ ∏_{σ∈Σ} ℂ^×, where k = (k_σ) ∈ ℤ^Σ_{≥0} and (ν_σ) ∈ ℤ^Σ.
items.note: Check: |z^{-(k+2ν)}(z z̄)^{k/2+ν}| = 1, so χ_∞ is unitary. On 𝒦^+_σ = ℝ the restriction is sgn^{k_σ}, so χ|_{𝔸_{𝒦^+}^×} has finite-order infinity type. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.2 — the sets S_ram, S and S′
items.statement: S_ram := S_π ∪ S_χ ∪ S_𝒦, where S_χ is the set of finite primes v of O_{𝒦^+} for which χ_v = ⊗_{w|v} χ_w is ramified and S_𝒦 the set of finite primes of O_{𝒦^+} that ramify in 𝒦. S is a finite set of finite rational primes with p ∉ S such that, for every rational prime ℓ, if a prime of 𝒦^+ above ℓ lies in S_ram then ℓ ∈ S. S′ is the set of primes of 𝒦^+ lying above the primes of S; in particular S′ ⊇ S_ram.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.2.1 — the spherical Siegel–Weil sections and spherical vectors at v ∉ S′
items.statement: Let ℓ ≠ p be a finite rational prime with ℓ ∉ S. Then K_ℓ := G_4(ℤ_ℓ) is a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup of G(ℚ_ℓ) = G_4(ℚ_ℓ) = ∏_{v|ℓ} G_{4,v}, and f_ℓ = ⊗_{v|ℓ} f_v ∈ I_ℓ(χ_ℓ, s) is the unique K_ℓ-invariant section with f_ℓ(K_ℓ) = 1 (the sections used for the Eisenstein measure in [Eis15]). For each prime v ∉ S′, φ_v ∈ π_v and φ′_v ∈ π_v^∨ are the normalized spherical vectors with ⟨φ_v, φ′_v⟩_{π_v} = 1. Such v are split or inert in 𝒦; for split v, U_{1,v} ≅ GL_n(𝒦_v^+).
items.note: Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.2.1 — the unramified local doubling integral (cited; corrected for the paper's normalisations)
items.statement: Let v ∉ S′, with the sections f_v and spherical vectors φ_v, φ′_v of §4.2.1, and with I(χ, s) normalised as in §4.1.2 (G acting on the right, sections transforming by χ(det Δ(p))|det Δ(p)|^{-s-n/2} on U_4). Then d_{n,v}(s, χ_v^{-1}) · I_v(φ_v, φ′_v, f_v, s) = L_v(s + 1/2, π_v, χ_v^{-1}), where d_{n,v}(s, χ) = ∏_{r=0}^{n-1} L_v(2s + n − r, χ|_{𝒦^+} η_v^r) as in (53) and L_v(s, π_v, χ) = L_v(s, BC(π_v) ⊗ χ∘det) is the standard Godement–Jacquet factor of the local base change. For split v this reduces to [Jac79] and [GPSR87, §6], for inert v to [Li92, §3]. [Printed: d_{n,v}(s, χ_v) I_v(φ_v, φ′_v, f_v, s) = L_v(s + 1/2, π_v, χ_v).]
items.note: Cited, not proved. The statement is corrected; see the source issue on §4.2.1. The paper's printed version has χ_v where, with its own right-action normalisation of I(χ, s), χ_v^{-1} appears. Direct check for n = 1 at a split unramified v, π_v = β a character of U(1)_v ≅ 𝒦_w^×: I_v = L(s+½, βχ_{w̄}^{-1}) L(s+½, β^{-1}χ_w^{-1}) / L(2s+1, (χ_wχ_{w̄})^{-1}). These characters are also those that occur at p in Theorem 4.3.10 (π_b ⊗ χ_{2,w} = π_b ⊗ χ_{w̄}^{-1} and π̃_a ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{-1} = π̃_a ⊗ χ_w^{-1}).Source issues: sourceIssues E41. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (53) — the normalizing factor d_{n,v}(s, χ_v)
items.statement: d_{n,v}(s, χ_v) = d_{n,v}(s) := ∏_{r=0}^{n−1} L_v(2s + n − r, χ_v|_{𝒦^+} η_v^r), where η_v is the character of 𝒦_v^+ attached by local class field theory to 𝒦_w/𝒦_v^+ (w a prime of 𝒦 above v).
items.note: Footnote 7 says that, comparing with [Li92, §3] and [Li92, Theorem 3.1], the formula [HLS06, (3.1.2.5)] has a typographical error: the n − 1 should not appear in the exponent. Check for n = 1: L(2s+1, χ|_{𝒦^+}) is the normalising factor for the Eisenstein series on U(1,1) ⊃ SL_2. With the paper's normalisation of I(χ,s) the factor that actually normalises the spherical section is d_{n,v}(s, χ_v^{-1}): for n = 1 at split v, f^Φ(1) = L(2s+1, (χ_wχ_{w̄})^{-1}). See unramified-zeta. Source issues: sourceIssues E41. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.2.1 — the standard Euler factor of U_{1,v} equals the Godement–Jacquet factor of the base change (cited from HLS06)
items.statement: For each v ∉ S′, L_v(s, π_v, χ_v) = L_v(s, BC(π_v) ⊗ χ_v∘det), where L_v(s, π_v, χ_v) is the standard local Langlands Euler factor attached to the unramified representation π_v of U_{1,v}, the unramified character χ_v of 𝒦_v and the standard representation of the L-group of U_{1,v}, BC is local base change from U_{1,v} to GL_n(𝒦_v), and the right side is the standard Godement–Jacquet Euler factor.
items.note: Cited from [HLS06, p. 439]. Footnote 8 notes a typographical error there: base change to GL_m should read GL_n. v4 cites [HLS06, p. 45], an internal page number; v5 uses the journal page. Source issues: sourceIssues E41. Planned: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.4 plans the unramified Euler polynomial of an L-group representation, the partial Euler product and the comparison with AL.1–3.

items.name: §4.2.2 — open-orbit facts for the doubling embedding at v ∈ S′ (cited from HLS06)
items.statement: Let v ∈ S′. Then P_v·(U_{1,v} × 1_n) ⊆ P_v·U_{3,v} is open in U_{4,v}; P_v w = P_v·(−1_n, 1_n) ⊆ P_v·U_{3,v}, where P_v w P_v is the big cell; and P_v ∩ (U_{1,v} × 1_n) = {(1_n, 1_n)}. Consequently (P_v·(U(V) × 1_n)) ∩ P_v w P_v is an open neighbourhood of w in P_v w P_v, hence of the form P_v w 𝔘 for some open subset 𝔘 of the unipotent radical N_v of P_v.
items.note: Cited from [HLS06, p. 439] and [HLS06, (3.2.1.5)]. Check: in (V_d, V^d)-coordinates (−1_n, 1_n) = (0, −1; −1, 0), which lies in the big cell. The paper never defines w explicitly. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.2.2 — the local Siegel sections f_v = f^-_{L_v} at v ∈ S′
items.statement: Let v ∈ S′, φ_v ∈ π_v and φ′_v ∈ π′_v with ⟨φ_v, φ′_v⟩_{π_v} = 1, and K_v an open compact subgroup of G_{1,v} (read U_{1,v}) fixing φ_v. Choose a lattice L_v small enough that 𝔘_v contains N(L_v) := {(1_n, x; 0, 1_n) | x ∈ L_v} (N identified with Δ′(N)) and that P_v w N(L_v) ⊆ P_v·(−1_n·K_v × 1_n) ⊆ P_v·U_{3,v}. Then P_v w N(L_v) = P_v·(𝒰_v × 1_n) for an open neighbourhood 𝒰_v of −1_n contained in −1_n·K_v. Let δ_{L_v} be the characteristic function of N(L_v). There is a Siegel section f_{L_v} supported on P_v w P_v with f_{L_v}(wx) = δ_{L_v}(x) for all x ∈ N_v [HLS06, pp. 449–50]. Define f_v := f^-_{L_v} ∈ I(χ_v, s) by f^-_{L_v}(g) = f_{L_v}(g·(−1, 1)), g ∈ U_{4,v}.
items.note: f^-_{L_v} is the translate by (−1, 1) ∈ U_{3,v} = U_{1,v} × U_{1,v} of the sections of [HLS06, §§3.3.1–3.3.2]. The paper states that where they are nonzero, its Fourier coefficients agree with those of the sections in [Eis15, §2.2.9] and [Shi97], so the p-adic interpolation of q-expansion coefficients is unaffected. Lemma 4.2.3 needs L_v to be small also relative to the conductor of χ_v; see the source issue. Source issues: sourceIssues E42, sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 4.2.3 — the local zeta integral at v ∈ S′ is a volume
items.statement: Let v ∈ S′ and f_v = f^-_{L_v} (§4.2.2), where L_v is in addition chosen so small that χ_v(det(1_n − x)) = 1 for all x ∈ L_v, and f_{L_v} is normalised with w = (−1_n, 1_n). Then the support of f^-_{L_v} on U_{1,v} × 1_n is −1_n·𝒰_v × 1_n, f^-_{L_v} restricted to U_{1,v} × 1_n is the characteristic function of −1_n·𝒰_v × 1_n, and I_v(φ_v, φ′_v, f_v, s) = volume(𝒰_v). [Printed without the extra condition on L_v and with the argument χ in place of s: 'I_v(φ_v, φ′_v, f_v, χ) = volume(𝒰_v)'.]
items.note: The printed proof is: the support claim, then f^-_{L_v} = δ_{−1_n·𝒰_v × 1_n} on U_{1,v} × 1_n, then π_v(g)φ_v = φ_v on K_v ⊇ −1_n·𝒰_v. The extra hypotheses are needed: for u in the support, f^-_{L_v}((u,1)) = χ_v(det(1_n − X))^{-1} δ_{L_v}(X) with X = (u+1)^{-1}(u−1). See source issue. Neither hypothesis restricts the choices, since L_v may be shrunk. Source issues: sourceIssues E42, sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.1 — χ_{w,1}, χ_{w,2} and the characters ψ_w, ψ_{w,s} of P_n(𝒦_w)
items.statement: Via the isomorphism (9) for G_4, G(ℚ_p) ≅ ℚ_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} GL_{𝒦_w}(W_w) and P(ℚ_p) ≅ ℚ_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} P_n(𝒦_w), with P_n ⊂ GL_𝒦(W) the parabolic stabilizing V^d. So M(ℚ_p) ≅ ℚ_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} GL_{𝒦_w}(V_{d,w}) × GL_{𝒦_w}(V^d_w) and N(ℚ_p) ≅ ∏_{w∈Σ_p} N_n(𝒦_w) (N_n the unipotent radical of P_n); here U_w := U ⊗_𝒦 𝒦_w. For w ∈ Σ_p let χ_{w,1} = χ_w and χ_{w,2} = χ_{w̄}^{-1}, identifying 𝒦_w = 𝒦^+_{w^+} = 𝒦_{w̄} with w^+ = w|_{𝒦^+} = w̄|_{𝒦^+}. Writing elements of P_n with respect to W = V_d ⊕ V^d, define ψ_w : P_n(𝒦_w) → ℂ^×, ψ_w((A, B; 0, D)) = χ_{w,1}(det D) χ_{w,2}(det A), and ψ_{w,s}((A, B; 0, D)) = χ_{w,1}(det D) χ_{w,2}(det A) |det(A^{-1}D)|_w^{-s}.
items.note: On U_4(ℚ_p), ∏_w ψ_{w,s} is the restriction of χ(det∘Δ)|det∘Δ|^{-s}, because the w̄-component of Δ(p) has determinant ν^n/det A_w. The paper cites 'the isomorphisms 9', i.e. equation (9) of §2.2 (v4 cited 2.2.2). Source issues: sourceIssues E43, sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (54) — the section f_{p,s} at p as a product of local sections
items.statement: Given ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} f_{w,s} ∈ ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} Ind_{P_n(𝒦_w)}^{GL_{𝒦_w}(W_w)}(ψ_{w,s}) (normalized induction), set f_{p,s}(g) = |ν|_p^{sn/2} ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} f_{w,s}(g_w) for g = (ν, (g_w)) ∈ G(ℚ_p). The restriction of f_{p,s} to U_4(ℚ_p) lies in the restriction of I_p(χ_p, s). On all of G(ℚ_p), the factor |ν|_p^{sn/2} has to be replaced by ∏_{w∈Σ_p} χ_{w̄}(ν)^n for f_{p,s} to lie in I_p(χ_p, s), reading the absolute values of §4.1.2 as the idelic module of 𝒦. [The paper asserts: 'Then, as explained in [Eis15], f_p ∈ I_p(χ_p, s).']
items.note: Statement corrected; see the source issue on (54). Only the restriction to U_4 enters the zeta integrals (51), so §4 is unaffected. The exponent was |ν|_p^{-sn/2} in v1–v4 and is |ν|_p^{+sn/2} in v5. Marcil (arXiv:2311.05466, (33)) uses |ν|_p^{(s−n/2)n/2}. Source issues: sourceIssues E43. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (55) — the Godement-type Siegel–Weil section f^{Φ_w} attached to a Schwartz function Φ_w
items.statement: A level structure at p for P_1 gives an O_w-basis of L_{1,w}, hence 𝒦_w-bases of V_w, V^d_w, V_{d,w} (via their identifications with V_w) and of W_w = V_{d,w} ⊕ V^d_w. These identify GL_{𝒦_w}(V_w) ≅ GL_n(𝒦_w) and GL_{𝒦_w}(W_w) ≅ GL_{2n}(𝒦_w), with P_n(𝒦_w) the block upper-triangular and M_n(𝒦_w) the block-diagonal n × n-block matrices. Let w ∈ Σ_p, and let Φ_w : Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, W_w) → ℂ be a Schwartz function. Write Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, W_w) = Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, V_{d,w}) ⊕ Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, V^d_w), X = (X_1, X_2), and 𝐗 = {X : X(V_w) = V^d_w} = {(0, X) | X : V_w ≅ V^d_w}, identified with GL_{𝒦_w}(V_w) via V_w → V^d_w ≅ V_w. Define f^{Φ_w}(g) := χ_{2,w}(det g) |det g|_w^{n/2 + s} ∫_𝐗 Φ_w(Xg) χ_{1,w}^{-1}χ_{2,w}(det X) |det X|_w^{n+2s} d^×X, g ∈ GL_{2n}(𝒦_w). Linear maps act on W_w on the right, and d^×X is the right Haar measure on 𝐗 ≅ GL_n(𝒦_w). Then f^{Φ_w} ∈ Ind_{P_n(𝒦_w)}^{GL_{2n}(𝒦_w)} ψ_{w,s} (normalized induction).
items.note: Verified: for p = (A, B; 0, D), (0, X)p = (0, XD), and substituting X ↦ XD^{-1} gives f^{Φ}(pg) = χ_1(det D)χ_2(det A)|det A|^{n/2+s}|det D|^{-n/2-s} f^{Φ}(g) = ψ_{w,s}(p)δ_{P_n}(p)^{1/2} f^{Φ}(g). Footnote 9: this basis of W_w is not in general the one attached to the level structure for P_4. Footnote 10: the difference from [Eis15, (21)] is due to normalized versus unnormalized induction. Source issues: sourceIssues E52. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.3.1 — partitions of the signature and the characters μ_{i,w}, ν_{i,w}
items.statement: Let (a_w, b_w) be the signature associated to w | p and (L_1, ⟨·,·⟩_1). For each w ∈ Σ_p fix partitions a_w = n_{1,w} + ⋯ + n_{t(w),w} and b_w = n_{t(w)+1,w} + ⋯ + n_{r(w),w}. Let μ_{1,w}, …, μ_{r(w),w} be characters of O_w^×, μ_w = (μ_{1,w}, …, μ_{r(w),w}) and μ = ∏_{w∈Σ_p} μ_w. Each μ_{i,w} is viewed as a character of GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w) via det. Put ν_{i,w} = χ_{1,w}^{-1} χ_{2,w} μ_{i,w} (i = 1, …, r(w)) and ν_w = (ν_{1,w}, …, ν_{r(w),w}).
items.note: ν_{i,w} = χ_w^{-1}χ_{w̄}^{-1}μ_{i,w} on O_w^×. Its conductor involves the conductor of χ_{w̄}, which (56) does not control; see source issue. Source issues: sourceIssues E44. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.1 — the set 𝔛_w and the function φ_{ν_w} on M_n(𝒦_w)
items.statement: Let 𝔛_w ⊂ M_n(O_w) consist of the matrices (A, B; C, D) with A ∈ M_{a_w}(O_w), D ∈ M_{b_w}(O_w), such that the leading principal (n_{1,w} + ⋯ + n_{i,w})-minor of A lies in O_w^× for i = 1, …, t(w) and the leading principal (n_{t(w)+1,w} + ⋯ + n_{i,w})-minor of D lies in O_w^× for i = t(w)+1, …, r(w). Let A_i (resp. D_i) be the determinant of the leading principal i × i minor of A (resp. D). Define φ_{ν_w} : M_n(𝒦_w) → ℂ, supported on 𝔛_w, by φ_{ν_w}(X) = ν_{t(w),w}(det A) · ∏_{i=1}^{t(w)−1} (ν_{i,w}ν_{i+1,w}^{-1})(A_{n_{1,w}+⋯+n_{i,w}}) · ν_{r(w),w}(det D) · ∏_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)−1} (ν_{i,w}ν_{i+1,w}^{-1})(D_{n_{t(w)+1,w}+⋯+n_{i,w}}) for X = (A, B; C, D) ∈ 𝔛_w.
items.note: The printed formula writes ν_{t(w),w}(A) for ν_{t(w),w}(det A) and contains a stray '·×'. The product telescopes: for A block upper triangular with diagonal blocks a_1, …, a_t, the A-part equals ∏_i ν_{i,w}(det a_i), and similarly for D. φ_{ν_w} depends only on leading principal minors of the A- and D-blocks, so φ_{ν_w}(ᵗX) = φ_{ν_w}(X). This transpose-invariance is what makes the Fourier-transform convention in (57) harmless in (85). Source issues: sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (56) — the level t, the group Γ_w(t) and the character μ_w on it
items.statement: Let t ≥ max_{w∈Σ_p, 1≤i≤r(w)} (1, ord_w(cond(μ_{i,w})), ord_w(cond(χ_w)), ord_{w̄}(cond(χ_{w̄}))) (56), and let Γ_w = Γ_w(t) ⊂ GL_n(O_w) be the subgroup of matrices whose entries below the n_{i,w} × n_{i,w} diagonal blocks lie in 𝔭_w^t and whose upper-right a_w × b_w block also lies in 𝔭_w^t. For m ∈ Γ_w with diagonal blocks m_i put μ_w(m) = ∏_i μ_{i,w}(det m_i). [Printed (56) omits the term ord_{w̄}(cond(χ_{w̄})) and has unbalanced parentheses.]
items.note: Corrected statement; see source issue on (56). Γ_w(t) is block upper triangular modulo 𝔭_w^t, with the a × b block also ≡ 0, and μ_w is a character of it because each μ_{i,w} has conductor ≤ 𝔭^t. In v4 this is (4.3.3), p. 45, same text; also present in v1. Source issues: sourceIssues E44, sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (57) — the Schwartz functions Φ_{1,w} and Φ_{2,w} = φ̂_{ν_w}
items.statement: Φ_{1,w} is the function on M_{n×n}(𝒦_w) supported on Γ_w(t) with Φ_{1,w}(x) = μ_w(x) for x ∈ Γ_w(t). Φ_{2,w} is defined by (57) Φ_{2,w}(x) = φ̂_{ν_w}(x) = ∫_{M_{n×n}(𝒦_w)} φ_{ν_w}(y) e_w(−trace(ᵗy x)) dy.
items.note: The additive character e_w and the measure dy are not defined in the paper. The computations of Lemma 4.3.2 need e_w to have conductor O_w (true for e_p∘tr_{𝒦_w/ℚ_p}, since p is unramified in 𝒦 by the standing hypothesis of §1.4.1) and dy to be self-dual (vol M_n(O_w) = 1). This Fourier transform F_− differs from Godement–Jacquet's Φ̂(x) = ∫Φ(y)ψ(tr(yx))dy [Jac79] by x ↦ −ᵗx, so F_GJ∘F_− is φ ↦ φ∘ᵗ. Since φ_{ν_w} is transpose-invariant, Φ_{2,w} is too and coincides with Marcil's Godement–Jacquet-normalised Φ_{2,w} (arXiv:2311.05466, Remark 3.4) in this setting, and (85) (Φ^{(4)})^∧ = φ_ν(1_a ⊕ ·) holds exactly. See readingNotes. Source issues: sourceIssues E52. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (58) — the Siegel–Weil section f_{w,s} = f^{χ,μ}_w at w | p (and f_{p,s})
items.statement: For X = (X_1, X_2) ∈ Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, W_w) = Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, V_{d,w}) ⊕ Hom_{𝒦_w}(V_w, V^d_w), with X_1, X_2 identified with matrices via the basis of V_w from the level structure at p for P_1, let Φ_w(X) = Φ_{χ,μ,w}(X_1, X_2) = vol(Γ_w)^{-1} Φ_{1,w}(−X_1) · Φ_{2,w}(2X_2). Define (58) f_{w,s} := f^{χ,μ}_w := f^{Φ_w} = f^{Φ_{χ,μ,w}} (by (55)), and f_{p,s} ∈ I_p(χ_p, s) by (54).
items.note: Φ_w is given in the polarization coordinates (V_d, V^d). In the coordinates W_w = V_w ⊕ V_w used from §4.3.6 on, where (Y_1, Y_2) = (X_1 + X_2, X_2 − X_1), it is vol(Γ_w)^{-1}Φ_{1,w}((Y_2 − Y_1)/2)Φ_{2,w}(Y_1 + Y_2). The §4.3.6 computation instead uses Vol(Γ_w)^{-1}Φ_{1,w}(Y_1)Φ_{2,w}(Y_2); see the source issue on §4.3.6, which is decisive for whether Theorem 4.3.10 computes the zeta integral of this section. The paper states that Φ_{χ,μ,w} is a partial Fourier transform in the second variable in the sense of [Eis15, Lemma 10], which is what makes it compatible with the Eisenstein measure. Source issues: sourceIssues E52. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.
