items.name: §4.3.1 — Φ_{χ,μ,w} is a partial Fourier transform in the second variable (cited from Eis15)
items.statement: φ̂_{ν_w} is the Fourier transform of φ_{ν_w} as in [Eis15, Lemma 10], and Φ_{χ,μ,w}(X_1, X_2) is a partial Fourier transform in the second variable in the sense of [Eis15, Lemma 10]. This links the section (58) to the q-expansion coefficients of the p-adic Eisenstein measure.
items.note: Cited, not proved. The factor 2 in Φ_{2,w}(2X_2) and the sign in Φ_{1,w}(−X_1) belong to the polarization coordinates. The pairing between V_d and V^d is 2⟨·,·⟩_V: ⟨(x,−x), (y,y)⟩_W = 2⟨x,y⟩_V. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2(i) — equivariance of φ_{ν_w} under Γ_w
items.statement: Assume t satisfies (56), including t ≥ ord_{w̄}(cond(χ_{w̄})). For γ_1, γ_2 ∈ Γ_w and X ∈ M_n(𝒦_w), φ_{ν_w}(ᵗγ_1 X γ_2) = μ_w(γ_1γ_2) χ_{1,w}^{-1}χ_{2,w}(det γ_1γ_2) φ_{ν_w}(X).
items.note: The paper says only that it 'follows immediately from the definition of φ_{ν_w}'. Proof: modulo 𝔭^t, γ_i is block diagonal (a-part block upper triangular, b-part block upper triangular), so the leading principal minors of the A- and D-blocks of ᵗγ_1Xγ_2 are those of X times unit determinants, up to factors in 1 + 𝔭^t. This needs every ν_{i,w} = χ_w^{-1}χ_{w̄}^{-1}μ_{i,w} to be trivial on 1 + 𝔭^t, hence the conductor of χ_{w̄} must be bounded; see source issue on (56), which gives a counterexample with n = 2 otherwise. Source issues: sourceIssues E44. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 4.3.2(ii) — factorization and supports of Φ_{2,w}
items.statement: Assume t as in (56) (with the conductor of χ_{w̄} included). For X = (A, B; C, D) with A ∈ M_{a_w×a_w}(𝒦_w), B ∈ M_{a_w×b_w}(𝒦_w), C ∈ M_{b_w×a_w}(𝒦_w), D ∈ M_{b_w×b_w}(𝒦_w): Φ_{2,w}(X) = Φ^{(1)}_w(A) Φ^{(2)}_w(B) Φ^{(3)}_w(C) Φ^{(4)}_w(D), with Φ^{(2)}_w = char_{M_{a_w×b_w}(O_w)}, Φ^{(3)}_w = char_{M_{b_w×a_w}(O_w)}, supp(Φ^{(1)}_w) ⊆ 𝔭_w^{-t}M_{a_w×a_w}(O_w) and supp(Φ^{(4)}_w) ⊆ 𝔭_w^{-t}M_{b_w×b_w}(O_w). Explicitly, with 𝔛^{(1)} = {α ∈ M_{a_w}(O_w) : (α, 0; 0, 1) ∈ 𝔛} and 𝔛^{(4)} = {δ ∈ M_{b_w}(O_w) : (1, 0; 0, δ) ∈ 𝔛}: Φ^{(1)}_w(A) = ∫_{𝔛^{(1)}} φ_{ν_w}((α, 0; 0, 1)) e_w(−tr(ᵗα A)) dα = Vol(M_{a_w×a_w}(𝔭_w^t)) Σ_{x = (α,0;0,1) ∈ 𝔛 mod 𝔭_w^t} φ_{ν_w}(x) e_w(−tr(ᵗα A)) char_{𝔭_w^{-t}M_{a_w×a_w}(O_w)}(A), and Φ^{(4)}_w(D) = ∫_{𝔛^{(4)}} φ_{ν_w}((1, 0; 0, δ)) e_w(−tr(ᵗδ D)) dδ = Vol(M_{b_w×b_w}(𝔭_w^t)) Σ_{x = (1,0;0,δ) ∈ 𝔛 mod 𝔭_w^t} φ_{ν_w}(x) e_w(−tr(ᵗδ D)) char_{𝔭_w^{-t}M_{b_w×b_w}(O_w)}(D).
items.note: Proof as printed: expand Φ_{2,w}(X) = ∫ φ_{ν_w}(Y) e_w(−tr(Y ᵗX)) dY over Y = (α, β; γ, δ) ∈ 𝔛. φ_{ν_w} depends only on (α, δ), and 𝔛 = 𝔛^{(1)} × M(O) × M(O) × 𝔛^{(4)}. The support bounds use invariance of φ under translation by 𝔭^t, which again needs the conductor of χ_{w̄}. The first line of the printed Φ^{(4)} formula has 'e_w(−trace δ^tA)dα' for e_w(−trace ᵗδD)dδ; see source issue. Needs e_w of conductor O_w and self-dual measures. v4 also printed char_{M_{a×b}} for Φ^{(3)}, corrected in v5. Source issues: sourceIssues E44, sourceIssues E45. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.3 — the parabolics B_{a_w}, B_{b_w}, R_{a_w,b_w}, R_w and the Levi L_{a_w,b_w}
items.statement: B_{a_w} ⊆ GL_{a_w} is the standard parabolic for the partition a_w = n_{1,w} + ⋯ + n_{t(w),w}. B_{b_w} ⊆ GL_{b_w} is the standard parabolic for b_w = n_{t(w)+1,w} + ⋯ + n_{r(w),w}. R_{a_w,b_w} ⊆ GL_n is the standard parabolic for n = a_w + b_w, with Levi L_{a_w,b_w} = GL_{a_w} × GL_{b_w}, and R_w ⊂ R_{a_w,b_w} is the parabolic with R_w ∩ L_{a_w,b_w} = B_{a_w} × B_{b_w}^{op}.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.3 — the characters μ′_{i,w}, μ′_{a_w}, μ′_{b_w}, μ′_w, μ′
items.statement: For w ∈ Σ_p define μ′_{i,w} = χ_{2,w}^{-1} μ_{i,w}^{-1} if 1 ≤ i ≤ t(w), and μ′_{i,w} = χ_{1,w}^{-1} μ_{i,w} if t(w)+1 ≤ i ≤ r(w). Let μ′_{a_w} = ⊗_{i=1}^{t(w)} μ′_{i,w}, μ′_{b_w} = ⊗_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)} μ′_{i,w}, μ′_w = ⊗_{i=1}^{r(w)} μ′_{i,w} = μ′_{a_w} ⊗ μ′_{b_w} and μ′ = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} μ′_w, characters (via determinants) of ∏_{i≤t(w)} GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w), ∏_{i>t(w)} GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w), ∏_{i=1}^{r(w)} GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w) and ∏_w ∏_i GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w) respectively.
items.note: Corrected: the paper prints μ′_{a_w} = ⊗_{i=1}^{t(w)} μ_{i,w} (missing prime), which contradicts μ′_w = μ′_{a_w} ⊗ μ′_{b_w}; see source issue. μ′_{i,w} = χ_{w̄}μ_{i,w}^{-1} for i ≤ t(w) involves χ_{w̄}. Source issues: sourceIssues E44, sourceIssues E46. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.3 — the local representations π_{i,w}, π_{a_w}, π_{b_w}, π_w as quotients of induced representations
items.statement: For w ∈ Σ_p and 1 ≤ i ≤ r(w), let τ_{i,w} be an unramified irreducible admissible representation of GL_{n_{i,w}}(𝒦_w), β_{i,w} a character of GL_{n_{i,w}}(𝒦_w) with β_{i,w}|_{GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w)} = μ′_{i,w}, and π_{i,w} = τ_{i,w} ⊗ β_{i,w}. Let Ind_{B_{a_w}}^{GL_{a_w}}(⊗_{i=1}^{t(w)} π_{i,w}) ↠ π_{a_w}, Ind_{B_{b_w}^{op}}^{GL_{b_w}}(⊗_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)} π_{i,w}) ↠ π_{b_w} and Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w}) ↠ π_w be irreducible admissible quotients. By composition π_w is a quotient of Ind_{R_w}^{GL_n}(⊗_{i=1}^{r(w)} π_{i,w}).
items.note: Induction is normalized. Under the paper's right-action identification U_{1,w} ≅ GL_n(𝒦_w) (row vectors), π_w corresponds to the contragredient of π_w under the usual left-action identification. This matters for comparing L-factors; see unramified-zeta. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.3 — contragredients and the pairings ⟨·,·⟩_{a_w}, ⟨·,·⟩_{b_w}, ⟨·,·⟩_w on induced models
items.statement: Let τ̃_{i,w}, β̃_{i,w} be the contragredients of τ_{i,w}, β_{i,w} and π̃_{i,w} = τ̃_{i,w} ⊗ β̃_{i,w} (the contragredient of π_{i,w}); π̃_{a_w}, π̃_{b_w}, π̃_w are the contragredients of π_{a_w}, π_{b_w}, π_w. For w ∈ Σ_p (printed: Σ) and 1 ≤ i ≤ r(w), ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{i,w}} : π_{i,w} × π̃_{i,w} → ℂ is the tautological pairing. Set (·,·)_{a_w} = ⊗_{i=1}^{t(w)} ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{i,w}} and (·,·)_{b_w} = ⊗_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)} ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{i,w}}. Then ⟨φ, φ̃⟩_{a_w} = ∫_{GL_{a_w}(O_w)} (φ(k), φ̃(k))_{a_w} dk on Ind_{B_{a_w}}^{GL_{a_w}}(⊗π_{i,w}) × Ind_{B_{a_w}}^{GL_{a_w}}(⊗π̃_{i,w}), and ⟨φ, φ̃⟩_{b_w} = ∫_{GL_{b_w}(O_w)} (φ(k), φ̃(k))_{b_w} dk on Ind_{B_{b_w}^{op}}^{GL_{b_w}}(⊗π_{i,w}) × Ind_{B_{b_w}^{op}}^{GL_{b_w}}(⊗π̃_{i,w}). These are perfect GL_{a_w}(𝒦_w)- and GL_{b_w}(𝒦_w)-invariant pairings identifying the pairs as contragredients and the pairings with the tautological ones. Dually one gets inclusions π̃_{a_w} ↪ Ind_{B_{a_w}}^{GL_{a_w}}(⊗π̃_{i,w}) and π̃_{b_w} ↪ Ind_{B_{b_w}^{op}}^{GL_{b_w}}(⊗π̃_{i,w}), under which ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{a_w}}, ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{b_w}} are induced from ⟨·,·⟩_{a_w}, ⟨·,·⟩_{b_w}. Likewise (·,·)_w = ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{a_w}} ⊗ ⟨·,·⟩_{π_{b_w}} gives a pairing ⟨·,·⟩_w on Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w}) × Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π̃_{a_w} ⊗ π̃_{b_w}) and an inclusion π̃_w ↪ Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π̃_{a_w} ⊗ π̃_{b_w}) (hence π̃_w ↪ Ind_{R_w}^{GL_n}(⊗π̃_{i,w})), such that ⟨·,·⟩_{π_w} is induced from ⟨·,·⟩_w.
items.note: Standard facts about normalized induction: ∫_K⟨φ(k), φ̃(k)⟩dk is invariant. The Haar measures on GL_m(O_w) are not specified. The volume identity used in (72) needs them normalised to total mass 1. Source issues: sourceIssues E160. Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Jacquet functors and duals.

items.name: (59) — the pairing on π_w computed in the induced model
items.statement: For φ ∈ π_w and φ̃ ∈ π̃_w, let ϕ ∈ Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w}) project to φ, and let ϕ̃ ∈ Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π̃_{a_w} ⊗ π̃_{b_w}) be the image of φ̃. Then ⟨φ, φ̃⟩_{π_w} = ∫_{GL_n(O_w)} ⟨ϕ(k), ϕ̃(k)⟩_w dk.
items.note: Immediate from the construction of the inclusion π̃_w ↪ Ind(π̃_{a_w} ⊗ π̃_{b_w}) dual to the quotient map. Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Jacquet functors and duals.

items.name: §4.3.4, (60) — the level r ≥ 2t and the congruence subgroups Γ_{R,w}, Γ_{a_w,w}, Γ_{b_w,w}, Γ_{a_w,b_w}
items.statement: Let t satisfy (56) and let r ≥ 2t (60). Put Γ_{R,w} = {γ ∈ GL_n(O_w) | γ mod 𝔭_w^r ∈ R_w(O/𝔭_w^r O)}, Γ_R = ∏_{w∈Σ_p} Γ_{R,w}; Γ_{a_w,w} = {γ ∈ GL_{a_w}(O_w) | γ mod 𝔭_w^r ∈ B_{a_w}(O/𝔭_w^r O)}, Γ_a = ∏_w Γ_{a_w,w}; Γ_{b_w,w} = {γ ∈ GL_{b_w}(O_w) | γ mod 𝔭_w^r ∈ B_{b_w}(O/𝔭_w^r O)}, Γ_b = ∏_w Γ_{b_w,w}; Γ_{a_w,b_w} = {γ ∈ GL_n(O_w) | γ mod 𝔭_w^r ∈ R_{a_w,b_w}(O/𝔭_w^r O)}. The character μ′_w extends to a character of both Γ_R and its transpose ᵗΓ_R by μ′_w(γ) = ∏_{i=1}^{r(w)} μ′_{i,w}(det γ_{ii}), where γ = (γ_{ij}) is the block form for n = n_{1,w} + ⋯ + n_{r(w),w}. Similarly μ′_{a_w} (resp. μ′_{b_w}) extends to Γ_{a_w,w} and ᵗΓ_{a_w,w} (resp. Γ_{b_w,w} and ᵗΓ_{b_w,w}), and likewise for μ̃′_w, μ̃′_{a_w}, μ̃′_{b_w}.
items.note: The paper justifies the extension 'by the choice of r'. It needs each μ′_{i,w} to have conductor ≤ 𝔭^r. μ′_{i,w} = χ_{w̄}μ_{i,w}^{-1} for i ≤ t(w), and cond(χ_{w̄}) is not bounded by (56); see source issue on (56). The printed sentence says 'the character μ_w extends' and writes r_w for r(w); μ′_w is meant. μ̃′ is not defined explicitly: μ̃′_{i,w} = (μ′_{i,w})^{-1}, the restriction of β̃_{i,w}. Γ_{a_w,b_w} = GL_n(O_w) ∩ R_{a_w,b_w}(𝒦_w)Γ_{R,w} (used on p. 57): checked. Source issues: sourceIssues E44, sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.4, (61)–(66) — the test vectors φ_{i,w}, φ_{a_w}, φ_{b_w}, φ_w ∈ π_w
items.statement: For w ∈ Σ_p and 1 ≤ i ≤ r(w) let 0 ≠ φ_{i,w} ∈ π_{i,w} satisfy π_{i,w}(k)φ_{i,w} = μ′_{i,w}(k)φ_{i,w} for all k ∈ GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w). Such a vector exists and is unique up to scalars since τ_{i,w} is unramified. Let φ^0_{a_w} = ⊗_{i=1}^{t(w)} φ_{i,w}, φ^0_{b_w} = ⊗_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)} φ_{i,w}. (61) φ_{a_w} ∈ Ind_{B_{a_w}}^{GL_{a_w}}(⊗_{i≤t(w)} π_{i,w}) is the unique function with support B_{a_w}(𝒦_w)Γ_{a_w,w} and φ_{a_w}(γ) = μ′_{a_w}(γ)φ^0_{a_w} for γ ∈ Γ_{a_w,w}. (62) φ_{b_w} ∈ Ind_{B_{b_w}^{op}}^{GL_{b_w}}(⊗_{i>t(w)} π_{i,w}) is the unique function with support B_{b_w}^{op}(𝒦_w)ᵗΓ_{b_w,w} and φ_{b_w}(γ) = μ′_{b_w}(γ)φ^0_{b_w} for γ ∈ ᵗΓ_{b_w,w}. Assumption (63): the images φ_{a_w} ∈ π_{a_w}, φ_{b_w} ∈ π_{b_w} are nonzero. Let φ^0_w = φ_{a_w} ⊗ φ_{b_w} ∈ π_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w}. (64) φ_w ∈ Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w}) is the unique function with support R_{a_w,b_w}(𝒦_w)Γ_{R,w} and φ_w(γ) = μ′_w(γ)φ^0_w for γ ∈ Γ_{R,w}. Assumption (65): the image φ_w ∈ π_w is nonzero. Then (66) π_w(γ)φ_w = μ′_w(γ)φ_w for all γ ∈ Γ_{R,w}.
items.note: these are 𝔛^{(1)}, 𝔛^{(4)} of Lemma 4.3.2 and (85). Consistency checked: on B(𝒦_w) ∩ Γ = B(O_w), the prescription φ(γ) = μ′(γ)φ^0 agrees with left equivariance, because π_{i,w}(k)φ_{i,w} = μ′_{i,w}(k)φ_{i,w}. (66) follows since the support is right Γ_{R,w}-invariant. Remark 8.3.10 says the anti-ordinary vector φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} satisfies (64) and (70) with R_w = B_w and all n_{i,w} = 1 for r large. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.4, (67)–(70) — the dual test vectors φ̃_{i,w}, φ̃_{a_w}, φ̃_{b_w}, φ̃_w ∈ π̃_w
items.statement: Let 0 ≠ φ̃_{i,w} ∈ π̃_{i,w} satisfy π̃_{i,w}(k)φ̃_{i,w} = μ̃′_{i,w}(k)φ̃_{i,w} for k ∈ GL_{n_i}(O_w), and let φ̃^0_{a_w} = ⊗_{i=1}^{t(w)} φ̃_{i,w}, φ̃^0_{b_w} = ⊗_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)} φ̃_{i,w}. Suppose φ̃_{a_w} ∈ π̃_{a_w}, φ̃_{b_w} ∈ π̃_{b_w}, φ̃_w ∈ π̃_w satisfy: (67) the image ϕ̃_{a_w} of φ̃_{a_w} in Ind_{B_{a_w}}^{GL_{a_w}}(⊗_{i≤t(w)} π̃_{i,w}) has ϕ̃_{a_w}(1) = φ̃^0_{a_w}, and the image ϕ̃_{b_w} of φ̃_{b_w} in Ind_{B_{b_w}^{op}}^{GL_{b_w}}(⊗_{i>t(w)} π̃_{i,w}) has ϕ̃_{b_w}(1) = φ̃^0_{b_w}; (68) the image ϕ̃_w of φ̃_w in Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π̃_{a_w} ⊗ π̃_{b_w}) has ϕ̃_w(1) = φ̃_{a_w} ⊗ φ̃_{b_w}; (69) π̃_w(γ)φ̃_w = μ̃′_w(γ)φ̃_w for all γ ∈ ᵗΓ_{R,w}. Consequence (70): the support of ϕ̃_w contains R_{a_w,b_w}(𝒦_w)ᵗΓ_{R,w}.
items.note: (70) follows from (68) and (69): ϕ̃_w(γ) = μ̃′_w(γ)ϕ̃_w(1) ≠ 0 for γ ∈ ᵗΓ_{R,w}, then left R-equivariance. The paper says that (64) and (70) correspond to Remark 4.1.5(i), and (60) to Remark 4.1.5(ii). From (69) with γ = diag(γ_a, 1) one gets π̃_{a_w}(γ_a)φ̃_{a_w} = μ̃′_{a_w}(γ_a)φ̃_{a_w} for γ_a ∈ ᵗΓ_{a_w,w}, which the 'similar considerations' before (72) need. Existence of such vectors is not asserted here; it is supplied by Remark 8.4.8. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (71) — ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ in terms of the a- and b-parts
items.statement: ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} = Vol(Γ_{a_w,b_w}) · ⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}} · ⟨φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩_{π_{b_w}}, where the volume is taken with respect to the chosen Haar measure on GL_n(O_w).
items.note: Proof: by (59) and the support (64), the integrand vanishes off Γ_{a_w,b_w} = GL_n(O_w) ∩ R_{a_w,b_w}(𝒦_w)Γ_{R,w}. Each k ∈ Γ_{a_w,b_w} is k = (1, B; 0, 1)(A, 0; 0, D)(1, 0; C, 1) with B ∈ M_{a×b}(O_w), A ∈ GL_a(O_w), D ∈ GL_b(O_w) and C ∈ M_{b×a}(𝔭_w^r). The paper prints 𝔭_w^t; see source issue. Then ϕ_w(k) = π_{a_w}(A)φ_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w}(D)φ_{b_w} and ϕ̃_w(k) = π̃_{a_w}(A)φ̃_{a_w} ⊗ π̃_{b_w}(D)φ̃_{b_w}, so the integrand is constant. All steps checked. Source issues: sourceIssues E49. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (72) — ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ = Vol(Γ_{R,w}) ∏_i ⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩ ≠ 0
items.statement: ⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}} = Vol(Γ_{a_w,w}) ∏_{i=1}^{t(w)} ⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩_{π_{i,w}} and ⟨φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩_{π_{b_w}} = Vol(Γ_{b_w,w}) ∏_{i=t(w)+1}^{r(w)} ⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩_{π_{i,w}}. Since Vol(Γ_{R,w}) = Vol(Γ_{a_w,b_w}) Vol(Γ_{a_w,w}) Vol(Γ_{b_w,w}), it follows that (72) ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} = Vol(Γ_{R,w}) ∏_{i=1}^{r(w)} ⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩_{π_{i,w}} ≠ 0, each ⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩ being nonzero by the choice of φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}. [Printed: the product in (72) runs over i = 1, …, t(w).]
items.note: Corrected upper limit r(w); see source issue. The volume identity holds with Haar measures on GL_n(O_w), GL_{a_w}(O_w), GL_{b_w}(O_w) of total mass 1: [GL_n(O):Γ_R] = [GL_n(O):Γ_{a,b}][GL_a(O):Γ_a][GL_b(O):Γ_b]. The paper does not state this normalisation. The nonvanishing of ⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩ uses μ̃′_{i,w} = (μ′_{i,w})^{-1}, so that the μ′- and μ̃′-isotypic lines are dual. The b-part uses ᵗΓ_{b_w,w}, of the same volume as Γ_{b_w,w}. Source issues: sourceIssues E47. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 4.3.5 — the natural test vectors φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} satisfy the conditions of §4.3.4
items.statement: In §§8.3 and 8.4 specific vectors φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} and φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} in local constituents of the global representations of interest are shown to satisfy the conditions imposed in §4.3.4 (see Remarks 8.3.10 and 8.4.8; printed 'Remarks 4.3.5 and 8.4.8'). They are the natural choices from the viewpoint of Hida theory and (anti-)ordinary forms, so the main result of §4.3.6 shows that the local zeta integral for them contributes a factor at p of the expected form for a p-adic L-function.
items.note: Forward pointer. Remark 8.3.10 (p. ~135) states that φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} satisfies (64) and (70) with R_w = B_w and n_{i,w} = 1 for r ≫ 0; Remark 8.4.8 does the same for φ^{♭,a-ord}. The self-reference 'Remarks 4.3.5' is a misprint (v4: 'Remarks 4.3.5 and 8.3.8'). Source issues: sourceIssues E48, sourceIssues E160. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.6 — the V_w ⊕ V_w coordinates and the translated section f̃_{w+}
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p, (a_w, b_w) the signature at w, n = a_w + b_w. The ordered K_w-basis of V_w coming from the level structure for P_1 gives a K_w-basis of W_w = V_w ⊕ V_w; it identifies GL_{K_w}(W_w) with GL_{2n}(K_w) and GL_{K_w}(V_w) × GL_{K_w}(V_w) ⊆ GL_{K_w}(V_w ⊕ V_w) with the block-diagonal subgroup GL_n(K_w) × GL_n(K_w) ⊆ GL_{2n}(K_w). This differs from the identification coming from W_w = V_{d,w} ⊕ V^d_w; in the new coordinates the set 𝐗 = {X ∈ Hom_{K_w}(V_w, W_w) : X(V_w) = V^d_w} consists of the elements (X, X), X ∈ GL_n(K_w) (because V^d = {(x, x)}). In the zeta-integral computation the Siegel section f_w^{χ,μ} of (58) is replaced by its right translate f̃_{w+}(g) := f_w^{χ,μ}(g · γ_{V_w}), where γ_{V_w} is the matrix of (73), written in the V_w ⊕ V_w basis with block sizes (a_w, b_w, a_w, b_w): γ_{V_w} = [[1_{a_w},0,0,0],[0,0,0,1_{b_w}],[0,0,1_{a_w},0],[0,1_{b_w},0,0]] (the translation of Remark 3.1.4). Writing Z_1 = Xg = [Z_1', Z_1''], Z_2 = X = [Z_2', Z_2''] with Z_i' ∈ M_{n×a_w}(K_w), Z_i'' ∈ M_{n×b_w}(K_w), one has (Z_1, Z_2)·γ_{V_w} = ([Z_1', Z_2''], [Z_2', Z_1'']), and the paper evaluates Φ = Φ_{χ,μ,w} there as vol(Γ_w)^{-1} Φ_{1,w}(Z_1', Z_2'') Φ_{2,w}(Z_2', Z_1''), i.e. it uses the Schwartz function Φ'(Y_1, Y_2) = vol(Γ_w)^{-1}Φ_{1,w}(Y_1)Φ_{2,w}(Y_2) in the V_w ⊕ V_w coordinates.
items.note: The identification 𝐗 = {(X,X)} is correct since V^d = {(x,x)}, V_d = {(x,−x)} (§4.1.1, p. 42). The paper does not convert Φ_{χ,μ,w}, defined in §4.3.1 relative to W_w = V_{d,w} ⊕ V^d_w as vol(Γ_w)^{-1}Φ_{1,w}(−X_1)Φ_{2,w}(2X_2), to the new coordinates; in V_w ⊕ V_w coordinates that function is vol(Γ_w)^{-1}Φ_{1,w}((Y_2 − Y_1)/2)Φ_{2,w}(Y_1 + Y_2), not a product. The function Φ' actually used gives the section g ↦ χ_{2,w}((−1)^n) f_w^{χ,μ}(g·γ_{V_w}·h) with h ∈ GL(W_w) having matrix M·diag(−1_n, ½·1_n) in the V_{d,w} ⊕ V^d_w basis (M = [[1_n, −1_n],[1_n, 1_n]] the change of basis). See sourceIssues E52. Printed misprint 'GL_n(V_w) × GL_n(K_w)' for GL_n(K_w) × GL_n(K_w) (sourceIssues E50). The switch of decompositions is attributed to the usual doubling-method practice [GPSR87]. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.6 — the local zeta integral Z_w at w | p and Z_p
items.statement:
Let w ∈ Σ_p and identify K_w = K^+_{w+}, so π_w, π̃_w become representations π_{w+}, π̃_{w+} of U_{1,w+} ≅ GL_n(K_w), and φ_w ∈ π_w, φ̃_w ∈ π̃_w (the vectors of §4.3.4, (61)–(69)) become φ_{w+}, φ̃_{w+}. The local zeta integral Z_{w+}(φ_{w+}, φ̃_{w+}, f̃_{w+}, s) — the numerator of the local factor I_{w+} = Z_{w+}/⟨φ_{w+}, φ̃_{w+}⟩ of (51) — is
Z_w := ∫_{GL_n(K_w)} χ_{2,w}(det g) |det g|_w^{s + n/2} ∫_{GL_n(K_w)} Φ((Xg, X)·γ_{V_w}) χ_{1,w}^{-1}χ_{2,w}(det X) |det X|_w^{2s+n} ⟨π_w(g)φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} d^×X d^×g,
where χ_{1,w} = χ_w, χ_{2,w} = χ_{w̄}^{-1}, Φ = Φ_{χ,μ,w} read as in §4.3.6 (see sec-4-3-6-coordinates) and γ_{V_w} is (73). Put Z_p := ∏_{w∈Σ_p} Z_w.
items.note: Obtained from (55) with g ↦ (g, 1)·γ_{V_w}: (X, X)·(g, 1) = (Xg, X). Printed 'χ_{2,w}(g)' means χ_{2,w}(det g); the factor χ_{2,w}(det γ_{V_w}) = χ_{2,w}(−1)^{b_w} (det γ_{V_w} = (−1)^{b_w}, a permutation matrix exchanging b_w pairs of coordinates) coming from (55) is dropped; Z_p is printed as ∏ Z_{w+}(φ_{w+}, φ̃_{w+}, f_{w+}, χ) (f for f̃, χ for s). See sourceIssues E52, sourceIssues E51. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (74) — Z_w as an integral over GL_n(K_w) × GL_n(K_w)
items.note: Checked: substitute g = X^{-1}Z_1; χ_{2,w}(det g)χ_{1,w}^{-1}χ_{2,w}(det X) = χ_{2,w}(det Z_1)χ_{1,w}^{-1}(det Z_2); |det g|^{s+n/2}|det X|^{2s+n} = |det Z_1Z_2|^{s+n/2}; ⟨π_w(g)φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ = ⟨π_w(Z_1)φ_w, π̃_w(Z_2)φ̃_w⟩ by invariance of the pairing; d^×g d^×X = d^×Z_1 d^×Z_2. The paper writes the evaluation as 'Φ((Xg, X)) = …', omitting γ_{V_w}. The evaluation of Φ itself is the questionable step (sourceIssues E52). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.6 — block LDU coordinates on GL_n and the formulas (75), (76)
items.statement:
Let n = a + b. Off a null set, every Z_1 ∈ GL_n(K_w) is uniquely Z_1 = (1 0; C_1 1)(A_1 0; 0 D_1)(1 B_1; 0 1) and every Z_2 ∈ GL_n(K_w) is uniquely Z_2 = (1 B_2; 0 1)(A_2 0; 0 D_2)(1 0; C_2 1), with A_i ∈ GL_a(K_w), D_i ∈ GL_b(K_w), C_i, ᵗB_i ∈ M_{b×a}(K_w); if d^×g = dg/|det g|_w^m on GL_m(K_w) (dg an additive Haar measure) then d^×Z_1 = |det A_1^{b} det D_1^{−a}|_w dC_1 d^×A_1 d^×D_1 dB_1 and d^×Z_2 = |det A_2^{−b} det D_2^{a}|_w dC_2 d^×A_2 d^×D_2 dB_2. In these coordinates Z_1' = (A_1; C_1A_1), Z_1'' = (A_1B_1; C_1A_1B_1 + D_1), Z_2' = (A_2 + B_2D_2C_2; D_2C_2), Z_2'' = (B_2D_2; D_2), so
(75) Φ_{1,w}(Z_1', Z_2'') = Φ_{1,w}((A_1, B_2D_2; C_1A_1, D_2)),
(76) Φ_{2,w}(Z_2', Z_1'') = Φ_{2,w}((A_2 + B_2D_2C_2, A_1B_1; D_2C_2, C_1A_1B_1 + D_1)).
items.note: Verified: the maps (A,B,C,D) ↦ (A, AB; CA, CAB + D) and (A,B,C,D) ↦ (A + BDC, BD; DC, D) have Jacobians |det A|^{2b} and |det D|^{2a}; dividing by |det|^n gives the stated densities. The paper does not fix Haar measures at p; these decompositions tie the measures on GL_n, GL_a, GL_b together and hold for the normalization d^×g = dg/|det g|^m with the same additive normalization (vol M_m(O_w) = 1, forced by Φ^{(2)}_w = char_{M(O_w)} in Lemma 4.3.2). General linear algebra; used for any doubling computation of this type. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.7 (support part) — support of Φ_{1,w}·Φ_{2,w} in the LDU coordinates
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p, t as in (56), Φ_{1,w} (supported on Γ_w(t), equal to μ_w there) and Φ_{2,w} = φ̂_{ν_w} as in §4.3.1, and Z_1, Z_2 in the coordinates of (75), (76). The product Φ_{1,w}((A_1, B_2D_2; C_1A_1, D_2)) · Φ_{2,w}((A_2 + B_2D_2C_2, A_1B_1; D_2C_2, C_1A_1B_1 + D_1)) is zero unless all of the following hold: A_1 ∈ Γ_{a_w,w}(t); C_1 ∈ p_w^t M_{b_w×a_w}(O_w); D_2 ∈ Γ_{b_w,w}(t); B_2 ∈ p_w^t M_{a_w×b_w}(O_w); C_2 ∈ M_{b_w×a_w}(O_w); A_2 ∈ p_w^{−t} M_{a_w×a_w}(O_w); B_1 ∈ M_{a_w×b_w}(O_w); D_1 ∈ p_w^{−t} M_{b_w×b_w}(O_w). Here Γ_{a_w,w}(t) (resp. Γ_{b_w,w}(t)) denotes the matrices in GL_{a_w}(O_w) (resp. GL_{b_w}(O_w)) whose entries below the diagonal n_{i,w}×n_{i,w} blocks lie in p_w^t. When these conditions hold the product equals μ_{a_w}(A_1)μ_{b_w}(D_2)Φ^{(1)}_w(A_2)Φ^{(4)}_w(D_1).
items.note: Proof in the paper: Lemma 4.3.2 and the definition of Φ_{1,w}. Checked: membership in Γ_w(t) forces A_1, D_2 invertible over O_w with the stated block conditions and C_1A_1, B_2D_2 ∈ p^t; Lemma 4.3.2(ii) gives A_1B_1, D_2C_2 integral and A_2 + B_2D_2C_2, C_1A_1B_1 + D_1 ∈ p^{−t}; the final value statement (implicit in the paper, explicit in Marcil 2023, Lemma 4.1) uses that Φ^{(1)}_w, Φ^{(4)}_w are invariant under translation by integral matrices (φ_{ν_w} is supported on M_n(O_w)). The notation Γ_{a_w,w}(t) is not defined in the paper (§4.3.4 defines Γ_{a_w,w} at level p^r). The displayed product in the statement overflows the right margin of p. 60 (closing brackets lost). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 4.3.7 (factorization part) — the identity (77) with J_1, J_2
items.statement:
Assume the support conditions of Proposition 4.3.7 and in addition (needed for the proof; see note) A_1 ∈ Γ_{a_w,w}, D_2 ∈ Γ_{b_w,w} (level p^r, §4.3.4) and B_2C_1 ∈ p_w^r M_{a_w}(O_w), C_1B_2 ∈ p_w^r M_{b_w}(O_w) (automatic when r = 2t). Then
(77) Φ_{1,w}(Z_1', Z_2'') Φ_{2,w}(Z_2', Z_1'') ⟨π_w(Z_1)φ_w, π̃_w(Z_2)φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} = Vol(Γ_{a_w,b_w}) · J_1 · J_2, where
(78) J_1 = χ_{2,w}(det A_1)^{−1} Φ^{(4)}_w(D_1) |det D_1^{a_w}|_w^{1/2} ⟨φ_{b_w}, π̃_{b_w}(D_1^{−1})φ̃_{b_w}⟩_{π_{b_w}},
(79) J_2 = χ_{1,w}(det D_2) Φ^{(1)}_w(A_2) |det A_2^{b_w}|_w^{1/2} ⟨φ_{a_w}, π̃_{a_w}(A_2)φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}}.
items.note: Printed: (77) is asserted 'when all of the above conditions are met', i.e. for A_1 ∈ Γ_{a_w,w}(t), D_2 ∈ Γ_{b_w,w}(t), B_2, C_1 ∈ p^t. The proof uses (66) for diag(A_1,1)(1 B_1; 0 1) and (69) for diag(1,D_2)(1 0; C_2 1), valid only at level p^r, and on p. 61 replaces (1 0; C 1)(A 0; 0 D) by (1 0; C_1 1)(1 0; 0 D_1) with A = 1 − B_2C_1 ∈ 1 + p^{2t}M, D = (1 + CB_2)D_1, which needs these to lie in Γ(r), i.e. r ≤ 2t, while (60) assumes r ≥ 2t (used in levi-coefficient-factorization). So the printed proof covers only r = 2t (and A_1, D_2 of level r). See sourceIssues E53; the integrated identity (Corollary 4.3.8) still holds. The displayed intermediate step on p. 60 omits Φ^{(1)}_w(A_2)Φ^{(4)}_w(D_1) (sourceIssues E54). Marcil 2023 (Lemma 4.2, Proposition 4.3) takes Φ_{1,w} of level p^r, which avoids the problem. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.6 — matrix coefficient of φ_w, φ̃_w at a Levi element
items.note: Proof (checked): by (59), ⟨φ_w, π̃_w(m)φ̃_w⟩ = ∫_{GL_n(O_w)} ⟨φ_w(k), φ̃_w(km)⟩ dk; supp φ_w ∩ GL_n(O_w) = Γ_{a_w,b_w}; for k = (1 B; 0 1)diag(A, D)(1 0; C 1) with C ∈ p^r one has (1 0; C 1)m = m(1 0; D_1CA_2 1) with D_1CA_2 ∈ p^{r−2t} ⊂ O_w — the only place where r ≥ 2t is used — so φ̃_w(km) = δ_{R_{a,b}}^{1/2}(m)(π̃_{a_w}(AA_2) ⊗ π̃_{b_w}(DD_1^{−1}))φ̃_w(1), with δ^{1/2}(m) = |det A_2|^{b_w/2}|det D_1|^{a_w/2}, and φ_w(1) = φ_{a_w} ⊗ φ_{b_w}, φ̃_w(1) = φ̃_{a_w} ⊗ φ̃_{b_w} ((64), (68)). The paper's remark 'since r ≥ 2t, A_2 ∈ p^{−⌊r/2⌋}M…, D_1 ∈ p^{−⌊r/2⌋}M…' serves this step. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 4.3.8 — factorization of Z_w into two Godement–Jacquet-type integrals
items.statement:
Z_w = Vol(Γ_{a_w,b_w}) · I_1 · I_2, where
I_1 = ∫_{GL_{b_w}(K_w)} χ_{2,w}(det D) Φ^{(4)}_w(D) |det D|_w^{s + b_w/2} ⟨π_{b_w}(D)φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩_{π_{b_w}} d^×D,
I_2 = ∫_{GL_{a_w}(K_w)} χ_{1,w}^{−1}(det A) Φ^{(1)}_w(A) |det A|_w^{s + a_w/2} ⟨φ_{a_w}, π̃_{a_w}(A)φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}} d^×A,
with Haar measures d^×g = dg/|det g|^m (vol M_m(O_w) = 1) on GL_n, GL_{a_w}, GL_{b_w}, Z_w as in zeta-integral-z-w (for the section described in sec-4-3-6-coordinates).
items.note: Proof: (74), Proposition 4.3.7 and (82). Checked: the integrand of (82) equals χ_{2,w}(det D_1)Φ^{(4)}(D_1)⟨π_{b_w}(D_1)φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩|det D_1|^{s+b/2} × χ_{1,w}^{−1}(det A_2)Φ^{(1)}(A_2)⟨φ_{a_w}, π̃_{a_w}(A_2)φ̃_{a_w}⟩|det A_2|^{s+a/2} (exponents s + n/2 − a + a/2 = s + b/2 and s + n/2 − b + b/2 = s + a/2); the (A_1, C_1, B_2, D_2)-integral is Vol(Γ_w(t)) (the map to (A_1, B_2D_2; C_1A_1, D_2) has Jacobian 1), cancelling vol(Γ_w)^{-1}, and B_1, C_2 give Vol(M(O_w))² = 1. For r > 2t the printed proof applies (77) outside its range (sourceIssues E53); the identity still holds: A_1 = u·a_1, u ∈ N^-(p^t), a_1 ∈ Γ_{a_w,w}, is absorbed by the measure-preserving change of variables (C_1, A_2, B_2) ↦ (C_1u, u^{−1}A_2, u^{−1}B_2) (Φ^{(1)} is invariant under A ↦ u^{−1}A by Lemma 4.3.2(i)), and similarly for D_2; the residual factors in 1 + p^{2t}M are invisible after the Godement–Jacquet functional equation, because A ↦ ⟨π_{a_w}(A)φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩ on 𝔛^{(1)} (and D ↦ ⟨φ_{b_w}, π̃_{b_w}(D)φ̃_{b_w}⟩ on 𝔛^{(4)}) is invariant under right multiplication by 1 + p^{2t}M. The proof on p. 63 prints spurious products ∏_{w|p} and 'Γ_{a_w}(t)' (sourceIssues E55). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The Godement–Jacquet local functional equation (as cited, [Jac79, (1.1.3), (1.3.7)])
items.statement:
Let F be a non-archimedean local field, ψ a non-trivial additive character of F, (Π, V) an irreducible admissible representation of GL_m(F) with contragredient Π̃, f(g) = ⟨Π(g)v, ṽ⟩ a matrix coefficient and f̌(g) = f(g^{−1}). For Φ ∈ S(M_m(F)) put Z(Φ, s, f) = ∫_{GL_m(F)} Φ(g) f(g) |det g|^s d^×g and Φ̂(x) = ∫_{M_m(F)} Φ(y) ψ(tr(yx)) dy with dy self-dual for (x, y) ↦ ψ(tr(xy)). Then Z(Φ, s + (m−1)/2, f) converges for Re s ≫ 0, continues meromorphically, Z(Φ, s + (m−1)/2, f)/L(s, Π) is entire, and
Z(Φ̂, 1 − s + (m−1)/2, f̌) = γ(s, Π, ψ) Z(Φ, s + (m−1)/2, f), γ(s, Π, ψ) = ε(s, Π, ψ) L(1 − s, Π̃)/L(s, Π).
items.note: Cited, not proved; stated here in the standard form of Godement–Jacquet (LNM 260, Thm 3.3) and Jacquet's Corvallis article — I could not consult [Jac79] to confirm its equation numbering. Applied to I_1 with Π = π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}, m = b_w, s ↦ s + 1/2, f(D) = χ_{2,w}(det D)⟨π_{b_w}(D)φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩: this gives (84) exactly (1 − (s + 1/2) + (b_w − 1)/2 = −s + b_w/2, f̌(D) = χ_{2,w}^{−1}(det D)⟨φ_{b_w}, π̃_{b_w}(D)φ̃_{b_w}⟩). For I_2 the matrix coefficient A ↦ ⟨φ_{a_w}, π̃_{a_w}(A)φ̃_{a_w}⟩χ_{1,w}^{−1}(det A) is one of Π = π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}. The Fourier transform in [Jac79] is ∫Φ(y)ψ(tr(yx))dy, whereas EHLS's Φ_{2,w} uses ∫φ(y)e_w(−tr(ᵗy x))dy; the two compose to φ(ᵗx) for ψ = e_w — see eq-85. Planned: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 plans the Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals, factors and local functional equation for GL_n.

items.name: ε(s, Π, ψ) ε(1 − s, Π̃, ψ) = ω_Π(−1)
items.statement: For an irreducible admissible representation Π of GL_m(F) (F non-archimedean) with central quasi-character ω_Π and a non-trivial additive character ψ, ε(s, Π, ψ) ε(1 − s, Π̃, ψ) = ω_Π(−1).
items.note: Standard consequence of applying the Godement–Jacquet functional equation twice; the paper uses it without reference in Remark 4.3.11, with ω_Π taken to be the central character of π_{a_w} although Π = π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w} there (sourceIssues E59). Planned: AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 plans the Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals, factors and local functional equation for GL_n.

items.name: Equation (85) — Fourier inversion for Φ^{(4)}_w and Φ^{(1)}_w; the sets 𝔛^{(1)}, 𝔛^{(4)}
items.statement: Let ^ denote the Godement–Jacquet Fourier transform Φ ↦ ∫Φ(y)e_w(tr(yx))dy on M_{b_w}(K_w) (resp. M_{a_w}(K_w)) with self-dual measure (vol M(O_w) = 1). Then (Φ^{(4)}_w)^∧(D) = φ_{ν_w}(diag(1_{a_w}, D)) (85), and (Φ^{(1)}_w)^∧(A) = φ_{ν_w}(diag(A, 1_{b_w})). In particular (Φ^{(4)}_w)^∧ is supported on 𝔛^{(4)} = ᵗΓ_{b_w,w}Γ_{b_w,w} = {δ ∈ M_{b_w}(O_w) : the leading principal (n_{t(w)+1,w} + ⋯ + n_{i,w})-minors of δ are units, t(w) < i ≤ r(w)}, and (Φ^{(1)}_w)^∧ on 𝔛^{(1)} = ᵗΓ_{a_w,w}Γ_{a_w,w} (the analogous set in M_{a_w}(O_w)); both sets are independent of r and t.
items.note: Paper: 'From its definition'. Checked: Φ^{(4)}_w = F(δ ↦ φ_{ν_w}(diag(1, δ))) with F(φ)(x) = ∫φ(y)e_w(−tr(ᵗy x))dy (Lemma 4.3.2), and (F_GJ∘F)(φ)(x) = φ(ᵗx) for ψ = e_w (the minus sign in F cancels the plus sign in F_GJ; the transpose comes from tr(ᵗy x) versus tr(yx)). Since φ_{ν_w} is a function of leading principal minors of the diagonal blocks, φ_{ν_w}(diag(1, ᵗD)) = φ_{ν_w}(diag(1, D)), so (85) holds as printed. With ψ = e_w^{−1} one would get φ_{ν_w}(−ᵗD) = ∏_{i>t(w)}ν_{i,w}(−1)^{n_{i,w}}φ_{ν_w}(diag(1,D)) instead. 𝔛^{(4)} = ᵗΓ_bΓ_b is the Iwahori factorization of the big cell N^-(O)L(O)N(O). This needs e_w trivial exactly on O_w (true for K_w/Q_p unramified); e_w is not defined in this part of the paper. This is the check requested in the Marcil lead: harmless (see readingNotes). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.3.9 — the matrix coefficients of φ_{b_w}, φ_{a_w} on 𝔛^{(4)}, 𝔛^{(1)}
items.note: Uses (62) (φ_{b_w} is μ'_{b_w}-equivariant under ᵗΓ_{b_w,w}), (69) with ᵗΓ_{R,w} ∩ GL_{b_w} = Γ_{b_w,w} (φ̃_{b_w} is μ̃'_{b_w} = μ'^{−1}_{b_w}-equivariant), (61), Lemma 4.3.2(i) and μ'_{i,w} = χ_{1,w}^{−1}μ_{i,w} (i > t(w)), χ_{2,w}^{−1}μ_{i,w}^{−1} (i ≤ t(w)). Printed with 'μ_{b_w}(γ_2^{−1})' for μ'_{b_w}(γ_2^{−1}) and 'χ_{2,w}(D)' for χ_{2,w}(det D) (sourceIssues E56). The a-part is not written in the paper; I derived it (note the order of the factors differs from the b-part: after the functional equation the a-side coefficient is ⟨π_{a_w}(A)φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩, which is what matches 𝔛^{(1)} = ᵗΓ_aΓ_a). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.10 (I_1) — the b-part as a ratio of L- and ε-factors
items.statement:
With ε-factors taken with respect to ψ = e_w (the additive character for which (85) holds) and L, ε the Godement–Jacquet factors of GL_{b_w}(K_w) (twists by χ_{2,w}∘det):
I_1 = L(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) / [ε(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{−1})] · Vol(𝔛^{(4)}) · ⟨φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩_{π_{b_w}}.
items.note: Proof: the functional equation (godement-jacquet) turns I_1 into (84); by eq-85 and matrix-coefficient-big-cell the dual integrand equals ⟨φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩ on 𝔛^{(4)} (where |det D| = 1) and vanishes off it. Checked; correct as printed for ψ = e_w. The paper leaves ψ implicit. Toy check (n = b_w = 1, unramified): I_1 = L(s + 1/2, π)/L(1/2 − s, π^{−1}). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.10 (I_2) — the a-part (corrected by a sign)
items.statement:
With ψ = e_w as in thm-4-3-10-a and ω the central character of π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w} (so ω(−1) = ω_{π_{a_w}}(−1)χ_{1,w}(−1)^{a_w} ∈ {±1}):
I_2 = L(s + 1/2, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) / [ε(s + 1/2, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})] · Vol(𝔛^{(1)}) · ⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}}
= ω(−1) · ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) / L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) · Vol(𝔛^{(1)}) · ⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}}.
The printed formula is the second expression without the factor ω(−1).
items.locator: arXiv:1602.01776v5, §4.3.9, Theorem 4.3.10, p. 64 ('The computation of I_2 is similar', p. 65)
items.note: I_2 is a Godement–Jacquet integral for Π = π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1} at s + 1/2; the functional equation gives γ(s + 1/2, Π, ψ)^{−1} times ∫(Φ^{(1)}_w)^∧(A)|det A|^{−s+a/2}χ_{1,w}(det A)⟨π_{a_w}(A)φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩d^×A = Vol(𝔛^{(1)})⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩ (eq-85, matrix-coefficient-big-cell). Rewriting 1/ε(s + 1/2, Π) = ω_Π(−1)ε(1/2 − s, Π̃) (epsilon-factor-duality) produces the sign. Tate-integral check (n = a_w = 1): I_2 = Z(Φ^{(1)}, (πχ_{1})^{−1}, s + 1/2) and Z(Φ̂^{(1)}, πχ_1, 1/2 − s) = Vol(O_w^×) with no sign, so the printed I_2 is off by (πχ_1)(−1). With ψ = e_w^{−1} instead, I_2 would be right and I_1 off by ω_{π_{b_w}⊗χ_{2,w}}(−1). See sourceIssues E57. Marcil 2023, Theorem 4.5, reproduces the printed form. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 4.3.10 — the main local theorem at p: Z_w and I_w (83)
items.statement:
Let 𝔙_w := Vol(𝔛^{(1)})Vol(𝔛^{(4)}) and let L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) be the ratio defined in local-l-eps-factors (the ratio printed in the formula for Z_w). Then (with ψ = e_w, and for the section of sec-4-3-6-coordinates)
Z_w = Vol(Γ_{a_w,b_w}) I_1 I_2 = ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) · L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) · 𝔙_w · ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w},
and hence (83) I_w = Z_w/⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} = ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) · L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) · 𝔙_w.
items.note: Exact printed statement: 'Theorem 4.3.10. The integrals I_1 and I_2 are related to familiar L-functions as follows. I_1 = L(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) / [ε(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{−1})] · Vol(𝔛^{(4)}) · ⟨φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩_{π_{b_w}}; I_2 = ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) / L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) · Vol(𝔛^{(1)}) · ⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩_{π_{a_w}}. Consequently, upon setting 𝔙_w := Vol(𝔛^{(1)})Vol(𝔛^{(4)}), Z_w = [L(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) · ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1})] / [ε(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{−1}) · L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})] · 𝔙_w · ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}, and thus I_w = L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) · 𝔙_w · ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}, (83) where L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) is the ratio of L-factors and ε-factors that appear in the formula for Z_w.' Corrections: (i) the sign ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) from thm-4-3-10-b (sourceIssues E57); (ii) (83) has an extra factor ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}: by (51) I_w = Z_w/⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩, and the proof itself says the consequence follows 'from Corollary 4.3.8 and Equations (71) and (51)' (sourceIssues E58). Z_w uses Corollary 4.3.8 and (71): ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ = Vol(Γ_{a_w,b_w})⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩⟨φ_{b_w}, φ̃_{b_w}⟩. The whole theorem concerns the section discussed in sourceIssues E52. Proof of I_1, I_2: [Jac79] functional equation. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The local factor L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) at w | p
items.statement:
For w ∈ Σ_p, with π_{a_w}, π_{b_w} the irreducible admissible representations of GL_{a_w}(K_w), GL_{b_w}(K_w) of §4.3.3 (π_w an irreducible quotient of Ind_{R_{a_w,b_w}}^{GL_n}(π_{a_w} ⊗ π_{b_w})), χ_{1,w} = χ_w, χ_{2,w} = χ_{w̄}^{−1}, and L, ε the Godement–Jacquet factors (ψ = e_w):
L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) := L(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) · ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) / [ε(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{−1}) · L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})],
'the ratio of L-factors and ε-factors that appear in the formula for Z_w'.
items.note: Defined by the theorem itself. By Remark 4.3.11 this equals ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) · [L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1})/(ε(s + 1/2, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}))] · [L(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w})/(ε(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{−1}))]; the true zeta integral is 𝔙_w times the bracketed product without the sign (sourceIssues E57). The shape is that of the modified Euler factor of [Coa89, §2, (18b)] (Remark 4.3.11). A formalisation needs the Godement–Jacquet L- and ε-factors of GL_m over a p-adic field with a fixed ψ and self-dual measures. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.2 plans the Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals, factors and local functional equation for GL_n.

items.name: The volume factor 𝔙_w
items.statement: 𝔙_w := Vol(𝔛^{(1)}) Vol(𝔛^{(4)}), where 𝔛^{(1)} = ᵗΓ_{a_w,w}Γ_{a_w,w} ⊂ GL_{a_w}(O_w), 𝔛^{(4)} = ᵗΓ_{b_w,w}Γ_{b_w,w} ⊂ GL_{b_w}(O_w) (eq-85) and the volumes are taken for the Haar measures d^×A, d^×D of Corollary 4.3.8.
items.note: Independent of r and t. With d^×g = dg/|det g|^m (vol M_m(O_w) = 1) one has 𝔙_w = ∏_{i=1}^{r(w)} vol_{add}(GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w)) = ∏_i ∏_{k=1}^{n_{i,w}}(1 − q_w^{−k}); this is the normalization under which (87) holds. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 4.3.11 — rewriting ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}); the Euler factor at p (86)
items.statement: Let ω denote the central quasi-character of π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w} (printed: of π_{a_w}). Then ε(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}) = ω(−1)/ε(s + 1/2, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}), so L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) = ω(−1) · L(1/2 + s, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) / [ε(s + 1/2, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}^{−1}) L(−s + 1/2, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})] · L(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) / [ε(s + 1/2, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(−s + 1/2, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}^{−1})], and ∏_{w|p} L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) equals the product (86) of these expressions over w | p. The true local integral is I_w/𝔙_w = [the same expression without ω(−1)] (see thm-4-3-10-b).
items.note: The ε-identity is epsilon-factor-duality with Π = π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w}; its central character is ω_{π_{a_w}} χ_{1,w}^{a_w}, not ω_{π_{a_w}} (sourceIssues E59). The paper's 'I_w/𝔙 = …' (without ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩) agrees with the corrected (83), not with the printed one (sourceIssues E58), and its rewritten I_2 omits the factor ⟨φ_{a_w}, φ̃_{a_w}⟩. The remark also compares (86) with the modified Euler factor of [Coa89, §2, (18b)] (no proof). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 4.3.12 — the volume identity (87)
items.statement:
With Haar measures d^×g = dg/|det g|^m (vol M_m(O_w) = 1) on GL_n, GL_{a_w}, GL_{b_w}: for every r ≥ 1,
(87) 𝔙_w = Vol(Γ_{R,w}) · Vol(ᵗΓ_{R,w}) / Vol(Γ_{R,w} ∩ ᵗΓ_{R,w}).
Hence (with the corrected (83)) I_w / (Vol(Γ_{R,w})Vol(ᵗΓ_{R,w})) = ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w) / Vol(Γ_{R,w} ∩ ᵗΓ_{R,w}). The quantities 𝔙_w and I_w are independent of r; the two sides of the last identity are not. If n_{i,w} = 1 for all i, then R_w is the Borel B_w, Γ_{R,w} = I^0_{w,r} (the w-factor of the image of I^0_{r,V} = I^0_r under (14)), and ᵗΓ_{R,w} = ᵗI^0_{w,r} is identified with the corresponding factor of I^0_{r,−V}.
items.note: Printed: 'I_w/(Vol(Γ_{R,w})·Vol(ᵗΓ_{R,w})) = L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w)⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}/Vol(Γ_{R,w} ∩ ᵗΓ_{R,w}). The right-hand side (and hence the left-hand side) is easily seen to be independent of r.' That is false: by (72) ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ = Vol(Γ_{R,w})∏_i⟨φ_{i,w}, φ̃_{i,w}⟩, and Vol(Γ_{R,w})/Vol(Γ_{R,w} ∩ ᵗΓ_{R,w}) = |N_{R_w}(O_w/p_w^r)| = q_w^{r·dim N_{R_w}} (sourceIssues E60). (87) is not proved in the paper; checked: ᵗΓ_{R,w}Γ_{R,w} = N^-_{R}(O)L_R(O)N_R(O) (Iwahori factorization), whose volume is ∏_i vol_{add}(GL_{n_{i,w}}(O_w)) = Vol(𝔛^{(1)})Vol(𝔛^{(4)}), and Vol(HK) = Vol(H)Vol(K)/Vol(H ∩ K). With the normalization Vol(GL_m(O_w)) = 1 (implicit in (72)) (87) fails by the constant vol_{add}(GL_n(O_w))/(vol_{add}(GL_{a_w}(O_w))vol_{add}(GL_{b_w}(O_w))). Used in Remark 4.6.2 and in the proof of Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.4.1 — archimedean groups, U_σ, K°_σ and the Harish-Chandra decomposition
items.statement: Identify Σ with Σ_{K^+} (σ ↦ σ|_{K^+}). Let G* = GU_1^+ = R_{K^+/Q} GU^+(V) (printed R_{K/Q}), GU^+(V) the full unitary similitude group of V, so G*(R) = ∏_{σ∈Σ_{K^+}} G_σ with G_σ = GU^+(V)_{K^+_σ} ≅ GU^+(a_σ, b_σ). For h : R_{C/R}G_{m,C} → G*_R as in §2.1 the image of h lies in the subgroup G of tuples (g_σ) whose similitude factor ν(g_σ) is independent of σ (the group of the Shimura variety). U_∞ = C(R) ⊆ G(R) is the centralizer of a standard h (§2.3.2); U_σ = U_∞ ∩ G_σ; K°_σ ⊂ U_σ its maximal compact subgroup, ≅ U(a_σ) × U(b_σ); k_σ = Lie(U_σ) = 𝔷_σ ⊕ Lie(K°_σ) with 𝔷_σ the R-split centre of 𝔤_σ = Lie(GU^+(a_σ, b_σ)); 𝔤_σ = k_σ ⊕ p^-_σ ⊕ p^+_σ (Harish-Chandra decomposition, defined over σ(K) since h is standard). h factors through a rational torus T (= J_{0,n}) ⊂ G; T_σ is the σ-component of T(R), 𝔱_σ its Lie algebra; R^+_σ is a positive system for T_σ in which the roots on p^+_σ are positive, 𝔟^+_σ the corresponding Borel subalgebra, R^{+,c}_σ ⊂ R^+_σ the positive compact roots.
items.note: Printed 'R_{K/Q}GU^+(V)': GU^+(V) is a group over K^+ and G*(R) is a product over Σ_{K^+}, so R_{K^+/Q} is meant (sourceIssues E61). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (88) — the holomorphic module D(τ_σ) = D(κ_σ)
items.statement: For σ ∈ Σ and an irreducible representation (τ_σ, W_{τ_σ}) of U_σ, D(τ_σ) := U(𝔤_σ) ⊗_{U(k_σ ⊕ p^-_σ)} W^∨_{τ_σ} (88), with k_σ acting on W^∨_{τ_σ} through τ_σ^∨ and p^-_σ acting by 0. The highest weight of τ_σ relative to R^{+,c}_σ is written κ_σ = (c_σ; κ_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ κ_{a_σ,σ}; κ^c_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ κ^c_{b_σ,σ}) ∈ Z × Z^{a_σ} × Z^{b_σ}, c_σ the character of 𝔷_σ, and one writes D(κ_σ) := D(τ_σ).
items.note: A generalized Verma module; as a U(p^+_σ)-module it is free, generated by 1 ⊗ W^∨_{τ_σ} (PBW). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (89) — strongly positive types
items.note: Checked: the right side of (89) is non-increasing exactly when −κ^c_{1,σ} − a ≥ −κ_{a,σ} + b. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (90) — the anti-holomorphic module D_c(τ_σ)
items.statement: D_c(τ_σ) := D(τ_σ)^∨ ≅ U(𝔤_σ) ⊗_{U(k_σ ⊕ p^+_σ)} W_{τ_σ} (90); it is the complex conjugate of D(τ_σ) with respect to the R-structure on 𝔤_σ, called the anti-holomorphic representation of type τ_σ, and written D_c(κ_σ).
items.note: Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.4.1 — D(κ), D_c(κ) are (anti-)holomorphic discrete series with one-dimensional (𝔤, U)-cohomology
items.statement: If τ_σ is strongly positive, then D(κ_σ) (resp. D_c(κ_σ)) is the (U(𝔤_σ), U_σ)-module of a holomorphic (resp. anti-holomorphic) discrete series representation of G_σ, and dim H^{ab}(𝔤_σ, U_σ; D(κ_σ) ⊗ 𝒲_σ) = dim H^{ab}(𝔤_σ, U_σ; D_c(κ_σ) ⊗ 𝒲_σ^∨) = 1, where 𝒲_σ has highest weight (89) and its dual 𝒲^∨_σ has highest weight (c_σ; −a_n, …, −a_1) = (c_σ; κ_{1,σ} − b, …, κ_{a,σ} − b, κ^c_{1,σ} + a, …, κ^c_{b,σ} + a) (91).
items.note: 'It is well known' — no reference given. (91) checked from (89). The printed (91) has a stray ';' after κ_{1,σ} − b. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Minimal U_σ-type; holomorphic and anti-holomorphic vectors
items.statement: The minimal U_σ-type of D(κ_σ) is 1 ⊗ W^∨_{τ_σ} ⊂ U(𝔤_σ) ⊗_{U(k_σ⊕p^-_σ)} W^∨_{τ_σ} (its elements are the holomorphic vectors); the minimal U_σ-type of D_c(κ_σ) is 1 ⊗ W_{τ_σ} ⊂ U(𝔤_σ) ⊗_{U(k_σ⊕p^+_σ)} W_{τ_σ} (the anti-holomorphic vectors).
items.note: §4.4.14 instead describes the minimal type of D_c(κ) as 1 ⊗ W^∨_{τ_σ} (sourceIssues E70). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.4.2 — tube domain and the canonical automorphy factors J, J', j, j'
items.statement: Take G_σ = G_{4,σ} ≅ GU(n, n) and τ_σ scalar. Let M_n = Spec P(n) be the affine scheme of n×n matrices over Z, P(n)_σ its base change to O_σ = σ(O_K). The Siegel parabolic P_n and U_σ give an unbounded realization of a component X^+_σ ⊂ X_σ as a tube domain in p^+_{4,σ} ([Har86, (5.3.2)]); a basis of L_1 and the identifications of V with V_d, V^d identify p^+_{4,σ} with M_n(C) and X^+_σ with X_{n,n} := {z ∈ M_n(C) : ℶ_σ(ᵗz̄ − z) > 0}, where ℶ_σ ∈ X^+_σ, the fixed point of U_σ, is a diagonal matrix with entries in σ(K) of trace zero to K^+. g_σ = (a_σ b_σ; c_σ d_σ) ∈ G_σ acts by g_σ(z) = (a_σz + b_σ)(c_σz + d_σ)^{−1}. For z = (z_σ) ∈ X = ∏X_σ and g = (g_σ): J'(g_σ, z_σ) = c̄_σ ᵗz_σ + d̄_σ, J(g_σ, z_σ) = c_σz_σ + d_σ, J'(g, z) = ∏_σ J'(g_σ, z_σ), J(g, z) = ∏_σ J(g_σ, z_σ); j_{g_σ}(z_σ) = j(g_σ, z_σ) = det J(g_σ, z_σ) (= ν(g_σ)^{−n} det(g_σ) det J'(g_σ, z_σ) = ν(g_σ)^n det(ḡ_σ)^{−1} det J'(g_σ, z_σ)), j(g, z) = ∏_σ j_{g_σ}(z_σ). For g ∈ G_σ put J(g) = J(g, ℶ_σ), J'(g) = J'(g, ℶ_σ), j(g) = det J(g), j'(g) = det J'(g): C^∞ functions on G_σ with values in GL(n, C), resp. C^×; any polynomial in J, J' is annihilated by p^-_σ and lies in a finite-dimensional k_σ-subrepresentation of C^∞(G_σ).
items.note: The two expressions for j in parentheses agree because |det g|² = ν(g)^{2n}; checked on diagonal elements diag(a, ν ᵗā^{−1}) for the form (0 1; −1 0). Classical (Shimura). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.4.2 — the holomorphic module D²(χ_σ) and the map ι(χ_σ) (92)
items.statement: Let χ = ||•||^m · χ_0 be an algebraic Hecke character of K, m ∈ Z, with χ_{0,σ}(z) = z^{−a(χ_σ)} z̄^{−b(χ_σ)} at each archimedean σ. D²(χ_σ) = D²(m, χ_{0,σ}) is the holomorphic (Lie(G_{4,σ}), U_σ)-module with highest U_σ-type Λ(χ_σ) = Λ(m, χ_{0,σ}) = (m − b(χ_σ), …, m − b(χ_σ); −m + a(χ_σ), …, −m + a(χ_σ); •) (notation of [Har97, (3.3.2)]; • the unspecified character of the R-split centre of U_σ). Let v(χ_σ) be the tautological generator of the Λ(m, χ_{0,σ})-isotypic (highest U_σ-type) subspace. The map of (U(𝔤_σ), U_σ)-modules ι(χ_σ) : D²(χ_σ) → C^∞(G_σ) (92) is the U(𝔤_σ)-linear extension of ι(χ_σ)(v(χ_σ)) = J_{χ_σ}(g) := j(g)^{−m + a(χ_σ)} · j'(g)^{−m + b(χ_σ)} · ν(g)^{n(m + a(χ_σ) + b(χ_σ))}; C(G_σ, χ_σ) denotes its image.
items.note: Here m refers to the factorization χ = ||•||^m χ_0 with algebraic χ_0; in §4.5.4 and §4.6 the same letter m is used for χ = ||•||^m χ_u with χ_u unitary (the two differ by (a(χ_σ) + b(χ_σ))/2; §5.3.1 renames the first one μ) (sourceIssues E71). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Remark 4.4.3 — J_{χ_σ} depends only on χ_σ (on the unitary group)
items.statement: The restriction of J_{χ_σ} to U(n, n) = ker ν depends only on the archimedean character χ_σ = ||•||^m_σ χ_{0,σ}: its exponents −m + a(χ_σ), −m + b(χ_σ) are determined by χ_σ(z) = z^{m − a(χ_σ)} z̄^{m − b(χ_σ)}. The factor ν(g)^{n(m + a(χ_σ) + b(χ_σ))} is not: replacing (m, χ_0) by (m − k, ||•||^k χ_0) changes its exponent by −3nk.
items.note: Printed without the restriction to U(n, n) (sourceIssues E62). Harmless because similitude factors are ignored (Remark 4.5.3), but Definition 5.3.2 invokes this remark to say f_σ does not depend on the factorization of χ_σ. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (93)–(95) — branching of D²(m, χ_{0,σ}) to U(a_σ, b_σ) × U(b_σ, a_σ)
items.statement:
For m in the closed right half-plane bounded by the centre of symmetry of the functional equation of the Eisenstein series (as in [Har08]), the restriction of D²(m, χ_{0,σ}) to U_{3,σ} = U(a_σ, b_σ) × U(b_σ, a_σ) decomposes as an infinite direct sum of irreducible holomorphic discrete series:
(93) D²(m, χ_{0,σ}) = ⊕_{κ_σ ∈ C_3(m, χ_{0,σ})} D(κ_σ) ⊗ D(κ^♭_σ ⊗ χ_{0,σ}) = ⊕_{κ_σ ∈ C_3(χ_σ)} D(κ_σ) ⊗ D(κ^♭_σ ⊗ χ_σ),
(94) C_3(χ_σ) = C_3(m, χ_{0,σ}) = {(−m + b(χ_σ) − r_{a_σ}, …, −m + b(χ_σ) − r_1; m − a(χ_σ) + s_1, …, m − a(χ_σ) + s_{b_σ})},
(95) r_1 ≥ r_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ r_{a_σ} ≥ 0, s_1 ≥ s_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_{b_σ} ≥ 0.
Here κ^♭_σ is given explicitly in (121); identifying holomorphic representations of U(b_σ, a_σ) with anti-holomorphic representations of U(a_σ, b_σ), D(κ^♭_σ) ≅ D(κ_σ)^∨. Twisting by χ_{0,σ} and by χ_σ agree on U(b_σ, a_σ).
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'Compare [Har97, Lemma 3.3.7] when a(χ_σ) = 0' (printed 'a(χ_s)', sourceIssues E63). Footnote 11: the sign change relative to Λ(χ_σ) comes from the duality in (88). Only a special case (a(χ_σ) = 0) is covered by the reference as cited. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (96)–(97) — the parameters (α, β), ρ, ρ^υ
items.statement: For σ ∈ Σ let (α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ)) = (−m + b(χ_σ), …, −m + b(χ_σ); m − a(χ_σ), …, m − a(χ_σ)) ∈ Z^{a_σ + b_σ} and (α(χ), β(χ)) = ((α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ)))_{σ∈Σ} (96). For κ = (κ_σ)_{σ∈Σ} with κ_σ ∈ C_3(χ_σ): ρ_σ = κ_σ − (α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ)) = (−r_{a_σ}, …, −r_1; s_1, …, s_{b_σ}), ρ^υ_σ = (r_1, …, r_{a_σ}; s_1, …, s_{b_σ}), ρ = (ρ_σ)_σ, ρ^υ = (ρ^υ_σ)_σ (97). The involution υ on the parameters corresponds to an algebraic involution υ of the torus T; given χ, the algebraic characters ρ, ρ^υ, κ determine one another.
items.note: Used for the Eisenstein measure (§5.3, Theorem 8.2.2) and the main theorem. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.4 — injectivity of ι(χ_σ); C(G_σ, χ_σ) is free of rank one over U(p^+_σ)
items.statement: For χ = ||•||^m χ_0 with m in the closed right half-plane bounded by the centre of symmetry of the functional equation of the Eisenstein series, the map ι(χ_σ) of (92) is injective for all σ. In particular its image C(G_σ, χ_σ) is a free U(p^+_σ) ≅ S(p^+_σ)-module of rank 1.
items.note: Proof: D²(χ_σ) is always free of rank one over U(p^+_σ) (PBW), and for m in the indicated range it is irreducible as a U(𝔤_σ)-module (asserted without reference; this is the irreducibility of scalar-type generalized Verma modules for U(n,n) beyond the last reduction point); ι(χ_σ) ≠ 0, hence injective. Correct given the irreducibility. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Definition 4.4.5 — critical pairs (κ, χ)
items.statement: Let κ = (κ_σ, σ ∈ Σ) with κ_σ the highest weight of an irreducible representation τ_σ of U_σ, and let (χ_σ, σ ∈ Σ) be the archimedean parameter of an algebraic Hecke character χ of K. The pair (κ, χ) (or the triple (κ, m, χ_0)) is critical if κ_σ ∈ C_3(χ_σ) for all σ ∈ Σ. If π is an anti-holomorphic automorphic representation of G_1 of type κ, (π, χ) is critical if (κ, χ) is critical.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 4.4.6 — critical m and critical values
items.statement: When K is imaginary quadratic, [Har97, §3] shows that, for fixed π and χ, the set of m such that (π, m, χ_0) is critical is exactly the set of critical values of L(s + 1/2, π, χ) that are ≥ the centre of symmetry of the functional equation; the paper states that the same holds for an arbitrary CM field.
items.note: The general CM case is asserted ('The verification is simple but superfluous unless one wants to compare the results … to conjectures on critical values') and not proved; not used later in the paper. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (98) — the element δ_{χ_σ,κ_σ} ∈ U(p^+_4) and rational structures
items.statement: Let v_{κ_σ} ⊗ v_{κ^♭_σ⊗χ_σ} be a highest weight vector in the minimal K_3-type of D(κ_σ) ⊗ D(κ^♭_σ ⊗ χ_σ) (relative to compact maximal tori in U_{3,σ} as in §4.4.1). Since D²(χ_σ) is free of rank one over U(p^+_4) on v(χ_σ) ∈ Λ(χ_σ), there is a unique δ_{χ_σ,κ_σ} ∈ U(p^+_4) with δ_{χ_σ,κ_σ} · v(χ_σ) = v_{κ_σ} ⊗ v_{κ^♭_σ⊗χ_σ} (98); it depends on the choice of basis vectors but is otherwise well defined up to scalars. D(κ_σ) ⊗ D(κ^♭_σ ⊗ χ_σ) has a natural rational structure over the field of definition E(τ_σ, χ_σ) of τ_σ ⊠ τ^♭_σ ⊗ χ_σ; span(v_{κ_σ} ⊗ v_{κ^♭_σ⊗χ_σ}) is the E(τ_σ, χ_σ)-line spanned by that vector, which is always chosen rational over E(τ_σ, χ_σ).
items.note: Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.4.7 — holomorphic projection pr_{κ,σ}, pr^{hol}_{κ,σ}, pr^{hol}
items.statement: pr_{κ,σ} : D²(χ_σ) → D(κ_σ) ⊗ D(κ^♭_σ ⊗ χ_σ) is the natural projection given by (93). pr^{hol}_{κ,σ} = pr^{hol;a_σ,b_σ}_{κ,σ} : D²(χ_σ) → span(v_{κ_σ} ⊗ v_{κ^♭_σ⊗χ_σ}) is pr_{κ,σ} followed by orthogonal projection onto the highest weight component of the holomorphic subspace (the minimal K_3-type). D²(χ_σ)^{hol;a_σ,b_σ} := ⊕_{κ_σ ∈ C_3(m,χ_σ)} im(pr^{hol}_{κ,σ}) and pr^{hol} := ⊕ pr^{hol}_{κ,σ} : D²(χ_σ) → D²(χ_σ)^{hol;a_σ,b_σ}.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (99)–(100) — S(p^+_4) ≅ P(n), j(a_σ, b_σ), the polynomials p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) and operators δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ)
items.statement: Since h is standard, U(𝔤_σ) and U(p^+_{4,σ}) ≅ S(p^+_{4,σ}) have models over O_σ, and the identification of §4.4.2 gives an isomorphism of O_σ-algebras S(p^+_{4,σ}) ≅ P(n)_σ (99). Write X ∈ M_n as X = (A(X) B(X); C(X) D(X)) with A(X) ∈ M_{a_σ}, D(X) ∈ M_{b_σ}; this gives j(a_σ, b_σ) : P(a_σ)_σ ⊗ P(b_σ)_σ ↪ P(n)_σ ≅ U(p^+_{4,σ}). For i ≤ a_σ, j ≤ b_σ let Δ_i(X) ∈ P(a_σ)_σ, Δ'_j(X) ∈ P(b_σ)_σ be the leading principal i-minor of A and j-minor of D. For r_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ r_{a_σ,σ} ≥ r_{a_σ+1,σ} = 0 and s_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_{b_σ,σ} ≥ s_{b_σ+1,σ} = 0 as in (95), put r̃_{i,σ} = r_{i,σ} − r_{i+1,σ}, s̃_{j,σ} = s_{j,σ} − s_{j+1,σ}, and p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ)(X) = j(a_σ, b_σ)(∏_{i=1}^{a_σ} Δ_i(X)^{r̃_{i,σ}} · ∏_{j=1}^{b_σ} Δ'_j(X)^{s̃_{j,σ}}) (100), a polynomial of degree Σ_i r_{i,σ} + Σ_j s_{j,σ}. δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) ∈ U(p^+_σ) is the element corresponding to p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) under (99). GL(a_σ) × GL(a_σ) (resp. GL(b_σ) × GL(b_σ)) acts on P(a_σ)_σ (resp. P(b_σ)_σ) through (g_1, g_2)(X) = ᵗg_1^{−1} X g_2, preserving degree; representations of GL(a_σ), GL(b_σ) are indexed by highest weights for the upper-triangular Borel.
items.note: The A and D blocks of p^+_4 are the directions normal to 𝔤_3 (p^+_3 is the B, C part), so p(r̃, s̃) · v(χ) lies in the sum of minimal K_3-types — the mechanism behind (93). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 4.4.8 — GL(u) × GL(u)-decomposition of P(u)^d (classical Schur–Weyl / Howe duality)
items.statement: Let u = a_σ or b_σ. As a representation of GL(u) × GL(u), the degree-d subspace P(u)^d_σ ⊂ P(u)_σ decomposes as P(u)^d_σ ≅ ⊕_μ [F^{μ,∨} ⊗ F^μ], where μ runs over u-tuples c_1 ≥ c_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ c_u ≥ 0 with Σ_i c_i = d. For μ = (c_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ c_u ≥ c_{u+1} = 0) the highest weight space F^{μ,+} ⊂ [F^{μ,∨} ⊗ F^μ] is spanned by Δ^μ = ∏_{i=1}^{u} Δ_i^{c_i − c_{i+1}}. One writes P(u)^+_σ = ⊕_μ F^{μ,+}.
items.note: Proof: 'the case n = k = r of Theorem 5.6.7 of [GW09]' (cited). Printed 'r-tuples' and '∏_{i=1}^{r}' where u is meant (r is Goodman–Wallach's letter) (sourceIssues E64). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §4.4.7 — the differential operators D(κ, χ) and D^{hol}(κ, χ)
items.statement: For (κ, χ) critical and ρ^υ_σ = (r_{i,σ}; s_{j,σ}) determined by κ_σ via (94), (97): D(ρ^υ_σ) = D(κ_σ, χ_σ) := δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ), D(ρ^υ) = D(κ, χ) := ∏_σ D(κ_σ, χ_σ); D^{hol}(ρ^υ_σ) = D^{hol}(κ_σ, χ_σ) := pr^{hol}_{κ,σ} δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ), D^{hol}(ρ^υ) = D^{hol}(κ, χ) := ∏_σ D^{hol}(κ_σ, χ_σ).
items.note: Defined inside the statement of Corollary 4.4.9. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 4.4.9 (a) — non-vanishing of the holomorphic projection of δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) · v(χ_σ)
items.statement: Let (κ, χ) be critical. For each σ ∈ Σ, the a_σ + b_σ-tuple ρ^υ_σ = (r_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ r_{a_σ,σ} ≥ 0; s_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_{b_σ,σ} ≥ 0) attached to κ_σ by (94), (97) satisfies pr^{hol}_{κ,σ}(δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) · v(χ_σ)) = P_{κ_σ,χ,σ} · v_{κ_σ} ⊗ v_{κ^♭_σ⊗χ_σ} with P_{κ_σ,χ,σ} a non-zero scalar in E(τ_σ, χ_σ)^×.
items.note: Printed as 'there is a unique a_σ + b_σ-tuple … as above such that …'; uniqueness is automatic since ρ^υ_σ is determined by κ_σ and χ_σ. Printed 'δ(r̃_σ, s̃_s)' (sourceIssues E65). Proof: j(a_σ, b_σ)(P(a_σ)^+_σ ⊗ P(b_σ)^+_σ) is spanned by the p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ); the composition δ(a_σ, b_σ)^+ ⊗ v(χ_σ) ↪ D²(χ_σ) → D²(χ_σ)^{hol;a_σ,b_σ} is an isomorphism ([Har86, §7.11], cited); comparing T_σ-weights, the image of δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) · v(χ_σ) lies in the κ_σ-line and is non-zero. Rationality from [Har86, Lemma 7.3.2]. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Corollary 4.4.9 (b) — D(κ, χ) = Σ_{κ† ≤ κ} δ(κ, κ†) ∘ D^{hol}(κ†, χ)
items.statement: Let (κ, χ) be critical. For all κ† ≤ κ there exist unique elements δ(κ, κ†) ∈ U(p^+_3), defined over number fields, such that D(κ, χ) = Σ_{κ† ≤ κ} δ(κ, κ†) ∘ D^{hol}(κ†, χ), and δ(κ, κ) is the scalar ∏_σ P_{κ_σ,χ,σ}.
items.note: Asserted to be 'formal consequences of the decomposition (93) and the fact that the decomposition is rational over an appropriate reflex field, cf. Lemma 7.3.2 of [Har86]'. As literally stated (δ(κ, κ†) ∈ U(p^+_3) applied to the highest-weight line) existence is not justified when the minimal K_3-types have dimension > 1 (sourceIssues E66); with δ(κ, κ†) read as vector-valued differential operators it is fine, and that is all §8.1 (Proposition 8.1.3) needs. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (101) — the canonical embedding of π_f into coherent cohomology of Sh(V_4)
items.statement: View G_4 as the rational similitude group of a maximally isotropic hermitian space V_4 with Shimura variety Sh(V_4). Let Λ(χ) = (Λ(χ_σ), σ ∈ Σ) be the character of U_∞ whose restriction to U_σ is Λ(χ_σ), L(χ) the one-dimensional space on which U_∞ acts by Λ(χ) (realizable over a number field E(χ_∞) depending only on χ_∞), and 𝓛(χ) the automorphic line bundle on Sh(V_4) defined by the dual of Λ(χ) restricted to U_∞ ∩ G_4(R), with fibre L(χ) at the fixed point h of U_∞. If π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f is an automorphic representation of G_4 with π_∞ ≅ D²(χ) = ⊗_{σ∈Σ} D²(χ_σ) and π_f irreducible smooth, there is a canonical embedding π_f ≅ π_f ⊗ H^0(𝔓_h, U_∞; D²(χ) ⊗ L(χ)) ↪ H^0(Sh(V_4)^{tor}, 𝓛(χ)^{can}) (101).
items.note: Stated without proof or reference. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (102)–(105) — Maass–Shimura operators δ^d_χ and δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) on C^∞ modular forms
items.statement: Let Ω = Ω_{Sh(V_4)}. For d ≥ 0 and a ring O, P(n)^d(O) is the O-module of O-valued degree-d polynomials on M_n and P(n)^{d,*}(O) = Hom_O(P(n)^d, O); U_∞ acts canonically on P(n)^d, defined over the integer ring of the field E(h) of definition of the standard CM point h. The Maass operator of degree d ([Har86, §7.9]) is a C^∞ differential operator δ^d_χ : 𝓛(χ) → 𝓛(χ) ⊗ Sym^d Ω (102), whose target is the automorphic vector bundle attached to L(χ) ⊗ P(n)^{d,*} (via (99)); on automorphic forms δ^d_χ : 𝒜(G_4, L(χ)_h) → 𝒜(G_4, L(χ)_h ⊗ P(n)^{d,*}) (103). For φ ∈ P(n)^d ≡ Sym^d p^+_4, δ^d_χ(φ)(f) = [δ^d_χ(f) ⊗ φ] (104), the bracket being the contraction P(n)^{d,*} ⊗ P(n)^d → E(h). For sequences r̃ = (r̃_σ), s̃ = (s̃_σ) as in §4.4.7 with d = Σ_σ[Σ_i r_{i,σ} + Σ_j s_{j,σ}] (the degree of p(r̃, s̃)), put p(r̃, s̃) = ∏_σ p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) and δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) = δ^d_χ(p(r̃, s̃)) : H^0(Sh(V_4)^{tor}, 𝓛(χ)^{can}) → 𝒜(G, L(χ)_h) (105). Under (101), δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) is multiplication by p(r̃, s̃) ∈ Sym^d p^+_4, mapping H^0(𝔓_h, U_∞; D²(χ) ⊗ L(χ)_h) = ⊗_σ C v_{χ_σ} ⊗ L(χ)_h to p(r̃, s̃) ⊗ ⊗_σ C v_{χ_σ} ⊗ L(χ)_h ⊂ D²(χ) ⊗ L(χ)_h.
items.note: Printed degree condition 'Σ_σ[Σ_i r̃_{i,σ} + Σ_j s̃_{j,σ}] = d' is wrong: Δ_i has degree i, so deg p(r̃, s̃) = Σ_σ[Σ_i i·r̃_{i,σ} + Σ_j j·s̃_{j,σ}] = Σ_σ[Σ_i r_{i,σ} + Σ_j s_{j,σ}] (sourceIssues E67). The p-adic counterparts are [Eis12]; not treated in this range. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans Katz's algebraic and p-adic differential operators and CM periods.

items.name: Proposition 4.4.11 — the operators D(κ, χ), D^{hol}(κ, χ) on modular forms ([Har86, Prop. 7.11.11])
items.statement: Let (κ, χ) be critical as in Corollary 4.4.9. Fix a level subgroup K_4 ⊂ G_4(A_f) and K_1 × K_2 ⊂ G_3(A_f) ∩ K_4. Let S^∞_{κ,V}(K_1, C) be the space of C^∞ modular forms of type κ on Sh(V_1) of level K_1, S^∞_{κ^♭,−V}(K_2, C) analogously, and S_{κ,V}, S_{κ^♭,−V} the holomorphic ones. There are differential operators D(κ, χ) : H^0(_{K_4}Sh(V_4)^{tor}, 𝓛(χ)^{can}) → S^∞_{κ,V}(K_1, C) ⊗ S^∞_{κ^♭,−V}(K_2, C) ⊗ χ∘det and D^{hol}(κ, χ) : H^0(_{K_4}Sh(V_4)^{tor}, 𝓛(χ)^{can}) → S_{κ,V}(K_1, C) ⊗ S_{κ^♭,−V}(K_2, C) ⊗ χ∘det which give the operators δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) and pr^{hol} ∘ δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) upon pullback to functions on G_4(A) and restriction to G_3(A).
items.note: 'The following Proposition restates Proposition 7.11.11 of [Har86]' — cited, not proved. Used in §8.1. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans Katz's algebraic and p-adic differential operators and CM periods.

items.name: (106) — Hodge types attached to D_c(τ_σ)
items.statement:
Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of GU(V) whose component at σ is an anti-holomorphic discrete series D_c(τ_σ), and Π its base change to GL(n)_K (ignoring the split centre), which is cohomological with Π^∨ ≅ Π^c. Attach to D_c(τ) the Hodge structure given by the rule assigning a motive to Π: it is pure of weight n − 1 with Hodge types, each of multiplicity one, (106):
(κ_1 − b + n − 1, b − κ_1), …, (κ_a, n − 1 − κ_a), (n − 1 − a − κ^c_b, κ^c_b + a), …, (−κ^c_1, κ^c_1 + n − 1),
(κ^c_1 + n − 1, −κ^c_1), …, (κ^c_b + a, n − 1 − a − κ^c_b), (n − 1 − κ_a, κ_a), …, (b − κ_1, κ_1 − b + n − 1),
i.e. the first row is (κ_i + n − b − i, b − 1 + i − κ_i) for i = 1, …, a followed by (j − 1 − κ^c_j, n − j + κ^c_j) for j = b, …, 1, and the second row consists of the swapped pairs. The pairs are labelled (p_i, q_i), i = 1, …, 2n, in order of appearance; (p_i, q_i) is in the first row iff i ≤ n.
items.note: The paper also asserts that Π 'is cuspidal', which is false in general (sourceIssues E68). The general formula for the i-th pair is my reading of the two ends printed; all pairs sum to n − 1. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hypothesis 4.4.13 — critical interval hypothesis
items.statement: The weights (κ, κ^c) are adapted to the signature (a, b): for every pair (p_i, q_i) in (106), p_i ≠ q_i, and p_i > q_i if and only if i ≤ n.
items.note: A standing hypothesis (kind 'definition' as an assumption). Equivalent form in hyp-4-4-13-criterion. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.4.12 — Hypothesis 4.4.13 holds iff 2κ_a > n − 1 and −2κ^c_1 > n − 1
items.statement: Hypothesis 4.4.13 holds if and only if 2κ_a > n − 1 and −2κ^c_1 > n − 1.
items.note: 'One checks'. Checked: in the first row p − q = 2κ_i + n + 1 − 2b − 2i (minimal at i = a, where it equals 2κ_a − n + 1) and p − q = 2j − 1 − n − 2κ^c_j (minimal at j = 1, where it equals −2κ^c_1 − n + 1); the second row is the first with p, q swapped. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.4.12 — the Hodge polygon Hodge(κ, κ^c) = Hodge(D_c(τ))
items.statement: Hodge(κ, κ^c) = Hodge(D_c(τ)) is 'the polygon in the right half-plane connecting the vertices (i, p_i)', with (p_i, q_i) the pairs of (106).
items.note: As printed this is not the usual Hodge polygon (whose vertices are (i, sum of the i smallest p's)); only used in Proposition 8.3.12, whose proof is omitted and which 'will not be used' (sourceIssues E69). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §4.4.14 — the test vectors φ_{κ,+}, φ_{κ,−} at archimedean places
items.statement: When τ_σ is strongly positive with highest weight κ = κ_σ, write D(κ) = D(τ_σ), D_c(κ) = D_c(τ_σ). For a cuspidal automorphic representation π of G with π_σ = D_c(κ), the zeta integral uses a factorizable φ = ⊗_v φ_v ∈ π with φ_σ a vector in the minimal U_σ-type of D_c(κ), namely the highest weight vector φ_{κ,+} or the lowest weight vector φ_{κ,−}; if w_0 is the longest element of the Weyl group of T_σ relative to R^+_σ, then φ_{κ,+} (resp. φ_{κ,−}) is a T_σ-eigenvector of weight −w_0(κ) (resp. −κ).
items.note: Printed: the minimal U_σ-type of D_c(κ) is '1 ⊗ W^∨_{τ_σ}' — the stated weights are those of W^∨_{τ_σ}, but §4.4.1 gives 1 ⊗ W_{τ_σ} (sourceIssues E70). (50) takes φ_∞ = φ_{κ_σ,−}, φ^♭_∞ = φ_{κ^♭_σ,−}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 4.5.2 — ι(m, χ_σ)(D²(m, χ_σ)) consists of sections of I_σ(m − n/2, χ)
items.statement: As subspaces of C^∞(G_σ), ι(m, χ_σ)(D²(m, χ_σ)) ⊂ I_σ(m − n/2, χ).
items.note: 'An easy computation, similar to that in [Har97]' — proof omitted, not checked. The parameters are not reconciled with §4.5.4 and Definition 5.3.2, which put f_σ in I(χ_{u,σ}, m), nor is the argument order (I(χ, s) in §4.1.2 versus I_σ(s, χ) here) (sourceIssues E71). Similitude factors omitted (Remark 4.5.3). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Remark 4.5.3 — similitude factors omitted
items.statement: In §4.5 (and in the archimedean sections) similitude factors are omitted; 'strictly speaking, these should be included; but they do not change the theory in any significant way.'
items.note: A convention a formaliser must undo; compare rem-4-4-3 (the ν-factor of J_χ). Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (107) — the archimedean Siegel–Weil section f_σ
items.statement: For an archimedean place σ the local section f_σ = f_σ(χ_σ, c) ∈ I(χ_{u,σ}, m) is assumed to be f_σ(χ_σ, c, g) = B(χ_σ, κ_σ) D(κ_σ, m, χ_{u,σ}) J_{m,χ_{u,σ}}(g), g ∈ G_{4,σ} (107), where J_{m,χ_{u,σ}} ∈ C^∞(G_4) is the canonical automorphy factor of §4.4.2, D(κ_σ, m, χ_{u,σ}) the differential operator D(κ_σ, χ_σ) of Corollary 4.4.9 and B(χ_σ, κ_σ) a non-zero algebraic scalar.
items.note: Notation mixes χ_u (unitary part, §4.6) with J, D defined in §4.4.2 for χ = ||•||^m χ_0 (sourceIssues E71). The same shape of section is required in Definition 5.3.2. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.5 — non-vanishing of the archimedean zeta integral
items.statement: Let σ be archimedean, f_σ as in (107), and φ_σ ⊗ φ^♭_σ an anti-holomorphic vector in the highest weight subspace of the minimal K_σ-type of π_σ ⊗ π^♭_σ. Then the local factor I_σ(φ_σ, φ^♭_σ, f_σ, m) is not equal to 0.
items.note: Proof: if D(κ_σ, χ_σ) is replaced by D^{hol}(κ_σ, χ_σ) in (107) this is [Har08, Remark (4.4)(iv)] (cited, see har08-rem-4-4-iv); since φ_σ ⊗ φ^♭_σ is anti-holomorphic, the pairing of D(κ_σ, χ_σ)J with it factors through the projection onto D^{hol}(κ_σ, χ_σ)J, which is P_{κ_σ,χ,σ} ≠ 0 times the holomorphic one by Corollary 4.4.9. The argument is sound given those inputs; 'highest weight subspace' here versus φ_{κ,−} (lowest weight) in Proposition 4.5.6 is part of sourceIssues E70. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: [Har08, Remark (4.4)(iv)] — non-vanishing for the holomorphic section (as used)
items.statement: For f_σ = B(χ_σ, κ_σ) D^{hol}(κ_σ, χ_σ) J_{m,χ_σ} (the holomorphic projection of the section (107)) and φ_σ ⊗ φ^♭_σ the anti-holomorphic vector of Proposition 4.5.5, the archimedean doubling zeta integral I_σ(φ_σ, φ^♭_σ, f_σ, m) is non-zero.
items.note: Cited from [Har08], not proved here; statement reconstructed from the way it is used. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Proposition 4.5.6 — the archimedean factor I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ) is a non-zero algebraic number (after Garrett)
items.statement: Let I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ) := I_σ(φ_σ, φ^♭_σ, f_σ, m) with φ_σ = φ_{κ_σ,−}, φ^♭_σ = φ_{κ^♭_σ,−} and f_σ given by (107). Then I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ) is a non-zero algebraic number.
items.note: 'Due to Garrett [Gar08]'; not proved here. Non-vanishing is Proposition 4.5.5. For algebraicity the paper's own account of [Gar08] is 'algebraic up to a predictable power of the transcendental number π, which can be normalized away' and Remark 4.5.7 says loc. cit. treats F imaginary quadratic ('the same reasoning applies in general'); the normalization removing the power of π (Haar measure at σ, the constant B(χ_σ, κ_σ)) is not specified (sourceIssues E72). Background in the text: one-dimensional extreme K-type computed in [Shi97, Shi00]; one factor one-dimensional: [Gar08, p. 12]; general case left open, symplectic analogue [Liu19a] matching [CPR89]. Later work (Eischen–Liu, arXiv:2006.04302) computes these integrals; not checked here. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Remark 4.5.7 — Shimura's formula and the precision of Garrett's result
items.statement: When κ_σ is a scalar representation, Shimura obtains an explicit formula for the local zeta integral. In general, as explained at the end of [Har08, §5], Garrett's calculation determines the value of the integral up to an element of a specific complex embedding of the CM field F (imaginary quadratic in loc. cit.; the paper asserts the same reasoning applies in general); this is not needed in the paper.
items.note: Expository; the extension beyond imaginary quadratic F is asserted without proof. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: (108) — the normalizing Euler factors D_v(χ), D^S(χ), D(χ)
items.statement: Write χ = ||•||^m · χ_u with χ_u a unitary Hecke character of K; let χ^+ be the restriction of χ_u to the idèles of K^+ (a character of finite order) and η = η_{K/K^+} the quadratic idèle class character of K/K^+. For a finite place v of K^+, D_v(χ) = ∏_{r=0}^{n−1} L_v(2m + n − r, χ^+ · η^r); in the notation of (53), D_v(χ) = d_{n,v}(m, χ_v) (χ_v meaning χ_{u,v}). For a finite set S of finite places, D^S(χ) = ∏_{v∉S} D_v(χ), and D(χ) = D^∅(χ) (108), products over finite places.
items.note: Consistent with (53): d_{n,v}(s, χ_{u,v}) = ∏_r L_v(2s + n − r, χ_{u,v}|_{K^+} η^r) at s = m. Used in Definition 5.3.2 (normalization of the Eisenstein measure) and §9. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 4.6.1 — the global formula for the doubling zeta integral
items.statement:
Let π be as in §4.1.4, χ = ||•||^m χ_u, and let S' be the set of places of §4.2 (containing S_π ∪ S_χ ∪ S_K, no place above p). Let φ ∈ π, φ^♭ ∈ π^♭ be factorizable as in (48), with local components at p and ∞ as in (49) and (50), the chosen unramified vectors outside S' ∪ Σ_p ∪ {∞}, and the choices of §4.2.2 at v ∈ S'. Let f = ⊗_v f_v ∈ ⊗_v I_v(χ_{u,v}, m) be the section chosen in §§4.2–4.5 (at p: the section of §4.3.6, see sec-4-3-6-coordinates). Then
D(χ) · I(φ, φ^♭, f, m) = ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩ · ∏_{v|p} D_v(χ) · I_p · I_∞(χ, κ) · I_{S'} · L^{S' ∪ Σ_p}(m + 1/2, π, χ_u),
where I_{S'} = ∏_{v∈S'} D_v(χ) · vol(U_v) (Lemma 4.2.3), I_∞(χ, κ) = ∏_σ I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ) is the product of the factors of Proposition 4.5.6, I_p = ∏_{w∈Σ_p} I_w = ∏_{w|p} ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) L(m + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_{u,w}) 𝔙_w (Theorem 4.3.10 at s = m), and ⟨•, •⟩ is the L² inner product on cusp forms.
items.note: Exact printed statement: 'Theorem 4.6.1. Let the test vectors φ ∈ π and φ^♭ ∈ π^♭ be chosen to be factorizable vectors as in (48), with the local components at p and ∞ given as in (49) and (50), respectively. Assume the local components at finite places outside S = S_π are unramified vectors, and the local choices at ramified places are as in 4.2.2. Moreover, assume the Siegel–Weil section f_s ∈ I(χ, s) is chosen as in the preceding sections. Write χ = ||•||^m χ_u. Then we have the equality D(χ)·I(φ, φ^♭, f, s) = ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩ · I_p(χ, κ) I_∞(χ, ρ^υ) I_S L^S(s + 1/2, π, χ_u) where I_S = ∏_{v∈S} D_v(χ)·volume(𝒰_v), I_∞(χ, κ) = ∏_σ I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ) is the product of factors described in Proposition 4.5.6, I_p = L_p(s, ord, π, χ) × ∏_w [𝔙_w · ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}], where 𝔙_w is the factor that appears in (83), and we define L_p(s, ord, π, χ) := ∏_{w|p} L(s, ord, π_w, χ_w). Finally, ⟨•, •⟩ is the L² inner product on cusp forms.' Corrections, all from the unfolding (51) with d_{n,v}I_v = L_v(s + 1/2, π_v, χ_v) off S' ∪ Σ_p (§4.2.1), I_v = vol(U_v) on S' (Lemma 4.2.3) and I_w from Theorem 4.3.10: the identity holds at s = m for f ∈ I(χ_u, m) (D(χ) is the normalizing factor at s = m); the places above p contribute ∏_{v|p}D_v(χ)·I_p and no standard Euler factor, so L^S must omit them; I_p has no factor ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ and involves L(m + 1/2, ord, …) with the sign of thm-4-3-10-b; S must be S' (sourceIssues E58, sourceIssues E73, sourceIssues E74). Used (as 'Proposition 4.6.1') in Corollary 9.1.8 and Main Theorem 9.2.2; the Main Theorem's formula drops ∏⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩, consistent with the correction. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: L_p(s, ord, π, χ) — the product of the local factors at p
items.statement: L_p(s, ord, π, χ) := ∏_{w|p} L(s, ord, π_w, χ_w), with L(·, ord, π_w, χ_w) as in local-l-eps-factors.
