items.note: In Theorem 4.6.1 the factor that actually appears is L_p(s + 1/2, ord, π, χ) = ∏_w L(s + 1/2, ord, π_w, χ_w), by (83); the printed I_p uses L_p(s, ord, π, χ) (sourceIssues E73), and Main Theorem 9.2.2 writes L_p(m, ord, π', χ_u) next to L^S(m + 1/2, π', χ_u). Marcil 2023, Theorem 4.6, writes E_p(s + 1/2, …). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 4.6.2 — I_p normalized by the volumes of I^0_{r,±V}
items.statement: Assume n_{i,w} = 1 for all i, w (the ordinary case of the paper). By (87) and the identification of volumes in Remark 4.3.12, I_p / (Vol(I^0_{r,V}) Vol(I^0_{r,−V})) = ∏_{w|p} ω_{π_{a_w}⊗χ_{1,w}}(−1) · L_p(s + 1/2, ord, π, χ) / Vol(I^0_{r,V} ∩ I^0_{r,−V}).
items.note: Printed: 'I_p/(Vol(I^0_{r,V})Vol(I^0_{r,−V})) = L_p(s, ord, π, χ) ∏_w⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}/Vol(I^0_{r,V} ∩ I^0_{r,−V})', inheriting sourceIssues E58 and sourceIssues E73. The proof of Main Theorem 9.2.2 cites this remark and ends with Ω = ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩/(Vol(I^0_{r_1,V} ∩ I^0_{r_1,−V})Q[π', χ]) — without ∏_w⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩, i.e. consistent with the corrected form. The volume of the Q_p^× similitude factor is ignored. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.1 — M-valued measures on a compact totally disconnected space
items.statement: Let X be a compact, totally disconnected topological space and R a p-adic ring (p-adically complete and separated). C(X,R) is the R-module of maps X → R that are continuous for the p-adic topology on R; one has C(X,Z_p) ⊗̂_{Z_p} R ≅ C(X,R). For a p-adically complete R-module M, an M-valued measure on X is an element of the R-module Meas(X,M) := Hom_{Z_p}(C(X,Z_p), M) = Hom_R(C(X,R), M).
items.note: Standard; no proof given. The equality of the two Hom's uses that M is p-adically complete and that C(X,R) is the p-adic completion of C(X,Z_p) ⊗ R (Z_p-linear maps into a p-adically complete module are automatically p-adically continuous). Same text in v1 §6.1 (p. 64). Library: Mathlib 082e2d3 defines `AbstractMeasure X R E := C(X, R) →L[R] E` (Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/Measure/Basic.lean), the E-valued measures on a topological space X over a topological ring R, with Dirac measures, pushforward and the two product measures (`prodMk`, `prodMk'`, equal for profinite X, Y); for M with its p-adic topology, continuous R-linear maps are all R-linear maps, which is the paper's definition. The identifications C(X, ℤ_p) ⊗̂ R ≅ C(X, R) and Hom_{ℤ_p}(C(X, ℤ_p), M) = Hom_R(C(X, R), M) are not in Mathlib; PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L0 plans scalar extension of measures.

items.name: §5.1 — measures on a profinite abelian group = completed group ring Λ_{X,R}
items.statement: If X is a profinite abelian group, Meas(X,R) is identified with the completed group ring R[[X]]; in particular Meas(X,R) is a ring (under convolution). Writing X = lim_i X/X_i, where X = X_0 ⊃ X_1 ⊃ X_2 ⊃ … is a neighbourhood basis of the identity consisting of open subgroups of finite index, Λ_{X,R} := lim_i R[X/X_i] (= R[[X]] = Meas(X,R)), a topological ring for the inverse-limit topology; it is compact when R is compact (e.g. R finite over Z_p).
items.note: The paper states 'This is a compact topological ring' with no compactness hypothesis on R (sourceIssues E75). The identification Meas(X,R) = lim_i Hom(C(X/X_i,Z_p),R) = lim_i R[X/X_i] uses density of the locally constant functions. The notation X_i for open subgroups clashes with the factors X_1, X_2 of Lemma 5.1.1 (harmless). Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.1 — measures on a product of profinite groups
items.statement: Suppose X = X_1 × X_2 is a product of profinite abelian groups and R a p-adic ring. Then there is a natural isomorphism Meas(X_1 × X_2, R) ≅ Meas(X_1, Meas(X_2, R)).
items.note: Stated as 'immediate'; no proof. Both sides equal lim_{i,j} R[X_1/U_i × X_2/V_j]; Meas(X_2,R) = R[[X_2]] is p-adically complete. Used in §5.2.2 (measures in Meas(X_p, Meas(T_H, V^ord(K^p,R)))) and in §7.4 ('a V-valued measure on X_p × T is the same thing as a measure on X_p with values in V-valued measures on T'). Part of the former section summary 'restriction-measures'. Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence.

items.name: Fact 5.1.2 (Mazur) — integration of characters against measures
items.statement: Let X be a profinite abelian group and identify a measure μ ∈ Meas(X,R) with an element f ∈ Λ_{X,R}. For every continuous homomorphism χ : X → R_1^×, with R_1 a p-adic R-algebra, ∫_X χ dμ := μ(χ) = χ(f), where χ(f) is the image of f under the ring homomorphism Λ_{X,R} → R_1 induced by χ. Convention: for R_1 = R, χ also denotes the homomorphism Λ_{X,R} → R, so that χ defines an R-valued point of Λ_{X,R}.
items.note: Attributed to Mazur ('well-known'); no reference and no proof. μ(χ) means the R_1-linear extension of μ to C(X,R_1), evaluated at χ. Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence.

items.name: Lemma 5.1.3 — measures are determined by finite-order characters; Kummer congruences
items.statement: Suppose X = lim_m X_m is a profinite abelian group (X_m finite). Suppose R is a ring that is flat over Z_p (and p-adically complete, as for all coefficient rings of measures in §5.1) and contains a primitive n-th root of unity for each n dividing the order of X_m, for every m. Then (i) each R-valued measure on X is completely determined by its values on the locally constant continuous homomorphisms χ : X → R^×; and (ii) any function α from the continuous characters of X to R determines an R-valued measure on X whenever the values of α on the R-valued locally constant characters of X satisfy the usual Kummer congruences (as in [Kat78, §4.0]): for every finite family of locally constant characters χ_i and elements c_i ∈ R[1/p], if Σ_i c_i χ_i(x) ∈ p^N R for all x ∈ X, then Σ_i c_i α(χ_i) ∈ p^N R.
items.note: Cited, not proved: 'a version of a well-known lemma (see [Kat78, Proposition 4.1.2] for the formulation below)'. The paper only says 'the usual Kummer congruences'; the explicit form above is the standard one of [Kat78, §4.0]. The printed hypothesis 'for each n dividing the order of X_m for some m' is to be read 'for every m'. The measure in (ii) is determined by α's values on locally constant characters; the other values of α play no role. Used in §7.4 (the congruence properties of Lemma 5.1.3; Proposition 7.4.15 takes R 'satisfying the conditions of Lemma 5.1.3'). In v2/v3 Lemma 5.1.3 was a different statement (compact p-adic Lie groups, O_{C_p}-valued); the present form dates from v4 (p. 79). Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence.

items.name: §5.2 — the space X_p (limit of ray class groups of conductor p^r)
items.statement: For each integer r > 0 let U_r = (O ⊗ Ẑ^p)^× × (1 + p^r O ⊗ Z_p) ⊂ (K ⊗ Ẑ)^×, where K is the CM field, O = O_K and Ẑ^p = ∏_{ℓ≠p} Z_ℓ, and put X_p := lim_r K^× \ (K ⊗ Ẑ)^× / U_r. This is the projective limit of the ray class groups of K of conductor (p^r); in particular it is a profinite abelian group.
items.note: Continuous characters of X_p are p-adic avatars of Hecke characters of K unramified outside p. Present since v1 §6.2 (p. 64). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 plans the inverse limit of ray class groups of p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus, its character space and locally algebraic Hecke characters.

items.name: §5.2 — X_{p,N_0}: the variant with tame level N_0
items.statement: For N_0 prime to p let U_{r,N_0} = (1 + N_0 O ⊗ Ẑ^p)^× × (1 + p^r O ⊗ Z_p) ⊂ U_r (units of O ⊗ Ẑ^p congruent to 1 mod N_0, times principal units of level p^r at p), and X_{p,N_0} := lim_r K^× \ (K ⊗ Ẑ)^× / U_{r,N_0}. From §5.2.2 on a tame level N_0 is fixed and X_p denotes X_{p,N_0}.
items.note: X_p = X_{p,N_0} is the domain of the Eisenstein measure (§5.3) and of the p-adic L-functions. Characters of X_{p,N_0} may ramify at primes dividing N_0, which matters for condition (1) of Definition 5.3.2 (sourceIssues E84). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L0 plans the inverse limit of ray class groups of p-power conductor and fixed tame modulus, its character space and locally algebraic Hecke characters.

items.name: §5.2.1 — identification of H_1(Z_p) with H_2(Z_p); characters of T_{H_3}(Z_p) as pairs
items.statement: In the situation of §3 (P_1 = P, P_2 its opposite with −⟨·,·⟩ and h(¯·), P_3 = P_1 ⊕ P_2, P_4 the doubled datum; H_i = GL_{O_{B_i}⊗Z_p}(L_i^+)), the isomorphism (36) gives H_1/Z_p ≅ ∏_{w|p} GL_{a_w}(O_w), H_2/Z_p ≅ ∏_{w|p} GL_{b_w}(O_w), H_3/Z_p ≅ ∏_{w|p} GL_{a_w}(O_w) × GL_{b_w}(O_w), H_4/Z_p ≅ ∏_{w|p} GL_n(O_w). Identify H_1(Z_p) with H_2(Z_p) by h_1 = (h_{1,w})_{w|p} ↦ h_2 = (h_{2,w})_{w|p}, h_{2,w} = h_{1,w̄} (b_w = a_{w̄}; O_w ≅ Z_p ≅ O_{w̄}). This identifies T_{H_2}(Z_p) with T_{H_1}(Z_p), and T_{H_4}(Z_p) = T_{H_3}(Z_p) = T_{H_1}(Z_p) × T_{H_2}(Z_p) with T_{H_1}(Z_p) × T_{H_1}(Z_p); so characters ψ of T_{H_3}(Z_p) are identified with pairs (ψ_1, ψ_2) of characters of T := T_{H_1}(Z_p). det : H_1(Z_p) → (O ⊗ Z_p)^× = ∏_{w|p} O_w^× denotes the composite of (36) with the product of the determinants of the GL-factors.
items.note: Notation used throughout §§5, 7, 8. T_{H_3} = T_{H_4} because H_3 ⊂ H_4 is a block-diagonal Levi containing the diagonal torus. Present since v1 §6.2.1 (p. 64). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.2.1 — the twisted characters ψ_χ^{-1} and ψ'_χ = ψ^△_χ
items.statement: Let ψ be a finite-order Q̄_p^×-valued character of T = T_{H_1}(Z_p). For a finite-order Q̄_p^×-valued character χ of X_p put ψ_χ^{-1} := ψ^{-1} · (χ ∘ det), a character of T (det : H_1(Z_p) → (O ⊗ Z_p)^× followed by (O ⊗ Z_p)^× → X_p), and let ψ'_χ = ψ^△_χ be the character of T_{H_3}(Z_p) identified with the pair (ψ, ψ_χ^{-1}).
items.note: The paper writes ψ'_χ in the first definition and in (109) and ψ^△_χ in the second definition and in §5.2.2; both denote the character (ψ, ψ_χ^{-1}). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.2.1 — admissible R-measure on X_p of weight κ, character ψ, level K_3^p
items.statement: Let κ = (κ_σ) be an O'-character of T = T_{H_1}(Z_p) as in §2.9.1 (O' the ring of integers of the extension of Q_p generated by the images of the embeddings of K) and κ' the O'-character of T_{H_3}(Z_p) identified with the pair (κ, κ^∨); let ψ be a finite-order Q̄_p^×-valued character of T; let K_i^p ⊂ G_i(A_f^p), i = 1, 2, be open compact subgroups with ν(K_1^p) = ν(K_2^p); let R be a p-adic O'[ψ]-algebra; and put K_3^p = (K_1^p × K_2^p) ∩ G_3(A_f^p). An admissible R-measure on X_p of weight κ, character ψ and level K_3^p is a measure μ(·) = μ(κ,ψ,·) ∈ Meas(X_p; V^ord(K_3^p, R)) such that for every finite-order Q̄_p^×-valued character χ of X_p, μ(χ) = μ(κ,ψ,χ) ∈ V^ord_{κ'}(K_3^p, ψ'_χ, R[χ]), the module of ordinary p-adic modular forms on G_3 of weight κ', character ψ'_χ and tame level K_3^p over R[χ] (§§2.9.1, 2.9.6).
items.note: The paper writes the ambient module as V^ord_{κ'}(K_3^p, R), which is not defined in §2.9 (only V^ord(K^p,R) and V^ord_κ(K^p,ψ,R) are), and writes ν(K_1) = ν(K_2) for ν(K_1^p) = ν(K_2^p) (sourceIssues E76). v1 (p. 64) and v4 (p. 80) wrote the value as V^ord_{κ'}(K^p, ψ'_χ, R[χ]). Part of the former section summary 'restriction-measures'. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.2.1 — scalar measures μ_ℓ = ℓ ∘ μ
items.statement: Let μ be an admissible R-measure on X_p of weight κ, character ψ and level K_3^p, R' any p-adic R-algebra, and ℓ : V^ord_{κ'}(K_3^p, R) → R' an R-linear functional. Then μ_ℓ(·) = μ_ℓ(κ,ψ,·) := ℓ ∘ μ(κ,ψ,·) is an R'-valued measure on X_p.
items.note: Immediate (R-linear maps between p-adically complete modules are p-adically continuous). v1 (p. 65) and v4 (p. 80) had V^{ord,cusp} as the source of ℓ. This is the mechanism by which scalar p-adic L-functions are extracted in §7 (pairing with Hida-family vectors). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.2.1, (109) — admissible R-measure on X_p of weight ρ, character ψ, shift (α,β), level K_3^p
items.statement: Let ψ, K_i^p (with ν(K_1^p) = ν(K_2^p)), K_3^p and R be as in the preceding definition. Let ρ = (ρ_σ) be an O'-character of T = T_{H_1}(Z_p) as in §2.9.1 and ρ^△ the O'-character of T_{H_3}(Z_p) identified with the pair (ρ, ρ^∨); ρ^△ coincides with (ρ, ρ^♭), ρ^♭ being defined by analogy with (121). Let (α,β) be a character of T_{H_3}(Z_p), written as a pair of characters of T_{H_1}(Z_p) ≡ T_{H_2}(Z_p). An admissible R-measure on X_p of weight ρ, character ψ, shift (α,β) and level K_3^p is a measure μ(·) = μ(ρ,ψ,·) ∈ Meas(X_p; V^ord(K_3^p, R)) such that for every finite-order Q̄_p^×-valued character χ of X_p, ∫_{X_p} χ dμ := μ(χ) = μ(ρ,ψ,χ) ∈ V^ord_{ρ^△·(α,β)}(K_3^p, ψ^△_χ, R[χ])   (109), where ψ^△_χ = (ψ, ψ^{-1}·χ∘det).
items.note: The printed ambient Meas(X_p; V^ord_{ρ^△·(α,β)}(K_3^p,R)) uses undefined notation (sourceIssues E76); (109) prints ψ'_χ, which equals ψ^△_χ. 'The measure is said to have shift (α,β) if it satisfies (109)' (p. 84) and Corollary 8.2.4 (shift (1,χ)) use this notion. The identity ρ^△ = (ρ, ρ^♭) refers forward to (121) and is not checked here. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.2.2 — admissible R-measure on X_p × T_H of character ψ, shift sh, twist υ, level K^p
items.statement: Fix H = H_1 with diagonal torus T_H, a tame level N_0 and X_p = X_{p,N_0}. Suppose given a continuous homomorphism sh : T_{H_3}(Z_p) → X_p; by duality it gives sh^* : C(X_p,R) → C(T_{H_3}(Z_p),R) for any ring R, taking characters to characters. Suppose given an algebraic automorphism υ : T_H → T_H, and for a function ρ on T_H put ρ^υ(t) = ρ(υ(t)). Let K^p = K_3^p = (K_1^p × K_2^p) ∩ G_3(A_f^p) and ψ, R as before. An admissible R-measure on X_p × T_H of character ψ, shift sh, twist υ and level K^p is a measure μ(·) = μ(ψ,sh,·) ∈ Meas(X_p, Meas(T_H(Z_p), V^ord(K^p,R))) such that for every finite-order Q̄_p^×-valued character χ of X_p and every algebraic character ρ of T_H, μ(χ)(ρ^υ) = μ(ψ,sh,χ)(ρ^υ) ∈ V^ord_{ρ^△·sh^*(χ)}(K^p, ψ^△_χ, R[χ]).
items.note: Corrected (sourceIssues E77): the paper writes sh^* : C(X_p,R) → C(T_H(Z_p),R), but sh has domain T_{H_3}(Z_p) and sh^*(χ) must be a character of T_{H_3}(Z_p) for ρ^△·sh^*(χ) to make sense (§7.4 writes sh^*(χ) = (α(χ),β(χ))). 'sh … as before' refers to nothing earlier: in §5.2.1 the shift was a fixed character (α,β). By Lemma 5.1.1, Meas(X_p, Meas(T_H, V)) = Meas(X_p × T_H, V). This is the notion used in §7.4 (Lemma 7.4.2 ff., Proposition 7.4.15). Part of the former section summary 'restriction-measures'. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1 — the weight space Y_H and its algebraic points Y_H^alg
items.statement: Let T_H = T_{H_1} and Σ = {σ ∈ Σ_K : p_σ ∈ Σ_p}, a CM type of K. Y_H is the formal scheme over Z_p with Y_H(R) = Hom_cont(X_p × T_H(Z_p), R^×) for complete Z_p-algebras R. Y_H^alg ⊂ Y_H(C_p) is the set of pairs (χ, c) where χ : X_p → R^× (for some R ⊂ C_p) is the p-adic character associated with an algebraic Hecke character of K, denoted χ^class, and c = ψρ^υ is a locally algebraic character of T_H(Z_p): ρ an algebraic character, υ the involution of T_H of (97), ψ a character of finite order; equivalently c ∈ C_r(T_H(Z_p),R)·ρ^υ for some r ≥ 0, with C_r = functions invariant under the r-th congruence subgroup (Lemma 7.4.2). χ^class need not be unitary: the variable 's' is absorbed into the infinity type of χ.
items.note: The paper prints 'c ∈ C_r(T_H(Z_p),R)'; since C_r(T,O) = C(T/T_r,O) consists of locally constant functions, the correct statement is c ∈ C_r(T_H(Z_p),R)·ρ^υ (sourceIssues E78). The opening of §5.3 ('we take χ … to be a unitary Hecke character') is superseded by 'we are not requiring χ^class to be unitary here'. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1, (110) — the set Y_H^class of classical points (positivity condition)
items.statement: For (χ,c) ∈ Y_H^alg with c = ψρ^υ, fix an integer μ such that for each σ ∈ Σ, χ_σ = ||•||_σ^μ χ_{0,σ} with χ_{0,σ}(z) = z_σ^{-a(χ_σ)} z̄_σ^{-b(χ_σ)}, and let κ = (κ_σ)_{σ∈Σ} be the weight attached to (χ, ρ) by (96)–(97): κ_σ = ρ_σ + (α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ)), (α(χ_σ),β(χ_σ)) = (−μ+b(χ_σ), …, −μ+b(χ_σ); μ−a(χ_σ), …, μ−a(χ_σ)) ∈ Z^{a_σ+b_σ}. Then Y_H^class ⊂ Y_H^alg is defined by (χ,c) ∈ Y_H^class ⇔ κ_σ ∈ C_3(μ, z_σ^{-a(χ_σ)} z̄_σ^{-b(χ_σ)}) for all σ ∈ Σ   (110), where C_3(m, χ_{0,σ}) = {(−m+b(χ_σ)−r_{a_σ}, …, −m+b(χ_σ)−r_1; m−a(χ_σ)+s_1, …, m−a(χ_σ)+s_{b_σ}) : r_1 ≥ … ≥ r_{a_σ} ≥ 0, s_1 ≥ … ≥ s_{b_σ} ≥ 0} is the set (94) of highest weights in the decomposition (93). Equivalently: ρ^υ_σ = (r_1, …, r_{a_σ}; s_1, …, s_{b_σ}) with r_1 ≥ … ≥ r_{a_σ} ≥ 0 and s_1 ≥ … ≥ s_{b_σ} ≥ 0 for every σ ∈ Σ.
items.note: The paper does not say how κ depends on (χ,c) in (110); the relation κ = ρ + (α(χ),β(χ)) is made explicit only in §8.2 ('ρ and κ contain the same information, relative to the shift (1,χ)') and Remark 8.2.5 (sourceIssues E80). It writes C_3(μ,χ_σ) for the set of (93), whose own notation is C_3(χ_σ) = C_3(m, χ_{0,σ}) (sourceIssues E81). Same as (5.3.1) in v4 (p. 81). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1 — (110) does not depend on the factorization χ_σ = ||•||^μ χ_{0,σ}
items.statement: Condition (110) is independent of the choice of the integer μ, i.e. of the factorization χ_σ = ||•||_σ^μ χ_{0,σ}.
items.note: Asserted without proof; the paper writes 'independent of the choice of m', a misprint for μ (sourceIssues E81). Check: replacing μ by μ+1 replaces (a(χ_σ), b(χ_σ)) by (a+1, b+1) because ||z||_σ = z z̄, and the entries −μ+b−r_i and μ−a+s_j of C_3 are unchanged. Verified. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1, (111) — the ordinary projector e_κ
items.statement: Write χ = ||•||^m · χ_u with χ_u unitary (notation of §4.6), let χ^+ be the finite-order idèle class character of K^+ obtained by restricting χ_u, and let D^S(χ), D(χ) be the normalizing factors of (108). Let U_{p,κ} = ∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_{j=1}^n U_{w,j,κ}, where U_{w,j,κ} = |κ'(t_{w,j})|_p^{-1} U_{w,j} is the κ-normalized U-operator attached to the double coset U_{w,j} = K_r t^+_{w,j} K_r of (23) (the index i of (23) is superfluous since G is the similitude group of a single hermitian space). The ordinary projector is the operator e_κ = lim_{N→∞} U_{p,κ}^{N!}   (111).
items.note: The paper says 'with notation as in (23)', but (23) defines only the unnormalized U_{w,i,j}; U_{w,j,κ} = |κ'(t_{w,j})|_p^{-1}U_{w,j} is defined only in §6.6 (p. 98) (sourceIssues E79, introduced in v5: in v2–v4 e_κ was defined in §6.5.6/§6.6.6 after the U_{w,j,κ}). In Definition 5.3.2 e_κ is applied to forms on G_3, through the G_1-factor (the t^+_{w,j} have similitude 1, so (t^+_{w,j},1) ∈ G_3(Q_p)). The limit exists on p-adically complete modules (Hida). Recalled as 'the definition (111)' in §6.6.6. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Definition 5.3.2 — axiomatic Eisenstein measure
items.statement: Let K_i^p ⊂ G_i(A_f^p), i = 3, 4, be open compact with K_3^p ⊂ K_4^p ∩ G_3(A_f^p), and let S be the set of primes at which K_4^p and K_3^p do not contain a hyperspecial maximal compact subgroup. An axiomatic Eisenstein measure on X_p × T_H(Z_p) of level S, relative to the set Y_H^class, of level K_4^p and with coefficients in R is a measure dEis on X_p × T_H(Z_p) with values in V(K_3^p, R) (p-adic modular forms on G_3 of tame level K_3^p) such that for every pair (χ = ||•||^m · χ_u, c = ψρ^υ) ∈ Y_H^class, with κ = κ(χ,c) the weight of (110), there is a factorizable Siegel section f(χ,c) = ⊗'_v f_v(χ_v, c) ∈ ⊗'_v I_v(χ_{u,v}, m) such that: (1) if v is a finite place, v ∤ p, outside S (χ_v being unramified for all χ ∈ Y_H^class, which requires S to contain the primes dividing N_0), then f_v(χ_v,c) is the unramified vector in I_v(χ_{u,v}, m) with f_v(χ_v,c)(1) = 1; (2) if v ∈ S, then f_v(χ_v,c) is independent of the pair (χ,c); (3) for every prime w | p and every archimedean place σ ∈ Σ_w, the local section f_σ(χ_σ,c) depends only on χ_σ^class and κ_w (and on the choice of signature), and has the form f_σ(χ_σ,c,g) = B(χ_σ,κ_σ) D(κ_σ,m,χ_{u,σ}) J_{m,χ_{u,σ}}(g), g ∈ G_{4,σ}, where J_{m,χ_{u,σ}} ∈ C^∞(G_{4,σ}) is the canonical automorphy factor of §4.4.2 (it depends only on χ_σ, Remark 4.4.3), D(κ_σ,m,χ_{u,σ}) = D(κ_σ,χ_σ) = δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) is the differential operator of Corollary 4.4.9, and B(χ_σ,κ_σ) ∈ Q̄^×; in particular f_σ(χ_σ,c,g) does not depend on the factorization of χ_σ; (4) for every prime w | p, the local section f_w(χ_w,c) depends only on χ_w and ψ_w (and on the choice of signature); (5) e_κ ∘ ∫_{X_p×T_H(Z_p)} (χ,c) dEis = D^S(χ) · e_κ ∘ res_3 E_{f(χ,c)} for all (χ,c) ∈ Y_H^class, where D^S(χ) = ∏_{v∉S} D_v(χ), D_v(χ) = ∏_{r=0}^{n−1} L_v(2m+n−r, χ^+ η^r) (η = η_{K/K^+}) is the normalizing factor (108), res_3 is the restriction (45) from G_4 to G_3, and e_κ is the ordinary projector (111).
items.note: Corrections (sourceIssues E84): the paper's condition (1) reads 'If v is a finite place outside S – so in particular χ_v is unramified for all χ ∈ Y_H^class – then …'. Since S consists of primes away from p, this literally includes v | p, contradicting (4) and the ramified sections at p of §4.3; and unramifiedness of χ_v outside S is not implied by the definition of S (characters of X_{p,N_0} may ramify at primes dividing N_0). κ is the weight attached to (χ,c) by (97) (sourceIssues E80). The paper writes J_{m,χ_{0,σ}} in the explanatory clause and D(κ_σ,m,χ_{u,σ}) for Corollary 4.4.9's D(κ_σ,χ_σ) (sourceIssues E86). The prose before the definition says dEis takes values in p-adic modular forms on G_4; in the definition its values are already restricted to G_3 (V(K_3^p,R)), consistent with Corollary 8.2.4. The ordinary projector in (5) is new in v5: v4 (Definition 5.3.2, p. 82) had ∫(χ,c)dEis = D^S(χ)·res_3 E_{f(χ,c)}. The local choices of §§4.2.1, 4.2.2, 4.3, 4.5 satisfy the conditions (p. 85); the measure of Theorem 8.2.2 satisfies them by Corollary 8.2.4 (shift (1,χ)); Lemma 9.1.5 deduces the equivariance Assumption 7.4.4 from them.the former section summary 'restriction-measures' is split into this item and the items of §§5.1–5.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1 — Eisenstein measure normalized at S; the notation D^?(χ)
items.statement: The measure dEis is normalized at S if, instead of condition (5) of Definition 5.3.2, one has e_κ ∘ ∫_{X_p×T_H(Z_p)} (χ,c) dEis = D(χ) · e_κ ∘ res_3 E_{f(χ,c)} for all (χ,c) ∈ Y_H^class, where D(χ) = D^∅(χ) = ∏_v D_v(χ) (product over all finite places). One writes D^?(χ), ? = S or ? = ∅, when it is not specified whether dEis is normalized.
items.note: Corrected (sourceIssues E83): the paper prints ∫(χ,c)dEis = D(χ)·res_3E_{f(χ,c)} without e_κ — a leftover from v4, where condition (5) had no e_κ; (113) uses e_κ on both sides with D^?(χ). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1 — Eisenstein measure with shift (α,β)
items.statement: The measure dEis is said to have shift (α,β) if it satisfies (109), i.e. (reading (109) weight by weight, or in the two-variable form of §5.2.2 with sh^*(χ) = (α(χ),β(χ))) its specializations at χ and ρ^υ take values in V^ord_{ρ^△·(α,β)}(K_3^p, ψ^△_χ, R[χ]). Definition 5.3.2 makes no mention of a shift; the Eisenstein measure of §8.2 comes with the shift specified in Corollary 8.2.4 (shift (1,χ)).
items.note: (109) is formulated for measures on X_p of fixed weight ρ; the paper does not spell out how it applies to a measure on X_p × T_H(Z_p). v4 (p. 82) referred to Corollary 5.4.3 (the Eisenstein measure was then in §5.4). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1 — normalizing at S by multiplying by the Euler factors at S
items.statement: One obtains a measure normalized at S from an unnormalized one by multiplying by the product of the local Euler factors at S, i.e. by χ ↦ D(χ)/D^S(χ) = ∏_{v∈S} ∏_{r=0}^{n−1} L_v(2m+n−r, χ^+ η^r).
items.note: Asserted without proof. For v ∈ S at which χ is unramified, L_v(2m+n−r, χ^+η^r) = (1 − η^r(ϖ_v) q_v^{r−n} χ(ϖ_v))^{-1} (χ evaluated at the idèle ϖ_v of K^+), the evaluation at χ of the inverse of 1 − η^r(ϖ_v) q_v^{r−n}[ϖ_v] ∈ Λ_{X_p}; this element need not be a unit of the Iwasawa algebra, so in general the product is only a pseudo-measure (sourceIssues E82). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §5.3.1 — the local sections of Part II satisfy Definition 5.3.2; existence of the measure
items.statement: The factorizable sections f(χ,c) chosen in §4.2.1 (v ∉ S), §4.2.2 (v ∈ S), §4.5 (archimedean places) and §4.3 (v | p) satisfy the conditions of Definition 5.3.2; the choices at p and at ∞ depend on the signature of G_1. The existence of the Eisenstein measure corresponding to these choices is proved in [Eis15, Eis12] (Theorem 8.2.2, Corollary 8.2.4). In the applications, the integrals of the elements of Y_H^class against dEis determine dEis completely.
items.note: Cited; the verification is carried out in §8.2 (Corollary 8.2.4, proved by comparison with Proposition 8.1.3). The last sentence (density of Y_H^class) is not proved here. The section numbers cited (4.2.1, 4.2.2, 4.3, 4.5) are correct in v5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (112) — the holomorphic section f^holo and the Eisenstein series E^holo
items.statement: For (χ = ||•||^m χ_u, c) ∈ Y_H^class put f^holo(χ,c) = ⊗_{σ∈Σ} J_{m,χ_{u,σ}} ⊗ ⊗_{v∤∞} f_v(χ_v, c), and E^holo_{χ_u,c}(m) = E_{f^holo(χ_u,c)}(m)   (112), the Siegel Eisenstein series on G_4 attached to f^holo, at s = m.
items.note: The paper indexes the archimedean factors by σ ∈ Σ_F (Σ_F = Hom(F,C), F the reflex field); the archimedean places of G_4 are indexed by the CM type Σ (sourceIssues E86). It writes both f^holo(χ,c) and f^holo(χ_u,c) for the same section. Same in v4 (5.3.2), p. 83. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (113) — the interpolation property rewritten with E^holo
items.statement: Condition (5) of Definition 5.3.2 (and its normalized version) is equivalent to e_κ ∘ ∫_{X_p×T_H(Z_p)} (χ,c) dEis = D^?(χ) · (∏_{σ∈Σ} B(χ_σ,κ_σ)) · e_κ ∘ res_3 D(κ,m,χ_u) E^holo_{χ_u,c}(m) for all (χ = ||•||^m χ_u, c) ∈ Y_H^class   (113), where D(κ,m,χ_u) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} D(κ_σ,χ_σ) is the differential operator of Corollary 4.4.9, acting on the archimedean components.
items.note: Follows from condition (3), since the differential operator D(κ,m,χ_u) commutes with forming the Eisenstein series. The printed (113) omits the scalar ∏_σ B(χ_σ,κ_σ) (sourceIssues E85), and so is correct exactly when B ≡ 1, which is how it is used in §9 (e.g. D(χ)·L(res_3 D(κ,m,χ_0)E^holo) in the proof of Theorem 9.2.2). v4 (5.3.3) had the same formula without e_κ and without B. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.1 — the Shimura variety Sh(V) = lim_K M_{K,L}
items.statement: Let P = (K, c, O, L, ⟨·,·⟩, h) be a PEL datum of unitary type attached to a hermitian pair (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V) as in §§2.1–2.3, with m = 1 factor (the index i is dropped). Let G = G_P (a group scheme over Z; G(A_f) = GU(V)(A_f)), X = X_P the G(R)-conjugacy class of h, Z_G the centre of G, and take □ = ∅ (moduli problems over the reflex field F). For open compact K ⊂ G(A_f), _KSh(V) is the Shimura variety of the datum (G,X) at level K, i.e. the F-scheme M_{K,L}, and Sh(V) := lim_K _KSh(V) = lim_K M_{K,L}.
items.note: Footnote 12: if a_σ b_σ = 0 for all σ ∈ Σ_K (definite case), (G,X) does not satisfy Deligne's axioms [Del79], but the 'Shimura variety' still makes sense following [Lan12] because (G,X) comes from a PEL datum. Planned: ShimuraVarieties V8 plans the algebraic tower; PELModuli M3 plans the complex comparison and the ker¹(Q, G)-indexed decomposition into Shimura varieties.

items.name: §6.1 — dimension of _KSh(V)
items.statement: Each _KSh(V) has dimension dim_C X = d = (1/2) Σ_{σ∈Σ_K} a_σ b_σ (= Σ_{σ∈Σ} a_σ b_σ, where (a_σ, b_σ) is the signature at σ and a_{σc} = b_σ).
items.note: Standard: X is a product over σ ∈ Σ of hermitian symmetric domains of U(a_σ,b_σ), of dimension a_σ b_σ; d = dim p_h^+ = dim p_h^-. Planned: ShimuraVarieties V1 plans the analytic tower; ShimuraData D2 plans real reductive groups and hermitian domains.

items.name: §6.1 — Sh(−V), the datum P^c and the groups G_1, G_2
items.statement: Sh(−V) is the Shimura variety of the hermitian pair (V, −⟨·,·⟩_V), with PEL datum P^c = (K, c, O, L, −⟨·,·⟩, h^c), h^c(z) = h(z̄). Objects attached to (V,⟨·,·⟩_V) (resp. (V,−⟨·,·⟩_V)) receive a subscript V (resp. −V) when the notation does not already distinguish them. G_1 = GU(V), G_2 = GU(−V) as in §3.1; canonically G_{P^c} = G_P = G.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.1.1 — automorphic vector bundles and canonical models
items.statement: Automorphic vector bundles on Sh(V) = Sh(G,X) are given by a ⊗-functor G-Bun(X̂) → Bun(Sh(V)), where X̂ is the compact dual (a flag variety for G) and G-Bun is the ⊗-category of G-equivariant vector bundles. The base point h determines P_h ∈ X̂, the stabilizer of the Hodge filtration on L ⊗ R, and a fibre functor G-Bun(X̂) → Rep_C(P_h) ≅ Rep_C(P_0) (identifications of §2.6.1). For an irreducible representation W of P_0 factoring through the Levi quotient H_0, ω_W is the corresponding automorphic vector bundle; it has a canonical model over a number field F(W) ⊃ F contained in K'. For W = W_κ (the H_0-representation of highest weight κ of §2.6.3; W_κ := W_κ(C)), the bundle ω_κ of §2.6.4 is the base change to K' of the canonical model of ω_{W_κ}. The ω_κ, defined over the toroidal compactifications, are the canonical extensions of the automorphic vector bundles, and their twists by the ideal sheaves of the boundary are the subcanonical extensions.
items.note: Recalled without proof (theory of canonical models and canonical extensions of Harris/Milne; cf. [Har90]). The comparison of the ω_κ of §2.6.4 (defined through the H_0-torsor E) with the canonical models is asserted. Planned: AutomorphicBundles B1 plans canonical principal bundles; AutomorphicBundles B2 plans automorphic vector bundles attached to representations of the Levi.

items.name: §6.1.2 — coherent cohomology H^i(Sh(V),ω_κ), subcanonical version, interior cohomology H^i_!
items.statement: H^i(Sh(V), ω_κ) := lim_{K,Σ} H^i(_KSh(V)_Σ, ω_κ), the limit over toroidal compactifications _KSh(V)_Σ at finite levels K; H^i(Sh(V), ω_κ^sub) := lim_{K,Σ} H^i(_KSh(V)_Σ, ω_κ(−D_Σ)), with boundary D_Σ = _KSh(V)_Σ − _KSh(V); and H^i_!(Sh(V), ω_κ) := im{H^i(Sh(V), ω_κ^sub) → H^i(Sh(V), ω_κ)}. For i = 0 the compactification is superfluous by Koecher's principle, except possibly when n = 2 and F = Q. The ground field may be any extension of K', and the definitions make sense over O_{K',(p')} for levels K = G(Z_p)K^p or K = I_r K^p.
items.note: The paper writes 'H^i(Sh(V),ω_κ) instead of H^0(Sh(V)^tor,ω_κ)'; H^0 is a misprint for H^i (sourceIssues E87). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicBundles B3 plans canonical and subcanonical extensions and independence of the fan.

items.name: §6.1.2 — Harish-Chandra decomposition, P_h and K_h
items.statement: g = Lie(G(R))_C = p_h^- ⊕ k_h ⊕ p_h^+ is the Harish-Chandra decomposition attached to h (eigenspace decomposition for ad h(√−1)); P_h := p_h^- ⊕ k_h = Lie(P_h(R))_C (the Lie algebra of P_h(C)); K_h := U_∞ = C(R), the centralizer of h in G(R). Via P_h(C) ≅ P_0(C) and C(C) ≅ H_0(C), W_κ is a (P_h, K_h)-module (p_h^- acting trivially). dim p_h^± = d.
items.note: §2.7.2 (p. 28) says instead that G(C) ≅ G_0(C) identifies Lie(P_0(C)) with k ⊕ p^+, whereas §6.1.3 (p. 88) identifies Lie(P_0(C)) with P_h = p_h^- ⊕ k_h (sourceIssues E90). §6 consistently uses P_h = p^- ⊕ k: holomorphic forms are annihilated by p_h^-, the holomorphic tangent space is p_h^+, the canonical bundle is Hom(∧^d p_h^+, C). Planned: ShimuraData D2 plans real reductive groups and hermitian domains; AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 plans (g, K)-modules.

items.name: (114) — interior coherent cohomology as (P_h,K_h)-cohomology of cusp forms
items.statement: Let A_0(G) be the space of cusp forms on G(A). Over C there is a natural identification of G(A_f)-modules H^i_!(Sh(V), ω_κ) = H^i(P_h, K_h; A_0(G) ⊗ W_κ)   (114), for i = 0 and i = d (the paper states it for all i). For i = 0 it restates the identification (§2.7.2) of S_κ(K,C) with the space of U_∞ × K-invariant smooth functions f : G(A) → W_κ annihilated by p_h^-.
items.note: Stated for all i without proof or reference. [Har90] embeds cuspidal (P_h,K_h)-cohomology into interior coherent cohomology; equality is clear for i = 0 and follows for i = d by Serre duality — the only degrees used in the paper (sourceIssues E88). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.1.3, (115)–(116) — the ⋆ involution on weights; the integer a(κ)
items.statement: There is an anti-holomorphic involution ⋆ of G-Bun(X̂) taking a G-equivariant bundle to its complex conjugate. On representations of P_0 factoring through H_0 (identified over C with the stabilizer C of h in G_{/R}) it takes W_κ to W_{κ^⋆}, whose restriction to the maximal compact subgroup of U_∞ = C(R) ⊂ H_0(C) is dual to that of W_κ and whose restriction to R^× ⊂ G(R) coincides with that of W_κ. For κ = (κ_0, (κ_σ)_{σ∈Σ_K}), κ_σ = (κ_{σ,1}, …, κ_{σ,b_σ}): κ^⋆ = (κ^⋆_0, (κ^⋆_σ)), κ^⋆_0 = −κ_0 + a(κ), κ^⋆_σ = (−κ_{σ,b_σ}, …, −κ_{σ,1})   (115), and W_{κ^⋆} ≅ W_κ^∨ ⊗ ν^{a(κ)}, where a(κ) = 2κ_0 + Σ_{σ∈Σ_K} Σ_{j=1}^{b_σ} κ_{σ,j}   (116).
items.note: a(κ) is the exponent of the central character: t ∈ R^× ⊂ G(R) corresponds under (15) to (t^2, (t·1_{b_σ})) ∈ H_0, so acts on W_κ by t^{a(κ)} and on W_κ^∨ ⊗ ν^{a(κ)} by t^{−a(κ)+2a(κ)} = t^{a(κ)} (checked). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.1.3 — the c-semilinear K_h-equivariant isomorphism φ ↦ φ^⋆ : W_κ → W_{κ^⋆}
items.statement: There is a unique (up to scalar) c-semilinear, K_h-equivariant isomorphism W_κ ≅ W_{κ^⋆}. In the model W_κ = {φ : H_0 → C : φ(bx) = κ(b)φ(x), b ∈ B_{H_0}} of §2.6.3, writing h ∈ H_0(C) as (h_0, (h_σ)) ∈ C^× × ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} GL_{b_σ}(C) via (15), one such isomorphism is φ ↦ φ^⋆, φ^⋆(h) = h_0^{a(κ)} · conj(φ((h̄_0^{-1}, (w_σ ᵗh̄_σ^{-1})))) (conj = complex conjugation of the value), where w_σ ∈ GL_{b_σ}(C) is the longest element of the Weyl group and ¯ is complex conjugation. Since G(C) ≅ G_0(C) identifies Lie(P_0(C)) with P_h and Lie(H_0(C)) with k_h, φ ↦ φ^⋆ is P_h-equivariant up to c-semilinearity.
items.note: 'The K_h-invariance follows easily from (17)': verified — for k ∈ U_∞, (17) (h_0 ᵗh̄_σ^{-1} = h_σ) gives (k̄_0^{-1}, (ᵗk̄_σ^{-1})) = k·z with z the central element (k_0^{-2}, (k_0^{-1})) (the scalar k_0^{-1}), which acts on W_κ by k_0^{-a(κ)} and cancels the factor h_0^{a(κ)}. φ^⋆ ∈ W_{κ^⋆} was checked on the torus. Uniqueness: Schur's lemma, U_∞ being Zariski-dense in H_0(C). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.1.3 — the characters κ_h^± of Hom(∧^d p_h^±, C) and the Serre-dual weight κ^D
items.statement: The element h = (h_0, (h_σ)) ∈ H_0(C) acts on the line Hom_C(∧^d p_h^±, C) by multiplication by h_0^{∓d} ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} det(h_σ)^{±a_σ}, i.e. by the character κ_h^± = (∓d, (κ^±_{h,σ})), κ^±_{h,σ} = (±a_σ, …, ±a_σ) ∈ Z^{b_σ}. The H_0(C)-representation Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, W_{κ^⋆}) = Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, C) ⊗_C W_{κ^⋆} is identified with W_{κ^D}, κ^D := κ^⋆ + κ_h^+ (the identification depends on a choice of basis of the line ∧^d p_h^-); thus W_{κ^D} ≅ Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, C) ⊗ W_κ^∨ ⊗ ν^{a(κ)}.
items.note: Corrected (sourceIssues E89): the paper prints det(h_σ)^{±2a_σ} and κ^±_{h,σ} = (±2a_σ, …, ±2a_σ). With ±2a_σ the character is non-trivial (t^{±2d}) on the centre R^×, impossible for a character of ∧^d of a piece of the adjoint representation; the direct computation (p_h^± ≅ ⊕_{σ∈Σ} Hom between Λ_{0,σ} and Λ^∨_{0,σ}, with h acting on Λ^∨_{0,σ} by h_σ and on Λ_{0,σ} by h_0 ᵗh_{σc}^{-1}) gives the exponents ±a_σ; for the modular curve (U(1,1), d = 1) it gives the weight-2 canonical bundle. The overall sign pattern (∓d, ±a_σ) is the paper's; it matches the §2.7.2 identification Lie(P_0) = k ⊕ p^+ and flips under the §6.1.3 identification Lie(P_0) = P_h (sourceIssues E90). The arguments of §§6.2–6.5 use only the intrinsic W_{κ^D} = Hom(∧^d p_h^+, W_{κ^⋆}). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.1.3 — the inclusion i_{κ^⋆} : W_{κ^⋆} ↪ Hom(∧^d p_h^-, W_{κ^D})
items.statement: The Killing form on g defines an H_0(C)-equivariant contraction ∧^d p_h^- ⊗_C ∧^d p_h^+ → C, hence an H_0(C)-equivariant inclusion i_{κ^⋆} : W_{κ^⋆} ↪ Hom_C(∧^d p_h^- ⊗_C ∧^d p_h^+, W_{κ^⋆}) = Hom_C(∧^d p_h^-, W_{κ^D}).
items.note: Used in (117) and (122). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.1, (117)–(119) — complex conjugation c_B on automorphic forms
items.statement: Let π be a (g,K_h) × G(A_f)-representation occurring in A_0(G) and π̄ the complex conjugate representation (the functions φ̄(g) = conj(φ(g)), φ ∈ π); φ ↦ φ̄ is c-semilinear, K_h × G(A_f)-equivariant and g-equivariant up to c-semilinearity. The c-semilinear G(A_f)-equivariant map (π ⊗_C W_κ)^{K_h} → (π̄ ⊗_C W_{κ^⋆})^{K_h} → Hom_C(∧^d p_h^-, π̄ ⊗_C W_{κ^D})^{K_h}, φ ⊗ ϕ ↦ φ̄ ⊗ ϕ^⋆ followed by id ⊗ i_{κ^⋆}   (117), induces a c-semilinear G(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism c_B : H^0(P_h, K_h; π ⊗_C W_κ) → H^d(P_h, K_h; π̄ ⊗_C W_{κ^D})   (118). Taking π = A_0(G) (so π̄ = π) gives a c-semilinear G(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism c_B : H^0_!(Sh(V), ω_κ) ≅ H^d_!(Sh(V), ω_{κ^D})   (119).
items.note: Corrected (sourceIssues E91): (117) prints Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, ⊗ π̄ ⊗_C W_{κ^D})^{K_h}; the target of i_{κ^⋆} is Hom_C(∧^d p_h^-, W_{κ^D}), and top-degree (P_h,K_h)-cochains are K_h-maps from ∧^d p_h^-. The isomorphism in (118) is asserted: conjugation takes p_h^- -invariant vectors of π to p_h^+-invariant vectors of π̄, whose images in top-degree cochains represent H^d. (119) uses (114) in degrees 0 and d. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.2 — the anti-holomorphic identification X_h ≅ X ≅ X_{h^c}
items.statement: P^c = (K, c, O, L, −⟨·,·⟩, h^c), h^c(z) = h(z̄), is the PEL datum of (V, −⟨·,·⟩_V), with reflex field F_{−V} = cF_V = cF; canonically G_{P^c} = G_P = G, and the stabilizers of h and h^c in G(R) coincide: K_h = U_∞ = K_{h^c}. With X := G(R)/U_∞, the identifications X ≅ X_h = X_P (g ↦ ghg^{-1}) and X ≅ X_{h^c} = X_{P^c} (g ↦ gh^cg^{-1}) pull back complex-conjugate complex structures, so X_h ≅ X ≅ X_{h^c} is anti-holomorphic; a holomorphic function on X_{h^c} defines an anti-holomorphic function on X_h and vice versa. The Harish-Chandra decompositions satisfy p_h^± = p_{h^c}^∓ and k_h = k_{h^c}.
items.note: Explains the map F_∞ of (124). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.2, (120) — H_{0,−V}, the identification H_{0,V} = H_{0,−V}, and κ^♭
items.statement: The automorphic sheaves on Sh(−V) come from representations of H_{0,−V}, canonically identified with H_{0,V} = H_0 by switching the roles of Λ_0 and Λ_0^∨. The analogue of (15) is H_{0,−V/S_0} ≅ G_m × ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} GL_{O⊗O,σ}(Λ_{0,σ}) ≅ G_m × ∏_{σ∈Σ_K} GL_{a_σ}(S_0)   (120), and the identification H_{0,V} = H_{0,−V} is (h_0, (h_σ)) ↦ (h_0, (h_0 ᵗh_{σc}^{-1})). A dominant character κ of the diagonal torus T_{H_{0,−V}} gives W_{κ,−V} and ω_{κ,−V} on Sh(−V). For a dominant character κ = (κ_0, (κ_σ)) of T_{H_{0,V}}, κ^♭ := (κ_0, (κ_{σc})) is a dominant character of T_{H_{0,−V}}.
items.note: Consistent with (15): h ∈ H_0 acts on Λ_{0,σ} ≅ Hom(Λ^∨_{0,σc}, Z(1)) by h_0 ᵗh_{σc}^{-1}, and rank Λ_{0,σ} = a_σ = b_{σc}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (121) — the identification W_{κ^♭,−V} ≅ W_{κ^⋆,V}
items.statement: With respect to H_{0,−V} = H_{0,V}, there is an explicit identification of H_0-representations W_{κ^♭,−V} ≅ W_{κ^⋆,V}, φ ↦ ((h_0, (h_σ)) ↦ φ((h_0, (w_σ h_0 ᵗh_{σc}^{-1}))))   (121).
items.note: The paper prints '(h, (h_σ)) ↦' for '(h_0, (h_σ)) ↦' (sourceIssues E92). Checked: with j(y) = (y_0, (y_0 ᵗy_{σc}^{-1})) the identification, the map is equivariant for right translation, left B-equivariance holds, and on the torus κ^♭(t_0, (w_σ t_0 t_{σc}^{-1} w_σ^{-1})) = κ^⋆(t) (t_0-exponent κ_0 + ΣΣκ_{σ,j} = a(κ) − κ_0). Referred to in §4.4 (p. 70) as 'an explicit formula for κ^♭ in (121)' and in §5.2.1 for ρ^♭. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.2, (122)–(124) — the C-linear isomorphism F_∞ (no complex conjugation)
items.statement: For π a (g,K_h) × G(A_f)-representation occurring in the automorphic forms on G(A), the natural map (π^{p^-_{h^c}} ⊗_C W_{κ^♭,−V})^{K_{h^c}} = (π^{p^+_h} ⊗_C W_{κ^⋆,V})^{K_h} → Hom_C(∧^d p_h^-, π ⊗ W_{κ^D,V})^{K_h} (via id ⊗ i_{κ^⋆})   (122) induces a C-linear G(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism F_∞ : H^0(P_{h^c}, K_{h^c}; π ⊗_C W_{κ^♭,−V}) → H^d(P_h, K_h; π ⊗_C W_{κ^D,V})   (123); for π = A_0(G) it gives a C-linear G(A_f)-equivariant isomorphism F_∞ : H^0_!(Sh(−V), ω_{κ^♭,−V}) ≅ H^d_!(Sh(V), ω_{κ^D,V})   (124). No complex conjugation is involved: F_∞ identifies a class on G_2 represented by a holomorphic modular form with a class on G_1 represented by an anti-holomorphic one, because G_1 = G_2 canonically while the hermitian symmetric domains have opposite complex structures.
items.note: Uses p_h^± = p_{h^c}^∓ and (121). The isomorphism property is asserted as for c_B. §6.5.1 uses F_∞ to identify anti-holomorphic representations of G_2 with holomorphic ones of G_1 and vice versa. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.3 — the standard K-basis, the involution I and the automorphism g ↦ ḡ
items.statement: Since h is standard (§2.3.2), V has a K-basis in which ⟨·,·⟩_V is a diagonal matrix D = diag(d_1, …, d_n), d_i ∈ K^+, and the image of h is diagonal in the induced bases of V_σ = V ⊗_{K,σ} C. If every prime of K^+ above p splits in K, the K-basis and the lattice L can be chosen so that D also diagonalizes the perfect hermitian pairing on L ⊗ Z_(p); such choices are fixed. Let I : V → V be the K^+-linear involution acting by c on the coordinates; L ⊗ Z_(p) is I-stable and I on L ⊗ Z_p interchanges L^+ and L^-. In the fixed basis G_{/Q} ⊂ Res_{K/Q} GL_n(K), and c induces an automorphism g ↦ ḡ = IgI of G_{/Q}, which takes h to h^c and preserves U_∞. The composite X_h ≅ X → X ≅ X_{h^c}, ghg^{-1} ↦ ḡ h^c ḡ^{-1}, is holomorphic; hence the induced map Sh(V)(C) → Sh(−V)(C) is holomorphic and a morphism of Shimura varieties over C.
items.note: The paper writes 'g^c = IgI' for ḡ. The existence of the simultaneous diagonalization at p is asserted. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.3, (125) — the element δ_p ∈ G(Q_p) modifying conjugation at p
items.statement: For w | p fix L_w = L_w^+ ⊕ L_w^- and O_w-bases of L_w^± (§2.2); level structures at p for P^c are defined by L_w^{c,±} = L_w^±, so that I^0_{w,−V} = ᵗI^0_{w,V} = ᵗ(I^0_{w,V})^{-1} in this O_w-basis. Let β_w ∈ GL_{K_w}(V ⊗_K K_w) ≅ GL_n(K_w) take the K_w-basis induced by the fixed K-basis to the fixed O_w-basis of L_w, and, with D the Gram matrix of ⟨·,·⟩_V in the fixed K-basis (G acting on column vectors, so ḡ_w = ν(g) D^{-1} ᵗg_w^{-1} D), let δ_p = (1, (D^{-1} ᵗβ_w^{-1} β_w^{-1})_{w∈Σ_p}) ∈ Q_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} GL_n(K_w) ≅ G(Q_p) (isomorphism determined by the fixed K-basis). Then δ̄_p = δ_p^{-1}, δ_p^{-1} conj(G(Z_p)) δ_p = G(Z_p), and δ_p^{-1} Ī^0_{r,V} δ_p = I^0_{r,−V}   (125); indeed δ_p^{-1} ḡ δ_p = ν(g)·ᵗg'^{-1} in O_w-coordinates g' = β_w^{-1} g_w β_w.
items.note: The paper prints δ_p = (1, D ᵗβ_w^{-1} β_w^{-1}) and states (125) without proof ('Then'). With the Gram-matrix convention the printed δ_p gives δ̄_p = δ_p^{-1} only when D^2 commutes with β_w ᵗβ_w, and δ_p^{-1}ḡδ_p = ν(g)·u ᵗg'^{-1} u^{-1} with u = ᵗβ_w D^{-2} ᵗβ_w^{-1}, which need not normalize the Iwahori ᵗI^0; the printed formula is right if D denotes the matrix of the dual pairing (or G acts on row vectors), or if β_w is diagonal (sourceIssues E93). The middle identity holds for either choice (δ_p ∈ G(Z_p) when the d_i are p-units). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.3, (126) — the automorphism g ↦ g^† and the levels K^†
items.statement: Define the automorphism g ↦ g^† of G(A) by g^† = ν(g)^{-1} δ_p^{-1} ḡ δ_p, and for K ⊂ G(A_f) let K^† be the image of K under †. If K = G(Z_p)K^p then K^† = G(Z_p)·(K^p)^† with (K^p)^† = {ν(k)^{-1} k̄ : k ∈ K^p}; this equals G(Z_p)K̄^p when K^p contains the scalars ν(k)^{-1}, k ∈ K^p (e.g. for principal congruence subgroups). Moreover (K_{r,V})^† = K^†_{r,−V}   (126), and the map Sh(V)(C) → Sh(−V)(C) induced by g ↦ ḡδ_p identifies _{K_{r,V}}Sh(V) with _{K^†_{r,−V}}Sh(−V).
items.note: The paper states K^† = G(Z_p)K̄^p 'as a consequence of (125)' without the condition on scalars (sourceIssues E94); the level actually matched by g ↦ ḡδ_p and by the moduli description of Proposition 6.2.4 is G(Z_p)K̄^p. On G(R), g^† = ν(g)^{-1}ḡ, and † is an involution there. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 6.2.4 — the isomorphism _{K_{r,V}}Sh(V) ≅ _{K^†_{r,−V}}Sh(−V) on moduli problems
items.statement: The isomorphism _{K_{r,V}}Sh(V) ≅ _{K^†_{r,−V}}Sh(−V) is defined over O_{K',(p')}. On moduli problems it sends a tuple (A, λ, ι, α, φ) classified by M_{P,K_r,L}(R) to the tuple (A, λ, ι ∘ c, α ∘ I, φ ∘ I) classified by M_{P^c,K_r^†,L}(R), for any O_{K',(p')}-algebra R.
items.note: 'The following Proposition is then obvious'; no proof. Plausibility check: I is c-semilinear, so α ∘ I is O-linear for ι ∘ c; since ⟨Ix, Iy⟩_V is the complex conjugate of ⟨x, y⟩_V, the alternating form attached to ⟨·,·⟩_V changes sign under I, matching −⟨·,·⟩ in P^c. Unchanged from v4 (p. 90). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.3 — κ^† and the map φ ↦ φ^† : W_{κ,V} → W_{κ^†,−V}
items.statement: g ↦ g^† takes p_h^± to p_{h^c}^± and P_h to P_{h^c}; its action on K_h is, via (17), (h_0, (h_σ)) ↦ (h_0^{-1}, (ᵗh_σ^{-1})). Let κ^† := κ^♭ · ||ν||^{-a(κ)} (i.e. κ^†_0 = κ_0 − a(κ), κ^†_σ = κ_{σc}), so that W_{κ^†,−V} ≅ W_{κ^∨,V} ≅ W_{κ,V}^∨, κ^∨ = (−κ_0, (−κ_{σ,b_σ}, …, −κ_{σ,1})). The map W_{κ,V} → W_{κ^†,−V} = W_{κ^♭,−V} ⊗ ||ν||^{-a(κ)}, φ ↦ φ^†, φ^†((h_0, (h_σ))) = φ((h_0, (h_{σc}))) · h_0^{-a(κ)}, satisfies (k^† · φ)^† = k · φ^† for all k ∈ K_{h^c} = K_h. Hence under the isomorphism Sh(V) ≅ Sh(−V) defined by g ↦ g^†, ω_{κ^†,−V} pulls back to ω_{κ,V}.
items.note: Checked: φ^† ∈ W_{κ^†,−V} (torus weight (κ_0 − a(κ), (κ_{σc}))), and κ^† pulled back along H_{0,V} = H_{0,−V} is κ^∨. The equivariance was checked for signature (1,1) over an imaginary quadratic field, where k^† = k^{-1} for k ∈ U_∞. Here ||ν||^{-a(κ)} is used for the algebraic character ν^{-a(κ)}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.2.3, (127)–(130) — the C-linear isomorphisms F^†
items.statement: There are C-linear isomorphisms F^† : H^i_!(Sh(V), ω_{κ,V}) ≅ H^i_!(Sh(−V), ω_{κ^†,−V})   (127), G(A_f)-equivariant up to the automorphism †, inducing F^† : H^i_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_{κ,V}) ≅ H^i_!(_{K_r^†}Sh(−V), ω_{κ^†,−V})   (128) even over O_{K',(p')}-algebras R ⊂ C; in particular F^† : S_{κ,V}(K_{r,V}, ψ; R) ≅ S_{κ^†,−V}(K^†_{r,−V}, ψ^†; R)   (129) for R ⊂ C any O_{K',(p')}[ψ]-algebra, where ψ^† = ψ^{-1} when both are viewed as characters of the diagonal torus of the right side of (9) via the isomorphisms (10). In terms of automorphic forms: for π a (g,K_h) × G(A_f)-representation in the automorphic forms on G(A), π^† := {φ^†(g) = φ(g^†) : φ ∈ π}; π → π^† is C-linear and g- and K_h-equivariant up to †, and (π ⊗_C W_{κ,V})^{K_h} → (π^† ⊗_C W_{κ^†,−V})^{K_{h^c}}, φ ⊗ ϕ ↦ φ^† ⊗ ϕ^†, is a C-linear isomorphism intertwining the actions of g and g^†, g ∈ G(A_f); it induces F^† : H^i(P_h, K_h; π ⊗_C W_{κ,V}) ≅ H^i(P_{h^c}, K_{h^c}; π^† ⊗_C W_{κ^†,−V})   (130), which for π = A_0(G) (π^† = π) is the F^† of (127).
items.note: (128)–(129) over O_{K',(p')} rest on Proposition 6.2.4. ψ^† = ψ^{-1} reflects that † is transpose-inverse at p in the O_w-bases; not checked in detail. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.3, (131) — Serre duality between H^0_!(ω_κ) and H^d_!(ω_{κ^D})
items.statement: Since W_{κ^D} = Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, W_{κ^⋆}) ≅ Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, C) ⊗_C W_κ^∨ ⊗ ν^{a(κ)}, the contraction W_κ ⊗ W_κ^∨ → C gives an H_0(C)-homomorphism W_κ ⊗_C W_{κ^D} → Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, C) ⊗ ν^{a(κ)}, hence a map ω_κ ⊗ ω_{κ^D} → Ω^d_{Sh(V)} ⊗ L(κ), where L(κ) is the automorphic line bundle of the character ν^{a(κ)} (topologically the trivial bundle, ν^{a(κ)} being trivial on G^der, but with non-trivial G(A_f)-action). For a level K and a toroidal compactification _KSh(V) ↪ _KSh(V)_Σ this extends to pairings ω_κ ⊗ ω_{κ^D}^sub → Ω^d_{_KSh(V)_Σ} ⊗ L(κ) and ω_κ^can ⊗ ω_{κ^D} → Ω^d ⊗ L(κ). As in [Har90, Cor. 2.3], Serre duality then defines a perfect pairing H^0_!(Sh(V), ω_κ) ⊗ H^d_!(Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}) → lim_{K,Σ} H^d(_KSh(V)_Σ, Ω^d_{Sh(V)_Σ} ⊗ L(κ))   (131).
items.note: Cited from [Har90, Cor. 2.3]; perfectness on interior cohomology is not proved here. Ω^d is the automorphic bundle of Hom(∧^d p_h^+, C), p_h^+ being the holomorphic tangent space. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.3, (132) — the canonical Serre-duality pairing ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ
items.statement: The function g ↦ ||ν(g)||^{-a(κ)} defines a global section of L(κ)^∨ and therefore an isomorphism lim_{K,Σ} H^d(_KSh(V)_Σ, Ω^d ⊗ L(κ)) ≅ lim_{K,Σ} H^d(_KSh(V)_Σ, Ω^d). The right-hand side is identified by the trace map with the space C(π_0(V)) of functions on the compact space π_0(V) of similitude components of Sh(V); composing with the projection of C(π_0(V)) onto the invariant line C(π_0(V))^{G(A)} (integration over π_0(V) against an invariant measure of rational total mass) gives the canonical perfect pairing ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ : H^0_!(Sh(V), ω_κ) ⊗ H^d_!(Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}) → C   (132).
items.note: Whether g ↦ ||ν(g)||^{-a(κ)} is a section of L(κ)^∨ or of L(κ) depends on the convention for the U_∞-action; with §2.7.2's f(gu) = u^{-1}·f(g) it is a section of L(κ). §6 is internally consistent with the opposite convention (sourceIssues E97). The normalisation is made explicit in (133). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 6.3.1 — Tamagawa normalization of the Serre pairings
items.statement: In what follows the Tamagawa number (Tamagawa measure) is used to normalize the Serre-duality pairings; this is likely to introduce a factor of a power of 2 when comparing the results with those predicted by motivic conjectures.
items.note: Normalization convention; affects comparisons of the p-adic L-function with motivic predictions only up to powers of 2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.3, (133) — ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ in terms of automorphic forms and its normalization
items.statement: Let p = p_h^+ ⊕ p_h^-. ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ is the pairing H^0(P_h, K_h; A_0(G) ⊗ W_κ) ⊗ H^d(P_h, K_h; A_0(G) ⊗ W_{κ^D}) → C given by multiplication of cusp forms, contraction of coefficients and integration. Precisely: let dg be the Tamagawa measure, factored as dg = dg_∞ · dg_f with dg_f taking rational values on open compact subgroups of G(A_f) and dg_∞ = dk_h × dx × dt/t, where dk_h gives the compact group K_h/Z_G(R)^0 volume 1, dt/t is Haar measure on the split part of the centre of G(R) (≅ R_{>0}; it disappears in the integral) and dx is a basis of (∧^{2d} p)^∨ (rational over the reflex field of h). Let [ϕ, ϕ'] denote the contraction W_κ ⊗_C Hom_C(∧^d p_h^-, Hom_C(∧^d p_h^+, W_κ^∨ ⊗ ν^{a(κ)})) → Hom_C(∧^{2d} p, C(ν^{a(κ)})) and [ϕ, ϕ']_{dx} ∈ C(ν^{a(κ)}) its value identified via dx. For φ ∈ (A_0(G)^{p_h^-} ⊗_C W_κ)^{K_h} and φ' ∈ Hom_C(∧^d p_h^-, A_0(G) ⊗_C W_{κ^D})^{K_h}: ⟨φ, φ'⟩^Ser_κ = ∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)} [φ(g), φ'(g)] · ||ν(g)||^{-a(κ)} dg_f   (133) = ∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)} [φ(g), φ'(g)]_{dx} · ||ν(g)||^{-a(κ)} dg. The basis dx is fixed from now on and the subscript dx is omitted.
items.note: In the dg_f form, the top-degree form [φ,φ'] is integrated in the archimedean directions. Printed slips: 'dk_∞' vs 'dk_h … gives K_h measure 1' (K_h = U_∞ contains the non-compact R_{>0}), 'Lebesgue measure on the center Z_{G(R)} ≅ R^×' (the centre of G(R) is R_{>0} × (S^1)^{[K^+:Q]}), and 'It we use' (sourceIssues E95). v4 (6.3.3) used dg only. The sign of the exponent of ||ν|| depends on the convention of sourceIssues E97. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: (134) — the hermitian Petersson pairing
items.note: Sesquilinear because c_B is c-semilinear. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.4.1, (135)–(137) — the level-normalized Serre pairing ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r}
items.statement: For an open compact K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p) and K_r = K^p · I_r (I_r = I_{r,V}), define ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} : H^0_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ) ⊗ H^d_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}) → C   (135) by ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} = (1/Vol(I^0_{r,V})) ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ   (136), where the volume of I^0_r is taken with respect to the measure of (133). If φ and φ' are K_r-invariant, ⟨φ, φ'⟩_{κ,K_r} = (1/Vol(I^0_r)) ∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)} [φ(g), φ'(g)] · ||ν(g)||^{-a(κ)} dg   (137).
items.note: Purpose: ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ is canonical but not compatible with traces between levels (a failure of the right side of (133)). Printed slips: 'the volume Vol(I_r^0) of K_r^0', and ⟨φ,φ'⟩_{κ,K} in (137) for ⟨φ,φ'⟩_{κ,K_r} (sourceIssues E96). The normalization depends only on the p-part I_r of the level; I_r ⊂ I^0_r are the level subgroups at p (§2.5; cf. §8.3). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.4.1, (138) — compatibility of ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} with normalized traces
items.statement: If r' ≥ r, φ is K_r-invariant and φ' is K_{r'}-invariant, then ⟨φ, φ'⟩_{κ,K_{r'}} = ⟨φ, trace_{K_r/K_{r'}}(φ')⟩_{κ,K_r}, where trace_{K_r/K_{r'}}(φ') = (#(I^0_r/I_r) / #(I^0_{r'}/I_{r'})) Σ_{γ∈K_r/K_{r'}} γ · φ'   (138). The analogous relation holds for φ K_{r'}-invariant and φ' K_r-invariant.
items.note: Proof in the text: I_r/I_{r'} ≅ K_r/K_{r'} and Vol(I^0_r) = Vol(I^0_{r'}) · #(I^0_r/I^0_{r'}) = Vol(I^0_{r'}) · #(I_r/I_{r'}) · #(I^0_r/I_r)/#(I^0_{r'}/I_{r'}). Verified (uses the K_r-invariance of φ and of ||ν||, and I_{r'} ⊂ I_r ⊂ I^0_r, I_{r'} ⊂ I^0_{r'} ⊂ I^0_r). The paper writes 'φ' by K'_r' for K_{r'} (sourceIssues E96). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.4.2, (139) — integral structure on top-degree coherent cohomology by duality
items.statement: Let O_{K',(p')} be as in §2.6.3, fix V and write ω_κ = ω_{κ,V}. The O_{K',(p')}-structure on H^0_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_{κ,V}) is S_κ(K_r, O_{K',(p')}) (§§2.5, 2.6.5, 2.9). The O_{K',(p')}-structure on H^d_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}) is defined to be dual to it under ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r}: for every O_{K',(p')}-algebra R, H^d_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}, R) := Hom_{O_{K',(p')}}(S_κ(K_r, O_{K',(p')}), R)   (139), the identification being induced by ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r}.
items.note: Integral models of the schemes are deliberately not used (the special fibres become more singular as r grows). Used in §6.6 (T^d-Hecke algebras) and §7. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.4.2, (140) — traces preserve the integral structures on H^d
items.statement: The integral structures (139) are respected by the trace maps: φ ∈ H^d_!(_{K_{r+1}}Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}, R) ⇒ trace_{K_r/K_{r+1}} φ ∈ H^d_!(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_{κ^D}, R)   (140).
items.note: Follows from (138): for f ∈ S_κ(K_r, O) ⊂ S_κ(K_{r+1}, O), ⟨f, trace φ⟩_{κ,K_r} = ⟨f, φ⟩_{κ,K_{r+1}} ∈ R. Verified. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5 — convention: automorphic representations are irreducible (g,K_h) × G(A_f)-modules
items.statement: An automorphic representation of G always means an irreducible (g, K_h) × G(A_f)-representation occurring in the space of automorphic forms on G(A), where K_h is the stabilizer of h in G(R) (which need not project to the maximal compact subgroup of G(R)/Z_G(R)). This allows holomorphic and anti-holomorphic representations to be distinguished.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.1 — holomorphic and anti-holomorphic cuspidal representations of type (κ,K)
items.statement: Let π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G (irreducible; π_f an irreducible admissible representation of G(A_f), π_∞ an irreducible (g,K_h)-module) and K ⊂ G(A_f) open compact. π is holomorphic (resp. anti-holomorphic) of type (κ,K) if H^0(P_h, K_h; π_∞ ⊗_C W_κ) ≠ 0 (resp. H^d(P_h, K_h; π_∞ ⊗_C W_{κ^D}) ≠ 0) and π_f^K ≠ 0. If π is holomorphic (resp. anti-holomorphic) of type (κ,K), then π̄ is anti-holomorphic (resp. holomorphic) of type (κ,K). With G fixed, π cannot be both unless G is definite; F_∞ of (123) identifies anti-holomorphic representations of G_2 with holomorphic representations of G_1 and vice versa. Convention of the paper: the basic object π is an anti-holomorphic (and anti-ordinary, §6.6.6) cuspidal representation of G_1; it is then holomorphic as a representation of G_2, where the natural object is π^♭ (≅ π̄), again anti-holomorphic.
items.note: The statement about π̄ follows from c_B (118). 'Anti-holomorphic of type (κ,K)' refers to the weight κ of the holomorphic conjugate, with coefficients W_{κ^D}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 6.5.2 — rationality of π_f (Blasius–Harris–Ramakrishnan)
items.statement: If π is holomorphic or anti-holomorphic, then π_f is defined over a number field E(π); E(π) is always taken to contain K'.
items.note: Cited: 'by the considerations in [BHR94]'. Planned: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.4 plans rationality of cohomological cuspidal representations.

items.name: §6.5.3 — the archimedean central character of a representation of type κ
items.statement: Let ξ_π be the central character of π. If (π_∞ ⊗_C W_κ)^{K_h} ≠ 0 (for example if π is holomorphic of type (κ,K)), then ξ_{π,∞}(t) = t^{a(κ)} for t ∈ R^×, with the convention implicit in §§6.3–6.5 for the action of K_h on W_κ; with the conventions of §§2.6.3 and 2.7.2 taken literally (K_h acting on W_κ by right translation, invariants taken diagonally) one gets ξ_{π,∞}(t) = t^{−a(κ)}.
items.note: The paper states ξ_{π,∞}(t) = t^{a(κ)} without qualification (sourceIssues E97). Under §2.7.2, f(gu) = u^{-1}·f(g) and t ∈ R^× ⊂ U_∞ acts on W_κ by κ(t) = t^{a(κ)} ((15): t ↦ (t^2, t·1)), so f(gt) = t^{−a(κ)} f(g) while f(tg) = ξ_{π,∞}(t) f(g). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.3, (141) — the ♭ involution on cuspidal representations
items.statement: For a cuspidal automorphic representation π of G with central character ξ_π, π^♭ := π^∨ ⊗ |ξ_π ∘ ν| = π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)}   (141), the second expression when ξ_{π,∞}(t) = t^{a(κ)}.
items.note: π^∨ ⊗ |ξ_π ∘ ν| is convention-free; the explicit form ||ν||^{a(κ)} carries the sign of sourceIssues E97. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.3, (142) — π^♭ ≅ π̄; ♭ is an involution exchanging holomorphic and anti-holomorphic
items.statement: Because π ⊗ |ξ_π ∘ ν|^{-1/2} is unitary, π^♭ ≅ π̄   (142); when π occurs with multiplicity one, π^♭ and π̄ are the same space of automorphic forms. In particular π ↦ π^♭ is an involution of the set of cuspidal automorphic representations of G, and if π is holomorphic then π^♭ is anti-holomorphic, and vice versa.
items.note: Verified: π_0 = π ⊗ |ξ_π ∘ ν|^{-1/2} has unitary central character (|ξ_π(z z̄)| = |ξ_π(z)|^2) and is cuspidal, hence unitary, so π̄_0 ≅ π_0^∨ and π̄ ≅ π^∨ ⊗ |ξ_π ∘ ν|; (π^♭)^♭ = π because |ξ_{π^♭}| = |ξ_π|. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.3, (143) — the MVW involution: π_ℓ^† ≅ π_ℓ^∨ (Mœglin–Vignéras–Waldspurger)
items.statement: The involution g ↦ g^† of §6.2.3 is of the type considered in [MVW87, Ch. 4]: there is h_0 ∈ GL_{K^+}(V), c-semilinear for the K-action, with ⟨h_0 v, h_0 w⟩_V = ⟨w, v⟩_V and ḡ = h_0 g h_0^{-1} (in the fixed K-basis, h_0 = I acts by c on coordinates). Let π = ⊗_{ℓ≤∞} π_ℓ be an automorphic representation of G. If (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V) is unramified at ℓ, then π_ℓ^† ≅ (π_ℓ ∘ Ad(h_0)) ⊗ (ξ_{π,ℓ}^{-1} ∘ ν) ≅ π_ℓ^∨   (143). In particular, if π satisfies strong multiplicity one (expected when the places at which π or G is ramified all split in K/K^+ and the base change of π to GL_{n/K} is cuspidal), then π^† ≅ π^∨ and π^† ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)} = π^♭ = π̄; in any event (143) expresses the Hecke action on π^♭ through that on π^†, at least at the unramified primes ℓ.
items.note: Cited as 'a deep result proved in [MVW87, Chapitre 4] (cf. [HKS96])'. The paper prints '≅ π^∨' for π_ℓ^∨ and ξ_π for ξ_{π,ℓ} (sourceIssues E98). MVW prove π^δ ≅ π^∨ for isometry groups (here U(V)); the similitude version for GU(V) with the twist ξ_{π,ℓ}^{-1} ∘ ν is taken for granted (central characters agree: both sides have central character ξ_{π,ℓ}^{-1}). At ℓ ≠ p, π_ℓ^†(g) = π_ℓ(ν(g)^{-1} h_0 g h_0^{-1}) = ξ_{π,ℓ}(ν(g))^{-1} π_ℓ(Ad(h_0)g), consistent with the middle term. Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: §6.5.3, (144) — K^♭, ψ^♭, κ^♭ in terms of †
items.statement: K^♭ := K^†, ψ^♭ := ψ^†, and κ^♭ = κ^† · ν^{a(κ)}   (144) (the last restating κ^† = κ^♭ · ||ν||^{-a(κ)}).
items.note: Motivation: the doubling method pairs π with (a twist of) π^♭, while † is used to compare level structures and Hecke algebras. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.4, (145) — the canonical pairing ⟨·,·⟩_π : π ⊗ π^∨ → C
items.statement: For π a holomorphic cuspidal automorphic representation of G of type (κ,K), the canonical pairing ⟨·,·⟩_π : π ⊗ π^∨ → C is ⟨φ, φ'⟩_π = ∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)} φ(g) φ'(g) dg, φ ∈ π, φ' ∈ π^∨ (realized in automorphic forms)   (145), dg the Tamagawa measure.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.4, (146) — ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ in terms of ⟨·,·⟩_π
items.statement: Let w_1, …, w_m be a basis of W_κ and w_1^∨, …, w_m^∨ the dual basis of W_κ^∨; since W_{κ^D} is a twist of W_κ^∨ by a character, the w_i^∨ also give a basis of W_{κ^D}. For φ ∈ (π^{p_h^-} ⊗_C W_κ)^{K_h} and φ' ∈ Hom(∧^d p_h^-, π^♭ ⊗_C W_{κ^D})^{K_h}, write φ = Σ_i φ_i ⊗ w_i and φ' = Σ_j φ'_j ⊗ w_j^∨ (φ'_j ∈ π^♭, via the fixed basis dx). Then ⟨φ, φ'⟩^Ser_κ = Σ_i ⟨φ_i, φ'_i · ||ν||^{-a(κ)}⟩_π   (146).
items.note: Follows from (133) (dg form) by contracting coefficients; φ'_i · ||ν||^{-a(κ)} ∈ π^∨ because π^♭ = π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)}. Printed 'w_i^∨, …, w_m^∨' and 'ω_i^∨' for w_1^∨, …, w_m^∨ and w_i^∨ (sourceIssues E99). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.5.4, (147) — the χ-twisted Serre pairing ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_{κ,χ}
items.statement: Let χ be a Hecke character of type A_0. Using the twisted pairing of Remark 4.1.6 (for φ_1 ∈ π and φ_2 ∈ π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1} ∘ det, ⟨φ_1, φ_2⟩_χ is the L^2 pairing of φ_1 with φ_2 ⊗ χ ∘ det), define ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_{κ,χ} : π ⊗ (π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1} ∘ det) → C by ⟨φ, φ'⟩^Ser_{κ,χ} = Σ_i ⟨φ_i, φ'_i ||ν||^{-a(κ)}⟩_{π,χ}   (147), with φ_i, φ'_i as in (146).
items.note: The paper cites '(4.1.6)', which is Remark 4.1.6 (there is no equation (4.1.6)), and omits the target '→ C' (sourceIssues E99). New in v5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The Hecke algebra T_{K_r,κ,R} of level K_r and weight κ
items.statement: For any S_0-algebra R ⊂ C, T_{K_r,κ,R} is the R-subalgebra of End_C(S_κ(K_r;C)) = End_C(H^0(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ)) generated by the normalized operators U_{w,j,κ} = |κ′(t_{w,j})|_p^{-1}·U_{w,j} (w ∈ Σ_p, 1 ≤ j ≤ n), where κ′ is related to κ as in (30) (κ′ = κ_norm = (κ_{σ,i′} − b_{σ,i′})), and by the Hecke operators T(g) = T_r(g) = [K_r g K_r] for g ∈ G(A_f^S), where S = S(K^p) is the set of places of 𝒦^+ at which K^p does not contain a hyperspecial maximal subgroup. The R-modules S_κ(K_r;R) and S_κ(K_r,ψ;R) are stable under the U_{w,j,κ} and the T(g), g ∈ G(A_f^S), so the cusp forms over C can be replaced by those over R in the definition. If R = S_0 the subscript R is omitted.
items.note: Standing notation of §6.6: G = G_1 = GU(V) (unitary similitude group of the hermitian 𝒦-space V, 𝒦 CM with totally real 𝒦^+); K = K_r = K^p·I_r ⊂ G(A_f) with I_r ⊂ I^0_r ⊂ G(Z_p) as in §2.5 (I^0_r/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p)); S_κ(K_r;R) = cusp forms of weight κ and level K_r (= H^0(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ) over C); T(g) = T_r(g) = [K_r g K_r]; U_{w,j} = K_r t^+_{w,j} K_r, U^-_{w,j} = K_r t^-_{w,j} K_r as in (23) (the index i of (23) is dropped since V is a single hermitian space); S_0 = O_{𝒦′,(p′)}. The meaning of G(A_f^S) for the Q-group G is fixed in footnote 13 (item group-g-a-f-s). The stability of S_κ(K_r;R) under the Hecke operators is asserted without proof (p. 99); over p-adic R the U-operators are Hida's operators of §2.9.5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Footnote 13 — the group G(A_f^S) of Hecke operators away from S
items.statement: G(A_f^S) = ∏_p G(Q_p)^S, the product over rational primes p. If p is not divisible by a prime in S then G(Q_p)^S = G(Q_p). In general let 𝒫 be the set of primes of 𝒦^+ dividing p, 𝒫 = 𝒫_1 ⊔ 𝒫_2 with 𝒫_1 split in 𝒦 and 𝒫_2 non-split. Then G(Q_p) = ∏_{v∈𝒫_1} GL(n,𝒦^+_v) × G_{𝒫_2}, where G_{𝒫_2} is the subgroup of ((x_w),t) ∈ ∏_{w∈𝒫_2} GL(n,𝒦_w) × Q_p^× such that each x_w preserves the hermitian form on V(𝒦_w) with similitude factor t. Writing S ∩ 𝒫_i = S_{p,i}: G(Q_p)^S = ∏_{v∈𝒫_1∖S_{p,1}} GL(𝒦^+_v) × G_{𝒫_2} if S_{p,2} is empty, and G(Q_p)^S = ∏_{v∈𝒫_1∖S_{p,1}} GL(𝒦^+_v) otherwise.
items.note: The footnote adds that one could also ignore all divisors of p if one of them belongs to S, since dropping finitely many generators from the unramified Hecke algebra changes nothing. ‘GL(𝒦^+_v)’ in the last two formulas means GL(n,𝒦^+_v). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The Hecke algebras T^-_{K_r,κ,R} and T^d_{K_r,κ,R}; the ±V convention
items.statement: T^-_{K_r,κ,R} and T^d_{K_r,κ,R} are defined like T_{K_r,κ,R} but with U_{w,j,κ} replaced by U^-_{w,j,κ} = |κ′(t_{w,j})|_p·U^-_{w,j}; for T^d one also replaces S_κ(K_r;C) by H^d(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ) = H^d(Sh(V), ω_κ)^{K_r} (d = dimension of Sh(V)). A subscript ‘V’ (resp. ‘−V’) is added to notation when needed to indicate that it relates to the hermitian pair (V, ⟨·,·⟩_V) (resp. (V, −⟨·,·⟩_V)).
items.note: Standing notation of §6.6: G = G_1 = GU(V) (unitary similitude group of the hermitian 𝒦-space V, 𝒦 CM with totally real 𝒦^+); K = K_r = K^p·I_r ⊂ G(A_f) with I_r ⊂ I^0_r ⊂ G(Z_p) as in §2.5 (I^0_r/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p)); S_κ(K_r;R) = cusp forms of weight κ and level K_r (= H^0(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ) over C); T(g) = T_r(g) = [K_r g K_r]; U_{w,j} = K_r t^+_{w,j} K_r, U^-_{w,j} = K_r t^-_{w,j} K_r as in (23) (the index i of (23) is dropped since V is a single hermitian space); S_0 = O_{𝒦′,(p′)}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.1(i) — Serre duality isomorphism T ↦ T^d
items.statement: Let R ⊂ C be a subring. There exists a unique R-algebra isomorphism T_{K_r,κ,R} ⥲ T^d_{K_r,κ^D,R}, T ↦ T^d, such that U^d_{w,j,κ} = U^-_{w,j,κ^D} and T(g)^d = ||ν(g)||^{a(κ)}·T(g^{-1}).
items.note: Proof: ‘follows from Serre duality’ (the pairing ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ of (132), under which the adjoint of U_{w,j,κ} on H^0(ω_κ) is U^-_{w,j,κ^D} on H^d(ω_{κ^D})). κ^D is the Serre-dual weight (W_{κ^D} = Hom_C(∧^d p^+_h, W_{κ⋆})), ν the similitude character, a(κ) as in (115)–(116). Standing notation of §6.6: G = G_1 = GU(V) (unitary similitude group of the hermitian 𝒦-space V, 𝒦 CM with totally real 𝒦^+); K = K_r = K^p·I_r ⊂ G(A_f) with I_r ⊂ I^0_r ⊂ G(Z_p) as in §2.5 (I^0_r/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p)); S_κ(K_r;R) = cusp forms of weight κ and level K_r (= H^0(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ) over C); T(g) = T_r(g) = [K_r g K_r]; U_{w,j} = K_r t^+_{w,j} K_r, U^-_{w,j} = K_r t^-_{w,j} K_r as in (23) (the index i of (23) is dropped since V is a single hermitian space); S_0 = O_{𝒦′,(p′)}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.1(ii) — the ♭-isomorphism T_{K_r,κ,V,R} ≅ T_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,−V,R}
items.statement: Let R ⊂ C be a subring. There exists a unique R-algebra isomorphism T_{K_r,κ,V,R} ⥲ T_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,−V,R}, T ↦ T^♭, such that U^♭_{w,j,κ} = U^{-1}_{w,n,κ^♭}·U_{w,n−j,κ^♭} and T(g)^♭ = T(g^†). (The paper adds ‘= T(ḡ)’; away from p one has g^† = ν(g)^{-1}ḡ, so T(g^†) = T(ν(g)^{-1})·T(ḡ), which equals T(ḡ) when ν(g) is a local unit; see source issue on Lemma 6.6.1(ii).)
items.note: Proof: from the isomorphism F^† of (127)–(129) (the MVW-type involution g ↦ g^† = ν(g)^{-1}δ_p^{-1}ḡδ_p of §6.2.3). K^♭ = K^†, κ^♭ = κ^†·ν^{a(κ)}, ψ^♭ = ψ^† (144). Printed statement ends ‘T(g)^♭ = T(g^†) = T(ḡ)’; the corrected statement drops the last equality (issue ‘Lemma 6.6.1(ii)’). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.1(iii) — complex conjugation isomorphism T^-_{K_r,κ,R} ≅ T^d_{K_r,κ^D,cR}
items.statement: Let R ⊂ C be a subring. There exists a unique isomorphism T^-_{K_r,κ,R} ⥲ T^d_{K_r,κ^D,cR} that maps r ∈ R to c(r) (complex conjugation), U^-_{w,j,κ} to U^-_{w,j,κ^D}, and T(g) to T(g).
items.note: Proof: from the complex-conjugation isomorphism c_B (cf. (134)). The printed statement says ‘maps … U^-_{w,j,κ^D} to U^-_{w,j,κ^D}’; the source generator must be U^-_{w,j,κ} (source issue ‘Lemma 6.6.1(iii)’). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hecke algebras with nebentypus T_{K_r,κ,ψ,R}, T^d_{K_r,κ,ψ,R}
items.statement: For a nebentypus ψ of level r (a character of T_H(Z_p) factoring through T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p)), T_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} and T^d_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} are the quotients of T_{K_r,κ,R} and T^d_{K_r,κ,R} obtained by restriction to the invariant subspaces S_κ(K_r,ψ,C) ⊂ S_κ(K_r,C) and H^d(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_κ)^ψ, the subspace of H^d(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_κ) on which K^0_r (acting through T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p) as in §2.5) acts via ψ.
items.note: Standing notation of §6.6: G = G_1 = GU(V) (unitary similitude group of the hermitian 𝒦-space V, 𝒦 CM with totally real 𝒦^+); K = K_r = K^p·I_r ⊂ G(A_f) with I_r ⊂ I^0_r ⊂ G(Z_p) as in §2.5 (I^0_r/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^rZ_p)); S_κ(K_r;R) = cusp forms of weight κ and level K_r (= H^0(_{K_r}Sh(V), ω_κ) over C); T(g) = T_r(g) = [K_r g K_r]; U_{w,j} = K_r t^+_{w,j} K_r, U^-_{w,j} = K_r t^-_{w,j} K_r as in (23) (the index i of (23) is dropped since V is a single hermitian space); S_0 = O_{𝒦′,(p′)}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.2 — duality and ♭ isomorphisms with nebentypus
items.statement: The isomorphisms in Lemma 6.6.1(i)–(ii) induce R-algebra isomorphisms T_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} ⥲ T^d_{K_r,κ^D,ψ^{-1},R} and T_{K_r,κ,ψ,V,R} ⥲ T_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,ψ^♭,−V,R}.
items.note: ‘This is clear from the definitions.’ The first target is printed T^d_{K_r,ψ^{-1},ω_{κ^D},R} (notational slip, listed in the combined misprint entry). ψ^♭ = ψ^† = ψ^{-1} as characters of the diagonal torus (129). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: p-depleted Hecke algebras T^{?,p}_•
items.statement: For any of the Hecke algebras T^?_• above, T^{?,p}_• denotes the subalgebra generated over R by the T(g), g ∈ G(A_f^S) (omitting the U_{w,j,κ} and U^-_{w,j,κ}). The isomorphisms of Lemmas 6.6.1 and 6.6.2 restrict to isomorphisms of these p-depleted Hecke algebras.
items.note: The restriction claim is immediate since the isomorphisms send T(g) to multiples of T(g^{-1}), T(g^†), T(g). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.3 — the character λ^p_π of the p-depleted Hecke algebra
items.statement: Let π be a holomorphic cuspidal representation of G of type (κ,K_r).
