The natural action of T^p_{K_r,κ} on π^{K_r} is given by a character λ^p_π; these are compatible under the natural projections T^p_{K_r,κ} ↠ T^p_{K_{r′},κ}, r ≥ r′, so r is dropped from the notation. For an S_0-algebra R ⊂ C, λ^p_π extends R-linearly to a homomorphism of the Hecke algebras over R (same notation). Via Lemma 6.6.1(ii), λ^p_{π,V} = λ^p_π determines a homomorphism λ^{p,♭}_{π,V} of T^p_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,−V,R}.
items.note: ‘Holomorphic of type (κ,K)’ is defined in §6.5.1: H^0(𝔓_h,K_h;π_∞⊗W_κ) ≠ 0 and π_f^K ≠ 0. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (148) — λ^{p,♭}_{π,V} = λ^p_{π^♭,−V}
items.statement: For π holomorphic cuspidal of type (κ,K_r), the homomorphism λ^{p,♭}_{π,V} of T^p_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,−V,R} (the transport of λ^p_π by Lemma 6.6.1(ii)) satisfies λ^{p,♭}_{π,V} = λ^p_{π^♭,−V}, where π^♭ = π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)} (141).
items.note: Stated as a consequence of (143), the local isomorphism π^†_ℓ ≅ (π_ℓ∘Ad(h_0))⊗(ξ_π^{-1}∘ν) ≅ π^∨_ℓ at places ℓ where the hermitian pair is unramified, which the paper takes from [MVW87, Chapitre 4] (cf. [HKS96]); (143) is in §6.5.3. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hypothesis 6.6.4 — multiplicity one hypothesis for π
items.statement: (Multiplicity one hypothesis) For any holomorphic cuspidal π′ ≠ π of type (κ,K_r), λ^p_{π′} ≠ λ^p_π.
items.note: Expected to hold if S = S(K^p) consists only of places split in 𝒦/𝒦^+ (so local L-packets are singletons) and the base change of π to GL_n/𝒦 is cuspidal. The paper ‘generally assumes’ it (‘not indispensable, but it simplifies the notation’); a referee noted it can fail for π ramified at inert v (L-packets with several members), e.g. automorphic inductions; Remark 9.3.2 sketches a construction without it. Since π′ ≠ π is read as distinct automorphic subrepresentations, the hypothesis implies that π itself occurs with multiplicity one (the comment after Hypothesis 7.3.3 calls 7.3.3 ‘weaker’). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 plans the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs.

items.name: Multiplicity one for unitary groups ([Mok15], [KMSW14]) — cited
items.statement: When G is quasi-split, multiplicity one for (cuspidal automorphic representations of) the unitary group has been established by Mok [Mok15]; the general case has been proved under certain restrictive hypotheses by Kaletha, Mínguez, Shin and White [KMSW14]. Both rely in part on results announced by Arthur but not yet published at the time.
items.locator: arXiv:1602.01776v5, §6.6.3, p. 100; also after Hypothesis 7.3.3, p. 110
items.note: Cited, not proved; used only as motivation for Hypotheses 6.6.4 and 7.3.3 (‘As noted above, it is implied by [Mok15, KMSW14]’, p. 110 — under the hypotheses of those works: π′ with cuspidal base change, restrictive conditions in the non-quasi-split case). Planned: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 plans the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs; EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.7a plans unitary-to-GL_m base-change identities.

items.name: The isotypic subspace S_κ(K_r,C)(π) and the embedding j_π
items.statement: Fix a basis of the one-dimensional space H^0(𝔓_h,K_h; π_∞ ⊗_C W_κ) and an E(π)-rational spherical vector in π_f^S. Let S_κ(K_r,C)(π) be the λ^p_π-isotypic subspace of S_κ(K_r,C) for the action of T^p_{K_r,κ}. There is then an embedding of T^p_{K_r,κ}-modules j_π: H^0(𝔓_h,K_h; π^{K_r} ⊗_C W_κ) ≅ π_f^{K_r} ↪ S_κ(K_r,C)(π).
items.note: E(π) ⊃ 𝒦′ is the field of definition of π_f (Remark 6.5.2, [BHR94]). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.5(i) — the λ^p_π-isotypic subspace
items.statement: Let π be a holomorphic cuspidal automorphic representation of type (κ,K_r) satisfying Hypothesis 6.6.4. Then the injection j_π defines an isomorphism j_π: π_S^{K_S} ⊗ π_p^{I_r} ⥲ S_κ(K_r,C)(π), where K_S = ∏_{v∈S} K_v and π_S = ⊗_{v∈S} π_v.
items.note: No proof is given. It follows from strong multiplicity-one type reasoning: by Hypothesis 6.6.4 the λ^p_π-isotypic part of the cuspidal spectrum of level K_r is the single subrepresentation π, and π_f^{K_r} = π_S^{K_S} ⊗ π_p^{I_r} ⊗ (fixed spherical lines). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.5(ii) — the λ-component over a number field
items.statement: Let π be as in Lemma 6.6.5(i). Let λ be any extension of λ^p_π to a character of T_{K_r,κ,R}, where R ⊂ C is a finite extension of E(π) containing the values of λ, and let S_κ(K_r,R)[λ] be the localization of the T_{K_r,κ,R}-module S_κ(K_r,R) at the prime ideal p_λ = ker λ ⊂ T_{K_r,κ,R}. Then j_π defines an isomorphism j_π: π_S^{K_S} ⊗ π_p^{I_r}[λ] ⥲ S_κ(K_r,R)[λ] ⊗_R C = S_κ(K_r,C)[λ], provided π_p^{I_r}[λ] is read as the generalized eigenspace in π_p^{I_r} of the U_{w,j,κ} for the eigenvalues λ(U_{w,j,κ}) (it coincides with the eigenspace ‘on which each U_{w,j,κ} acts as λ(U_{w,j,κ})’ when the U_{w,j,κ} act semisimply, e.g. on ordinary parts).
items.note: The paper says S_κ(K_r,R)[λ] is ‘in other words … the λ-isotypic component’ and defines π_p^{I_r}[λ] as the eigenspace; localization at p_λ gives the generalized eigenspace. See source issue ‘Lemma 6.6.5(ii)’. No proof given. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.6 — the ordinary Hecke algebras T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}, T^ord_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} and ordinary cusp forms over non-p-adic R
items.statement: Suppose R ⊂ C is the localization of a finite S_0-algebra at the maximal prime determined by incl_p, or a p-adic algebra in the sense that ι_p(R) is p-adically complete. With the ordinary projector e_κ = lim_N U_{p,κ}^{N!}, U_{p,κ} = ∏_{w∈Σ_p}∏_{j=1}^n U_{w,j,κ} (111), set T^ord_{K_r,κ,R} = e_κ T_{K_r,κ,R} and T^ord_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} = e_κ T_{K_r,κ,ψ,R}. These are the rings obtained by restricting the Hecke operators to the stable subspaces S^ord_κ(K_r;R) and S^ord_κ(K_r,ψ;R). For R not p-adic, S^ord_κ(K_r;R) and S^ord_κ(K_r,ψ;R) are defined to be the intersections of S_κ(K_r;R) and S_κ(K_r,ψ;R) with the ordinary spaces over the p-adic completion of R (the completion of incl_p(R)).
items.note: 6–6.7); the big Hecke algebras are split off as big-ordinary-hecke-algebra and localized-big-hecke-algebra. Over p-adic R, S^ord_κ(K_r,ψ;R) = e S_κ(K_r,ψ;R) as in §2.9.6. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.6 — the anti-ordinary projector e^-_κ and anti-ordinary Hecke algebras
items.statement: Let U^-_{p,κ} = ∏_{w∈Σ_p}∏_{j=1}^n U^-_{w,j,κ} and e^-_κ = lim_N (U^-_{p,κ})^{N!} (as an operator, when it exists) — the anti-ordinary projector. Put T^{a-ord}_{K_r,κ,R} = e^-_κ T^d_{K_r,κ,R} and T^{a-ord}_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} = e^-_κ T^d_{K_r,κ,ψ,R}.
items.note: R as in §6.6.6. The limit exists on finite free modules over p-adically complete rings (standard Hida idempotent argument). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.7 — (anti-)ordinary versions of the duality and ♭ isomorphisms
items.statement: Suppose R is as in §6.6.6. The isomorphisms of Lemmas 6.6.1(i)–(ii) and 6.6.2 restrict to R-algebra isomorphisms: (i) T^ord_{K_r,κ,R} ⥲ T^{a-ord}_{K_r,κ^D,R} and T^ord_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} ⥲ T^{a-ord}_{K_r,κ^D,ψ^{-1},R}; (ii) T^ord_{K_r,κ,V,R} ⥲ T^ord_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,−V,R} and T^ord_{K_r,κ,ψ,V,R} ⥲ T^ord_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,ψ^{-1},−V,R}.
items.note: ‘This is immediate from the definitions’ (one proof for both parts, kept as one item). The printed second isomorphism in (i) has target T^{a-ord}_{K_r,κ,ψ^{-1},R}; κ must be κ^D (source issue ‘Lemma 6.6.7(i)’). In (ii) ψ^{-1} = ψ^♭. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.8 — the ordinary line π^ord_p
items.statement: Let π be a holomorphic cuspidal automorphic representation of G of type (κ,K_r). Put π^ord_p = e_κ π_p^{I_r}. This space has dimension at most one (Theorem 6.6.9) and does not depend on r, in the sense that e_κ π_p^{I_r} = e_κ π_p^{I_{r′}} for all r′ ≥ r.
items.note: The paper says the independence of r ‘is a consequence of’ Theorem 6.6.9; the inclusion e_κπ_p^{I_r} ⊆ e_κπ_p^{I_{r′}} and dimension ≤ 1 only give equality when e_κπ_p^{I_r} ≠ 0 — see source issue ‘π^ord_p independent of r’. The local theory of §8.3 (Lemma 8.3.2) supplies the missing step. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 6.6.9 (Hida) — the ordinary eigenspace has dimension ≤ 1
items.statement: For any irreducible admissible representation π_p of G(Q_p), the ordinary eigenspace e_κ π_p^{I_r} ⊂ π_p^{I_r} is of dimension ≤ 1, for any r.
items.note: A variant of [Hid98, Corollary 8.3]; the proof, an adaptation of Hida’s, is given in §8.3. The printed statement says ‘For any representation π_p’; irreducibility (as in Lemma 8.3.2, where the local proof is done) is needed — source issue ‘Theorem 6.6.9’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.8 — ordinary representations and the ordinary nebentypus
items.statement: π is ordinary if π^ord_p ≠ 0. Then π^ord_p is stable under I^0_r, so I^0_r acts on π^ord_p through a well-defined character ψ; its identification with a character of T_H(Z_p) (via I^0_r/I_r ≅ T_H(Z_p/p^r)) is called the ordinary nebentypus of π.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.8 — the anti-ordinary line π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r}
items.statement: For π holomorphic cuspidal of type (κ,K_r), π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r} = e^-_{κ^D} π_p^{♭,I_r} ⊂ π^♭_p. It is at most one-dimensional, and non-zero (hence one-dimensional) if and only if π^ord_p ≠ 0. It is not in general independent of r, but for r′ ≥ r, trace_{K_r/K_{r′}} π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r′} = π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r}.
items.note: The dimension/non-vanishing claim is referred to Lemma 8.3.6 and the trace relation to Lemma 8.3.7 (both in §8.3); trace_{K_r/K_{r′}} is the normalized trace of (138). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.8 — the Hecke character λ_π, its fields E(λ_π), R(λ_π) and reduction λ̄_π
items.statement: Suppose π is ordinary. λ_π is the (unique) extension of λ^p_π to the character of T_{K_r,κ} giving its action on π^ord_p ⊗ π^{p,K^p}. For R as in §6.6.6 this character factors through T^ord_{K_r,κ,ψ,R}, ψ the ordinary nebentypus of π. E(λ_π) is the finite extension of E(π) generated by the values of λ_π; R(λ_π) is the localization of the ring of integers of E(λ_π) at the maximal ideal determined by incl_p; λ_π is R(λ_π)-valued. λ̄_π is the reduction of λ_π modulo the maximal ideal of R(λ_π), viewed as taking values in the residue field of Z̄_(p).
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (149) — the set S(K_r,κ,π) of congruent ordinary forms
items.statement: S(K_r,κ,π) = {ordinary holomorphic π′ of type (κ,K_r) such that λ̄_{π′} = λ̄_π}. From §9.1.6 on, π′ ∈ S(K_r,κ,π) is also written when π and π′ are anti-holomorphic (and anti-ordinary); this means π′^♭ ∈ S(K_r,κ,π^♭), where π^♭ is holomorphic of type (κ,K_r) and (149) is used as stated.
items.note: π′ ranges over automorphic subrepresentations (see note to Hypothesis 6.6.4). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.10(i) — the ordinary λ_π-component over E
items.statement: Let π be a holomorphic cuspidal automorphic representation of type (κ,K_r) which is ordinary and satisfies Hypothesis 6.6.4. Let R ⊂ C be the localization of a finite extension of R(λ_π) at the prime determined by incl_p, or the p-adic completion of such a ring, and E = R[1/p]. Then S^ord_κ(K_r;E)[λ_π] = e_κ S_κ(K_r;E)[λ_π], and j_π restricts to an isomorphism j_π: π^ord_p ⊗ π_S^{K_S} ≅ π_S^{K_S} ⥲ S^ord_κ(K_r;E)[λ_π] ⊗_E C.
items.note: No proof given; follows from Lemma 6.6.5 and dim π^ord_p = 1 (Theorem 6.6.9). [λ_π] denotes the λ_π-isotypic component. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.10(ii) — the maximal ideal m_π and the modules S^ord_κ(K_r;R)_π, S^ord_κ(K_r;R)[π]
items.statement: With π, R, E as in Lemma 6.6.10: m_π is the maximal ideal of T_{K_r,κ,R} that is the kernel of the reduction of λ_π modulo the maximal ideal of R; S^ord_κ(K_r;R)_π is the localization of S^ord_κ(K_r;R) at m_π; and S^ord_κ(K_r;R)[π] := S^ord_κ(K_r;R)_π ∩ S^ord_κ(K_r;E)[λ_π].
items.note: For S^ord_κ(K_r;R)_π to be a finitely generated (free) R-module one needs R complete (Henselian) or large enough to contain the Hecke eigenvalues of all π′ ∈ S(K_r,κ,π) — source issue ‘localizations over non-complete R’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.10(ii) — ordinary lattices
items.statement: With π, R, E as in Lemma 6.6.10 (R complete, or containing the Hecke eigenvalues of every π′ ∈ S(K_r,κ,π)): S^ord_κ(K_r;R)[π] is identified by j_π with an R-lattice in π^ord_p ⊗ π_S^{K_S} ≅ π_S^{K_S}, and S^ord_κ(K_r;R)_π is identified with an R-lattice in ⊕_{π′∈S(K_r,κ,π)} π′^{,ord}_p ⊗ (π′_S)^{K_S}. This last identification is via ⊕_{π′} λ_{π′}.
items.note: Printed index set S(K_s,κ,π) is a misprint for S(K_r,κ,π) (source issue). The hypothesis in parentheses is added (source issue ‘localizations over non-complete R’). No proof given. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The dual modules Ŝ_κ, Ŝ^ord_κ and their Serre-duality models H^d_{κ^D}(K_r,R), H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,R)
items.statement: Ŝ_κ(K_r;R) = Hom_R(S_κ(K_r;R),R) and Ŝ^ord_κ(K_r;R) = Hom_R(S^ord_κ(K_r;R),R), modules over T_{K_r,κ,R} (resp. T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}) through the Hecke action on S_κ(K_r;R). The normalized Serre duality of §6.4 identifies Ŝ_κ(K_r;R) with H^d_{κ^D}(K_r,R) = {φ ∈ H^d(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_{κ^D}) : ⟨S_κ(K_r;R),φ⟩_{κ,K_r} ⊆ R}. Let S^{ord,⊥}_κ(K_r;R) ⊂ H^d_{κ^D}(K_r,R) be the annihilator of S^ord_κ(K_r;R) for ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r}. Serre duality identifies Ŝ^ord_κ(K_r;R) with H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,R) = {φ ∈ H^d_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_{κ^D})/S^{ord,⊥}_κ(K_r;R) : ⟨S^ord_κ(K_r;R),φ⟩_{κ,K_r} ⊆ R}. Each is a T_{K_r,κ,R}-module through its action on S_κ(K_r;R) or, equivalently, via Lemma 6.6.1(i); so H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R) is a T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}-module.
items.note: ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} = Vol(I^0_{r,V})^{-1}⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ (136). Footnote 14: ω_{κ^D} is the subcanonical extension of its restriction to the open Shimura variety, so H^d(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_{κ^D}) is represented by cusp forms and the pairing is well defined. In the definition of H^{d,ord} the quotient should be by the C-span of S^{ord,⊥}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.11 — anti-ordinary part of H^d as dual of ordinary forms
items.statement: The natural map H^d_{κ^D}(K_r;R) → H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R), which is restriction to S^ord_κ(K_r;R), induces an isomorphism e^-_{κ^D} H^d_{κ^D}(K_r;R) ⥲ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R) (150).
items.note: Proof: ‘an immediate consequence of Lemma 8.3.4(iii)’ (a local statement on pairing with the dual vector; §8.3). A direct argument: under ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} the adjoint of U_{w,j,κ} is U^-_{w,j,κ^D} (Lemma 6.6.1(i)), so e_κ and e^-_{κ^D} are adjoint; for φ = e^-φ one has ⟨s,φ⟩ = ⟨e_κ s,φ⟩, and e_κS_κ(K_r;R) = S^ord_κ(K_r;R). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The embedding j^∨_{π^♭} of the anti-holomorphic partner
items.statement: Let π be a holomorphic cuspidal automorphic representation of G of type (κ,K_r). Then π^♭ is anti-holomorphic of type (κ,K_r). The choice of a basis of the one-dimensional space H^d(𝔓_h,K_h; π^♭_∞ ⊗_C W_{κ^D}) determines an injection j^∨_{π^♭}: H^d(𝔓_h,K_h; π^{♭,K_r} ⊗_C W_{κ^D}) ≅ π^{♭,K_r} ↪ H^d_{κ^D}(K_r;C) = H^d(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_{κ^D}).
items.note: Printed ‘π^♭ is anti-holomorphic of type (κ^♭,K_r)’; by §6.5.1 and the display itself (H^d with coefficients W_{κ^D}, invariants under K_r) the type is (κ,K_r) — source issue ‘p. 103, type of π^♭’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.12(i) — the anti-ordinary λ_π-component of H^{d,ord}
items.statement: Let π, R, E be as in Lemma 6.6.10. Let H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,R)_π be the localization of H^{d,ord}_{κ^D,V}(K_r,R) at m_{π^♭} (the maximal ideal corresponding to m_π), and H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,R)[π] = H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R)_π ∩ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;E)[λ_π], [λ_π] denoting the λ_π-isotypic component. Then the inclusion j^∨_{π^♭} restricts to an isomorphism j^∨_{π^♭}: π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r} ⊗ π^{♭,K_S}_S ≅ π^{♭,K_S}_S ⥲ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,E)[λ_π] ⊗_E C.
items.note: No proof given. The printed middle term is π^{K_S}_S (without ♭); listed in the combined misprint entry. The localization is written ‘at m_{π^♭}’ although H^{d,ord} is regarded as a T_{K_r,κ,R}-module via Lemma 6.6.1(i), for which the relevant ideal is m_π. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.12(ii) — anti-ordinary lattices
items.statement: With π, R, E as in Lemma 6.6.10: the map j^∨_{π^♭} identifies H^{d,ord}(K_r;R)[π] with an R-lattice in π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r} ⊗ π^{♭,K_S}_S, and H^{d,ord}(K_r;R)_π with an R-lattice in ⊕_{π′∈S(K_r,κ,π)} π′^{,♭,a-ord}_{p,r} ⊗ π′^{,♭,K_S}_S. This last identification is by ⊕ j^∨_{π′^{,♭}}.
items.note: Printed ‘π′^{,♭,ord}_{p,r}’ in the direct sum (should be a-ord; combined misprint entry). Same caveat on non-complete R as Lemma 6.6.10(ii). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.12(iii) — Serre duality pairings on ordinary lattices (corrected)
items.statement: With π, R as in Lemma 6.6.10 (R complete): normalized Serre duality ⟨·,·⟩_{κ,K_r} induces a perfect T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}-equivariant pairing (with respect to the isomorphisms of Lemma 6.6.7) S^ord_κ(K_r;R)_π ⊗_R H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R)_π → R, and a T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}-equivariant pairing S^ord_κ(K_r;R)[π] ⊗_R H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R)[π] → R which becomes perfect after ⊗_R E but whose image is in general the proper ideal C(π) (the congruence ideal of Definition 6.7.2; cf. Lemma 7.5.2), so it is perfect over R only when C(π) = R.
items.note: The printed statement asserts that both pairings are perfect over R; the first ([π]) one is not in general — source issue ‘Lemma 6.6.12(iii)’ (an error in a stated result, harmless downstream since §6.7 and §7.5 use exactly the failure of perfectness, measured by C(π)). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Ordinary of type (κ,K_r); the ring O_π and residue field k(π)
items.statement: For any r ≥ 0, π is ordinary of type (κ,K_r) if π is holomorphic of type (κ,K_r) and the image of j_π has non-trivial intersection with S^ord_κ(K_r,R) for R as in Lemma 6.6.10 (this is independent of R). In that case λ_π takes values in a p-adic integer ring O_π with residue field k(π), and λ̄_π: T_{K_r,κ} → k(π) denotes the reduction of λ_π modulo the maximal ideal of O_π.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §6.6.13 — change-of-level maps (151), (152)
items.statement: For fixed κ and r′ ≥ r, consider the inclusion S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R) → S^ord_{κ,V}(K_{r′},R) (151) and the dual map Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_{r′},R) → Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R) (152).
items.note: Under (159) the dual map (152) is the normalized trace (Lemma 7.4.9). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.6.14 — the old forms form a direct factor
items.statement: Let R be either a local Z_(p)[λ_π]-algebra or a finite flat Z_p[λ_π]-algebra. Then the image of the map (151) is an R-direct factor of S^ord_{κ,V}(K_{r′},R), identified with the submodule of I_r/I_{r′}-invariants of the latter. Moreover, the morphism (152) is surjective.
items.note: Proof: ‘The first assertion is obvious; the second is an immediate consequence of the first.’ For R flat over the discrete valuation ring Z_(p)[λ_π] (or Z_p[λ_π]) the invariants of a finite group on a torsion-free module are saturated, hence a direct summand, and invariants commute with flat base change; for a non-flat local Z_(p)[λ_π]-algebra ‘obvious’ is not justified — source issue ‘Lemma 6.6.14’. ‘I_r/I_{r′}-invariants’ means K_r-invariants (I_{r′} need not be normal in I_r). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.7.1 — the period lattices L[π] and L_π are rank one
items.statement: Let R be as in Lemma 6.6.10. The images L[π] = Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r})^{-1}·⟨H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π], H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭]⟩^Ser_κ and L_π = Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r})^{-1}·⟨H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π], H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)_{π^♭}⟩^Ser_κ are rank one R-submodules of C, generated by positive real numbers Q[π] and Q_π respectively. Here the identification (124) (F_∞: H^0_!(Sh(−V),ω_{κ^♭,−V}) ≅ H^d_!(Sh(V),ω_{κ^D,V})) is used to evaluate the pairings.
items.note: Proof: π_f and π^♭_f ≅ π̄_f are defined over E(π); Schur’s lemma with irreducibility and admissibility shows ⟨·,·⟩^Ser is a C^×-multiple of a pairing with values in E(π) on the E(π)-structures, and the hermitian nature of the Petersson pairing and its relation (134) with Serre duality shows the multiple is a positive real number (‘essentially explained in [Har13a]’); since R is a DVR and the modules are finite, the result follows. The finiteness of the localized module needs R complete (source issue ‘localizations over non-complete R’). The normalizing volume Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r}) differs from (136) (Vol(I^0_{r,V})) and from the main theorem’s Vol(I^0_{r,V} ∩ I^0_{r,−V}); see readingNotes. Standing assumption of §6.7: G = G_1; π is an anti-holomorphic representation of G of type (κ,K), anti-ordinary at p with character ψ; π^♭ is then holomorphic, realized via F_∞ (124) in H^d on −V. R is as in Lemma 6.6.10 (a discrete valuation ring). H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π] ⊂ H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)_π are the saturated λ-isotypic lattice and the localization, as in Lemma 6.6.12. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The unnormalized and normalized periods Q[π], Q_π
items.statement: Q[π] and Q_π are the positive real generators of the rank-one R-modules L[π] and L_π of Lemma 6.7.1; they are well defined up to multiplication by R^× and are called respectively the unnormalized and normalized periods of π. One also writes Q[π]_V and Q_{π,V} to emphasize G = G_1. Then Q[π^♭]_{−V} = Q[π]_V and Q_{π^♭,−V} = Q_{π,V}, and these periods are independent of r ≫ 0.
items.note: those are now period-invariants-twisted, congruence-ideal-twisted and lem-6-7-7. Independence of r is justified only as ‘essentially an easy consequence of the properties of anti-ordinary forms (see also Lemma 8.4.9)’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The orthogonal complement H^{d,ord}(K_r,R)[π]^⊥
items.statement: H^{d,ord}_{κ,ψ,V}(K_r,R)[π]^⊥ ⊂ H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)_{π^♭} is the orthogonal complement of H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K_r,ψ,R)[π] with respect to Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r})^{-1}⟨·,·⟩^Ser. It is the intersection of H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)_{π^♭} with ⊕_{π′≠π^♭} H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R[1/p])[π′].
items.note: Printed with ‘(K_r, ℝ)’ for (K_r, R) (combined misprint entry). Standing assumption of §6.7: G = G_1; π is an anti-holomorphic representation of G of type (κ,K), anti-ordinary at p with character ψ; π^♭ is then holomorphic, realized via F_∞ (124) in H^d on −V. R is as in Lemma 6.6.10 (a discrete valuation ring). H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π] ⊂ H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)_π are the saturated λ-isotypic lattice and the localization, as in Lemma 6.6.12. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Definition 6.7.2 — the congruence ideal C(π) = C_V(π)
items.statement: The congruence ideal C(π) = C_V(π) ⊂ R is the annihilator of H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)_{π^♭} / (H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭] + H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K_r,ψ,R)[π]^⊥).
items.note: The numerator is printed with subscript π rather than π^♭ (combined misprint entry). Remark 6.7.4 (expository): C(π) has a local component from possible congruences between π^{♭,ord}_p ⊗ π^{♭,K_S}_S and π^{♭,ord}_p ⊗ (π′_S)^{♭,K_S} for λ̄_π = λ̄_{π′}; when, for every rational prime q, either all or none of the primes of 𝒦^+ over q split in 𝒦, these can be viewed as representations of the integral Hecke algebra of K_S-biinvariant functions on GU(V)(A_{f,S}); separating global and local components is not addressed. Standing assumption of §6.7: G = G_1; π is an anti-holomorphic representation of G of type (κ,K), anti-ordinary at p with character ψ; π^♭ is then holomorphic, realized via F_∞ (124) in H^d on −V. R is as in Lemma 6.6.10 (a discrete valuation ring). H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π] ⊂ H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)_π are the saturated λ-isotypic lattice and the localization, as in Lemma 6.6.12. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; PadicFamilies L1 plans period modules and congruence modules.

items.name: Lemma 6.7.3 — c(π) = Q[π]/Q_π generates the congruence ideal
items.statement: Let c(π) ∈ R be such that c(π)·Q_π = Q[π]. Then c(π) is a generator of C(π).
items.note: Proof: ‘an elementary consequence of the definitions.’ Check: with M = H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K_r,ψ,R)_π, N = H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)_{π^♭} in perfect duality (Lemma 6.6.12(iii), localized part) up to the scalar Q_π, and M[π] a rank-one saturated summand, N → Hom(M[π],R) ≅ R is onto with kernel M[π]^⊥ and N[π^♭] maps onto c(π)R, so N/(N[π^♭]+M[π]^⊥) ≅ R/c(π)R. c(π) ∈ R because L[π] ⊂ L_π. Standing assumption of §6.7: G = G_1; π is an anti-holomorphic representation of G of type (κ,K), anti-ordinary at p with character ψ; π^♭ is then holomorphic, realized via F_∞ (124) in H^d on −V. R is as in Lemma 6.6.10 (a discrete valuation ring). H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π] ⊂ H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)_π are the saturated λ-isotypic lattice and the localization, as in Lemma 6.6.12. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The congruence ideal C(π,M) of a module and C(π,T)
items.statement: For a T^{♭,ord}_{K^♭,κ^♭,R}-module M, C(π,M) is the annihilator of M_{π^♭}/(M[π^♭] + M[π]^⊥), the notation having the same meaning as in Definition 6.7.2. In particular C(π,T) is the congruence ideal for T^ord_{K,κ,R} ⥲ T^{♭,ord}_{K^♭,κ^♭,R} considered as a free module over itself.
items.note: For a general M the orthogonal complement M[π]^⊥ presupposes a duality that is not specified; for M = T it must be read as T ∩ ⊕_{π′≠π}(T⊗E)[λ_{π′}] = ker λ_π, which gives (153) — source issue ‘C(π,M)’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; PadicFamilies L1 plans period modules and congruence modules.

items.name: §6.7.5 — the χ-twisted lattice H^{d,ord}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭]_χ
items.statement: Let χ be a Hecke character of type A_0. If the (anti-holomorphic) representation π^♭ contributes to H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}, let κ^♭⋆χ denote the coherent cohomology space to which π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det contributes, and define the R-module H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭]_χ := H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭⋆χ,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭ ⊗ χ^{-1}∘det].
items.note: The paper stresses this is not a simple algebraic twist of H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭]: even the rational structure is modified by a CM period attached to χ (examples in [Har97, §2.9] when 𝒦^+ = Q; printed ‘F^+ = Q’). The twisted pairings (4.1.6) and (147) give the twisted period invariants. New in v5 (absent from v4). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.7.6 — twisted period lattices are rank one (corrected display)
items.statement: Let R be as in Lemma 6.6.10 and χ a Hecke character of type A_0. The images L[π,χ] = Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r})^{-1}·⟨H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π], H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)[π^♭]_χ⟩^Ser_{κ,χ} and L_{π,χ} = Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r})^{-1}·⟨H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K,ψ,R)[π], H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭⋆χ,−V}(K^♭_r,ψ^{-1},R)_{π^♭⊗χ^{-1}∘det}⟩^Ser_{κ,χ} are rank one R-submodules of C, generated by positive real numbers Q[π,χ] and Q_{π,χ} respectively.
items.note: The printed display is a verbatim copy of Lemma 6.7.1 (no χ in the modules or pairing) while the conclusion names Q[π,χ], Q_{π,χ}; the corrected display uses the twisted module of §6.7.5 and the twisted Serre pairing ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_{κ,χ} of (147) — source issue ‘Lemma 6.7.6’. No proof given (‘The extension of Lemma 6.7.1’). New in v5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The twisted periods Q[π,χ] and Q_{π,χ}
items.statement: For a Hecke character χ of type A_0, Q[π,χ] and Q_{π,χ} are the positive real generators (well defined up to R^×) of the rank-one R-modules L[π,χ] and L_{π,χ} of Lemma 6.7.6 (defined with the twisted pairing (4.1.6)/(147) and the χ-twisted lattice of §6.7.5).
items.note: These are the periods entering Main Theorem 9.2.2 through Ω_{π′,χ} and P_{π′,χ} = Q_{π′,χ}^{-1}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The twisted congruence ideal C(π,χ)
items.statement: C(π,χ) ⊂ R is defined by analogy with C(π) (Definition 6.7.2), using the χ-twisted lattices of §6.7.5 and the twisted pairing.
items.note: Only defined ‘by analogy’; the explicit formula is Definition 6.7.2 with H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(…)[π^♭] replaced by its χ-twist. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.7.7 — c(π,χ) = Q[π,χ]/Q_{π,χ} generates C(π,χ)
items.statement: Let c(π,χ) ∈ R be such that c(π,χ)·Q_{π,χ} = Q[π,χ]. Then c(π,χ) is a generator of C(π,χ).
items.note: No proof given; same argument as Lemma 6.7.3. Used in the proof of Main Theorem 9.2.2 (Q[π′,χ] = c(π′,χ)Q_{π′,χ}). New in v5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Independence of C(π,χ) and c(π,χ) from χ (asserted)
items.statement: C(π,χ) and c(π,χ) do not depend on χ (so C(π,χ) = C(π) and c(π,χ) = c(π) up to R^×).
items.note: Asserted with the justification ‘since the family of p-adic Hecke characters is smooth, it is easy to see’; no argument — source issue ‘C(π,χ) independent of χ’. Repeated before Remark 6.7.12 (‘as noted above, does not actually depend on χ’). New in v5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Definition 6.7.9 — the Gorenstein hypothesis at finite level
items.statement: Let R be a sufficiently large finite flat p-adic integer ring. Write 𝕋 = 𝕋_π := (T^ord_{K,κ,R})_π. The 𝕋-module S^ord_κ(K,R)_π is said to satisfy the Gorenstein hypothesis if (a) there exists an isomorphism G = G_{K,κ,R}: 𝕋 ⥲ Hom_R(𝕋,R) of 𝕋-modules, and (b) S^ord_κ(K,R)_π is free over 𝕋. The T^ord_{K,κ,R}-module S^ord_κ(K,R) is said to satisfy the Gorenstein hypothesis if all its localizations at maximal ideals of T_{K,κ,R} satisfy (a) and (b).
items.note: 𝕋 (blackboard) denotes the localization of an ordinary Hecke algebra at a maximal ideal, bold T the non-localized one. Hypothesis 7.3.2 is the Λ-adic variant. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.7.10 — under Gorenstein, C_V(π) = C(π,𝕋) = C_{−V}(π^♭)
items.statement: Assume S^ord_κ(K,R)_π satisfies the Gorenstein hypothesis (Definition 6.7.9). Then C_V(π) = C(π,𝕋) = C_{−V}(π^♭).
items.note: ‘The following is then obvious.’ Check: under Gorenstein the dual lattice is ≅ Hom_R(𝕋,R)^m ≅ 𝕋^m, and the congruence module of 𝕋^m is (𝕋/(𝕋[λ_π]+ker λ_π))^m, with the same annihilator. Cited in §7.5 as ‘Corollary 6.7.10’ (misprint). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (153) — computing the congruence ideal of 𝕋
items.statement: Assume the multiplicity one hypothesis, so that 𝕋 localized at ker λ_π has rank 1. Let e_1,…,e_n be an R-basis of 𝕋, E = Frac(R), 𝕋_E = 𝕋 ⊗_R E = ⊕_i E_i indexed by the characters λ_{π_i} of 𝕋 (the minimal primes ker λ_{π_i}), with π = π_1 and R large enough that E_1 = E. Choose d_1,…,d_n ∈ 𝕋 forming a basis of 𝕋_E with d_1 an R-generator of 𝕋 ∩ E_1 and d_2,…,d_n an R-basis of 𝕋 ∩ ⊕_{i>1}E_i, and write e_i = ∑_j c_{ij} d_j with c_{ij} ∈ E. Then C(π,𝕋) = ϖ^m R with m = sup_{i: c_{i1}≠0} (−v(c_{i1})), v the valuation of R and ϖ a uniformizer.
items.note: Printed as ‘C(π,𝕋) = sup_{c_{i1}≠0} −v(c_{i1})’ (equating the ideal with the exponent) and with E_i ‘indexed by the maximal ideals λ_{π_i} of 𝕋’ — source issue ‘(153)’. Verification: the projection p_1: 𝕋 → E_1 has image (∑_i R c_{i1}) d_1 = ϖ^{min v(c_{i1})}R d_1 and 𝕋/(𝕋∩E_1 + 𝕋∩⊕_{i>1}E_i) ≅ p_1(𝕋)/R d_1 ≅ R/ϖ^m; m ≥ 0 because d_1 ∈ 𝕋. The dual basis e_i^* introduced in the text is not used. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 6.7.11 — C(π) = C(π^♭)
items.statement: The second isomorphism of Lemma 6.6.2 (T_{K_r,κ,ψ,V,R} ≅ T_{K^♭_r,κ^♭,ψ^♭,−V,R}) takes C(π) isomorphically to C(π^♭).
items.note: ‘The following lemma is then clear.’ The analogous assertion for C(π,χ) is omitted, since C(π,χ) does not depend on χ. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §7.1 — the big ordinary Hecke algebra T^ord_{K^p,κ,R}
items.statement: Let G = G_1, T_H = T_{H_1}(Z_p) the torus of §2.5, and R a p-adic ring. For r′ ≥ r the inclusion S^ord_κ(K_r,R) ⊂ S^ord_κ(K_{r′},R) defines by restriction a map of ordinary Hecke algebras T^ord_{K_{r′},κ,R} → T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}. Put T^ord_{K^p,κ,R} = lim_{←r} T^ord_{K^p_r,κ,R} (K^p_r = K_r = I_rK^p).
items.note: By Theorem 7.1.1 this is independent of (sufficiently regular) κ and is written T_{K^p,R} or T. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 7.1.1 (Hida) — independence of the weight (corrected: for sufficiently regular weights)
items.statement: For any pair of characters κ_1, κ_2 of T_H that are sufficiently regular (in the range of Hida’s classicality theorem (32)), there is a canonical isomorphism T^ord_{K^p,κ_1,R} ⥲ T^ord_{K^p,κ_2,R}. Accordingly T_{K^p,R} (or T) denotes any T^ord_{K^p,κ,R}.
items.note: Cited, not proved: ‘due to Hida’; by Remark 7.1.2, for unitary groups this and Theorem 7.2.1 are special cases of [Hid02, Theorem 7.1] and [Hid04, Chapter 8], proved under conditions (G1)–(G3) of [Hid02, §7] (see (32)), which were proved by Lan [Lan13]. The printed statement says ‘For any pair of characters κ_1, κ_2 of T_H’; since T^ord_{K^p,κ,R} is built from classical forms of weight κ, the regularity hypothesis is needed (e.g. for κ trivial there are no holomorphic cusp forms of weight 0 on a non-compact Shimura variety) — source issue ‘Theorem 7.1.1’. Remark 7.1.2 also says ‘Hida’s Theorems 7.1.1 and 7.3.1 are proved assuming (G1)–(G3)’ (probably meaning 7.1.1 and 7.2.1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hida’s conditions (G1)–(G3) hold for PEL unitary Shimura varieties ([Lan13]) — cited
items.statement: The conditions (G1)–(G3) of [Hid02, §7], under which Hida proves his control, classicality and weight-independence theorems for ordinary forms on PEL Shimura varieties, hold for the Shimura varieties used here: Theorem 6.4.1.1 of [Lan13] contains (G2) and part of (G1), the projectivity assertion in (G1) is [Lan13, Theorem 7.3.3.4], and (G3) is proved in [Lan13, §7.2.3].
items.locator: arXiv:1602.01776v5, §7.1, Remark 7.1.2, p. 108 (referring to §2.9.6, (32) and footnote 4, pp. 33–34)
items.note: Cited black box underlying Theorems 7.1.1, 7.2.1, 7.3.1; stated in §2.9.6, invoked here in Remark 7.1.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ShimuraCompactifications C5 plans Lan's integral PEL toroidal compactifications.

items.name: The big anti-ordinary Hecke algebra T^{a-ord}_{K^p,κ^D,R} and the isomorphism (154)
items.statement: By (140) the trace map trace_{K_r/K_{r′}} maps H^d_{κ^D}(K_{r′};R) to H^d_{κ^D}(K_r;R) for r′ ≥ r > 0, and by the definition of e^-_{κ^D} it maps e^-_{κ^D}H^d_{κ^D}(K_{r′};R) to e^-_{κ^D}H^d_{κ^D}(K_r;R), yielding natural homomorphisms T^{a-ord}_{K_{r′},κ^D,R} → T^{a-ord}_{K_r,κ^D,R} compatible with Lemma 6.6.7(i) and with T^ord_{K_{r′},κ,R} → T^ord_{K_r,κ,R}. Putting T^{a-ord}_{K^p,κ^D,R} = lim_{←r} T^{a-ord}_{K^p_r,κ^D,R}, the isomorphisms of Lemma 6.6.7(i) induce an isomorphism T^ord_{K^p,κ,R} ⥲ T^{a-ord}_{K^p,κ^D,R} (154). By Theorem 7.1.1, T^{a-ord}_{K^p,κ^D,R} is independent of κ^D and is written T^{a-ord}_{K^p,R}.
items.note: Printed with H^1_{κ^D} for H^d_{κ^D} (three times) and T^{a-ord}_{K^p,r} for T^{a-ord}_{K^p,R} — source issue ‘p. 108, H^1’ and combined misprint entry. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The ♭ big Hecke algebras and the isomorphisms (155)
items.statement: T^♭_{K^p,R} := T^ord_{K^{p,♭},κ^♭,R} = lim_{←r} T^ord_{K^{p,♭}_r,κ^♭,R} and T^{♭,ord}_{K^p,R} = T^{a-ord}_{K^{p,♭},κ^{♭,D},R} = lim_{←r} T^{a-ord}_{K^{p,♭}_r,κ^{♭,D},R}. There are isomorphisms T_{K^p,R} ⥲ T^♭_{K^{p,♭},R} ⥲ T^{♭,a-ord}_{K^{p,♭},R} (155), the first induced by those of Lemma 6.6.7(ii) and the second by the corresponding version of Lemma 6.6.7(i). Via (154) and (155), H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r;R), S_{κ^♭}(K^♭_r;R) and H^{d,ord}_{κ^{♭,D}}(K^♭_r;R) are regarded as T_{K^p,R}-modules.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §7.2 — the Iwasawa algebras Λ_R, Λ_{R,ε}, Λ^o_R, Λ^o_{R,ε}
items.statement: Λ_R = R[[T]] is the completed group algebra of T = T_H(Z_p). T_{K^p,R} is a Λ_R-module, t ∈ T acting as the Hecke operator K_r t K_r. For a tame character ε of T, Λ_{R,ε} is the localization of Λ_R at the maximal ideal defined by ε. Λ^o_R ⊂ Λ_R is the completed group algebra of the maximal pro-p subgroup of T, and Λ^o_{R,ε} is defined analogously.
items.note: Compare §2.10.2: Λ_H = O′[[T_H(Z_p)]] = Λ^o[Δ] with Δ the (prime-to-p) torsion subgroup, and the ω-isotypic decomposition S^ord = ⊕_ω S^ord_ω. Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence.

items.name: Theorem 7.2.1(i) (Hida) — finiteness and freeness of the big Hecke algebra
items.statement: For each tame character ε of T, the Hecke algebra T_{K^p,R,ε} is a finite, free Λ^o_{R,ε}-algebra.
items.note: Cited: ‘a special case of [Hid02, Theorem 7.1]’ (see also (33): S^ord_ω(K^p,R) is Λ^o_R-free of finite rank), under (G1)–(G3) proved in [Lan13]. v4 stated freeness over Λ_R, corrected in v5 to Λ^o_{R,ε}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 7.2.1(ii) (Hida) — the control theorem (corrected)
items.statement: Let κ be a sufficiently regular character of T and I_κ ⊂ Λ^o_R the kernel of the map Λ^o_R → R ⊂ C_p defined by κ. Then the natural homomorphism T_{K^p,R} ⊗_{Λ^o_R} Λ^o_R/I_κ → T_{K^p_1,κ,R} (level r = 1, where every nebentypus is tame) is an isomorphism. More generally, for r ≥ 1 and a finite-order character ψ of T of level r, T_{K^p,R} ⊗_{Λ_R} Λ_R/I_{κψ} ≅ T_{K_r,κ,ψ,R} (I_{κψ} ⊂ Λ_R the kernel of κψ), and T_{K^p,R} ⊗_Λ Λ_{r,κ} ≅ T_{K_r,κ,R} with Λ_{r,κ} = Λ/I_{r,κ} as in §7.4 (the form used in Proposition 7.4.12).
items.note: Cited from [Hid02, Theorem 7.1] (cf. (33)). The printed statement has target T_{K^p_r,κ,R} for unspecified r; the left side does not depend on r while the rank of the right side grows with r (it contains all nebentypes of level r), and I_κ does not kill forms whose nebentypus is non-trivial on the pro-p part of T, so the printed map is neither well defined nor an isomorphism for r ≥ 2 — source issue ‘control theorem 7.2.1(ii)/7.3.1(ii)’. ‘Sufficiently regular’ refers to the range in (32). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §7.3 — the localized big Hecke algebra 𝕋_π and the homomorphisms L_π, L̄_π
items.statement: Fix a cuspidal holomorphic automorphic representation π of G = G_1 which is ordinary of type (κ,K) as in §6.6. Let R = O_π, Λ_π = Λ_{O_π} := O_π[[T]] and Λ^o_π = Λ^o_{O_π}. The homomorphisms λ_π: T_{K,κ,O_π} → O_π and λ̄_π: T_{K,κ,O_π} → k(π) induce homomorphisms of Λ_π-algebras L_π: T_{K^p,O_π} → O_π and L̄_π: T_{K^p,O_π} → k(π). m_π = ker L̄_π and 𝕋 = 𝕋_π := T_{K^p,O_π,m_π} is the localization. 𝕋 designates an ordinary Hecke algebra (at fixed level I_r or not) localized at π, bold T a non-localized one. m_π ∩ Λ_π is the maximal ideal defined by some tame character of T.
items.note: Footnote 15: in the main theorem π denotes an anti-holomorphic representation. Replaces part of the earlier summary item ‘ordinary-hecke-algebra’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 7.3.1(i) — 𝕋_π is finite free over Λ^o_π
items.statement: The Hecke algebra 𝕋_π is a finite, free Λ^o_π-algebra.
items.note: ‘Immediate from Theorem 7.2.1’: 𝕋_π is a local direct factor of T_{K^p,O_π,ε} for the tame character ε cut out by m_π ∩ Λ_π, and a direct summand of a finite free module over the local ring Λ^o_{π} is free. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 7.3.1(ii) — control theorem for 𝕋_π (corrected)
items.statement: Let κ be sufficiently regular and I_κ ⊂ Λ^o_π the kernel of the map Λ^o_π → O_π ⊂ C_p defined by κ. Then the natural map 𝕋_π ⊗_{Λ^o_π} Λ^o_π/I_κ → 𝕋_{K^p_1,κ,O_π} is an isomorphism (level r = 1; at level r, specialize at κψ for a nebentypus ψ of level r whose tame part is the one fixed by m_π, with target 𝕋_{K_r,κ,ψ,O_π}, or replace Λ^o_π/I_κ by Λ_{r,κ}).
items.note: Printed with target 𝕋_{K^p_r,κ,O_π} for unspecified r; same issue as Theorem 7.2.1(ii). ‘Immediate from Theorem 7.2.1.’ Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hypothesis 7.3.2 — the Gorenstein hypothesis
items.statement: (Gorenstein Hypothesis) Let 𝕋̂_π = Hom_{Λ^o_π}(𝕋_π, Λ^o_π). Then (i) there exists an isomorphism G = G_π: 𝕋̂_π ⥲ 𝕋_π of free rank-one 𝕋_π-modules; (ii) Hom_{O_π}(lim_{→r} S^ord_κ(K^p_r, O_π), O_π)_{m_π} is a free 𝕋_π-module.
items.note: Transcribed exactly from the page image; the whole hypothesis is on p. 110 (the earlier item put it on p. 111). Here, for any r and K^p, 𝕋_π acts on Hom_{O_π}(S^ord_κ(K^p_r,O_π),O_π)_{m_π} by the natural action. ‘This is, of course, a variant of the condition 6.7.9’. v4 had Hom_{Λ_π}(𝕋_π,Λ_π); v2/v3 (Hypothesis 7.1.4) had 𝕋̂_π = Hom_{Λ_π}(𝕋_{π^♭},Λ_π) with the action twisted by ♭. Remark 9.3.1: verifiable by Taylor–Wiles methods when the residual Galois representation has large image, not valid in general. One of the hypotheses of Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The Gorenstein isomorphisms G_r at finite level
items.statement: Under Hypothesis 7.3.2, the isomorphism G_π induces compatible isomorphisms G_r: 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⥲ 𝕋_{r,κ} at finite level K_r, as in Definition 6.7.9, for r ≥ 1 (𝕋̂_{r,κ} = Hom_{O_π}(𝕋_{r,κ},O_π)).
items.note: Asserted without proof. It follows from Theorem 7.3.1: since 𝕋_π is finite free over Λ^o_π, 𝕋̂_π ⊗ Λ^o_π/I = Hom_{O_π}(𝕋_π ⊗ Λ^o_π/I, O_π), and control identifies 𝕋_π ⊗ Λ^o_π/I with the finite-level algebra — so only for κ sufficiently regular and with the level-r form of the control theorem (see thm-7-3-1-b). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The set S(K^p,π) of ordinary forms congruent to π in all weights and levels
items.statement: S(K^p,π) = ∪_{r≥1} ∪_{κ^1} S(K_r,κ^1,π): the automorphic representations π′ of varying level at p and weight with λ̄_{π′} = λ̄_π.
items.note: S(K_r,κ^1,π) as in (149); λ̄_{π′} and λ̄_π are compared through the big Hecke algebra (Theorem 7.1.1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Hypothesis 7.3.3 — global multiplicity one
items.statement: (Global Multiplicity One) Let π′ ∈ S(K^p,π). Then the representation π′ occurs with multiplicity one in the cuspidal spectrum of G.
items.note: Transcribed exactly; p. 110 confirmed. ‘This is the extension of Hypothesis 6.6.4 to all π′ ∈ S(K^p,π), but it is weaker because it refers to the global automorphic representation and not only to the corresponding character of the global unramified Hecke algebra. As noted above, it is implied by [Mok15, KMSW14].’ By Theorem 7.1.1 one may identify 𝕋_π with 𝕋_{π′} for π′ ∈ S(K^p,π). v4 stated it for π′ ∈ S(K_r,κ,π). Remark 9.3.2 sketches its removal. One of the hypotheses of Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 plans the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs.

items.name: §7.3.4 — the lattices Î_π and I_π
items.statement: Write O = O_π. By Hypothesis 7.3.2(ii), Hom_O(lim_{→r} S^ord_κ(K_r,O)_{m_π},O) is a free 𝕋_π-module of finite rank; fix a finite free O-module Î_π with a 𝕋_π-isomorphism 𝕋_π ⊗_O Î_π ⥲ Hom_O(lim_{→r} S^ord_κ(K_r,O)_{m_π},O) = lim_{←r} H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)_π. Specializing (tensoring with Λ^o_π/I_κ) gives 𝕋_{K^p_r,κ,O} ⊗_O Î_π ⥲ Hom_O(S^ord_κ(K_r,O)_{m_π},O) = H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)_π; restricting to λ_π-isotypic parts gives Î_π ⥲ T_{K^p_r,κ,O}[λ_π] ⊗_O Î_π = (T_{K^p_r,κ,O,π} ⊗_O Î_π)[λ_π] ⥲ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)[λ_π], and (j^∨_{π^♭})^{-1} yields an injection H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)[λ_π] ↪ π^{♭,a-ord}_{p,r} ⊗ π^{♭,K_S}_S ≅ π^{♭,K_S}_S (fixing a basis f^{a-ord}_{π^♭_p,r} of the line π^{♭,a-ord}_p), so Î_π is a free O-lattice in π^{♭,K_S}_S. Tensoring with T_{K^p_r,κ,O}/ker(λ_π) gives Î_π ⥲ T_{K^p_r,κ,O}/ker(λ_π) ⊗_O Î_π ⥲ Hom_O(S^ord_κ(K_r,O)[λ_π],O). With I_π = Hom(Î_π,O) one gets an O-module injection I_π ⥲ S^ord_κ(K_r,O)[λ_π] ↪ π^ord_p ⊗ π^{K_S}_S ≅ π^{K_S}_S (fixing a basis f^ord_{π_p} of π^ord_p).
items.note: The anti-ordinary subspace π^{♭,a-ord}_p ⊂ π^{♭,I_r}_p is the tensor product over w | p of the local anti-ordinary subspaces π_w^{a-ord,I_{w,r}} (Lemma 8.3.6). Printed ‘lim H^{d,ord}_κ’ (should be κ^D) and ‘tensoring over Λ_π with Λ_π/I_κ’ (should be Λ^o_π). The specialization step uses only Theorem 7.3.1(ii) (control for the Hecke algebra) although it needs control for the module of forms (Hida’s (33)) — source issue ‘§7.3.4 module control’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 7.3.5 (‘Minimality Hypothesis’) — finite-level freeness compatible with Î_π
items.statement: (Minimality Hypothesis) For every pair (κ^1,r^1) [with κ^1 sufficiently regular], there is an isomorphism of 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ^1,O,π}-modules 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ^1,O,π} ⊗ Î_π ⥲ Hom(S^ord_{κ^1}(K^p_{r^1},O)_{m_π},O) such that, when r^1 > r, the square formed with 𝕋_{K^p_r,κ^1,O,π} ⊗ Î_π ⥲ Hom_O(S^ord_{κ^1}(K^p_r,O)_{m_π},O) and the natural vertical maps commutes. Moreover [for κ^1 = κ, the weight of π], the specialization of this isomorphism at the O-valued point λ_π (tensoring both sides over 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ,O,π} with 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ,O,π}/ker(λ_π) ≃ O) gives a commutative diagram whose top row is 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ,O,π}/ker(λ_π) ⊗_O Î_π ⥲ Hom_O(S^ord_κ(K^p_{r^1},O)_{m_π},O) ⊗_{𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ,O,π}} 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ,O,π}/ker(λ_π), whose left vertical map is the identification with O ⊗_O Î_π, whose right vertical map goes to Hom_O(I_π,O), and whose bottom arrow is the tautological isomorphism Î_π ⥲ Hom(I_π,O).
items.note: Printed: ‘In view of the comment following Hypothesis 7.3.3, the following consequence of Hypotheses 7.3.2 and 7.3.3 follows from the preceding discussion and Theorem 7.1.1.’ No separate proof. The bracketed qualifications are added: the derivation uses the control theorem at (κ^1,r^1), which requires κ^1 sufficiently regular, and the ‘Moreover’ part specializes at λ_π, which is a point of the weight-κ algebra only (the printed tensor subscripts mix r, r^1, κ, κ^1) — source issues ‘Proposition 7.3.5’. History: in v2/v3 this was Hypothesis 7.1.7 (Minimality Hypothesis, ‘π minimal in the sense of Taylor–Wiles’); in v4 ‘Proposition 7.3.5 (Minimality)’, ‘a simple rephrasing of the preceding discussion’; v5 Main Theorem 9.2.2 still lists ‘Proposition-Hypothesis 7.3.5 (the Minimality Hypothesis)’ among its hypotheses, while Propositions 7.4.13 and 7.4.15 in v5 no longer assume it (v4 did). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The analogous lattice for π^♭ and the identification Î_{π^♭} = I_π
items.statement: Assuming Hom_O(lim_{→r} S^ord_{κ^♭}(K^♭_r,O)_{m^♭_π},O) is a free 𝕋_{π^♭}-module of finite rank, and using 𝕋_π ≅ 𝕋_{π^♭} from Lemma 6.6.7(ii), one fixes similarly a 𝕋_π-module isomorphism 𝕋_π ⊗_O I_π ⥲ Hom_O(lim_{→r} S^ord_{κ^♭}(K^♭_r,O)_{m^♭_π},O) = lim_{←r} H^{d,ord}_{κ^{♭,D}}(K^♭_r,O)_π with the corresponding properties. Since π ↦ π^♭, g ↦ g^♭, maps holomorphic forms to anti-holomorphic forms, the free O-module Î_{π^♭} is identified with I_π.
items.note: Printed ‘lim H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭}’ (should be κ^{♭,D}). The freeness over 𝕋_{π^♭} is an extra assumption (the ♭-analogue of Hypothesis 7.3.2(ii)), stated in running text. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §7.4 — level subgroups for the doubled group and the module 𝒱 of ordinary p-adic cusp forms on G_3
items.statement: Fix a prime-to-p level K^p_1 ⊂ G_1(A_f^p) and let K_{1,r} = I_rK^p_1 ⊂ G_1(A_f). Under the canonical identification G_2(A_f) = G_1(A_f), let K^p_2 = (K^p_1)^♭ ⊂ G_2(A_f) and K_{2,r} = K^♭_{1,r} ⊂ G_2(A_f). Let K^p = (K^p_1 × K^p_2) ∩ G_3(A_f^p) and K_{3,r} = (K_{1,r} × K_{2,r}) ∩ G_3(A_f). For O = O_π, 𝒱 = V^{ord,cusp}(K^p,O) (= V^{ord,cusp}_3(K^p,O)) is the space of ordinary p-adic cusp forms on G_3 with values in O; it is a Λ_O-module by the action on the first factor.
items.note: Remark 7.4.1: the Eisenstein measure does not generally take values in cusp forms, even after ordinary projection, but one localizes at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal; much of §7.4 applies without change to measures valued in ordinary p-adic forms. The ‘Guide to this section’ (p. 113) explains the aim: an element of Λ_{X_p}⊗̂𝕋⊗End_O(I_π) from a 𝒱-valued measure on X_p × T. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Finite-level quotients Λ_r of Λ and the perfect pairing Λ_r ⊗ C_r(T,O) → O
items.statement: Choose congruence subgroups T ⊃ … ⊃ T_r ⊃ T_{r+1} ⊃ … with ∩_r T_r = {1}. With Λ = Λ_π = O[[T]], let 𝓘_r ⊂ Λ be the augmentation ideal of T_r and Λ_r = Λ/𝓘_r. Let C_r(T,O) = C(T/T_r,O) be the free O-module of T_r-invariant functions on T. Then Λ_r = Hom_O(C_r(T,O),O); viewing Λ as O-valued distributions on T, the canonical pairing Λ_π ⊗ C(T,O) → O restricts to Λ ⊗ C_r(T,O) → O, which factors through a perfect pairing Λ_r ⊗ C_r(T,O) → O. η_r: C_r(T,O) ↪ C_{r+1}(T,O) is the canonical inclusion. An involution υ: T → T is fixed, and for ρ ∈ C(T,O), ρ^υ = ρ∘υ.
items.note: Standard (Mazur’s dictionary, Fact 5.1.2). Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.2 — equivariant measures on T as compatible families of Λ-linear maps (corrected)
items.statement: Fix a character ρ: T → O^× and let C_r(T,O)·ρ^υ ⊂ C(T,O) denote the multiples of ρ^υ by elements of C_r(T,O). There is an equivalence between (1) 𝒱-valued measures φ on T satisfying the equivariance φ(t·f) = υ(t)·φ(f) for f ∈ C(T,O), t ∈ T (t acting on f by translation and on 𝒱 through its Λ-module structure), and (2) collections φ_ρ = (φ_{r,ρ}) with φ_{r,ρ} ∈ Hom_Λ(C_r(T,O)·ρ^υ, 𝒱) satisfying η^*_r(φ_{r+1,ρ}) = φ_{r,ρ}, where η^*_r is induced by the dual of η_r. The equivalence is such that φ(f) = φ_{r,ρ}(f·ρ^υ) for f ∈ C_r(T,O).
items.note: ‘The next lemma follows from the definitions.’ Condition (1) is printed in v4 and v5 as φ(t·f) = ρ^υ(t)·φ(f) (a scalar), which forces φ to vanish on all finite-order characters ψ ≠ ρ^υ and hence φ = 0 unless ρ^υ has finite order; v2/v3 (Lemma 7.2.2) printed φ(t·f) = υ(t)·φ(f), adopted here — source issue ‘Lemma 7.4.2’. The exact placement of the twist by ρ^υ depends on the translation convention, which the paper does not fix. Consequence stated after the lemma: with 𝓘_{r,ρ} ⊂ Λ the annihilator of C_r(T,O)·ρ^υ and Λ_{r,ρ} = Λ_π/𝓘_{r,ρ}, equivariant measures on T with twist ρ^υ correspond to compatible collections of linear forms on Λ_{r,ρ}. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: The dual 𝒱̂ and the specialized measures φ_{χ,r,ρ}
items.statement: 𝓘_{r,ρ} ⊂ Λ is the annihilator of C_r(T,O)·ρ^υ and Λ_{r,ρ} = Λ_π/𝓘_{r,ρ}. 𝒱̂ = Hom_O(𝒱,O). Let φ be an equivariant measure on T with twist ρ^υ, assumed to be the specialization at a character χ of X_p of an admissible measure in two variables with shift sh^*(χ) = (α(χ),β(χ)) and twist υ as in §5.2.2; then φ is equivalent (Lemma 7.4.2) to φ_{χ,ρ} = (φ_{χ,r,ρ}).
items.note: Admissible measures on X_p × T_H with shift and twist are defined in §5.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 7.4.3 — the notation [⊗] for restrictions to G_3
items.statement: M_{κ_1}(K_{1,r},ψ_1;R) [⊗]_R M_{κ_2}(K_{2,r},ψ_2;R) denotes the image of res_4 (from M_{κ_1}(K_{1,r},ψ_1;R) ⊗_R M_{κ_2}(K_{2,r},ψ_2;R), forms on G_1 × G_2) in M_κ(K_{3,r},ψ;R); [⊗] is used more generally for restrictions of this kind from (classical or p-adic) modular forms on G_1 × G_2 to forms on G_3.
items.note: res_4 is defined in (45) (§3.2). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (156) and consequences — images of φ_{χ,r,ρ} are classical
items.statement: For κ = ρ·α(χ) sufficiently regular, Im(φ_{χ,r,ρ}) ⊂ S^ord_{(ρ·α(χ)),V}(K_{1,r},O) [⊗] S^ord_{(ρ^♭·β(χ)),−V}(K_{2,r},O) (156). Also 𝒱̂ = lim_{←r} Hom_O(S^ord_{ρ,V}(K_{1,r},O) [⊗] S^ord_{ρ^♭,−V}(K_{2,r},O), O). Hence, for κ = ρ·α(χ) sufficiently regular, Im(φ_{χ,r,ρ}) ⊂ Hom_O(Ŝ^ord_{(ρ·α(χ)),V}(K_{1,r},O), S^ord_{(ρ^♭·β(χ)),−V}(K_{2,r},O)).
items.note: Asserted without proof. (156) combines admissibility (values of weight ρ△·sh^*(χ) and level r nebentypus) with Hida’s classicality (32); the description of 𝒱̂ needs density of the classical ordinary forms of the fixed weight (ρ,ρ^♭) (for ρ sufficiently regular) in 𝒱. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Assumption 7.4.4 — Hecke equivariance of the measure (Garrett map property)
items.statement: Im(φ_{χ,r,ρ}) ⊂ Hom_{T_{r,ρ·α(χ)}}(Ŝ^ord_{(ρ·α(χ)),V}(K_{1,r},O), S^ord_{(ρ·α(χ))^♭,−V}(K_{2,r},O) ⊗ χ∘det), where T_{r,ρ·α(χ)} acts on S^ord_{(ρ·α(χ))^♭,−V}(K_{2,r},O) via the map of Lemma 6.6.7(ii).
items.note: ‘Expresses a basic property of the Garrett map that is the basis of the doubling method.’ φ_{χ,r,ρ} integrates functions locally equal to ρ^υ (not ρ) against the specialization at χ of a two-variable measure. Remark 7.4.5: one writes κ = ρ·α(χ) to emphasize the weight of the specialized Hecke algebra; T_κ = T_{r,ρ·α(χ)} ignores the twist by χ∘det; incorporating χ∘det into the subscript of the second S^ord replaces α(χ)^♭ by β(χ) of (156). Verified for axiomatic Eisenstein measures in Lemma 9.1.5. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (157) and ‘Assumption 7.4.6’ — localized equivariance and its Gorenstein reformulation
items.statement: Let π be an anti-holomorphic representation of G_1 of type (κ = ρ·α(χ), K_r) and φ_{χ,r,ρ,π} the composition of φ_{χ,r,ρ} with projection to the localization at m_π in the first variable. Then Assumption 7.4.4 implies Im(φ_{χ,r,ρ,π}) ⊂ Hom_{T^ord_{r,κ,V,π}}(Ŝ^ord_{κ,V,π}(K_{1,r},O), S^ord_{κ^♭,−V,π^♭}(K_{2,r},O) ⊗ χ∘det) (157). Both Ŝ^ord_{r,V,π} := Ŝ^ord_{κ,V,π}(K_{1,r},O) and S^ord_{r,−V,π^♭} := S^ord_{κ^♭,−V,π^♭}(K_{2,r},O) are free 𝕋_{r,κ,π}-modules of the same rank, and by §7.3.4 there are 𝕋_π-isomorphisms 𝕋_{r,κ,π} ⊗ Î_π ⥲ Ŝ^ord_{r,V,π} and 𝕋̂_{r,κ,π} ⊗ Î_π ⥲ S^ord_{r,−V,π^♭}. Hence (after tensoring with χ^{-1}∘det in the first line) Im(φ_{χ,r,ρ,π}) ⊂ Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ,π}}(Ŝ^ord_{r,V,π}, S^ord_{r,−V,π^♭} ⊗ χ∘det) ⥲ Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(𝕋_{r,κ,π} ⊗ Î_π, 𝕋̂_{r,κ,π} ⊗ I_{π^♭}) ⥲ Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(𝕋_{r,κ,π}, 𝕋̂_{r,κ,π}) ⊗_O End_O(I_{π^♭}).
items.note: Although labelled ‘Assumption 7.4.6’, it is derived (‘Thus Assumption 7.4.4 yields’); the freeness is attributed to the Gorenstein hypothesis (with control for κ sufficiently regular). The isomorphisms depend on choices, ‘but the final results will not depend on these’. Printed subscript 𝕋_{r,κ·a(χ)} in the second line should be 𝕋_{r,κ} (combined misprint entry). I_{π^♭} = Î_π via the identification Î_{π^♭} = I_π of §7.3.4. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Fact 7.4.7 — distribution relation for φ_{r,κ} under change of level
items.statement: Write C_r = C_r(T,O), drop O from the notation and ignore the twists by χ∘det (no localization at m_π). Let ι_r: S^ord_{r,V} ↪ S^ord_{r+1,V} be the tautological inclusion and ι^*_r: Ŝ^ord_{r+1,V} → Ŝ^ord_{r,V} its dual; let i^*_r: Hom_{T_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r,V}, S^ord_{r,−V}) → Hom_{T_{r+1,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r+1,V}, S^ord_{r+1,−V}) be ι^*_r in the contravariant variable composed with ι_r in the covariant variable. Under Assumption 7.4.4, for all r the image of φ_{r+1,κ} under η^*_r ⊗ id^*_{r+1} lies in Im(i^*_r); more precisely (η^*_r ⊗ id^*_{r+1})(φ_{r+1,κ}) = ι_r ∘ φ_{r,κ} ∘ (id_{C_r} ⊗ ι^*_r) (158) as maps from C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r+1,V} to S^ord_{r+1,−V}.
items.note: By the equivariance hypothesis the tensor products may be taken over Λ_π, and Hom_{T_{r+1,κ}} is relative to the Hecke action on Ŝ^ord_{r+1,V} and S^ord_{r+1,−V}. No proof: it follows from the compatibility η^*_r(φ_{r+1}) = φ_r of Lemma 7.4.2 and the fact that φ_r takes values in level-r forms. Printed ‘lies in Im(ι^*_r)’; the diagram’s vertical map is i^*_r (combined misprint entry). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §7.4.8 — Serre-duality model (159) of Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R_0)
items.statement: Let R_0 be a finite Z_(p)-algebra whose p-adic completion embeds in O_π. Identify S_{κ,V}(K_r,R_0) with an R_0-lattice in H^0_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_κ); let H^{0,ord}_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω_κ) be the C-span of S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R_0) and H^{d,ord}_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω^D_κ) the corresponding quotient of H^d_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω^D_κ); the Hecke action identifies H^{d,ord}_! with a direct summand of H^d_! in perfect pairing with H^{0,ord}_!. Then Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R_0) is identified with the R_0-lattice H^{d,ord}_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω^D_κ)(R_0) := {h ∈ H^{d,ord}_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω^D_κ) | ⟨f,h⟩_{κ,K_r} ∈ R_0 for all f ∈ S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R_0)} (159).
items.note: Lemma 7.4.9, Proposition 7.4.10 and Definition 7.4.11 are written with κ in place of ρ·α(χ). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.9 — ι^*_r is the normalized trace
items.statement: With respect to (159), the map ι^*_r: Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_{r+1},R_0) → Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,R_0) is given by the trace map t_r(h) = (#(I^0_r/I_r)/#(I^0_{r+1}/I_{r+1}))·∑_{γ∈K_r/K_{r+1}} γ(h). In particular t_r defines a surjective homomorphism H^{d,ord}_!(_{K_{r+1}}Sh(V),ω^D_κ)(R_0) → H^{d,ord}_!(_{K_r}Sh(V),ω^D_κ)(R_0).
items.note: Proof: ‘essentially a rewording of Section 6.4’ — by (138), ⟨ι_r f, h⟩_{κ,K_{r+1}} = ⟨f, t_r h⟩_{κ,K_r} with exactly this normalization (checked: Vol(I^0_r)/Vol(I^0_{r+1}) = #(I^0_r/I_r)·#(I_r/I_{r+1})/#(I^0_{r+1}/I_{r+1})). Surjectivity from Lemma 6.6.14. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Identification Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r,V}, S^ord_{r,−V}) ≃ 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭})
items.statement: Completing at m_π (O = O_π, subscript π omitted), as in Assumption 7.4.6: Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r,V}, S^ord_{r,−V}) ≃ Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ 𝕋_{r,κ} ⊗ Î_π, 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⊗ I_{π^♭}) = Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ 𝕋_{r,κ}, 𝕋̂_{r,κ}) ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭}) ≃ 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭}), ‘with appropriate modifications to accommodate a function Φ_X as above’, using Proposition 7.3.5 systematically.
items.note: The last step absorbs C_r because the tensor products are over Λ (Λ acts on 𝕋_{r,κ} through Λ_r). ‘Φ_X as above’ refers to nothing in v4/v5: the definition of measures of type Φ_X = (Φ_a,Φ_b) (v2/v3 eq. (7.2.2)) was deleted in v4 — source issue ‘Φ_X’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.10 — the measure {φ_{r,κ}} defines L(φ) ∈ 𝕋 ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭}), independent of the weight
items.statement: Let 𝕋 = 𝕋_π. With respect to the identifications Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r,V}, S^ord_{r,−V}) ≃ 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭}), (158), and the isomorphism G_r: 𝕋̂_{r,κ} ⥲ 𝕋_{r,κ} of the Gorenstein Hypothesis 7.3.2, the measure {φ_{r,κ}} defines an element L(φ_κ) ∈ lim_{←r} 𝕋_{r,κ} ⊗ I_{π^♭} ⊗ I_π ⥲ 𝕋 ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭}). Moreover, if κ^1 is a second sufficiently regular character, then L(φ_κ) and L(φ_{κ^1}) are identified with respect to the identifications 𝕋 ⥲ 𝕋_{K^p,κ,O_π} ⥲ 𝕋_{K^p,κ^1,O_π} of Theorem 7.1.1 (after localization at π). Thus {φ_{r,κ}} and {φ_{r,κ^1}} define the same element L(φ) ∈ 𝕋 ⊗ End_O(I_{π^♭}). Conversely, any such L(φ) defines a measure {φ_{r,κ}} for any sufficiently regular κ.
items.note: Proof: ‘a consequence of Lemma 7.4.9 and follows by unwinding the definitions.’ The existence of L(φ_κ) follows from (158), Lemma 7.4.9 and the compatibility of the G_r; the weight-independence (‘Moreover’) is not argued — source issue ‘Proposition 7.4.10’. Printed subscript Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ,♭}}. I_{π^♭} ⊗ I_π = End_O(I_{π^♭}) via Î_{π^♭} = I_π. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Measures on X_p × T from families of measures on T
items.statement: A 𝒱-valued measure on X_p × T is the same as a measure on X_p with values in 𝒱-valued measures on T (Lemma 5.1.1). In particular one obtains a 𝒱-valued measure on X_p × T from a collection, for all characters α of X_p, of 𝒱-valued measures φ_α of type α on T satisfying the congruence properties of Lemma 5.1.3; the construction of Proposition 7.4.10 adapts to the compact p-adic Lie group X_p.
items.note: Lemma 5.1.3 is the paper’s version of [Kat78, Proposition 4.1.2] (R flat over Z_p with enough roots of unity; Kummer congruences). 𝐓 is identified with the ordinary Hecke algebra of G = G_1 (with appropriate modifications for G_2). Planned: PadicMeasuresIwasawaAlgebras L1 plans completed group rings and the measure–group-ring equivalence; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Definition 7.4.11 — classical points X(κ,r,R), X^class(R), and λ_taut
items.statement: Fix a level r, a character κ and an O-algebra R. A continuous homomorphism λ: 𝐓 → R is classical of level p^r and weight κ if it factors through a homomorphism (still denoted) λ: 𝐓_{r,κ} → R which is of the form λ_π for some anti-holomorphic automorphic representation π of type (κ,K_{1,r}), with K_{1,r} = K^pI_r for some open compact K^p ⊂ G(A_f^p). X(κ,r,R) is the set of classical homomorphisms of level p^r and weight κ with values in R, and X^class(R) = ∪_{κ,r} X(κ,r,R); any λ ∈ X^class(R) is called classical. When R = 𝐓_{r,κ}, λ_taut: 𝐓_{r,κ} → 𝐓_{r,κ} is the identity; for π cuspidal anti-holomorphic of weight κ, λ_{taut,π}: 𝐓_{r,κ} → 𝕋_{r,κ,π} is λ_taut followed by localization at m_π.
items.note: When κ is sufficiently regular λ_taut ‘deserves to be called classical’: its composition with any map from 𝐓_{r,κ} to a p-adic field is attached to a classical form of weight κ. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.12 — the specializations L(φ_χ,κ,r) and the finite-level maps φ_{χ,r,κ}
items.statement: Let χ be a character of X_p and φ = dφ(x,t) a measure on X_p × T as in §5.2.2 with shift sh: sh^*(χ) = (α(χ),β(χ)). Let ρ be an algebraic character of T and κ = ρ·α(χ). Fix a cuspidal anti-holomorphic representation π of weight κ satisfying the hypotheses above (7.3.2, 7.3.3, Assumption 7.4.4). Consider L(φ_χ) = ∫_{X_p} χ(x)dφ(x,t), localized at m_π, as an element of 𝕋 ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}) (Proposition 7.4.10), and let L(φ_χ,κ,r) be its image in 𝕋_{r,κ} ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}). Equivalently L(φ_χ,κ,r) = ∫_{X_p×T} χ × λ_{taut,π} dφ(x,t), where integration against λ_{taut,π} amounts to the projection 𝐓 ↠ 𝐓 ⊗_Λ Λ_{r,κ} = 𝐓_{r,κ} followed by localization at m_π. Then L(φ_χ,κ,r) corresponds to the element φ_{χ,r,κ} ∈ Hom_{𝕋_{r,κ}}(C_r ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{r,V,π}, S^ord_{r,−V,π^♭} ⊗ χ∘det) under the identifications of Proposition 7.3.5, compatibly with the Gorenstein isomorphism G_r (from Proposition 7.4.10).
items.note: Proof: ‘just a restatement of the definition of the element L(φ) ∈ 𝕋 ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}) = 𝕋_π ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}) introduced in Proposition 7.4.10.’ The identity 𝐓 ⊗_Λ Λ_{r,κ} = 𝐓_{r,κ} is the level-r control theorem (see thm-7-2-1-b).Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.13 — abstract p-adic L-functions of families
items.statement: (Abstract p-adic L-functions of families) Let φ = dφ(x,t) be a measure on X_p × T such that, for each character χ of X_p, ∫_{X_p} χ(x)dφ(x,t) is a 𝒱-valued measure φ_χ of type χ satisfying Assumption 7.4.4. Fix a cuspidal anti-holomorphic representation π satisfying Hypotheses 7.3.2 and 7.3.3. Then there is an element L(φ) ∈ Λ_{X_p} ⊗̂ 𝕋 ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}) such that, for every R-valued character χ of X_p, the image of L(φ) under the map χ ⊗ Id: Λ_{X_p} ⊗̂ 𝕋 ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}) → 𝕋 ⊗ End_R(I_{π^♭}) given by contraction in the first factor, or equivalently integration against χ with respect to the first variable, is the element L(φ_χ) of Proposition 7.4.12.
items.note: No proof: ‘an elementary consequence of Proposition 7.4.10’ (with 𝕋 = 𝕋_π = 𝐓_{m_π}). Convention stated just before: an anti-holomorphic cuspidal representation satisfies Hypotheses 7.3.2 and 7.3.3 if its complex conjugate (or contragredient) does. v4 also assumed ‘7.3.5’. Transcription checked against the page image. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.4.14 — measures are determined by classical specializations of one weight ([Hid88, Lemma 3.3])
items.statement: The 𝒱-valued measure φ = φ_χ of type χ and the abstract L-function L(φ) are completely determined by their integrals against elements of the sets X(κ,r,O_{C_p}) for any fixed sufficiently regular κ and all r.
items.note: Cited as a standard fact (‘see, for example, [Hid88, Lemma 3.3]’); no proof. Underlying reason: for fixed κ the characters κψ, ψ of finite order of all levels, are Zariski dense in Spec Λ. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equations (160)–(161) — the scalar specializations L(χ,φ,r,κ,φ⊗φ^♭)
items.statement: Write End_R(I_{π^♭}) = Î_{π^♭} ⊗ I_{π^♭} ≃ Hom(Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}, R) (160). For φ⊗φ^♭ ∈ Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭} define L(χ,φ,r,κ,φ⊗φ^♭) = [L(φ_χ,κ,r), φ⊗φ^♭]_loc ∈ 𝕋_{r,κ} (161), where [•,•]_loc is the tautological pairing Hom(Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭},R) ⊗ Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭} → R (extended 𝕋_{r,κ}-linearly).
items.note: (160) uses Î_{π^♭} = I_π, so Î_{π^♭} ⊗ I_{π^♭} = I_π ⊗ I_{π^♭} = Hom(Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}, R). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 7.4.15 — the scalar p-adic L-function L(φ, φ⊗φ^♭) ∈ Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋
items.statement: Fix an embedding O_π ↪ C extending E(π) ⊂ C, and let R be a p-adic ring containing O_π and satisfying the conditions of Lemma 5.1.3. Let φ be an admissible R-measure on X_p × T as in §5.2.2. Assume Hypotheses 7.3.2 and 7.3.3. Let φ⊗φ^♭ ∈ Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}. Then there is a unique element L(φ, φ⊗φ^♭) ∈ Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 such that, for any classical χ: X_p → R^× and any λ ∈ X(κ,r,R) (with κ sufficiently regular), the image of L(φ, φ⊗φ^♭) under the map Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 → R induced by the character χ ⊗ λ equals λ ∘ L(χ,φ,r,κ,φ⊗φ^♭).
items.note: No proof: ‘We reformulate Proposition 7.4.12 in terms of Equation (161).’ Existence comes from Proposition 7.4.13 paired with φ⊗φ^♭; uniqueness from Lemma 7.4.14 and density of classical χ (Lemma 5.1.3). The measure must satisfy Assumption 7.4.4 (implicit). v4 assumed Hypotheses 7.3.2, 7.3.3 and 7.3.5 and had no ‘λ∘’. This is the form used for Corollary 9.2.1 and Main Theorem 9.2.2. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.1 — Hecke equivariance of the pairing with a λ_π-eigenclass
items.statement: Let h ∈ S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,O) and φ ∈ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)[π], in the notation of §6.6. Then the map 𝕋 → O, A ↦ ⟨A(h),φ⟩_{κ,K_r}, takes A to λ_π(A)·⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r}.
items.note: Proof: ⟨A(h),φ⟩_{κ,K_r} = ⟨h,A^♭(φ)⟩_{κ,K_r} = λ_{π^♭}(A^♭)⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} = λ_π(A)⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} (using (148)). Since H^{d,ord} is a Hecke module through the transpose action (Lemma 6.6.1(i)), the lemma is immediate from the definition of [π]; the proof writes A^♭ where the Serre adjoint is A^d. ‘The following is essentially obvious’; ⟨·,·⟩^Ser_κ as in (132). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Equation (162) — pairing with φ picks out the π-component; denominators bounded by C(π)
items.statement: h need not be an eigenform: extending O to contain O_{π′} for π′ ∈ S(K_r,κ,π^♭), write h = ∑_{π′∈S(K_r,κ,π^♭)} a_{π′} h_{π′} with a_{π′} ∈ O[1/p] and h_{π′} in the λ_{π′}-eigenspace for 𝕋. Then, under the hypotheses of Lemma 7.5.1, ⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} = a_π ⟨h_π,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} (162), and the denominator of a_π is bounded by the congruence ideal C(π) = C(π^♭).
items.note: The projection onto the (dual) λ_π-eigenspace can in general only be defined over O[1/p]. The text says ‘where of course h_π ∈ π^♭’ and ‘In what follows we are making use of Corollary 6.7.10’ (it is Lemma 6.7.10) — see combined misprint entry and issue ‘Corollary 6.7.10’. In §7.5 π is anti-holomorphic (π^♭ holomorphic) while Lemma 7.5.1 refers to §6.6 notation with π holomorphic. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.2 (first claim) — L_φ is a λ_π-eigenfunctional
items.statement: Let φ ∈ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)[π]. Then the linear functional h ↦ L_φ(h) := ⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} belongs to Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,O)[π].
items.note: Proof: from Lemma 7.5.1 (integrality from H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O) ≅ Ŝ^ord_κ(K_r,O)). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.2 (second claim) — values on S^ord[π] lie in the congruence ideal
items.statement: Let φ ∈ H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r,O)[π]. The restriction of L_φ to S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r,O)[π] takes values in the congruence ideal C(π) = C(π^♭) ⊂ O.
items.note: Proof cites Lemma 6.7.11 (C(π) = C(π^♭)); the containment itself is the definition of C(π) (Definition 6.7.2 with Lemma 6.7.3: ⟨S[π],H[π]⟩ = C(π)). This claim contradicts the printed perfectness of the [π]-pairing in Lemma 6.6.12(iii) whenever C(π) ≠ O. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Rational structures Î_{π,R}, Î_{π^♭,R}
