items.statement: Î_π (resp. Î_{π^♭}) was identified with an O-lattice in π^{a-ord}_p ⊗ π^{K^p}_{S^p} (resp. π^{♭,a-ord}_p ⊗ π^{♭,K^p}_{S^p}). Let R be a finite local Z_(p)[λ_π]-subalgebra of C that admits an embedding as a dense subring of O = O_π, and let Î_{π^♭,R}, Î_{π,R} be free R-modules given with isomorphisms Î_{π^♭,R} ⊗_R O ⥲ Î_{π^♭} and Î_{π,R} ⊗_R O ⥲ Î_π.
items.note: Used to compare p-adic and complex pairings (Lemma 7.5.3, §9). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 7.5.3 — L_φ(h) as a Petersson-type integral
items.statement: In the notation of Lemma 7.5.2, let φ ∈ Î_π. Identifying h with an element of H^0(𝔓_h(V),K_h; 𝒜_0(G) ⊗ W_κ)^{K_r} and φ with an element of H^d(𝔓_h(−V),K_h; 𝒜_0(G) ⊗ W_{κ^D})^{K^♭_r} as in (114), L_φ(h) = Vol(I^0_{r,V})^{-1} ∫_{G(Q)Z_G(R)\G(A)} [h(g),φ(g)]·||ν(g)||^{-a(κ)} dg, as follows from (133) and (136)–(137). (Printed with the factor 1/(Vol(I^0_{r,V})·Vol(I^0_{r,−V})).)
items.note: ‘The following lemma is then just a restatement of (133).’ The printed normalization 1/(Vol(I^0_{r,V})Vol(I^0_{r,−V})) disagrees with L_φ(h) := ⟨h,φ⟩_{κ,K_r} = Vol(I^0_{r,V})^{-1}⟨h,φ⟩^Ser (136)–(137); the product of two volumes is the natural normalization for the doubled group G_3, where Proposition 9.1.7 applies the ‘doubled’ lemma — source issue ‘Lemma 7.5.3’. Variants with the twist by a Hecke character χ (as in (4.1.6) and §6.7.5) are ‘left to the reader’. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Rationality and positivity of the Serre pairing on π_f × π̄_f ([Har13a]) — cited
items.statement: For π anti-holomorphic (or holomorphic) cuspidal with π_f and π^♭_f ≅ π̄_f defined over the number field E(π), the Serre duality pairing ⟨·,·⟩^Ser between the E(π)-rational structures of the π- and π^♭-isotypic coherent cohomology is a C^×-multiple of an E(π)-valued pairing, and the multiple can be taken to be a positive real number (by the hermitian nature of the Petersson pairing and (134)).
items.note: ‘This is essentially explained in [Har13a]’; used as a black box to define the periods Q[π], Q_π (and Q[π,χ], Q_{π,χ}). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.0 — standing parameters (χ, χ_σ, m, κ, (r̃_σ, s̃_σ)) for §8
items.statement: Throughout §8 (following the conventions of §4.4.2), χ, χ_σ, m, κ and (r̃_σ, s̃_σ) are tied together as follows: χ = ||•||^m · χ_0 is an algebraic Hecke character of 𝒦, with m ∈ ℤ and χ_{0,σ}(z) = z^{−a(χ_σ)} z̄^{−b(χ_σ)} at every archimedean place σ; χ_σ is the component of χ at the archimedean place σ; (r̃_σ, s̃_σ) is the tuple of integers attached to integers r_1 ≥ r_2 ≥ ⋯ ≥ r_{a_σ} ≥ 0, s_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_{b_σ} ≥ 0 as in Inequalities (95) (r̃_i = r_i − r_{i+1}, s̃_j = s_j − s_{j+1}); and κ is the highest weight determined by m, χ_σ and (r_σ, s_σ) by Equation (94): κ_σ = (−m + b(χ_σ) − r_{a_σ}, …, −m + b(χ_σ) − r_1; m − a(χ_σ) + s_1, …, m − a(χ_σ) + s_{b_σ}) ∈ C_3(χ_σ).
items.note: Pure convention. Equation (94) (p. 69) lists C_3(χ_σ) = {(−m+b(χ_σ)−r_{a_σ}, …, −m+b(χ_σ)−r_1; m−a(χ_σ)+s_1, …, m−a(χ_σ)+s_{b_σ})} and (95) is r_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ r_{a_σ} ≥ 0, s_1 ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_{b_σ} ≥ 0. Note that §8.2 uses a second factorisation χ = χ_unitary |·|^{−k/2}_{𝒦/ℚ} of the same kind of character. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.1(a) — the p-adic differential operator θ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) and its comparison with δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) at ordinary CM points
items.statement: Let (r̃, s̃) and χ be as in §8.0. For every prime-to-p level subgroup K^p there is a differential operator θ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) = θ^d_χ(p(r̃, s̃)) : V_χ(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) → V(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) on p-adic modular forms on G_4 (the p-adic operator attached to the polynomial p(r̃, s̃) of (100), i.e. to the highest-weight vector of weight (r̃, s̃) in the d-th tensor power of the standard representation), compatible with change of level subgroup, such that for every K^p, every f ∈ M_χ(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) and every ordinary CM pair (J′_0, h_0) as in §3.2.4: R_{κ,J′_0,h_0} ∘ res_{J′_0,h_0} ∘ δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃)(f) = res_{p,J′_0,h_0} ∘ θ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) ∘ R_{κ,G,X}(f), in the notation of Proposition 3.2.5; here δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) is the C^∞ differential operator of §4.4.10.
items.note: Cited, not proved: the operators are those of [EFMV18, §6–§7], constructed in [EFMV18, Theorem 5.1.13] (with the weight κ and the operator Θ^κ of [EFMV18] corresponding to the highest weight (r̃, s̃)); the comparison at CM points follows [Kat78, §5.1] and is in [Eis12, §10, esp. Prop. 10.2]. That the image of cusp forms is cuspidal follows from the action on q-expansions. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans Katz's algebraic and p-adic differential operators and CM periods.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.1(b) — the restricted operator θ(κ, χ) = res_3 ∘ θ^d_χ(r̃, s̃)
items.statement: Let (κ, χ) be critical as in Corollary 4.4.9. Fix a level subgroup K_4 ⊂ G_4(𝔸_f) and a subgroup K_1 × K_2 ⊂ G_3(𝔸_f) ∩ K_4. The composition of θ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) (Proposition 8.1.1(a)) with the pullback res_3 := (γ_{V_p} ∘ ι_3)^* defines an operator θ(κ, χ) : V_χ(G_4, K^p_4, 𝒪) → V_κ(G_1, K^p_1, 𝒪) ⊗ V_{κ♭}(G_2, K^p_2, 𝒪) ⊗ χ∘det, where the tensor product with χ∘det is defined by analogy with Proposition 4.4.11.
items.note: Cited: follows from [EFMV18, Remark 6.2.7] (earlier form in [Eis16, Definition 12]). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans Katz's algebraic and p-adic differential operators and CM periods.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.1(c) — ordinary projection of θ(κ, χ) agrees with that of δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃)
items.statement: Let θ(κ, χ)^cusp be the restriction of θ(κ, χ) to V^cusp_χ(G_4, K^p_4, 𝒪) and let e_κ be the ordinary projector (31) attached to the weight κ, as in §6.6.6. Then, upon pullback to functions on G_4(𝔸) and restriction to G_3(𝔸) (via the maps (28) for G_3 and G_4), e_κ ∘ θ(κ, χ)^cusp = e_κ ∘ δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) : V^cusp_χ(G_4, K^p_4, 𝒪) → S_{κ,V}(K_1) ⊗ S_{κ♭,−V}(K_2) ⊗ χ∘det.
items.note: Proof in the paper: the image of θ(κ, χ)^cusp lies in V^cusp_κ(G_1, K^p_1, 𝒪) ⊗ V^cusp_{κ♭}(G_2, K^p_2, 𝒪) ⊗ χ∘det, and the claim 'follows from the control theorem (32)'. Formaliser's caution: (32) (p. 33) identifies ordinary p-adic cusp forms of weight κ with classical ones only when κ_{σ,i,a_{σ,i}} + κ_{σc,i,b_{σ,i}} ≫ n_i r_i; this regularity is not among the stated hypotheses of (c). The comparison of the two p-adic forms can instead be made at CM points using (a), which is what Proposition 8.1.3 does. 'the ordinary projector of 31' means that of equation (31). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.1(d) — the p-adic holomorphic-projection operator θ^hol(κ, χ)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of (a) and (b) there is a differential operator θ^hol(κ, χ) : V_χ(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) → V(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) whose composition with the pullback res_3 coincides with the operator D^hol(κ, χ) of Proposition 4.4.11, upon pullback to functions on G_4(𝔸), restriction to G_3(𝔸), and identification of ordinary modular forms with p-adic modular forms via (28).
items.note: Proof: by induction on the size of κ, the last part of Corollary 4.4.9 shows D^hol(κ, χ) is the pullback of the differential operator attached to a polynomial P^hol(κ, χ) ∈ ⊗_σ 𝒫(n)_σ; θ^hol(κ, χ) is defined as the p-adic differential operator attached to the same polynomial (Eischen's construction). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 8.1.2 — decomposition of θ(κ, χ) through θ^hol
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 8.1.1, for every κ† ≤ κ there are p-adic differential operators θ(κ, κ†) : V_χ(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) → V(G_4, K^p, 𝒪) such that θ(κ, χ) = Σ_{κ† ≤ κ} res_3 ∘ θ(κ, κ†) ∘ θ^hol(κ†, χ).
items.note: Stated as 'the p-adic version of the last part of Corollary 4.4.9'; no proof is given (see sourceIssues E127). The operators are printed θ(κ, λ); the display and all later uses write θ(κ, κ†) (misprint, see source issues). Source issues: sourceIssues E126, sourceIssues E127. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 8.1.3 — ordinary projection of θ(κ, χ)(F) equals ordinary projection of the holomorphic projection of δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ)(F)
items.statement: Let F ∈ H^0(Sh(G_4), ℒ(χ)). Assume κ, (r̃_σ, s̃_σ), m, χ_σ are as in §8.0, and let e_κ be the ordinary projector of Proposition 8.1.1(c) and pr^hol_κ the holomorphic projection of §4.4.7. Then (e_κ ∘ θ(κ, χ))(F) = e_κ ∘ pr^hol_κ ∘ δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ)(F)  (163).
items.note: Proof: by Corollary 8.1.2 the left side is Σ_{κ†≤κ} e_κ ∘ res_3 θ(κ, κ†) ∘ θ^hol(κ†, χ)(F); by Proposition 3.2.5 (p-adic forms are determined by their values at ordinary CM points) it suffices that, after composing with res_{p,J′_0,h_0} for every ordinary CM datum (J′_0, h_0): (1) the terms with κ† < κ vanish — by Lemma 8.1.4 and 'the fact that the ordinary projector commutes with the differential operators'; (2) the κ† = κ term equals e_κ ∘ pr^hol_κ ∘ δ(r̃_σ, s̃_σ)(F) — by Proposition 8.1.1(c). This is the input to Corollary 8.2.4. See source issues on Corollary 8.1.2 and on step (1). Source issues: sourceIssues E126, sourceIssues E127, sourceIssues E128. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.1.4 — e_κ kills forms of lower weight
items.statement: For any κ† < κ, the ordinary projector e_κ = lim_{→N} U_{p,κ}^{N!} converges absolutely to 0 on S_{κ†}(K_r; R).
items.note: Proof: for each w, j, U_{w,j,κ} = |κ′(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U_{w,j} with κ′ as in §2.6.11, so U_{p,κ} = ∏_{w,j} |κ′^{−1}·κ†′(t_{w,j})|_p · U_{w,j,κ†}; κ† < κ gives the product ∏_{w,j} κ′^{−1}κ†′(t_{w,j}) positive p-adic valuation, so U_{p,κ} has norm < 1 on S_{κ†}(K_r; R) (where the U_{w,j,κ†} are integral) and U_{p,κ}^{N!} → 0. The paper says 'equivalent'; only the implication κ† < κ ⇒ positive valuation is needed (plausible because, if t_{w,j} are the elements t_j of the proof of Lemma 8.3.2, ∏_j t_{w,j} = diag(p^n, p^{n−1}, …, p^{n−a_w+1}, p, p², …, p^{b_w}) is strictly dominant for B_w; the sign conventions for κ′ of §2.6.11 were not re-checked here). Source issues: sourceIssues E128. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.2 — the type-A_0 character χ = χ_unitary|·|^{−k/2}, its infinity type (k, ν) and its p-adic avatar χ̃ on X_p
items.statement: Let χ_unitary be a unitary Hecke character of 𝒦 and χ = χ_unitary |·|^{−k/2}_{𝒦/ℚ}, a Hecke character of type A_0, χ = ∏_w χ_w. There are integers k, ν_σ ∈ ℤ such that for every a ∈ 𝒦^×, χ_∞(a) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} χ_σ(a) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} (1/σ(a))^k (σ̄(a)/σ(a))^{ν_σ}, with σ̄ := σc; put ν = (ν_σ)_{σ∈Σ}. Let χ̃_∞ : (𝒦 ⊗ ℤ_p)^× → Q̄_p^× be the p-adically continuous character with χ̃_∞(a) = incl_p ∘ χ_∞(a) for all a ∈ 𝒦; its restriction to (𝒪 ⊗ ℤ_p)^× is 𝒪_{ℂ_p}^×-valued. Define χ̃ : X_p → 𝒪_{ℂ_p}^× by χ̃((a_w)) = χ̃_∞((a_w)_{w|p}) ∏_{w∤∞} χ_w(a_w), where X_p = lim_r 𝒦^× \ (𝒦 ⊗ Ẑ)^× / U_r, U_r = (𝒪 ⊗ Ẑ^p)^× × (1 + p^r 𝒪 ⊗ ℤ_p) (§5.2).
items.note: Standard p-adic avatar of an algebraic Hecke character (the product ∏_{w∤∞} includes the places above p). χ̃ is trivial on 𝒦^× because χ is, and χ̃_∞ = incl_p∘χ_∞ on 𝒦. The phrase 'Let χ = χ_unitary|·|^{−k/2}. So χ is of type A_0' presupposes that χ_unitary has the appropriate infinity type. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; Tau Ceti's GlobalNumberFields Layer 10 plans infinity types and type-A_0 Hecke characters.

items.name: §8.2 — signature data (a, b), the character c = ψ·ρ^υ, and the Siegel section f(χ, c)
items.statement: For each σ ∈ Σ let n = a_σ + b_σ (a_σ, b_σ ≥ 0) be the signature partition, with further partitions a_σ = n_{1,σ} + ⋯ + n_{t(σ),σ} and b_σ = n_{t(σ)+1,σ} + ⋯ + n_{r(σ),σ}; put a = (a_σ)_{σ∈Σ}, b = (b_σ)_{σ∈Σ}. Let ψ be a finite-order character of T_H(ℤ_p), κ a dominant character as in §2.6.3, and ρ, ρ^υ as in (95), (97): ρ_σ = κ_σ − (α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ)) = (−r_{a_σ}, …, −r_1; s_1, …, s_{b_σ}), ρ^υ_σ = (r_1, …, r_{a_σ}; s_1, …, s_{b_σ}), where (α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ)) = (−m+b(χ_σ), …, −m+b(χ_σ); m−a(χ_σ), …, m−a(χ_σ)) (96); ρ and κ carry the same information relative to the shift (1, χ) imposed by χ. Put c = ψ·ρ^υ. f(χ, c) is a factorizable Siegel section meeting the conditions of Definition 5.3.2, with local sections as in §4.2.1 (v ∉ S), §4.2.2 (v ∈ S), §4.3 (v | p) and §4.5 (archimedean); the choices at p and ∞ depend on the signature of G_1. When ρ is trivial the Eisenstein series of f(χ, c) = f(χ, ψ) is holomorphic, and it is (a normalisation of) the algebraic automorphic form G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} of [Eis14, Equation (32)] (notation of [Eis15]), defined over 𝒪 and viewed over ℂ by extension of scalars.
items.note: The identification of the Eisenstein series of the §4 sections with G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} is asserted, not proved (see sourceIssues E130). Source issues: sourceIssues E130. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.2.1 — what G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} denotes
items.statement: The notation G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} (used to cite [EFMV18]) designates one of the Eisenstein series of §8.2: the section f(χ, ψ) is the Siegel section associated with χ_unitary, k, ν and ψ in [Eis14], and the Eisenstein series E_{f(χ,ψ)}(•) is the one denoted E_{k,ν}(•, χ, ψ, k/2) in [Eis15]; E_{f(χ,ψ)}(•) is normalised by the factor D(n, K, 𝔟, p, k) of [Eis15, Proposition 13] to cancel transcendental factors. Although (a, b) is omitted from the subscript, f(χ, c) and hence the Eisenstein series depend on the choice of (a, b).
items.note: Dictionary between this paper's sections and Eischen's Eisenstein series; used in the proof of Corollary 8.2.4 ('the translation mentioned in Remark 8.2.1'). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.2 — the parameters r_{i,σ}, s_{j,σ}, r̃, s̃, the character ρ^υ and the polynomial φ_κ
items.statement: As in §4.4.7, let r_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ r_{a_σ,σ} ≥ r_{a_σ+1,σ} = 0 and s_{1,σ} ≥ ⋯ ≥ s_{b_σ,σ} ≥ s_{b_σ+1,σ} = 0 be descending sequences of integers, ρ^υ_σ the corresponding character of the torus T_H, and r̃_{i,σ} = r_{i,σ} − r_{i+1,σ} (i = 1, …, a_σ), s̃_{j,σ} = s_{j,σ} − s_{j+1,σ} (j = 1, …, b_σ). Define ρ^υ := ∏_{σ∈Σ} ρ^υ_σ and φ_κ := ⊗_{σ∈Σ} p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ), with p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) as in Equation (100), identified with a polynomial function on the tangent space of the moduli space; p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ) is homogeneous of some degree d(σ) ≥ 0.
items.note: Statement corrected: the paper prints s̃_{j,σ} = r_{j,σ} − r_{j+1,σ} (see sourceIssues E129); the §4.4 definition (p. 72) has the correct s_{j,σ} − s_{j+1,σ}. Source issues: sourceIssues E129. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.2 — the p-adic differential operator θ^{(κ,a,b)} on p-adic automorphic forms on G_4
items.statement: The C^∞ operator δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) of §4.4.10 is realised algebro-geometrically by applying d times the algebraic differential operator D on automorphic forms on G_4 (built from the Gauss–Manin connection and the Kodaira–Spencer morphism, as in [Kat78, Ch. II], [Eis12, §6–§9], [Eis16, §3], [EFMV18, §3–§6]) and then projecting onto the highest-weight vector attached to (χ, (r̃, s̃)), after projecting modulo the anti-holomorphic subspace H^{0,1} of H^1_dR. The same construction over the Igusa tower over the ordinary locus of the Shimura variety of G_4, with H^{0,1} replaced by the unit-root splitting, gives a p-adic differential operator θ^{(κ,a,b)} on p-adic automorphic forms on G_4, raising the weight so that the output takes values in the space generated by the highest-weight vector for (χ, (r̃, s̃)). By [Eis12, §10] (extending [Kat78, Lemma 5.1.27] to unitary groups), θ^{(κ,a,b)}(f) and δ^d_χ(r̃, s̃)(f) agree at ordinary CM points up to periods, for any algebraic automorphic form f (precise form: (163)).
items.note: θ^{(κ,a,b)} is the operator written θ^d_χ(r̃, s̃) in Proposition 8.1.1(a) (the proof of Corollary 8.2.4 silently identifies res_3∘θ^{(κ,a,b)} with θ(κ, χ) of Proposition 8.1.1(b)); the superscript records its dependence on κ and on the signature (a, b). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3 plans Katz's algebraic and p-adic differential operators and CM periods.

items.name: Theorem 8.2.2 — the Eisenstein measure Eis_{a,b}
items.statement: Fix, for each σ ∈ Σ, the signature n = a_σ + b_σ and put a = (a_σ), b = (b_σ). There is a measure Eis_{a,b} (depending on a and b) on X_p × T_H(ℤ_p), with values in the space of p-adic modular forms on G_4, such that ∫_{X_p × T_H(ℤ_p)} χ̃ψ·ρ^υ Eis_{a,b} = θ^{(κ,a,b)}(G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ}) whenever (χ, c = ψ·ρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H. Here: χ = χ_unitary|·|^{−k/2}_{𝒦/ℚ} is of type A_0 with χ_∞(a) = ∏_{σ∈Σ} σ(a)^{−k}(σ̄(a)/σ(a))^{ν_σ}, ν = (ν_σ), and χ̃ : X_p → 𝒪_{ℂ_p}^× is its p-adic avatar (def-8-2-chi-tilde); ψ is a finite-order character of T_H(ℤ_p); ρ^υ = ∏_σ ρ^υ_σ with ρ^υ_σ = (r_{1,σ}, …, r_{a_σ,σ}; s_{1,σ}, …, s_{b_σ,σ}) as in Equation (97), and κ is the dominant weight determined by ρ and χ via (97) (κ_σ = ρ_σ + (α(χ_σ), β(χ_σ))); Y^class_H ⊂ Y^alg_H is the set of pairs (χ, c) satisfying the positivity condition (110), i.e. κ_σ ∈ C_3(μ, z_σ^{−a(χ_σ)} z̄_σ^{−b(χ_σ)}) for all σ ∈ Σ (Remark 8.2.5); G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ} is the holomorphic Eisenstein series on G_4 of [Eis14, Equation (32)], normalised by D(n, K, 𝔟, p, k) of [Eis15, Proposition 13], i.e. E_{f(χ,ψ)} for the Siegel section f(χ, ψ) (Remark 8.2.1); θ^{(κ,a,b)} is the p-adic differential operator of def-8-2-theta-kab attached to (χ, (r̃, s̃)), r̃_{i,σ} = r_{i,σ} − r_{i+1,σ}, s̃_{j,σ} = s_{j,σ} − s_{j+1,σ}, i.e. to the polynomial φ_κ = ⊗_σ p(r̃_σ, s̃_σ).
items.note: Not proved in the paper: introduced by 'From the p-adic q-expansion principle and the description of the q-expansion coefficients given in [Eis14, Section 3], we obtain the following theorem (similar to [EFMV18, Theorem 7.2.3])'. In the definite case it is [Eis15, Theorem 20], [Eis14, §5] (Remark 8.2.3). The qualifier 'whenever (χ, c) ∈ Y^class_H' was added in v5 (v4 Theorem 5.4.1, p. 84–85, lacks it). See sourceIssues E130.Source issues: sourceIssues E130. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.2.3 — the definite case is Eischen's Eisenstein measure
items.statement: When a_σ b_σ = 0 for all σ ∈ Σ (the definite case), the measure of Theorem 8.2.2 is the Eisenstein measure of [Eis15, Theorem 20] and [Eis14, Section 5].
items.note: Cited identification; in this case Theorem 8.2.2 is a theorem of Eischen. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 8.2.4 — dEis_{a,b} is an axiomatic Eisenstein measure with shift (1, χ)
items.statement: The measure dEis_{a,b} on X_p × T_H(ℤ_p) defined by ∫_{X_p × T_H(ℤ_p)} χ̃ψ·ρ^υ dEis_{a,b} = res_3 θ^{(κ,a,b)}(G_{k,ν,χ_unitary,ψ}) (for (χ, c = ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H; notation as in Theorem 8.2.2, res_3 the restriction from G_4 to G_3) is an axiomatic Eisenstein measure (Definition 5.3.2) with values in V(K^p_3, R), with shift (1, χ) (i.e. satisfying (109) with (α, β) = (1, χ)).
items.note: Proof in the paper: compare Theorem 8.2.2 with Definition 5.3.2; 'bearing in mind the translation of Remark 8.2.1' this reduces to comparing e_κ ∘ res_3 θ^{(κ,a,b)} with e_κ ∘ D^hol(κ, χ), which is Proposition 8.1.3. This is the bridge from the explicit measure to the axiomatics of §5.3 and §7 (used in Lemma 9.1.5, Corollary 9.1.8). Definition 5.3.2 requires (last bullet) e_κ ∘ ∫(χ, c) dEis = D_S(χ)·e_κ ∘ res_3 E_{f(χ,c)}. See sourceIssues E132.Source issues: sourceIssues E126, sourceIssues E132. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.2.5 — the classical set Y^class_H of the Eisenstein measure
items.statement: The set Y^class_H for the measure of Theorem 8.2.2/Corollary 8.2.4 is determined by the positivity conditions (110) — (χ, c) ∈ Y^class_H ⇔ κ_σ ∈ C_3(μ, z_σ^{−a(χ_σ)} z̄_σ^{−b(χ_σ)}) for all σ ∈ Σ — together with the relations between χ, m, (r_{i,σ})_i and (s_{j,σ})_j of Equation (94) and Inequalities (95).
items.note: (110) is on p. 83 (§5.3.1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.3 — the local groups G_w, the non-standard Borel B_w, the Iwahori subgroups I^0_{w,r} ⊃ I_{w,r}, and the modulus character δ_w
items.statement: Let G = G_1 and, for w | p, G_w = GL_n(𝒦_w); by (9), (10) there is an identification G(ℚ_p) ≅ ℚ_p^× × ∏_{w∈Σ_p} G_w (164). B_w ⊂ GL_n(𝒦_w) is the (non-standard) Borel subgroup of g = (A B; 0 D) with A ∈ GL_{a_w}(𝒦_w) upper triangular and D ∈ GL_{b_w}(𝒦_w) lower triangular; T_w ⊂ B_w is its diagonal torus and B^u_w its unipotent radical. I^0_{w,r} ⊂ GL_n(𝒪_w) is the subgroup of g with g mod p^r = (A B; 0 D), A ∈ GL_{a_w}(𝒪_w/p^r𝒪_w) upper triangular and D ∈ GL_{b_w}(𝒪_w/p^r𝒪_w) lower triangular (the mod p^r Iwahori subgroup for B_w); I_{w,r} ⊂ I^0_{w,r} is the subgroup where A and D are moreover unipotent. Under (164) the subgroups I_r ⊂ I^0_r of G(ℤ_p) of §2.5 are I^0_r ≅ ℤ_p^× ∏_{w∈Σ_p} I^0_{w,r} and I_r ≅ ℤ_p^× ∏_{w∈Σ_p} I_{w,r} (165). The modulus character δ_w : B_w → ℝ_{>0} is, for t = diag(t_1, …, t_n) ∈ T_w, δ_w(t) = ∏_{i=1}^{a_w} |t_i|_p^{n+1−2i} · ∏_{i=a_w+1}^{n} |t_i|_p^{2i−n−2a_w−1} = |t_1^{n−1} ⋯ t_{a_w}^{b_w−a_w+1} t_{a_w+1}^{1−n} ⋯ t_n^{b_w−a_w−1}|_p.
items.note: Statement corrected: the paper prints the exponent of t_{a_w} as b_w − a_w (see sourceIssues E131). a_w, b_w denote the signature (a_σ, b_σ) for the σ with 𝔭_σ = 𝔭_w. Source issues: sourceIssues E131. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.3.1 — weight condition (166), κ_norm, normalized Hecke operators u_{w,j}, u^GL_{w,j}, and the ordinary projectors e, e_w
items.statement: Let π be a cuspidal holomorphic representation of G(𝔸) of weight type (κ, K) as in §6.5.1, κ = (κ_σ)_{σ∈Σ_𝒦}, κ_σ ∈ ℤ^{a_σ} dominant, assumed to satisfy κ_σ + κ_{σc} ≥ n for all σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 (166) (as used in the proof of Lemma 8.3.2 this means κ_{σ,a_σ} + κ_{σc,b_σ} ≥ n for the smallest entries). Put κ_norm = (κ_norm,σ), κ_norm,σ = κ_σ − b_σ. Via (164), π_p ≅ μ_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π_w with μ_p a character of ℚ_p^× and π_w irreducible admissible representations of G_w. The Hecke operators u_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U_{w,j} (w ∈ Σ_p, 1 ≤ j ≤ n; U_{w,j} the double coset operator I_r t^+_{w,j} I_r, t_{w,j} as in §2.6.9) act on π_f^{K_r} = π_p^{I_r} ⊗ (⊗_{ℓ≠p} π_ℓ)^{K^p} through π_p^{I_r} with p-adically integral generalized eigenvalues, and e = lim_{m→∞} (∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_{j=1}^n u_{w,j})^{m!} acts on π_p^{I_r}. On π_p^{I_r} = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π_w^{I_{w,r}}, u_{w,j} acts through u^GL_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U^GL_{w,j}, U^GL_{w,j} the double coset operator I_{w,r} t_{w,j} I_{w,r} on π_w^{I_{w,r}}; its generalized eigenvalues are p-integral and e_w = lim_{m→∞} (∏_{j=1}^n u^GL_{w,j})^{m!} is a projector on π_w^{I_{w,r}}.
items.note: Footnote 16: the notion depends a priori on κ_norm (hence on κ and the signatures); there is at most one κ_norm for which a given π_p can be ordinary. The paper prints ∏_{i=1}^n u_{w,j} (index misprint). Source issues: sourceIssues E133. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.3.1 — ordinary representations and ordinary vectors (global at p and local at w)
items.statement: π is ordinary at p if π_p^{I_r} ≠ 0 for r ≫ 0 and, for any such r, there is 0 ≠ φ ∈ π_p^{I_r} with e·φ = φ; such φ is an ordinary vector for π_p. Equivalently there is φ ∈ π_p^{I_r}, r ≫ 0, which is a simultaneous eigenvector of the u_{w,j} with u_{w,j}·φ = c_{w,j}φ and |c_{w,j}|_p = 1. Via π_p = μ_p ⊗_w π_w, π_p is ordinary iff μ_p is unramified and each π_w is ordinary, i.e. there is φ_w ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}}, r ≫ 0, with e_w·φ_w = φ_w (an ordinary vector for π_w). The existence of an ordinary vector for π_w is equivalent to: (a) π_w^{I_{w,r}} ≠ 0 for all r ≫ 0; (b) for each such r there is 0 ≠ φ_w ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}} which is a simultaneous eigenvector of the u^GL_{w,j}, 1 ≤ j ≤ n, with u^GL_{w,j}·φ_w = c_{w,j}φ_w and |c_{w,j}|_p = 1. If the φ_w are ordinary vectors and μ_p is unramified then ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} φ_w is an ordinary vector for π_p.
items.note: Compare §6.6.8 (π^ord_p = e_κ π_p^{I_r}, p. 101). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.2 — uniqueness of the ordinary vector and the ordinary principal-series embedding (Hida)
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p and let π_w be an irreducible admissible representation of G_w = GL_n(𝒦_w) satisfying (a) and (b) of §8.3.1 for a weight κ satisfying (166). (i) Up to a scalar there is a unique ordinary vector φ^ord_w ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}}, and it is independent of r ≫ 0. (ii) There is a unique character α_w : T_w → ℂ^× such that π_w ↪ Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α_w (normalized induction) as the unique irreducible subrepresentation and φ^ord_w is identified with the unique simultaneous U^GL_{w,j}-eigenvector (1 ≤ j ≤ n) whose support contains B_w I_{w,r}, for r ≫ 0. In particular c_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} δ_w^{−1/2}(t_{w,j}) α_w(t_{w,j}).
items.note: (i) and (ii) are proved together. Proof (after [Hid98, §5]): with V = π_w, N = ∩_r I_{w,r} = B^u_w ∩ GL_n(𝒪_w), t_j = diag(p1_j, 1_{n−j}) (j ≤ a_w), diag(p1_{a_w}, 1_{n−j}, p1_{j−a_w}) (j > a_w), U_j = [N t_j N] on V^N = ∪_r V^{I_{w,r}} decomposes V^N = V^N_nil ⊕ V^N_inv with V^N_inv ≅ V_{B_w} (167) U_j-equivariantly (U_j acts on V_{B_w} by δ_w(t_j)^{−1}t_j) [Hid98, (5.3)]; an ordinary vector gives a quotient V_{B_w} ↠ ℂ(λ), λ(t_j) = |κ_norm(t_j)|_p δ_w(t_j) c_j, hence by Frobenius reciprocity [Cas95, Thm 3.2.4] an embedding V ↪ I(α), α = λδ^{−1/2}; β = |κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2}α is unit-valued; the key step is that β_x = |κ_norm|_p^{−1}δ_w^{−1/2}α^x (x in the Weyl group W) is unit-valued only for x = 1, because (166) and dominance make the character |κ_norm|_p δ_w^{1/2} regular; then I(α)_{B_w} ≅ ⊕_{x∈W} ℂ(α^xδ^{1/2}) [Hid98, Prop 5.4] and the ordinary eigenspace in V^N_inv is one-dimensional. The proof contains several misprints (sign of the character θ, exponents, indices), none affecting the conclusion — see source issues. This lemma is the proof of Theorem 6.6.9 (p. 101). Uniqueness of the irreducible subrepresentation holds because the Jacquet module of I(α) is multiplicity-free. Source issues: sourceIssues E131, sourceIssues E134, sourceIssues E135, sourceIssues E140. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 8.3.3 — the unique ordinary vector of π_p
items.statement: Suppose κ satisfies (166) and π_p is ordinary. Up to a scalar there is a unique ordinary vector φ^ord ∈ π_p^{I_r} for r ≫ 0; it is independent of r. Under π_p = μ_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π_w, φ^ord = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} φ^ord_w with φ^ord_w as in Lemma 8.3.2.
items.note: Immediate from Lemma 8.3.2 and the tensor decomposition (μ_p unramified).Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.4(i) — the contragredient of an ordinary π_w is the unique irreducible quotient of Ind α_w^{−1}
items.statement: Let w, π_w and κ be as in Lemma 8.3.2, π_w^∨ the contragredient and ⟨·,·⟩_w : π_w × π_w^∨ → ℂ the non-degenerate G_w-invariant pairing (unique up to scalar). With α_w as in Lemma 8.3.2(ii), π_w^∨ is isomorphic to the unique irreducible quotient of Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α_w^{−1}: Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α_w^{−1} ↠ π_w^∨.
items.note: Proof: Ind α_w^{−1} is the contragredient of Ind α_w [Cas95, Prop. 3.1.2], the pairing being ⟨ϕ, ϕ′⟩ = ∫_{GL_n(𝒪_w)} ϕ(k)ϕ′(k) dk [Cas95, Prop. 3.1.3]; dualise π_w ↪ Ind α_w. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.4(ii) — non-vanishing of ⟨φ^ord_w, φ^∨_{w,r}⟩
items.statement: For r ≫ 0 let φ^∨_{w,r} ∈ π_w^∨ be the image of the vector in Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α_w^{−1} supported on B_w I_{w,r}. Then c(π_w, r) := ⟨φ^ord_w, φ^∨_{w,r}⟩_w is non-zero and depends only on r.
items.note: Proof: with ϕ^ord ∈ Ind α_w corresponding to φ^ord_w (Lemma 8.3.2(ii)) and ϕ^∨_r the function supported on B_w I_{w,r}, B_w I_{w,r} ∩ GL_n(𝒪_w) = I^0_{w,r} = T_w(𝒪_w) I_{w,r} and ϕ^ord(tk′)ϕ^∨_r(tk′) = α_w(t)α_w^{−1}(t) = 1, so c(π_w, r) = vol(I^0_{w,r}) ≠ 0 (implicitly ϕ^ord(1) = ϕ^∨_r(1) = 1; the integral is printed over 'I^0_w'). Source issues: sourceIssues E140. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.4(iii) — pairing with φ^∨_{w,r} only sees the ordinary component
items.statement: Let 0 ≠ φ ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}} with e_w·φ = c(φ)φ^ord_w. Then ⟨φ, φ^∨_{w,r}⟩_w = c(φ)⟨φ^ord_w, φ^∨_{w,r}⟩_w.
items.note: Proof: write φ = c(φ)φ^ord_w + Σ_i φ_i with φ_i generalized U^GL_{w,j}-eigenvectors, e·φ_i = 0; their functions ϕ_i ∈ Ind α_w vanish on I^0_{w,r} (by the proof of Lemma 8.3.2(ii): v ↦ f_v(1) kills V^N_nil and the non-ordinary eigenspaces), so the integral over I^0_{w,r} only sees c(φ)ϕ^ord. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.3.5 — anti-ordinary Hecke operators u^−_{w,j}, the anti-ordinary projector e^−, and anti-ordinary vectors
items.statement: Let π be an anti-holomorphic representation of G(𝔸) of type (κ, K) as in §6.5.1 with κ satisfying (166) (equivalently π^♭ is cuspidal holomorphic of type (κ, K)). For r > 0 the Hecke operators u^−_{w,j} (w ∈ Σ_p, 1 ≤ j ≤ n), U^−_{w,j} the double coset operator I_r t^−_{w,j} I_r, act on π_f^{K_r} = π_p^{I_r} ⊗ (⊗_{ℓ≠p} π_ℓ)^{K^p} through π_p^{I_r} with p-integral generalized eigenvalues, and the anti-ordinary projector is e^− = lim_{m→∞} (∏_{w∈Σ_p} ∏_{j=1}^n u^−_{w,j})^{m!}. On π_p^{I_r} = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π_w^{I_{w,r}}, u^−_{w,j} acts through u^{GL,−}_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U^{GL,−}_{w,j}, U^{GL,−}_{w,j} = [I_{w,r} t_{w,j}^{−1} I_{w,r}], and e^−_w = lim (∏_j u^{GL,−}_{w,j})^{m!} is a projector on π_w^{I_{w,r}}. π is anti-ordinary at p of level r if π_p^{I_r} ≠ 0 and there is 0 ≠ φ ∈ π_p^{I_r} with e^−·φ = φ (an anti-ordinary vector of level r with respect to I_r); likewise with respect to I^♭_r := I^†_r (§6.5.3). This holds iff μ_p is unramified and for each w ∈ Σ_p there is 0 ≠ φ_w ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}} with e^−_w·φ_w = φ_w (an anti-ordinary vector for π_w of level r).
items.note: Normalisation inconsistency in the source: p. 131 prints u^−_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p U^−_{w,j} (exponent +1), p. 132 prints u^{GL,−}_{w,j} = |κ_norm(t_{w,j})|_p^{−1} U^{GL,−}_{w,j}; the proof of Lemma 8.3.6 (adjointness (170)) needs the latter. The paper also prints e_w for e^−_w in the last sentence. See sourceIssues E136. Source issues: sourceIssues E136, sourceIssues E133. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.6(i) — π_w is anti-ordinary iff π_w^∨ is ordinary
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p and π_w a constituent of π_p as in §8.3.5. The representation π_w is anti-ordinary of some level r if and only if π_w^∨ is ordinary; in that case π_w is anti-ordinary of all levels r ≫ 0.
items.note: Proof: the G_w-invariant pairing satisfies ⟨u^{GL,−}_{w,j} φ, φ′⟩_w = ⟨φ, u^GL_{w,j} φ′⟩_w ((170), (171)) since [I t^{−1} I] is adjoint to [I t I]; an eigenvector with unit eigenvalues on one side produces, via the non-zero functional ⟨φ^{a-ord}, ·⟩, a simultaneous eigenvector with the same unit eigenvalues on the other side (induction on j using commutativity). The induction step as written has a small gap (see sourceIssues E138); the conclusion is correct. Source issues: sourceIssues E136, sourceIssues E138. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.6(ii) — uniqueness and characterisation of the anti-ordinary vector
items.statement: If π_w is anti-ordinary of level r, then there is a unique (up to non-zero scalar) anti-ordinary vector φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}} of level r; it is characterised by ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, φ^{∨,ord}_w⟩_w ≠ 0 and ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, φ⟩_w = 0 for all φ ∈ π_w^{∨,I_{w,r}} belonging to a generalized eigenspace of some u^GL_{w,j} with non-unit eigenvalue (φ^{∨,ord}_w the ordinary vector of π_w^∨).
items.note: Statement corrected: the paper prints 'for all φ ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}} belonging to a generalized eigenspace of some u^{GL,−}_{w,j}', which does not type-check for the pairing π_w × π_w^∨ (see source issue). Proof: π_w^{∨,I_{w,r}} = ℂφ^{∨,ord}_w ⊕ V_1 ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ V_t with V_i joint generalized u^GL-eigenspaces having some non-unit eigenvalue (by the uniqueness in Lemma 8.3.2(i) — really by the one-dimensionality of the unit joint generalized eigenspace established in its proof), and (170) forces ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, V_i⟩_w = 0. Source issues: sourceIssues E137. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.3.7 — the anti-ordinary vector as the image of the B_w I_{w,r}-supported vector of Ind β_w; trace compatibility
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p and π_w a constituent of π_p as in §8.3.5, anti-ordinary. There is a unique character β_w : T_w → ℂ^× such that Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β_w ↠ π_w is the unique irreducible quotient and the anti-ordinary vector φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} ∈ π_w^{I_{w,r}} of level r is (up to non-zero scalar) the image of the vector of Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β_w with support B_w I_{w,r}. In particular the φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, r ≫ 0, can be chosen so that Σ_{γ ∈ I_{w,r}/(I^0_{w,r′} ∩ I_{w,r})} π_w(γ) φ^{a-ord}_{w,r′} = φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} for r′ ≥ r.
items.note: Proof: π_w^∨ is ordinary (Lemma 8.3.6(i)); take α_w for π_w^∨ as in Lemma 8.3.2(ii) and β_w = α_w^{−1}; π_w is then the unique irreducible quotient of Ind β_w, and by Lemmas 8.3.2(ii), 8.3.4(ii)–(iii) (applied to π_w^∨) the image of the B_w I_{w,r}-supported vector satisfies the characterisation of Lemma 8.3.6(ii). The trace relation holds with the normalisation of Remark 8.3.9 (value 1 at 1) once β_w is trivial on T_w(1 + p^r𝒪_w), which is where r ≫ 0 is needed (checked: the sum is I_{w,r}-invariant, supported on B_w I_{w,r}, with value 1 at 1). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 8.3.8 — the unique anti-ordinary vector of π_p
items.statement: Suppose κ satisfies (166). Then π_p is anti-ordinary if and only if π^♭_p is ordinary, and up to a scalar there is a unique anti-ordinary vector φ^{a-ord}_r ∈ π_p^{I_r} of level r for each r ≫ 0. Under π_p = μ_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π_w, φ^{a-ord}_r = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} with φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} as in Lemma 8.3.7.
items.note: No separate proof; follows from Lemmas 8.3.6, 8.3.7 (π^♭_w = π_w^∨ up to the similitude twist). The paper prints π_p^{I_{w,r}} for π_p^{I_r}. Source issues: sourceIssues E140. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.3.9 — normalisation of φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}
items.statement: The relation between the φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} for varying r (Lemma 8.3.7) is made explicit by normalising φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} to be the image of the vector of Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β_w with support B_w I_{w,r} and value 1 at 1.
items.note: This normalisation is used in Proposition 8.5.1(2) (Remark 8.5.2) and Lemma 8.4.9. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.3.10 — φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} is an admissible test vector for the local zeta integral at p
items.statement: For r sufficiently large, φ_w = φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} ∈ π_w satisfies the conditions (64) and (70) with R_w = B_w (and n_{i,w} = 1 for all i); in particular φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} is a suitable test vector for the calculations of §4.3.6.
items.note: Justified in the paper by 'the description of the anti-ordinary vector provided by Lemma 8.4.2' — the relevant description is Lemma 8.3.7 (mis-numbered cross-reference, see source issues). This remark links §8 to the local computation at p in §4.3. Source issues: sourceIssues E139. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.3.11 — total Hecke polynomial, Newton polygon Newt(π, w), Hodge polygon Hodge(π, w)
items.statement: Let π be a holomorphic or anti-holomorphic cuspidal automorphic representation of G(𝔸), π_p = μ_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π_w as in (164), and assume each π_w is an irreducible subquotient of Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β_w for some character β_w : T_w → ℂ^× (172). Write β_w = (β_{w,1}, …, β_{w,n}) with β_w(diag(t_1, …, t_n)) = ∏_i β_{w,i}(t_i) (the β_{w,i} are unique up to order). The total Hecke polynomial of π at w is H_w(T) = ∏_{i=1}^n (1 − β_{w,i}(ϖ_w)T)(1 − β_{w,i}^{−1}(ϖ_w)T) (173), and Newt(π, w) is the Newton polygon of H_w(T); Newt(π, w) = Newt(π^♭, w). With Σ_w = {σ ∈ Σ_𝒦 : 𝔭_σ = 𝔭_w} and π_{Σ_w} = ⊗_{σ∈Σ_w} π_σ = ⊗_{σ∈Σ_w} 𝔻_c(τ_σ) (notation (90)), the Hodge polygon Hodge(π, w) is the polygon in the right half-plane with vertices (i, Σ_{σ∈Σ_w} p_{i,σ}), where (p_{i,σ}, q_{i,σ}), i = 1, …, 2n, are the Hodge types of §4.4.12 (list (106)) attached to 𝔻_c(τ_σ).
items.note: (173) is printed with α_{w,i}; the characters were named β_{w,i} (misprint). The valuation used for the Newton polygon is that of incl_p (implicit). Not used later in the paper. Source issues: sourceIssues E141. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 8.3.12 — Newton and Hodge polygons meet at the midpoint (Panchishkin condition)
items.statement: Suppose π is (anti-)holomorphic and (anti-)ordinary. Then Newt(π_w) and Hodge(π_w) (i.e. Newt(π, w), Hodge(π, w) of §8.3.11) meet at the midpoint (n, Σ_{σ∈Σ_w} p_{i,σ}) [index i unbound as printed; presumably the Hodge vertex at abscissa n, i.e. (n, Σ_{σ∈Σ_w} p_{n,σ}) in the paper's vertex convention].
items.note: No proof: 'The proof is an elementary calculation and is omitted; it will not be used in what follows.' Motivic meaning: the restriction of scalars to ℚ of the motive attached to Π satisfies the Panchishkin condition [Pan94].See source issues (unbound index; omitted proof). Source issues: sourceIssues E142, sourceIssues E143. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.4, §8.4.1 — (anti-)ordinary theory for G_2: transposed Borel/Iwahori, intertwining back to B_w, U^{♭,GL}_{w,j}, and π^♭_w = π^∨_w
items.statement: Replacing G_1 by G_2, under (164) the Borel B_w and the groups I^0_{w,r}, I_{w,r} are replaced by their transposes ᵗB_w (= B^op_w, the opposite parabolic), ᵗI^0_{w,r}, ᵗI_{w,r}; vectors induced from B_w rather than ᵗB_w are obtained by composing with the standard intertwining operators between Ind^{G_w}_{B^op_w} and Ind^{G_w}_{B_w}. If π is a cuspidal holomorphic representation of G_1(𝔸) of weight type (κ, K) (§8.3.1), then π^♭ = π^∨ ⊗ ||ν||^{a(κ)} (§6.5.3) is cuspidal holomorphic of weight type (κ^♭, K^♭) on G_2(𝔸) (anti-holomorphic as a representation of G_1(𝔸)). If π is ordinary at p then so is π^♭ (for G_2), the role of U^GL_{w,j} being played by U^{♭,GL}_{w,j} = [ᵗI_{w,r} t_{w,j}^{−1} ᵗI_{w,r}]; writing π^♭_p = μ^♭_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π^♭_w via (164), π^♭_w = π_w^∨ and μ^♭_p = μ_p^{−1}|ν|_p^{a(κ)}.
items.note: The paper prints ᵗI_{w,j} for ᵗI_{w,r} in the double coset. Source issues: sourceIssues E144. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.4.2(i) — unique ordinary vector of π^♭_w (for G_2)
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p and r so large that π_w^{♭,ᵗI_{w,r}} ≠ 0 (equivalently π_w^{I_{w,r}} ≠ 0). Up to a scalar there is a unique ordinary vector φ^{♭,ord}_w ∈ π_w^{♭,ᵗI_{w,r}} (for the U^{♭,GL}_{w,j}); it is independent of r ≫ 0, and φ^{♭,ord}_w = (φ^ord_w)^∨.
items.note: Proof: φ(g) ↦ φ^∨(g) = φ(ᵗg^{−1}) maps Ind_{B_w} α → Ind_{ᵗB_w} α^{−1} and realises π^♭_w = π_w^∨ as the image of π_w (a subrepresentation of Ind_{ᵗB_w} α_w^{−1}); φ^∨ is ordinary iff φ is (the automorphism g ↦ ᵗg^{−1} carries I_{w,r} to ᵗI_{w,r} and t_{w,j} to t_{w,j}^{−1}); then Lemma 8.3.2(i). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.4.2(ii) — π^♭_w as quotient of Ind α^♭_w, α^♭_w = α_w^{−1}
items.statement: There is a unique character α^♭_w : T_w → ℂ^× such that Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α^♭_w ↠ π^♭_w is the unique irreducible quotient and φ^{♭,ord}_w is identified with the image of the simultaneous U^{♭,GL}_{w,j}-eigenvector (1 ≤ j ≤ n) with support B_w ᵗI_{w,r}, for r ≫ 0 (in particular its u^{♭,GL}_{w,j}-eigenvalue is c^♭_{w,j} = c_{w,j}). Moreover α^♭_w = α_w^{−1}, α_w as in Lemma 8.3.2(ii).
items.note: Proof: π^♭_w is the image of the standard intertwining operator Ind_{B_w} α_w^{−1} → Ind_{B^op_w} α_w^{−1}; 'the determination of the support of the eigenvector in Ind_{B_w} α_w^{−1} is an easy computation' (not written out). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 8.4.3 — the unique ordinary vector of π^♭_p
items.statement: Up to a scalar there is a unique ordinary vector φ^{♭,ord} ∈ π_p^{♭,ᵗI_r} for r ≫ 0; it is independent of r, and under π^♭_p = μ^♭_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π^♭_w, φ^{♭,ord} = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} φ^{♭,ord}_w with φ^{♭,ord}_w as in Lemma 8.4.2.
items.note: Analogue of Corollary 8.3.3. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.4.4 — anti-ordinary theory for G_2: U^{♭,GL,−}_{w,j}
items.statement: If π is anti-ordinary at p, then π^♭ is anti-ordinary at p (for G_2), the role of U^{GL,−}_{w,j} being played by U^{♭,GL,−}_{w,j} = [ᵗI_{w,r} t_{w,j} ᵗI_{w,r}].
items.note: Printed with ᵗI_{w,j} for ᵗI_{w,r}. Source issues: sourceIssues E144. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.4.5 — the anti-ordinary vector of π^♭_w and its trace compatibility
items.statement: Let w ∈ Σ_p and suppose π^♭_w is anti-ordinary with respect to ᵗI_{w,r} (equivalently, π_w is anti-ordinary with respect to I_{w,r}). There is a unique character β^♭_w : T_w → ℂ^× such that π^♭_w ↪ Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β^♭_w is the unique irreducible subrepresentation and the anti-ordinary vector φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} ∈ π_w^{♭,ᵗI_{w,r}} of level r is (up to non-zero scalar) the unique simultaneous U^{♭,GL,−}_{w,j}-eigenvector in Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β^♭_w with support containing B_w ᵗI_{w,r}. In particular the φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r}, r ≫ 0, can be chosen so that Σ_{γ ∈ ᵗI_{w,r}/(ᵗI^0_{w,r′} ∩ ᵗI_{w,r})} π^♭_w(γ) φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r′} = φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} for r′ ≥ r. Furthermore β^♭_w = β_w^{−1}, with β_w as in Lemma 8.3.7.
items.note: Proof: φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} = (φ^{a-ord}_{w,r})^∨ is anti-ordinary and is (up to scalar) the image under the standard intertwining operator Ind_{B^op_w} → Ind_{B_w} of the function φ′_r supported on B^op_w ᵗI_{w,r} with φ′_r(1) = 1; normalising φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} to be that image gives the trace relation because φ′_r satisfies it. The paper refers to 'Lemma 8.3.7(ii)' (no part (ii) exists) and writes the characters in the proof as α_w^{−1} where β^♭_w (= β_w^{−1} = α_w with α_w attached to π_w^∨) is meant — see source issues. Source issues: sourceIssues E145. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 8.4.6 — the unique anti-ordinary vector of π^♭_p
items.statement: Let I^♭_r = I^†_r. For each r ≫ 0 there is, up to a scalar, a unique anti-ordinary vector φ^{♭,a-ord}_r ∈ π_p^{♭,I^♭_r} of level r. Under π^♭_p = μ^♭_p ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} π^♭_w, φ^{♭,a-ord}_r = ⊗_{w∈Σ_p} φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} with φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} as in Lemma 8.4.5.
items.note: The anti-ordinary vectors on the U(−V) side are the test vectors φ̃_w of §4.3 (Remark 8.4.8). The paper prints φ^{♭,a-ord}_{−r} on the left of the factorisation and omits 'up to a scalar' (see source issues).Source issues: sourceIssues E146. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.4.7 — value at 1 of the normalised φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r}
items.statement: Under the normalisation in the proof of Lemma 8.4.5, φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} is identified with a function in Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} β^♭_w whose value at 1 is Vol(ᵗI^0_{w,r}).
items.note: Stated without computation (value of the intertwining integral at 1). Used in Lemma 8.4.9. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.4.8 — φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} is an admissible test vector φ̃_w
items.statement: For r sufficiently large, φ̃_w = φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} ∈ π^♭_w satisfies the conditions (68) with R_w = B_w (and n_{i,w} = 1 for all i); in particular φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} is also a suitable test vector for the calculations of §4.3.6.
items.note: The paper cites 'Lemma 8.4.2' (should be Lemma 8.4.5) and writes φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r} ∈ π_w (should be π^♭_w) in the last sentence. Source issues: sourceIssues E139. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.4 (before Lemma 8.4.9) — the ordinary vectors φ^{♭,ord}_{π_w}, φ^ord_{π^♭_w} and their normalisations
items.statement: Assume the hypotheses of Lemma 8.4.5 (π^♭_w anti-ordinary w.r.t. ᵗI_{w,r}, equivalently π_w anti-ordinary w.r.t. I_{w,r}); then π_w = (π^♭_w)^∨ is ordinary with respect to ᵗB_w and π^♭_w = π_w^∨ is ordinary with respect to B_w. Let ⟨·,·⟩_w be the canonical pairing on π_w × π^♭_w (via π^♭ = π^∨). Let φ^{♭,ord}_{π_w} ∈ π_w^{ᵗI_{w,r}} be the vector of Lemma 8.4.2 with π^♭_w replaced by (π^♭_w)^∨ = π_w, normalised to take the value 1 at 1, and φ^ord_{π^♭_w} ∈ π_w^{♭,I_{w,r}} the vector of Lemma 8.3.2 with π_w replaced by π_w^∨ = π^♭_w, normalised to take the value Vol(I^0_{w,r} · ᵗI^0_{w,r}) (independent of r) at 1. The anti-ordinary vectors are normalised as in Remarks 8.3.9 and 8.4.7.
items.note: I^0_{w,r}·ᵗI^0_{w,r} is the product set; it equals the set of g ∈ GL_n(𝒪_w) lying in the big cell B_w B^op_w mod p, hence is independent of r ≥ 1 (checked). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.4.9 — the normalised local anti-ordinary pairing is independent of r
items.statement: With the conventions of def-8-4-9-normalizations, ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r}⟩_w / Vol(I^0_{w,r} ∩ ᵗI^0_{w,r}) = ⟨φ^{♭,ord}_{π_w}, φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r}⟩_w / Vol(ᵗI^0_{w,r}) = ⟨φ^{a-ord}_{w,r}, φ^ord_{π^♭_w}⟩_w / Vol(I^0_{w,r}). In particular the left-hand side is independent of r.
items.note: Proof: identify ⟨·,·⟩_w with the pairing Ind_{B_w}(β_w) × Ind_{B_w}(β_w)^{−1} → ℂ, (ϕ, ϕ′) ↦ ∫_{GL_n(𝒪_w)} ϕ(k)ϕ′(k) dk; each ratio equals Vol(I^0_{w,r} ᵗI^0_{w,r}). Checked for the first ratio: the integrand is supported on I^0_{w,r} = B_w I_{w,r} ∩ GL_n(𝒪_w) and is identically Vol(ᵗI^0_{w,r}) there, giving Vol(I^0)Vol(ᵗI^0)/Vol(I^0 ∩ ᵗI^0) = Vol(I^0 ᵗI^0). Used for the r-independence in Lemma 8.5.3 and the Main Theorem. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.5 — the setting of the global consequences; π′ 'in the family determined by π'
items.statement: Let π be an anti-ordinary cuspidal anti-holomorphic representation of G_1 of weight type (κ, K_r), K_r = K^p I_r, and π^♭ as in §6.5.3; as a representation of G_2, π^♭ is an anti-ordinary cuspidal anti-holomorphic representation of weight type (κ^♭, K^♭_r), K^♭_r = (K^p)^† ᵗI_r, while as a representation of G_1 it is ordinary holomorphic. Assume π satisfies the Gorenstein, Minimality and Global Multiplicity One hypotheses (7.3.2, 7.3.5, 7.3.3). S is the set of finite primes not dividing p at which K^p is not hyperspecial maximal; I_π, Î_π are as in §7.3.4. An anti-holomorphic cuspidal representation π′ of G_1 is in the family determined by π if there is a non-trivial character λ_{π′} of the Hecke algebra 𝕋 = 𝕋_π giving the action of the unramified Hecke operators on π′; such π′ is given with a factorisation (4), and its factors π′_w, w | p, are (tempered) subquotients of principal series. The Borel subalgebras 𝔟^+_σ at archimedean σ are as in §4.4.1.
items.note: The paper refers to 'the Gorenstein, Minimality, and Global Multiplicity One Hypotheses of section 7.1'; they are Hypotheses 7.3.2, 7.3.3 and Proposition 7.3.5 in §7.3 (misprinted cross-reference, same in v4). Source issues: sourceIssues E147. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 8.5.1 — the anti-ordinary anti-holomorphic vectors φ_{r′}(v_S, π′) and their trace compatibility
items.statement: Fix v_S ∈ Î_π (possible uniformly in π′ by the Minimality Hypothesis). Let π′ be an anti-holomorphic representation of type (κ′, K_{r′}) in the family determined by π; let φ_{κ′,−} be a lowest weight vector in the anti-holomorphic subspace of π′_∞ as in (50); for finite v ∉ S ∪ Σ_p let φ′_v be a fixed generator of the spherical subspace of π′_v and φ′^♭_v the dual generator of the spherical subspace of π′^♭_v. Assume κ satisfies (166). Then: (1) for r′ ≫ 0 there is, up to scalar, a unique anti-ordinary anti-holomorphic vector φ_{r′}(v_S, π′) ∈ (π′)^{K_{r′}} whose factorisation (4) is fac_{π′,♭}(φ_{r′}(v_S, π′)) = φ_{κ′,−} ⊗ ⊗_{v∉S∪Σ_p} φ′_v ⊗ ⊗_{w|p} φ^{a-ord}_{w,r′} ⊗ v_S; (2) as r′ varies the φ_{r′}(v_S, π′) can be chosen so that, for r″ ≥ r′ ≫ 0, [#(I^0_{r′}/I_{r′}) / #(I^0_{r″}/I_{r″})] Σ_{γ∈I_{r′}/I_{r″}} γ·φ_{r″}(v_S, π′) = Σ_{γ∈I_{r′}/(I^0_{r″}∩I_{r′})} γ·φ_{r″}(v_S, π′) = φ_{r′}(v_S, π′).
items.note: Proof: 'follows directly from the results in the previous sections, in particular Lemmas 8.3.7 and 8.3.2' (with Corollary 8.3.8); (2) uses the normalisation of Remark 8.3.9 (Remark 8.5.2). The two sums in (2) agree because φ_{r″} is fixed by I^0_{r″} ∩ I_{r′} and [I^0_{r″} ∩ I_{r′} : I_{r″}] = #(I^0_{r″}/I_{r″}) / #(I^0_{r′}/I_{r′}) (checked). Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 8.5.2 — normalisation ensuring Proposition 8.5.1(2)
items.statement: To ensure property (2) of Proposition 8.5.1 one adopts, for φ^{a-ord}_{w,r″}, the normalisation of Remark 8.3.9.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §8.5 (after Remark 8.5.2) — the ♭-analogue of Proposition 8.5.1
items.statement: Fix v^♭_S ∈ I_π = Î_{π^♭} and let φ_{(κ′)^♭,−} be a lowest weight vector in the anti-holomorphic subspace of (π′)^♭_∞. Then there is, up to a scalar, a unique anti-ordinary anti-holomorphic vector φ_{r′}(v^♭_S, (π′)^♭) ∈ (π′)^{♭,K^♭_{r′}} satisfying the analogues of properties (1) and (2) of Proposition 8.5.1 (with the local vectors φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r′} of Lemma 8.4.5 at w | p).
items.note: Deduced 'from the results in Section 8.4' (Lemma 8.4.5, Corollary 8.4.6); no separate proof. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 8.5.3 — the normalised global pairing of anti-ordinary vectors: r-independence and integrality relative to Q[π′, χ]
items.statement: Let χ be a Hecke character of type A_0. The ratio ⟨φ_{r′}(v_S, π′), φ_{r′}(v^♭_S, (π′)^♭)_χ⟩_{π′,χ} / Vol(I^0_{r′,V} ∩ I^0_{r′,−V}) is independent of r′. If φ_{r′}(v_S, π′) ∈ H^{d,ord}_κ(K_{r′}, ψ′, R) and φ_{r′}(v^♭_S, (π′)^♭) ∈ H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭}(K^♭_{r′}, ψ′^{−1}, R)_χ, then its value lies in R·Q[π′, χ], and for appropriate choices of φ_{r′}(v_S, π′) and φ_{r′}(v^♭_S, (π′)^♭) it is a unit multiple of Q[π′, χ]. Here ⟨·,·⟩_{π′,χ} is the χ-twisted pairing of Remark 4.1.6/(147) (φ^♭_χ = φ^♭ ⊗ χ^{−1}∘det), H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭}(K^♭_{r′}, ψ′^{−1}, R)_χ and the period Q[π′, χ] are as in §6.7 (Lemma 6.7.6).
items.note: Proof: r′-independence from the anti-ordinarity of the two vectors and Lemma 8.4.9; the other claims are 'consequences of the definition of Q[π′, χ]'. The paper prints φ_{r′}(v^♭_S, π′) in the second hypothesis. Formaliser's caution: §6.7 normalises the Serre pairing by Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r}) (not I^0); see sourceIssues E149. This is what gives the p-integrality and p-unit claims for Ω_{π′,χ} in the Main Theorem. Source issues: sourceIssues E148, sourceIssues E149. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §9 'Review of notation' — roles of π, π^♭, Sh(V), Sh(−V) and the standing anti-ordinarity assumption
items.statement: Sh(V) is attached to G_1 and Sh(−V) to G_2 ≅ G_1. Classical points of the Hida families are cuspidal automorphic representations π (for Sh(V)) and π^♭ (for Sh(−V)). π is an anti-holomorphic automorphic representation of G_1, hence holomorphic as a representation of G_2 via G_2 ≅ G_1; π^♭ (identifiable with the complex conjugate of π) is holomorphic on G_1, giving holomorphic modular forms (of weight κ) on Sh(V), and anti-holomorphic on G_2. The input of the doubling integral is an anti-holomorphic vector on G_3 coming from a vector w ∈ π ⊗ π^♭, paired with the Eisenstein measure (values in p-adic modular forms on G_4, specialising to classical forms of weight κ ⊗ κ^♭ on G_3). Standing assumption for all of §9: π and π^♭ are anti-ordinary at all primes dividing p, and w has anti-ordinary local components at p.
items.note: The standing anti-ordinarity assumption is in force in Proposition 9.1.7, Corollaries 9.1.8, 9.2.1 and the Main Theorem 9.2.2 although not restated there. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 9.0.1 — anti-ordinary anti-holomorphic π is also ordinary
items.statement: Suppose π is an anti-ordinary and anti-holomorphic representation of G_1. Then the p-adic component π_p of π is also ordinary.
items.note: Proof in the paper: ordinarity is preserved under complex conjugation and under twist by a power of the similitude character; duality exchanges ordinary and anti-ordinary (Lemma 8.3.6); π is essentially unitary. The first assertion is not justified (see sourceIssues E150). Offered as reassurance; not used later (the Main Theorem assumes ordinarity and §9 assumes anti-ordinarity). Source issues: sourceIssues E150. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §9 (174)–(175) — the anti-ordinary test-vector space Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭} as a trace-compatible system
items.statement: The anti-ordinary subspace of π ⊗ π^♭ is denoted Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}, and is viewed as a trace-compatible system w_r ∈ Ŝ^ord_{κ,V}(K_r, R)[π] ⊗ Ŝ^ord_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r, R)[π^♭], ι^*_r(w_{r+1}) = w_r (174) (notation of Lemma 7.4.9). A vector φ ⊗ φ^♭ ∈ π ⊗ π^♭, viewed as an anti-holomorphic form of level K_r × K^♭_r on Sh(V) × Sh(−V), is taken in Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}, identified (via the factorisation (47)) with the subspace ⊗_{w|p} [φ^{a-ord}_{w,r} ⊗ φ^{♭,a-ord}_{w,r}] ⊗ ⊗_{σ|∞} [φ_{κ_σ,−} ⊗ φ_{κ^♭_σ,−}] ⊗ π^{K^p}_{S^p} ⊗ π^{♭,K̄^p}_{S^p} ⊂ π ⊗ π^♭ (175); i.e. the test vectors have local components as in (48), (49), (50). φ ⊗ φ^♭ is taken integral over 𝒪 = 𝒪_π, and is the anti-ordinary vector w = w_r. The system {w_r} satisfies (174) by Lemmas 8.3.7, 8.4.5 and Proposition 8.5.1; hence the normalised pairing with the Eisenstein measure is independent of r and one may take r = d ≥ 2t as in (60), as required by the local computation at p.
items.note: Links the anti-ordinary vectors of §8 to the p-adic test vectors of §4.3. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §9.1 — the pairing L_{φ⊗φ^♭}(φ_{r,ρ})(Ξ) and the measure Eis_{r,ρ,χ}
items.statement: Fix a Hecke character χ and let κ, ρ, ρ^υ determine one another as in (95), (97). Let φ_{r,ρ} be as in Statement 2 of Lemma 7.4.2 (a measure on T_H(ℤ_p) of type χ for a p-adic Hecke character χ of X_p). Choose Ξ ∈ C_r(T_H(ℤ_p), R)ρ^υ ⊂ C_r(T_H(ℤ_p), 𝒪)ρ^υ with φ_{r,ρ}(Ξ) ∈ S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r, R) ⊗ S^ord_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r, R) ⊗ χ∘det (176) (cf. (156)). For φ ⊗ φ^♭ ∈ [Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}] ⊂ π ⊗ π^♭, L_{φ⊗φ^♭}(φ_{r,ρ})(Ξ) is the value of the normalised canonical pairing (135) between S^ord_{κ,V}(K_r, R) ⊗ S^ord_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r, R) ⊗ χ∘det and H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r, R)[π] ⊗ H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,D}(K^♭_r, R)[π^♭] ⊗ χ^{−1}∘det ≅ [Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}] ⊗ χ^{−1}∘det (177) on φ_{r,ρ}(Ξ) and φ ⊗ φ^♭ ⊗ χ^{−1}∘det (the characters χ, χ^{−1} cancelling). This is applied to the measure Eis_{r,ρ,χ} attached by Lemma 7.4.2 to Ξ ↦ ∫_{X_p × T_H(ℤ_p)} (χ, Ξ) dEis, dEis an axiomatic Eisenstein measure as in §8.2.
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §9.1.1 — the twisted character λ^♭
items.statement: If λ : 𝐓_{K,κ,R} → ℂ is a character of the Hecke algebra, λ^♭(T) := λ(T^♭), where ♭ is the involution of Lemma 6.6.1(ii).
items.note: Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 9.1.2 — λ_{π̄} = λ^♭_π
items.statement: Let π be a cuspidal automorphic representation of G of type (κ, K). Then λ_{π̄} = λ^♭_π.
items.note: Proof: at unramified places from (148); by Hypothesis 6.6.4 and strong multiplicity one for the base change to GL(n)_𝒦, π̄ and π^♭ have isomorphic local components at all places split in 𝒦/𝒦^+, in particular at p; then uniqueness of the ordinary and anti-ordinary eigenspaces and the definition of ♭. Remark 9.3.2(6) asserts instead that the lemma only needs Hypothesis 7.3.3 (v4's proof cited 'strong multiplicity one (Hypothesis 7.3.3)') — see source issues. Source issues: sourceIssues E151. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Theorem 9.1.3 — the Garrett map preserves π (Garrett; Gelbart–Piatetski-Shapiro–Rallis)
items.statement: If φ ∈ π then G(φ) ∈ π. More precisely (the observation of [Gar84, GPSR87]): for φ ∈ π, I(φ, φ′, f, s) ≡ 0 unless φ′ ∈ π^∨, so G(φ) ∈ Hom(π^∨, ℂ) ≃ π.
items.note: Cited, not proved: the basic property of the doubling method from [Gar84] and [GPSR87]. Conventions: G(φ) is a form on G_2 ≅ G_1 (twisted by χ^{−1}∘det); 'G(φ) ∈ π' is up to these identifications.Missing: no layer plans it. Routed to the doubling Part II (route 1), which AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 imports.

items.name: Corollary 9.1.4 — the Garrett map as a Hecke-equivariant homomorphism
items.statement: The Garrett map defines a homomorphism I(χ_f, m) → Hom_{𝐓_{K,κ}}(H^0_!(_K Sh(V), ω_κ)^∨, H^0_!(_K Sh(−V), ω_{κ^♭})), and hence → Hom_{𝐓_{K,κ}}(H^d_!(Sh_K(V), ω^D_κ ⊗ L(−κ)), H^0_!(_K Sh(−V), ω_{κ^♭})), where the Hecke algebras act through the isomorphism of §6.6 and I(χ_f, m) is the finite part of the degenerate principal series I(χ, m). Equivalently, (F^†)^{−1} ∘ G(•, •) defines a homomorphism I(χ_f, m) → Hom_{𝐓_{K,κ},♭}(H^0_!(_K Sh(V), ω_κ)^∨, H^0_!(_{K^†} Sh(V), ω_{κ^†})) (Hom of modules for the ♭-twisted action). The factor L(−κ) is reinserted to respect the Hecke action; the action of 𝐓_{K,κ} on L(−κ) factors through the similitude map.
items.note: No proof beyond 'In terms of parameters, this becomes' after Theorem 9.1.3; the Hecke equivariance (with the involution ♭) implicitly uses Lemma 9.1.2. F^† is the isomorphism of §6.5.3.Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Lemma 9.1.5 — axiomatic Eisenstein measures satisfy the equivariance Assumption 7.4.4
items.statement: Let dEis be an axiomatic Eisenstein measure as in Definition 5.3.2. Then dEis satisfies the equivariance property of Assumption 7.4.4: for each χ, the specialisation φ_{χ,r,ρ} has Im(φ_{χ,r,ρ}) ⊂ Hom_{𝐓_{r,ρ·α(χ)}}(Ŝ^ord_{(ρ·α(χ)),V}(K_{1,r}, 𝒪), S^ord_{(ρ·α(χ))^♭,−V}(K_{2,r}, 𝒪) ⊗ χ∘det), with 𝐓_{r,ρ·α(χ)} acting on the second factor via Lemma 6.6.7(ii).
items.note: One-line proof: 'This corresponds to the equivariance property of the Garrett map stated in Corollary 9.1.4.' Allows §7.5 (Proposition 7.4.15) to be applied to dEis. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: §9.1.6, (179) — pairing the Eisenstein measure with the family: reduction to the holomorphic Eisenstein series
items.statement: Fix an anti-ordinary π ⊗ π^♭ as at the beginning of §9, let π′ range over S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π) (r^1, κ^1 varying), and choose test vectors φ ∈ Î_π, φ^♭ ∈ Î_{π^♭} anti-holomorphic, anti-ordinary and 𝒪-integral as after Lemma 9.0.1; by Proposition 7.3.5, Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭} is identified with the corresponding anti-holomorphic anti-ordinary subspace of π′ ⊗ π′^♭, the image of φ ⊗ φ^♭ being written φ′ ⊗ φ′^♭ (realised by λ_{π′} ∈ X(κ^1, r^1, R), Proposition 7.4.15; equivalently φ = 1 ⊗ φ′ in the free 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ^1,𝒪,π}-module 𝕋_{K^p_{r^1},κ^1,𝒪,π} ⊗ Î_π). Substituting Ξ = ψρ^υ (ψ ∈ C_r(T_H(ℤ_p), R), R ⊂ 𝒪): L_{φ′⊗φ′^♭}(∫_{X_p × T_H(ℤ_p)} (χ, ψρ^υ) dEis) = D(χ) · L_{φ⊗φ^♭}(res_3 D(κ, m, χ_0) E^holo_{χ_0,ψρ^υ}(m)) (179), with D(χ) as in (108), D(κ, m, ·) the differential operator of Corollary 4.4.9 and E^holo as in (112), (113).
items.note: Consequence of Definition 5.3.2 in the form (113) (normalised at S) and Lemma 9.1.5. (113), of which (179) is the specialisation, is written with χ_u (D(κ, m, χ_u) E^holo_{χ_u,c}(m)); (179) and Proposition 9.1.7 write χ_0 — a notational inconsistency (see source issues). Source issues: sourceIssues E152. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Proposition 9.1.7 — the pairing equals a normalised doubling zeta integral
items.statement: Assume π satisfies Hypotheses 7.3.2 and 7.3.3. Let φ ∈ Î_π, φ^♭ ∈ Î_{π^♭}, π′ ∈ S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π) for some r^1, κ^1, and φ′ ⊗ φ′^♭ the corresponding element of π′ ⊗ π′^♭. Suppose (χ, ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H with ψ ∈ C_r(T_H(ℤ_p), R), χ = ||•||^m χ_u, m ≥ n. Then L_{φ′⊗φ′^♭}(∫_{X_p × T_H(ℤ_p)} (χ, ψρ^υ) dEis) = D(χ) · [Vol(I^0_{r,V}) Vol(I^0_{r,−V})]^{−1} · I(φ′, φ′^♭, D(κ, m, χ_0) f^holo(χ_u, ψρ^υ), m), where I is the zeta integral of §4.1.4 and f^holo(χ_u, c) = ⊗_{σ∈Σ_F} J_{m,χ_u,σ} ⊗ ⊗_{v∤∞} f_v(χ_v, c) (112).
items.note: Proof: with [G_3] = G_3(ℚ)Z(ℝ)\G_3(𝔸) and dg^χ_2 = χ(det g_2)^{−1} dg_2, 'doubling' Lemma 7.5.3 (applying it to G_3) gives L_{φ′⊗φ′^♭}(res_3 D E^holo(m)) = [Vol Vol]^{−1} ∫_{[G_3]} D(κ, m, χ_0) E^holo_{f(χ_0,ψρ^υ)}((g_1, g_2), m) φ′(g_1) φ′^♭(g_2) ||ν(g_1)^{a(κ)}|| dg_1 dg^χ_2, then compare with (179) and the definition of the zeta integral. (113) has D(κ, m, χ_u) where this proposition has D(κ, m, χ_0), and the volumes are written at level r where r = r^1 is meant (see source issues); the reconciliation of the ν-factor and of the integration domain is implicit (sourceIssues E153). Source issues: sourceIssues E152, sourceIssues E153. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 9.1.8 — explicit value of the pairing via the local zeta integrals
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Proposition 9.1.7, suppose φ ⊗ φ^♭ lies in the space (175), so φ, φ^♭ have the corresponding factorisations at p and ∞, and let κ, ρ, ρ^υ determine one another as in (95), (97). Then L_{φ′⊗φ′^♭}(∫_{X_p × T_H(ℤ_p)} (χ, ψρ^υ) dEis) = D(χ) ∏_v I_v(φ_v, φ^♭_v, f_v, m) [schematic; by (51) and Proposition 9.1.7 this should carry ⟨φ′, φ′^♭⟩ and [Vol(I^0_{r,V})Vol(I^0_{r,−V})]^{−1}] = [Vol(I^0_{r,V}) Vol(I^0_{r,−V})]^{−1} ⟨φ′, φ′^♭_χ⟩_χ · I_p(χ, κ) I_∞(χ, ρ^υ) I_S L^S(m + 1/2, π′, χ_u), where the factors are those of Theorem 4.6.1 ('Proposition 4.6.1'): I_p = L_p(s, ord, π, χ) × ∏_w [𝔙_w ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w}], I_∞(χ, κ) = ∏_σ I_σ(χ_σ, κ_σ), I_S = ∏_{v∈S} D_v(χ)·volume(𝒰_v).
items.note: 'A consequence of the local computations summarised in Proposition [= Theorem] 4.6.1 and of Definition 5.3.2 and Corollary 8.2.4.' Formaliser's caution: with the trace-compatible normalisation of the test vectors, ⟨φ′, φ′^♭_χ⟩_χ is proportional to Vol(I^0_{r,V} ∩ I^0_{r,−V}) (Lemma 8.5.3) and so is ∏_w ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩ (Lemma 8.4.9); the right-hand side therefore depends on r while the left does not — the local pairings at p are counted twice (inherited from Theorem 4.6.1). See sourceIssues E58. Source issues: sourceIssues E154, sourceIssues E58, sourceIssues E156. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Corollary 9.2.1 — existence of the interpolating element L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) (unsimplified form)
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Corollary 9.1.8 there is a unique element L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) ∈ Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 such that, for any classical χ : X_p → R^× and any π′ ∈ S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π) for some r^1, the image of L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) under the map Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 → R induced by the character χ ⊗ λ_{π′} equals [Vol(I^0_{r^1,V}) Vol(I^0_{r^1,−V})]^{−1} ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩_χ · I_p(χ, κ^1) I_∞(χ, ρ^υ) I_S L^S(m + 1/2, π′, χ_u). Here λ_{π′} is the character of 𝕋 of §6.6.8, the local factors are those of Theorem 4.6.1, dEis is the axiomatic Eisenstein measure of Corollary 8.2.4, and L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) is the element L(φ, φ ⊗ φ^♭) of Proposition 7.4.15 for the measure dEis.
items.note: Reinterpretation of Corollary 9.1.8 via Proposition 7.4.15 (uniqueness from Lemma 7.4.14/Lemma 5.1.3: the element is determined by its classical specialisations). The same caveat as for Corollary 9.1.8 applies to the factor I_p (sourceIssues E58). The admissible range of (χ, π′) is that of Proposition 9.1.7 ((χ, ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H with κ^1 ↔ ρ, m ≥ n).Source issues: sourceIssues E58, sourceIssues E155, sourceIssues E156, sourceIssues E157. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Main Theorem 9.2.2 — the p-adic L-function L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) of the Hida family of π
items.statement: (Transcribed from p. 144–145.) Let π be a cuspidal anti-holomorphic automorphic representation of G_1 which is ordinary of type (κ, K), and let 𝕋 = 𝕋_π be the corresponding connected component of the ordinary Hecke algebra. Let φ and φ^♭ be respectively elements of R-bases of Î_π and Î_{π^♭}. Assume π satisfies the following Hypotheses: 1. Hypothesis 7.3.2 (the Gorenstein Hypothesis); 2. Hypothesis 7.3.3 (the Global Multiplicity One Hypothesis); 3. Proposition-Hypothesis 7.3.5 (the Minimality Hypothesis). There is a unique element L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) ∈ Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 with the following property. For any classical χ = ||•||^m χ_u : X_p → R^×, and for any π′ ∈ S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π) for some r^1, the image of L(Eis, φ ⊗ φ^♭) under the map Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 → R induced by the character χ ⊗ λ_{π′} equals c(π′, χ) · Ω_{π′,χ}(φ, φ^♭) I_∞(χ, κ^1) I_S L_p(m, ord, π′, χ_u) · L^S(m + 1/2, π′, χ_u) / P_{π′,χ}. Here λ_{π′} is the character of 𝕋 defined in Section 6.6.8 and Ω_{π′,χ}(φ, φ^♭) = ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩_χ / (Vol(I^0_{r^1,V} ∩ I^0_{r^1,−V}) · Q[π′, χ]) and P_{π′,χ} = Q^{−1}_{π′,χ}. Finally, the factor Ω_{π′,χ}(φ, φ^♭) is independent of r^1 and p-integral, and is a p-unit for appropriate choice of φ and φ^♭. — NOTATION SPELLED OUT: (Hyp 7.3.2) with Λ^o_π, T_π = 𝕋 and T̂_π = Hom_{Λ^o_π}(T_π, Λ^o_π): (i) there is an isomorphism 𝒢_π : T̂_π ≅ T_π of free rank-one T_π-modules; (ii) Hom_{𝒪_π}(lim_{→r} S^ord_κ(K^p_r, 𝒪_π), 𝒪_π)_{𝔪_π} is a free T_π-module. (Hyp 7.3.3) every π′ ∈ S(K^p, π) = ∪_{r≥1} ∪_{κ_1} S(K_r, κ_1, π) occurs with multiplicity one in the cuspidal spectrum of G. (Prop.-Hyp. 7.3.5) for every (κ_1, r_1) there is an isomorphism of 𝕋_{K^p_{r_1},κ_1,𝒪,π}-modules 𝕋_{K^p_{r_1},κ_1,𝒪,π} ⊗ Î_π ≅ Hom(S^ord_{κ_1}(K^p_{r_1}, 𝒪)_{𝔪_π}, 𝒪), compatible with r_1 > r and specialising at λ_π to the tautological Î_π ≅ Hom(I_π, 𝒪) (an anti-holomorphic π satisfies these if its complex conjugate/contragredient does, p. 119). 𝕋_π = T_{K^p,𝒪_π,𝔪_π} is the localisation of the big ordinary Hecke algebra at 𝔪_π = ker L̄_π (§7.3); Î_π is the fixed finite free 𝒪-module with 𝕋_π ⊗_𝒪 Î_π ≅ Hom_𝒪(lim_{→r} S^ord_κ(K_r, 𝒪)_{𝔪_π}, 𝒪) (§7.3.4), realised as a lattice of anti-ordinary vectors, and Î_{π^♭} = I_π = Hom(Î_π, 𝒪); Λ_{X_p,R} = R[[X_p]], X_p the ray class group of 𝒦 of conductor p^∞ (§5.2); S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π) is, for anti-holomorphic π (§6.6.8, §9.1.6), the set of anti-holomorphic anti-ordinary π′ with π′^♭ ∈ S(K_{r^1}, κ^1, π^♭) = {ordinary holomorphic π″ of type (κ^1, K_{r^1}) with λ̄_{π″} = λ̄_{π^♭}} (149); λ_{π′} is the character of 𝕋 through which 𝕋 acts on π′ (§6.6.8); φ^♭_χ = φ^♭ ⊗ χ^{−1}∘det and ⟨φ_1, φ_2⟩_χ is the L²-pairing of φ_1 with φ_2 ⊗ χ∘det (Remark 4.1.6), so ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩_χ = ⟨φ, φ^♭⟩, with φ, φ^♭ transported to π′ ⊗ π′^♭ by Prop. 7.3.5; I^0_{r,V} ⊂ G_1(ℤ_p) and I^0_{r,−V} ⊂ G_2(ℤ_p) are the Iwahori subgroups of level p^r for V and −V (§8.3, §8.4); Q[π′, χ] and Q_{π′,χ} are the positive real generators of the rank-one R-modules L[π′] = Vol(I_{V,r} ∩ I_{−V,r})^{−1}⟨H^{d,ord}_{κ,V}(K, ψ, R)[π′], H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r, ψ^{−1}, R)[π′^♭]_χ⟩^{Ser}_κ and L_{π′} (same with the localisation H^{d,ord}_{κ^♭,−V}(K^♭_r, ψ^{−1}, R)_{π′^♭}) (Lemma 6.7.6), and c(π′, χ) ∈ R is defined by c(π′, χ) Q_{π′,χ} = Q[π′, χ], a generator of the congruence ideal C(π′, χ) (Lemma 6.7.7), independent of χ; I_∞(χ, κ^1) = ∏_σ I_σ(χ_σ, κ^1_σ), the archimedean doubling zeta integrals of Proposition 4.5.6 (non-zero algebraic numbers, [Gar08]); I_S = ∏_{v∈S} D_v(χ) · volume(𝒰_v) with D_v(χ) = ∏_{r=0}^{n−1} L_v(2m + n − r, χ^+ η^r), χ^+ = χ_u|_{𝔸^×_{𝒦^+}}, η = η_{𝒦/𝒦^+} (Theorem 4.6.1, (108)); L_p(s, ord, π′, χ) := ∏_{w|p} L(s, ord, π′_w, χ_w) (Theorem 4.6.1), where L(x, ord, π_w, χ_w) = ω_{a_w}(−1) L(x, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ^{−1}_{1,w}) / [ε(x, π̃_{a_w} ⊗ χ^{−1}_{1,w}) L(1 − x, π_{a_w} ⊗ χ_{1,w})] · L(x, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) / [ε(x, π_{b_w} ⊗ χ_{2,w}) L(1 − x, π̃_{b_w} ⊗ χ^{−1}_{2,w})] with π_{a_w}, π_{b_w}, χ_{1,w}, χ_{2,w} as in §4.3 ((83), (86)); by (83) the factor produced by the zeta integral at s = m is L_p(m + 1/2, ord, π′, χ_u), not L_p(m, …) (see source issue); L^S(s, π′, χ_u) is the partial standard L-function of π′ twisted by χ_u with the Euler factors at v ∈ S, at the places above p (implicitly; replaced by L_p(·, ord, …)) and at ∞ removed. Implicit conditions: the §9 standing assumption (π, π^♭ anti-ordinary at all w | p), κ satisfying (166), and — as in Proposition 9.1.7 — (χ, ψρ^υ) ∈ Y^class_H with κ^1 ↔ ρ relative to χ via (95), (97), and m ≥ n.
items.note: Proof in the paper: from Corollary 9.2.1 by writing Q[π′, χ] = c(π′, χ) Q_{π′,χ} (Lemma 6.7.7) and using Remark 4.6.2 (I_p / (Vol(I^0_{r,V})Vol(I^0_{r,−V})) = L_p(s, ord, π, χ) ∏_w ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} / Vol(I^0_{r,V} ∩ I^0_{r,−V})); the final claim is Lemma 8.5.3. Unwinding, c·Ω/P = ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩_χ / Vol(I^0_{r^1,V} ∩ I^0_{r^1,−V}), so the asserted value is ⟨φ, φ^♭_χ⟩_χ Vol(I^0_{r^1,V} ∩ I^0_{r^1,−V})^{−1} I_∞ I_S L_p L^S(m+1/2, π′, χ_u): the factor ∏_{w|p} ⟨φ_w, φ̃_w⟩_{π_w} of Remark 4.6.2 has silently disappeared — which is what makes the Main Theorem r^1-independent (sourceIssues E58). Other source issues: L_p(m, …) should be L_p(m + 1/2, …); the admissible (χ, π′) are not restricted in the statement; the proof's second 'Vol(I^0_{r^1,V})' should be Vol(I^0_{r^1,−V}). v4 (p. 133–134) has the same formula with c(π′), Ω_{π′}, P_{π′}, Q[π′] (no χ), 'for any π′ congruent to π', and 'Hypothesis 7.3.5'. Endpoint of the paper (interpolation property (2) of the introduction).Source issues: sourceIssues E58, sourceIssues E73, sourceIssues E155, sourceIssues E158, sourceIssues E157. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 9.3.1 — on the Gorenstein Hypothesis
items.statement: The Gorenstein hypothesis can often be verified, via the Taylor–Wiles method, when the residual Galois representation attached to π has sufficiently general image ([Pil11], [Har13b] give examples); it is not valid in complete generality. Since the Gorenstein condition is open, replacing Λ_{X_p,R} ⊗̂ 𝕋 by the fraction fields of its irreducible components gives a more general statement: the method provides p-adic meromorphic functions on each such component, specialising at classical points as in the Main Theorem.
items.note: Commentary; the meromorphic generalisation is asserted, not proved. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 9.3.2 — Global Multiplicity One holds when the base change is cuspidal; sketch for removing Hypothesis 6.6.4
items.statement: For an automorphic representation of a unitary group such as G_1 whose base change to GL(n) is cuspidal, the global multiplicity one hypothesis 7.3.3 is a consequence of [Mok15, KMSW14]. The stronger Hypothesis 6.6.4 can be removed by: (1) letting <π> be the global L-packet {π′ : λ_{π′} = λ_π}; (2) <π> ⊂ S(K^p, π), and replacing the isomorphisms of Lemma 6.6.10 by j_{<π>} : ⊕_{π_i∈<π>} π^ord_p ⊗ π^{K_S}_{i,S} ≅ ⊕_{π_i∈<π>} π^{K_S}_{i,S} ≅ S^ord_κ(K_r; E)[λ_π] ⊗_E ℂ, with ⊕_{π_i∈<π>} S^ord_κ(K_r; R)[π_i] := S^ord_κ(K_r; R)_π ∩ S^ord_κ(K_r; E)[λ_π] identified with an R-lattice; (3) modifying Lemma 6.6.12 analogously (H^{d,ord}_{κ^D}(K_r, R)[π] then defines a lattice in the sum of the π^{♭,K_S}_{i,S}); (4) replacing Lemma 6.6.5(i) by j_{<π>} : ⊕_{π_i∈<π>} π^{K_S}_{i,S} ⊗ π_p^{I_r} ≅ S_κ(K_r, ℂ)(π); (5) replacing Î_π, Î_{π^♭} by direct sums over the π_i; (6) Lemma 9.1.2 only depends on Hypothesis 7.3.3. Alternatively one may use an idempotent e_{π,S} in the Hecke algebra relative to K_S isolating the π_v at inert v ∈ S (e_{π,S} ⋆ π_i = 0 for π_i ≠ π in <π>), redefining the spaces as its images; 'all of the main theorems remain true without modification'; better, an idempotent mod p lifted to characteristic 0.
items.note: Cites [Mok15, KMSW14] (endoscopic classification) for multiplicity one. The sketch is not a proof. Point (6) conflicts with the proof of Lemma 9.1.2, which invokes Hypothesis 6.6.4 (source issue). Source issues: sourceIssues E151.
