Planned: ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 plans the Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs; AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 9.3.3 — the Minimality Hypothesis
items.statement: The Minimality Hypothesis is a consequence of one part of the Gorenstein Hypothesis; it was included to work with a module [Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}] locally constant on the Hida family, and can be eliminated at the cost of a less clean statement.
items.note: Consistent with Proposition 7.3.5 being deduced from Hypotheses 7.3.2 and 7.3.3 (p. 111–112); the Main Theorem nevertheless lists it as hypothesis 3. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: Remark 9.3.4 — the factor I_S and exceptional zeros
items.statement: The volume factor I_S is a placeholder. Replacing I_S by Ĩ_S = ∏_{v∈S} L_v(m + 1/2, π_v, χ_{u,v})^{−1} I_S, the specialised value can be written c(π) · Ω_π(φ, φ^♭) · I_∞(χ, κ) Ĩ_S L_p(m, ord, π, χ_u) L(m + 1/2, π, χ_u) / P_π, with L(s, π, χ_u) the standard L-function without archimedean factors; the inverted Euler factors L_v(m + 1/2, π_v, χ_{u,v})^{−1} can produce exceptional zeros. Ideally one would choose an optimal vector in [Î_π ⊗ Î_{π^♭}] and adapt the local Eisenstein sections at S to it; the authors do not see how.
items.note: Uses the v4 notation c(π), Ω_π, P_π (without χ) of the Main Theorem; consistent reformulation since I_S L^S = Ĩ_S L. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses.

items.name: [Cas95, Thm. 3.2.4] — Frobenius reciprocity for normalised parabolic induction (as used in Lemma 8.3.2)
items.statement: For an admissible representation V of G_w = GL_n(𝒦_w), a Borel subgroup B_w with Levi T_w, and a character α of T_w, the map Hom_{G_w}(V, Ind^{G_w}_{B_w}(α)) → Hom_{B_w}(V_{B_w}, ℂ(λ)), ϕ ↦ (v̄ ↦ ϕ(v)(1)), is an isomorphism, where λ = αδ_w^{1/2}, V_{B_w} is the Jacquet module and Ind is unitary (normalised) induction.
items.note: Cited, not proved (Casselman's unpublished notes). Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Jacquet functors and duals.

items.name: [Cas95, Prop. 3.1.2, 3.1.3] — contragredient of an induced representation and the invariant pairing
items.statement: (Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α)^∨ ≅ Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α^{−1} (normalised induction), the duality being given by ⟨ϕ, ϕ′⟩ = ∫_{GL_n(𝒪_w)} ϕ(k) ϕ′(k) dk for ϕ ∈ Ind α, ϕ′ ∈ Ind α^{−1}.
items.note: Cited; also used in Lemma 8.4.9. Planned: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Jacquet functors and duals; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.3 plans smooth contragredient duality.

items.name: [Hid98, §5, (5.3), Prop. 5.4] — Hida's ordinary part of N-invariants and the Jacquet module
items.statement: (a) For an admissible representation V of GL_n(𝒦_w), with N = B^u_w ∩ GL_n(𝒪_w) and the double-coset operators U_j = [N t_j N] on V^N = ∪_r V^{I_{w,r}}: V^N = V^N_nil ⊕ V^N_inv (U_j nilpotent, resp. invertible), and the projection V → V_{B_w} induces a U_j-equivariant isomorphism V^N_inv ≅ V_{B_w}, U_j acting on V_{B_w} as δ_w(t_j)^{−1} t_j. (b) If the characters α^x (x ∈ W) are pairwise distinct, the Jacquet module I(α)_{B_w} of I(α) = Ind^{G_w}_{B_w} α is semisimple and ≅ ⊕_{x∈W} ℂ(α^x δ_w^{1/2}).
items.note: Cited ('by the same arguments explaining [Hid98, (5.3)]', 'just as in [Hid98]', 'cf. [Hid98, Prop. 5.4]'), adapted to the non-standard Borel B_w. Planned: AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L4 ('Ordinary unitary groups and the doubling method') plans EHLS in its exact setting, down to Main Theorem 9.2.2 and its three hypotheses; SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.2 plans induction, Frobenius reciprocity, Jacquet functors and duals.
